quotations.original: ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν  τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί, Λέων ἐπὶ τῷ, μετὰ δ’ αὐτὸν Παρθένος  αἱ δ’ ἐπί οἱ Χηλαὶ καὶ Σκορπίος αὐτὸς Τοξευτής τε καὶ Αἰγόκερως, ἐπὶ δ’ Αἰγοκερῆϊ Ὑδροχόος  δύο δ’ αὐτῷ ἔπ’ Ἰχθύες ἀστερόεντες, τοὺς δὲ μέτα Κριός, Ταῦρος δ’ ἐπὶ τῷ Δίδυμοί τε. ἐν τοῖς ἠέλιος φέρεται δυοκαίδεκα πᾶσιν πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.
quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name 'Circle of the figurines' (zōidiōn kuklos, i.e. the zodiac): in it is Cancer, after that there is Leo, after that is Virgo, and after that, the Claws and Scorpio itself, Sagittarius and Capricorn, and after Capricorn, Aquarius, and after it, the two starry Fish (i.e. Pisces), and after them Aries, and after it Taurus and Gemini. In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: τῷ δὲ μηνὶ τῷ Ξανθικῷ, ὃς Νισὰν παρ’ ἡμῖν καλεῖται καὶ τοῦ ἔτους ἐστὶν ἀρχή, τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ κατὰ σελήνην ἐν Κριῷ τοῦ ἡλίου καθεστῶτος  τούτῳ γὰρ τῷ μηνὶ τῆς ὑπ’ Αἰγυπτίους δουλείας ἠλευθερώθημεν
quotations.translation: (The sacrifice of pascha is celebrated) in the month of Xanthikos, which among us (sc. Jews) is called Nisan and is the beginning of the year, on the fourteenth (of the month) according to the Moon, when the Sun is in Aries—for in this month we were liberated from servitude to Egyptians

quotations.original: κατέναντι δὲ τῆς κεφαλῆς τῆς Μεγάλης Ἄρκτου ὁ Ἡνίοχος ἔχει τοὺς ὤμους λοξὸς ὢν ὑπὲρ τοὺς πόδας τῶν Διδύμων, ἔχων τὸν δεξιὸν πόδα κοινὸν τῷ ἐν ἄκρῳ τῷ ἀριστερῷ κέρατι τοῦ Ταύρου
quotations.translation: "Opposite the head of the Great Bear, the Charioteer, which stands at a slant, has its shoulders above the feet of the Twins (i.e. Gemini), sharing its right foot with the (star) at the tip of the left horn of the Bull (i.e. Taurus)"

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν 
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί (...) 
τοὺς δὲ μέτα Κριός, Ταῦρος δ’ ἐπὶ τῷ Δίδυμοί τε.
ἐν τοῖς ἠέλιος φέρεται δυοκαίδεκα πᾶσιν
πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι
κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.
quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name 'Circle of the figurines' (...) in it is Cancer (...) and after them Aries, and after it Taurus and Gemini

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: κατέναντι δὲ τῆς κεφαλῆς τῆς Μεγάλης Ἄρκτου ὁ Ἡνίοχος ἔχει τοὺς ὤμους λοξὸς ὢν ὑπὲρ τοὺς πόδας τῶν Διδύμων, ἔχων τὸν δεξιὸν πόδα κοινὸν τῷ ἐν ἄκρῳ τῷ ἀριστερῷ κέρατι τοῦ Ταύρου
quotations.translation: Opposite the head of the Great Bear, the Charioteer, which stands at a slant, has its shoulders above the feet of the Twins (i.e. Gemini), sharing its right foot with the (star) at the tip of the left horn of the Bull (i.e. Taurus)

quotations.translation: In it (sc. the Tropic of Cancer) are the middle of Cancer and the width-wise cross-section of the body of Leo

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν·
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί (...)

quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name 'Circle of the figurines': in it is Cancer (...) In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

’

quotations.original: νειόθι δὲ σπείρης μεγάλας ἐπιμαίεο Χηλάς· ἀλλ’ αἱ μὲν φαέων ἐπιδευέες, οὐδὲν ἀγαυαί
quotations.translation: At the bottom of the coil (sc. of the Crown), search for the great Claws, but they are poor in illumination, without any brilliance

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν·
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί, Λέων ἐπὶ τῷ, μετὰ δ’ αὐτὸν
Παρθένος· αἱ δ’ ἐπί οἱ Χηλαὶ καὶ Σκορπίος αὐτὸς
(...)
ἐν τοῖς ἠέλιος φέρεται δυοκαίδεκα πᾶσιν
πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι
κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.
quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name ‘Circle of the figurines’: in it is Cancer, after that there is Leo, after that is Virgo, and after that, the Claws (Libra) and Scorpio itself (...) In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

quotations.original: Σκορπίου· οὗτος διὰ τὸ μέγεθος εἰς δύο δωδεκατημόρια διαιρεῖται· καὶ τὸ μὲν ἐπέχουσιν αἱ χηλαί, θάτερον δὲ τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὸ κέντρον. τοῦτον, φασίν, ἐποίησεν Ἄρτεμις ἀναδοθῆναι <ἐκ> τῆς κολώνης τῆς Χίου νήσου, καὶ τὸν Ὠρίωνα πλῆξαι, καὶ οὕτως ἀποθανεῖν, ἐπειδὴ ἐν κυνηγεσίῳ ἀκόσμως αὐτὴν ἐβιάσατο· ὃν Ζεὺς ἐν τοῖς λαμπροῖς ἔθηκε τῶν ἄστρων, ἵν’ εἰδῶσιν οἱ ἐπιγινόμενοι ἄνθρωποι τὴν ἰσχύν τε αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν δύναμιν.
quotations.translation: On Scorpio: this one is divided into two dodekatamoria because of its size. One is occupied by the claws, and the other by the body and stinger. They say Artemis caused it to spring from the hill on the island of Chios and sting Orion, and that was how he died, since he made an unseemly assault on her while hunting—and Zeus placed him among the bright stars, so that people in the future would know his strength and power.

quotations.original: ὅταν δὲ αἱ Χηλαὶ ἀνατέλλωσι, συνανατέλλει μὲν αὐταῖς ὁ ζῳδιακὸς ἀπὸ Χηλῶν μοίρας ιϛʹ ἕως Σκορπίου μοίρας ϛʹ· μεσουρανεῖ δὲ ἀπὸ Καρκίνου ιηʹ ἕως Λέοντος ιαʹ
quotations.translation: When the Claws rise, there rises with them the zodiac from 16 degrees of Libra until 6 degrees of Scorpio, and culminates (lit. is in midheaven) from 18 of Cancer until 11 of Leo

quotations.original: ὅταν δὲ αἱ Χηλαὶ ἀνατέλλωσι, συνανατέλλει μὲν αὐταῖς ὁ ζῳδιακὸς ἀπὸ Χηλῶν μοίρας ιϛʹ ἕως Σκορπίου μοίρας ϛʹ· μεσουρανεῖ δὲ ἀπὸ Καρκίνου ιηʹ ἕως Λέοντος ιαʹ
quotations.translation: When the Claws rise, there rises with them the zodiac from 16 degrees of Libra until 6 degrees of Scorpio, and culminates (lit. is in midheaven) from 18 of Cancer until 11 of Leo

quotations.original: Τῶν δὲ Χηλῶν τοῦ Σκορπίου οἱ μὲν ἐν ἄκραις αὐταῖς ὡσαύτως διατιθέασι τῷ τε τοῦ Διὸς καὶ τῷ τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ. οἱ δὲ ἐν μέσαις τῷ τε τοῦ Κρόνου καὶ ἠρέμα τῷ τοῦ Ἄρεως
quotations.translation: Of the Claws of the Scorpion, the (stars) in the very tips (sc. of the claws) dispose (their effects) similarly to the (star) of Jupiter and the (star) of Mercury, and the ones in the middles, to the (star) of Saturn and the one of Mars

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν·
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί, Λέων ἐπὶ τῷ, μετὰ δ’ αὐτὸν
Παρθένος· αἱ δ’ ἐπί οἱ Χηλαὶ καὶ Σκορπίος αὐτός
(...)

πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι
κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.

In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

quotations.original: Σκορπίου· οὗτος διὰ τὸ μέγεθος εἰς δύο δωδεκατημόρια διαιρεῖται· καὶ τὸ μὲν ἐπέχουσιν αἱ χηλαί, θάτερον δὲ τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὸ κέντρον. τοῦτον, φασίν, ἐποίησεν Ἄρτεμις ἀναδοθῆναι <ἐκ> τῆς κολώνης τῆς Χίου νήσου, καὶ τὸν Ὠρίωνα πλῆξαι, καὶ οὕτως ἀποθανεῖν, ἐπειδὴ ἐν κυνηγεσίῳ ἀκόσμως αὐτὴν ἐβιάσατο· ὃν Ζεὺς ἐν τοῖς λαμπροῖς ἔθηκε τῶν ἄστρων, ἵν’ εἰδῶσιν οἱ ἐπιγινόμενοι ἄνθρωποι τὴν ἰσχύν τε αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν δύναμιν.
quotations.translation: On Scorpius: this one is divided into two dodekatemoria because of its size. One is occupied by the claws, and the other by the body and stinger. They say Artemis caused it to spring from the hill on the island of Chios and sting Orion, and that was how he died, since he made an unseemly assault on her while hunting—and Zeus placed him among the bright stars, so that people in the future would know his strength and power.

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ τὰ μέσα τοῦ Αἰγόκερω καὶ οἱ πόδες τοῦ Ὑδροχόου (...) τοῦ Σκορπίου τὸ κέντρον· εἶτα διὰ τοῦ Τοξότου πρὸς τὰ μέσα τοῦ Αἰγόκερω συνάπτει
quotations.translation: In it (sc. the Tropic of Capricorn) are the middle of Capricorn and the feet of Aquarius (...) the stinger of Scorpio, and then it joins to the middle of Capricorn via Sagittarius

quotations.original: Τοξότης οἶκος Διός, ἀρρενικόν, πυρῶδες, ἀνωφερές, φωνῆεν, κάθυγρον διὰ τὴν Ἀργώ, ἀγαθόν, πτερωτόν, εὐμετάβολον, δίσωμον, διφυές, αἰνιγματῶδες, ὀλιγόγονον, ἡμιτελές, ἡγεμονικόν, βασιλικόν
quotations.translation: Sagittarius is a house of Jupiter, a masculine (sign), of fire, ascending, vocal, moist on account of Argo, good, winged, variable, two-bodied, two-natured, enigmatic, of low fertility, half-complete, hegemonic, royal

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ τὰ μέσα τοῦ Αἰγόκερω καὶ οἱ πόδες τοῦ Ὑδροχόου (...) τοῦ Σκορπίου τὸ κέντρον· εἶτα διὰ τοῦ Τοξότου πρὸς τὰ μέσα τοῦ Αἰγόκερω συνάπτει.
quotations.translation: In it (sc. the Tropic of Capricorn) are the middle of Capricorn (the goat-horned one) and the feet of Aquarius (...) the stinger of Scorpio, and then it joins to the middle of Capricorn via Sagittarius.

quotations.original:
Νειόθι δ’ Αἰγοκερῆος, ὑπὸ πνοιῇσι νότοιο,
Ἰχθῦς ἐς Κῆτος τετραμμένος αἰωρεῖται.
quotations.translation: Beneath the goat-horned one (Capricorn), by the gusts of the south-wind, the (southern) Fish, turned towards the Sea-Monster (Cetus), is suspended.

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν·
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί, Λέων ἐπὶ τῷ, μετὰ δ’ αὐτὸν

πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι
κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.
quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name “Circle of the figurines”: in it is Cancer, after that there is Leo, after that is Virgo, and after that, the Claws and Scorpio itself, Sagittarius and Capricorn (the goat-horned one) (...). In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Αἰγόκερως οἶκος Κρόνου, θηλυκόν, τροπικόν, γεῶδες, φθοροποιόν, ἄγονον, κατωφερές, κατεψυγμένον, ἄφωνον, δουλικόν, κακῶν αἴτιον, ἀσελγές, λατρευτικόν, αἰνιγματῶδες, διφυές, κάθυγρον, ἡμιτελές, κυρτοειδές, χωλόν, δύσις κόσμου, μόχθων καὶ πόνων δηλωτικόν, λαοξοϊκόν, γεωργικόν.
quotations.translation: Capricorn (the goat-horned one) is a house of Saturn, a feminine (sign), tropic, of earth, destructive, infertile, descending, chilled (or, parched), unvoiced, of slaves, a source of evils, wanton, servile, enigmatic, two-natured, moist, half-complete, hunchbacked, lame, the descent of the cosmos, indicative of trouble and pain, of stonemasons, of farmers.

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ τὰ μέσα τοῦ Αἰγόκερω καὶ οἱ πόδες τοῦ Ὑδροχόου (...) τοῦ Σκορπίου τὸ κέντρον· εἶτα διὰ τοῦ Τοξότου πρὸς τὰ μέσα τοῦ Αἰγόκερω συνάπτει
quotations.translation: In it (sc. the Tropic of Capricorn) are the middle of Capricorn and the feet of Aquarius (...) the stinger of Scorpio, and then it joins to the middle of Capricorn via Sagittarius

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν·
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί, Λέων ἐπὶ τῷ, μετὰ δ’ αὐτὸν
Παρθένος· αἱ δ’ ἐπί οἱ Χηλαὶ καὶ Σκορπίος αὐτὸς
Τοξευτής τε καὶ Αἰγόκερως, ἐπὶ δ’ Αἰγοκερῆϊ 
Ὑδροχόος (...)
ἐν τοῖς ἠέλιος φέρεται δυοκαίδεκα πᾶσιν
πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι
κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.
quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name 'Circle of the figurines' (zōidiōn kuklos, i.e. the zodiac): in it is Cancer, after that there is Leo, after that is Virgo, and after that, the Claws and Scorpio itself, Sagittarius and Capricorn, and after Capricorn, Aquarius (...) In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἀνδρομέδα, τὸν μὲν ἀριστερὸν ὦμον ἔχουσα τῶν Ἰχθύων ὑπὲρ τοῦ πρὸς βορρᾶν, τὴν δὲ ζώνην ὑπὲρ τοῦ Κριοῦ, πλὴν τὸ Τρίγωνον, ὅ ἐστι μεταξύ· τὸν δ’ ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ ἀστέρα κοινὸν ἔχει τῷ τῆς κοιλίας τοῦ Ἵππου
quotations.translation: Andromeda, with her left shoulder above the northern part of the Fish (i.e. Pisces), her girdle above Aries, except for the Triangle, which is in between, and she shares the star in her head with that of the belly of the Horse

quotations.original:
ζωϊδίων δέ ἑ κύκλον ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν·
τῷ ἔνι Καρκίνος ἐστί, Λέων ἐπὶ τῷ, μετὰ δ’ αὐτὸν
Παρθένος· αἱ δ’ ἐπί οἱ Χηλαὶ καὶ Σκορπίος αὐτὸς
Τοξευτής τε καὶ Αἰγόκερως, ἐπὶ δ’ Αἰγοκερῆϊ 
Ὑδροχόος· δύο δ’ αὐτῷ ἔπ’ Ἰχθύες ἀστερόεντες, 
τοὺς δὲ μέτα Κριός, Ταῦρος δ’ ἐπὶ τῷ Δίδυμοί τε.
ἐν τοῖς ἠέλιος φέρεται δυοκαίδεκα πᾶσιν
πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄγων, καί οἱ περὶ τοῦτον ἰόντι
κύκλον ἀέξονται πᾶσαι ἐπικάρπιοι ὧραι.
quotations.translation: They call it (sc. the ecliptic) by the name 'Circle of the figurines': in it is Cancer, after that there is Leo, after that is Virgo, and after that, the Claws and Scorpio itself, Sagittarius and Capricorn, and after Capricorn, Aquarius, and after it, the two starry Fishes (i.e. Pisces), and after them Aries, and after it Taurus and Gemini. In all twelve of them the Sun moves along as it passes each year, and as it goes around this circle, all the seasons wax fruitful.

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἰχθύες εἰσὶν ἐν οὐρανῷ θῆλυ, κάθυγρον, πάρυγρον, δίσωμον, πολύγονον, λειχηνῶδες, λεπιδωτόν, νευρῶδες, κυρτωτόν, ἀλφῶδες, δίμορφον, ἄφωνον, πολυκίνητον, λεπρῶδες, ἀντικείμενον ἑαυτῷ διὰ τὸ τὸν μὲν νότιον εἶναι, τὸν δὲ βόρειον· ἔστι δὲ καὶ κάθυγρον, κατωφερές, δουλικόν, εὐμετάβολον, πολύγονον, δίσωμον, συνουσιαστικόν, μελοκοπούμενον, πλάνης αἴτιον, ποικίλον
quotations.translation: Pisces is a feminine (zodiac sign) in the heavens, moist, of the waterside, two-bodied, fertile, cankerous, scaly, sinewy, hunchbacked, spotted, two-formed, unvoiced, much-moved, leprous, in self-opposition on account of the one (part) being southerly and the other northerly. It is also moist, descending, of slaves, variable, fertile, two-bodied, sociable (or, promiscuous)

quotations.original: χρηματιστικὰ ζῴδια λέγεται τὰ δʹ κέντρα καὶ αἱ τούτων ἐπαναφοραί
quotations.translation: Active zodiac signs are called the 4 cardinal points (kentra) and their following places (epanaphorai)
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: χρηματίζοντες ⟨ἀστέρες⟩ λέγονται οἱ ἐπὶ δυνάμεως ἐπίκεντροι ἢ ἐπίκληροι καὶ οἱ ἐπὶ φάσεως ἢ οἱ τρίγωνοι Ἡλίου γινόμενοι. συγχρηματίζοντες δὲ οἱ κοινῶς ἔγκεντροι ἢ ἔγκληροι καὶ οἱ ἐπὶ φάσεως. ἀχρημάτιστοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ μὴ οὕτως ἔχοντες
quotations.translation: Stars that are active are called those in force (and) in cardinal points, or “heirs” (or, in lots), and those in phase, or those in trine with the Sun. (Stars) that are jointly active are those generally at cardinal points, or “heirs,” and those in phase. Inactive are those that are not in this disposition
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: χρηματίζοντες ⟨ἀστέρες⟩ λέγονται οἱ ἐπὶ δυνάμεως ἐπίκεντροι ἢ ἐπίκληροι καὶ οἱ ἐπὶ φάσεως ἢ οἱ τρίγωνοι Ἡλίου γινόμενοι. συγχρηματίζοντες δὲ οἱ κοινῶς ἔγκεντροι ἢ ἔγκληροι καὶ οἱ ἐπὶ φάσεως. ἀχρημάτιστοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ μὴ οὕτως ἔχοντες
quotations.translation: Stars that are active are called those in force (and) in cardinal points, or “heirs” (or, in lots), and those in phase, or those in trine with the Sun. (Stars) that are jointly active are those generally at cardinal points, or “heirs,” and those in phase. Inactive are those that are not in this disposition
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.translation: Helpers are called the stars that jointly possess (a zodiac sign) or are in aspect or are intervening

quotations.original: συνεργοί εἰσιν οἱ συνοδεύοντες, ὑπουργοὶ δὲ οἱ συμβάλλοντες

quotations.original: συμπαθεῖς εἰσιν οἱ κατ’ ἴσον ἀπέχοντες κατ’ ἐπιθεώρησιν ἀλλήλων σύμφωνοι· ἀσυμπαθεῖς δὲ οἱ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ἐπιθεωροῦντες ἀλλήλους· ὅπερ γίνεται ἐκ τῆς τῶν ἀσυνδέτων ζῳδίων ἀποστροφίας· ἔστιν δὲ ἀσύνδετα τὰ παρ’ ἑκάτερα καὶ τὰ διὰ ϛʹ καὶ ηʹ ζῳδίων ἀριθμούμενα
quotations.translation: Sympathetic (planets) are those that are an equal distance apart and harmonious in their aspect with each other, and unsympathetic are those that are not in any kind of aspect with each other, which results from the aversion of unconnected zodiac signs. Unconnected (zodiac signs) are those that are counted one after another and six and eight apart.
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: προστάσσειν λέγεται ὅταν ἐν ἰδίῳ οἴκῳ ἀστὴρ ὑπὲρ γῆς ἐπίκεντρος τύχῃ καὶ τὰ δύο φῶτα ἐπιθεωρῇ χρηματίζων· διὸ λέγεται προστάσσων ὅταν καὶ ἐν ὶδίῳ οἴκῳ ἐπίκεντρος τύχῃ καὶ συσχηματίζηται τῇ Σελήνῃ· ἐάν τις τύχῃ τῶν εʹ ἀστέρων ἐπίκεντρος, μὴ ⟨ἐπι⟩μαρτυρῶν τῇ Σελήνῃ, χρηματίζει· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἐπιμαρτυρεῖ τῇ Σελήνῃ τρίγωνος ἢ τετράγωνος ἢ διάμετρος, προστάσσει· ἐὰν δὲ ὡροσκοπῇ Ἥλιος, προστάσσει· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἡ Σελήνη αὐτῷ τύχῃ τρίγωνος, καὶ προστάσσει καὶ χρηματίζει ὁ Ἥλιος.
quotations.translation: It is called “to command” whenever a planet is in its own house, above the Earth, at a cardinal point, in aspect with the two luminaries, and active (chrëmatizō). Therefore it is called “to command” whenever (a planet) is both at a cardinal point, in its own house, and in configuration with the Moon. If one of the five planets is at a cardinal point and not in aspect with the Moon, it is active, and if it is in trine, quartile, or diametrical aspect (opposition) with the Moon, it commands. If the Sun is in the Ascendant, it commands, and if the Moon is also in trine aspect with it, the Sun both commands and is active.
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: ἰσχύοντες λέγονται ἀστέρες οἱ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐπικαίρων τῆς γενέσεως τόπων τύχοντες· τουτέστι ἐπίκεντροι· καὶ οἱ ἐπὶ φάσεως καὶ οἱ ἐπίκληροι καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς συνόδοις ἀκριβῶς ὄντες
quotations.translation: Those planets are said to be strong that are in the opportune places in a nativity—that is, at cardinal points—and those in phase and “heirs” (or, in lots) and those precisely in conjunction
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: κακοῦται ἀστὴρ ὅταν μὴ εἰς ἁρμόζοντα τύχῃ παρὼν ἢ περιέχηται ὑπὸ κακοποιῶν ἢ κατ’ ἐναντίον ἢ ἐπιδέκατον· ὅτι ἀγαθοποιὰ ζῴδιά εἰσιν ὁ ὡροσκόπος, τὸ μεσουράνημα, ιαʹ, εʹ θεός, θεά· κακοποιὰ δὲ βʹ, δʹ ϛʹ, ζʹ, ⟨ηʹ⟩, ιβʹ
quotations.translation: A planet is oppressed whenever it is present in an unsuitable (place?) or is surrounded by malefics or in a relation of opposition (to them) or being “tithed” (by them): benefic zodiac signs are the Ascendant, Midheaven, the 11th (place), the 5th, God, Goddess, and malefic ones are the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 7th, <8th,> 12th (places).
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: προσνεύων λέγεται ὁ ἀκολουθῶν τῷ προερχομένῳ
quotations.translation: The (planet) following is said to be “inclining towards” the (planet) preceding it.
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: ὁμοροοῦν λέγεται ζῴδιον τῇ Σελήνῃ τὸ ἐπαναφερόμενον ἐφ’ ὃ φέρεται· τὸ γὰρ αὐτὸ καὶ παράκολλον καλεῖται· ἀποσαλεῦον δὲ τὸ μηδὲ ὁροούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς Σελήνης ζῴδιον
quotations.translation: A zodiac sign is said to “be a neighbor” to the Moon that is in a following position (epanapheromai) to the (sign) in which (the Moon) is: the same (sign) is called “attached”; the zodiac sign that has no contiguity(?) with the Moon is “anchored offshore”
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: ὁμορόησις δέ ἐστιν, ὅταν ἐν τοῖς αὐτοῖς ὁρίοις ἀστέρες ὦσιν ἤτοι κατὰ σῶμα ἢ σχῆμα ἢ ἀλλήλους ἐφορῶσιν ὁρίοις ἀστέρος τοῦ αὐτοῦ.
quotations.translation: “Neighboring” is whenever planets are in the same terms, that is, either bodily or in configuration, or are in aspect with each other in the terms of the same planet
quotations.publication: CCAG I

quotations.original: ὡς ὁμορόησις λέγεται ὅταν ἐν τοῖς αὐτῶν ὁρίοις ἀστέρες ὦσιν ἢ κατὰ κόλλησιν ἢ κατὰ σχῆμα οἱονδήποτε ἀλλήλους ἐφορῶσιν ἐν ὁρίοις τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἀστέρος ὄντες· κενοδρομία δὲ ὅταν ἡ Σελήνη μηδενὶ συνάπτῃ μήτε ζῳδιακῶς μήτε μοιρικῶς μήτε κατὰ κόλλησιν μήτε κατὰ σχῆμα μήτε μὴν ἐντὸς λʹ μοιρῶν τῶν ἔγγιστα συναφὴν ἢ σύνοδον ποιεῖσθαι μέλλῃ· καὶ ὡς κακοῖ τὸ σχῆμα τὴν γένεσιν.
quotations.translation: (Antiochus says) that it is called “neighboring” whenever planets are in their terms, or are in attachment or in aspect with each other in any configuration in the terms of the same planet. “Running empty” is whenever the Moon is not in contact with any (planet), neither with respect to zodiac signs nor with respect to degrees nor in attachment(?) nor in configuration nor even about to make a union or conjunction within the next 30 degrees, and (Antiochus says) that this configuration oppresses the nativity.
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.3

quotations.original: ὡς ὁμορόησις λέγεται ὅταν ἐν τοῖς αὐτῶν ὁρίοις ἀστέρες ὦσιν ἢ κατὰ κόλλησιν ἢ κατὰ σχῆμα οἱονδήποτε ἀλλήλους ἐφορῶσιν ἐν ὁρίοις τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἀστέρος ὄντες· κενοδρομία δὲ ὅταν ἡ Σελήνη μηδενὶ συνάπτῃ μήτε ζῳδιακῶς μήτε μοιρικῶς μήτε κατὰ κόλλησιν μήτε κατὰ σχῆμα μήτε μὴν ἐντὸς λʹ μοιρῶν τῶν ἔγγιστα συναφὴν ἢ σύνοδον ποιεῖσθαι μέλλῃ· καὶ ὡς κακοῖ τὸ σχῆμα τὴν γένεσιν.
quotations.translation: (Antiochus says) that it is called “neighboring” whenever planets are in their terms, or are in attachment or in aspect with each other in any configuration in the terms of the same planet. “Running empty” is whenever the Moon is not in contact with any (planet), neither with respect to zodiac signs nor with respect to degrees nor in attachment(?) nor in configuration nor even about to make a union or conjunction within the next 30 degrees, and (Antiochus says) that this configuration oppresses the nativity.
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.3

quotations.original: τὴν κατὰ κράτος καθυπερτέρησιν λέγουσιν ὅταν ἐπὶ τοῦ θʹ ζῳδίου γένηται ἀστήρ· ὅταν δὲ μηδεὶς παρῇ ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐννάτου, ἰσχύει· γίνονται δὲ καθυπερτερήσεις καὶ μοιρικαὶ τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον· ὅταν δύο ἀστέρες ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ ζῳδίῳ τύχωσιν, καὶ ὁ μὲν ἐλάσσονας μοίρας ἐπέχων τὸν τὰς πλείονας μοίρας ἔχοντα καθυπερτερεῖ. οἷον ἔστω τὸν τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ ἀστέρα εἶναι Κριῷ περὶ μοῖραν ιʹ, τὸν δὲ τοῦ Κρόνου ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ ζῳδίῳ περὶ μοῖραν κεʹ· δῆλον ὅτι ὁ τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ τὸν τοῦ Κρόνου μοιρικῶς καθυπερτερεῖ.
quotations.translation: They call it “superiority by force (kata kratos kathuperterēsis)” whenever a planet (that is superior) is in the 9th zodiac sign (sc. the ninth place), and whenever no (planet) is in the ninth (but one is superior?), it is strong. Superiorities by degrees (kathuperterēseis moirikai) also happen in the following manner: whenever two planets are in the same zodiac sign, the one with fewer degrees is superior to the one with more degrees. For example, let it be the case that Mercury is in Aries at degree 10, and Saturn in the same zodiac sign at degree 25: it is clear that Mercury is superior to Saturn with respect to degrees.
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: DIŠ dUTU AN.GE6 GAR ERIN2.MEŠ LUGAL UG7.MEŠ
quotations.translation: If the Sun makes an eclipse: the troops of the king will die.

iti.ŠU mul.SIPA.ZI.AN.NA
d.NIN.ŠUBUR SUKKAL.MAḪ
quotations.translation:
Dûzu, constellation of the True Shepherd of Anu (Orion)
Ninšubur, the great Visir
quotations.publication: Casaburi, M. C. 2003. Tre-stelle-per-ciascun (-mese): l'Astrolabio B: edizione filologica. Annali/Supplemento

quotations.original: ¶ ina iti.ŠU BAR2 GAL UŠ₂-ma DUMU-šú AŠ.TE DAB ŠE.GIŠ.I₃ ⸢u?⸣ […]
quotations.translation: If in Dûzu the harvest a great king will die and his son will take the throne, Sesame [...]
quotations.publication: Gehlken, E. 2008. Die Adad-Tafeln der Omenserie Enuma Anu Enlil; T. 2: die ersten beiden Donnertafeln (EAE 42 und EAE 43). Zeitschrift für Orient-Archäologie, 1, 256-314.

quotations.transliteration: sẖ ḥm-nṯr n spd.t ỉmy-r(ꜣ) mšꜥ n ỉꜥḥ wꜥb n p(ꜣ) 5 sbꜣ ꜥnḫ.w
quotations.translation: Written by the prophet of Sothis, overseer of the moon's movement, and wrist of the five living stars.
quotations.publication: Griffith, F.Ll., Catalogue of the Demotic Graffiti of the Dodecaschoenus (Oxford, 1935 - 1937)

quotations.original: ἐν ἰδίαις λαμπήναις λέγονται οἱ ἀστέρες ὅταν ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων ὑψωμάτων τύχωσι
quotations.translation: The planets are said to be “in their own covered chariots” whenever they are at their own exaltations
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: δορυφόροι ἀστέρες λέγονται ἑῷοι μὲν ⟨οἱ⟩ προαναφερόμενοι Ἡλίῳ, ἑσπέριοι δὲ οἱ προανατέλλοντες μὲν Ἡλίῳ, τῇ δὲ Σελήνῃ ἐπαναφερόμενοι
quotations.translation: “Bodyguards” are called planets at dawn (or, in the east) when they rise before the Sun, and at evening (or, in the west) when they rise before the Sun and rise following the Moon
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: ¶ iti.KIN mul.PAN d.INANNA ELAM.MA.ki.KE₄ <DUMU.MUNUS AN.NA.KE₄>
quotations.translation: Month VI, constellation of the Bow, "Elamite" Inanna,
quotations.publication: Casaburi, M. C. 2003. Tre-stelle-per-ciascun (-mese): l'Astrolabio B: edizione filologica. Annali/Supplemento

quotations.original: αἱ πρὸ Ἡλίου ιεʹ ⟨μοῖραι⟩ εὐσεβῶν λέγονται, ὡς ἀπολελυμέναι ἤδη τῶν τοῦ Ἡλίου αὐγῶν· αἱ δὲ μεθ’ Ἡλίου μοῖραι ιεʹ ἀσεβῶν, ὅτι οἱ ἐκεῖ εὑρισκόμενοι ἀστέρες ἀδρανέστεροί εἰσιν ὑποπεπτωκότες ταῖς Ἡλίου αὐγαῖς
quotations.translation: The 15 <degrees> before the Sun are called those “of the pious,” as they are already “discharged from the service of” the rays of the Sun, and the 15 degrees after the Sun, those “of the impious,” because the planets found there are weaker, having “fallen at the feet” of the rays of the Sun.
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original:
iti.NE šu-ku-du d.nin-urta KI.NE.MEŠ
ut-tap-pa-ḫa di-pa-ru a-na d.a-nun-na-ke₄
in-na-aš₂-ši
quotations.translation: Month V, the arrow, Ninurta, the braziers are lightened, the torch is lifted to the Annunaki
quotations.publication: Casaburi, M. C. 2003. Tre-stelle-per-ciascun (-mese): l'Astrolabio B: edizione filologica. Annali/Supplemento

quotations.original: αἱ πρὸ Ἡλίου ιεʹ ⟨μοῖραι⟩ εὐσεβῶν λέγονται, ὡς ἀπολελυμέναι ἤδη τῶν τοῦ Ἡλίου αὐγῶν· αἱ δὲ μεθ’ Ἡλίου μοῖραι ιεʹ ἀσεβῶν, ὅτι οἱ ἐκεῖ εὑρισκόμενοι ἀστέρες ἀδρανέστεροί εἰσιν ὑποπεπτωκότες ταῖς Ἡλίου αὐγαῖς
quotations.translation: The 15 <degrees> before the Sun are called those “of the pious,” as they are already “discharged from the service of” the rays of the Sun, and the 15 degrees after the Sun, those “of the impious,” because the planets found there are weaker, having “fallen at the feet” of the rays of the Sun.
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: Σελήνης ἑσπερία ἀνατολὴ λέγεται ὅταν ἀπὸ συνόδου φέρηται μέχρι πανσελήνου, ἑῴα δὲ ἀνατολὴ ἀπὸ πανσελήνου μέχρι συνόδου
quotations.translation: It is called the Moon’s western rising whenever it moves from conjunction (with the Sun) to full Moon, and (the Moon’s) eastern rising (whenever it moves) from full Moon to conjunction
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: Σελήνης ἑσπερία ἀνατολὴ λέγεται ὅταν ἀπὸ συνόδου φέρηται μέχρι πανσελήνου, ἑῴα δὲ ἀνατολὴ ἀπὸ πανσελήνου μέχρι συνόδου
quotations.translation: It is called the Moon’s western rising whenever it moves from conjunction (with the Sun) to full Moon, and (the Moon’s) eastern rising (whenever it moves) from full Moon to conjunction
quotations.source: Sarapion of Alexandria, Various Names for Configurations of the Stars
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: ⸢ina⸣ ⸢iti⸣KIN.2.KAM UD.8.KAM ina dUTU.E₃ IGI ŠA₂ KUR ŠA₂?-ab
quotations.translation: in the intercalary month VI, day 8, at sunset morning first the middle
quotations.publication: Reiner, E., Pingree, D. (1975). Babylonian Planetary Omens: Part One. Enūma Anu Enlil Tablet 63: The Venus Tablet of Ammiṣaduqa. Undena.

quotations.original: (1) 1 ḪUN mi-⸢nu-u₂⸣ ki al 12 ḪUN LA₂-u₂ 11 LA₂ (2) 11 A.RA₂ 30 5.30 5.30 TA 45 (3) ZI ša₂ ḪUN ZI-ma 39.30
quotations.translation: (1) 1 Aries: whatever it is less than 12 Aries, it is less by 11. (2) 11 times (0);30 is 5;30. You 'tear out’ 5;30 from 45, (3) the subtraction for Aries, it is 39;30.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: (15') ki-i DIŠ.UD ša₂ SIG al-⸢la BE⸣ BAR.NUN u 2 ḪAB-rat DIRI-at BE BAR.NUN u 2 ḪAB-rat (16') TA lib₃-bi-šu₂ LA₂ ana ⸢GI₆ E-bi⸣
quotations.translation: If the DIŠ.UD of height exceeds the elongation, the ṣiliptu-coefficient, and the 2 for the disk you subtract the elongation, the ṣiliptu-coefficient, and the 2 for the disk from it and you call it GI₆.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: (1) 1 ḪUN mi-⸢nu-u₂⸣ ki al 12 ḪUN LA₂-u₂ 11 LA₂ (2) 11 A.RA₂ 30 5.30 5.30 TA 45 (3) ZI ša₂ ḪUN ZI-ma 39.30
quotations.translation: (1) 1 Aries: whatever it is less than 12 Aries, it is less by 11. (2) 11 times (0);30 is 5;30. You subtract (‘tear out’) 5;30 from 45, (3) the subtraction for Aries, it is 39;30.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original:
(1) ⸢ša₂ d⸣.GU₄.UD IGI ša₂ KUR a-na IGI ša₂ KUR
(2) TA 1 A EN 16 MAŠ₂ 1.46 TAB
quotations.translation: (1) For Mercury. Eastern appearance until eastern appearance (2) from 1 Leo until 16 Capricorn you add 1,46.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer

quotations.original: ša₂ GU₄.UD IGI ša₂ ŠU₂ ana IGI ša₂ ŠU₂ TA 6 ALLA EN 26 RIN₂ 2.40 TAB
quotations.translation: For Mercury: western appearance to western appearance from 6 Cancer until 26 Libra you add 2,40.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer

quotations.original: [M]U ana MU ŠU₂ ša₂ ŠU₂ u KUR ša₂ NIM
quotations.translation: Year by year, western setting and eastern rising.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: [M]U ana MU ŠU₂ ša₂ ŠU₂ u KUR ša₂ NIM
quotations.translation: Year by year, western setting and eastern rising.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: IGI ana IGI TA 25 MAŠ.MAŠ EN 30 GIR₂.TAB 30 TAB
quotations.translation: Appearance to appearance: from 25 Gemini until 30 Scorpio you add 30.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: TA UŠ ar₂-tu₂ ana ŠU₂ 17.45 KI DU ŠU₂
quotations.translation: From the second station to the setting it (Jupiter) proceeds (by) 17;45, (then) it sets.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.transliteration: Sbk | pꜣy=f ḫꜥ ỉmnṱ 1513 | tꜣy=f rnp.t ꜥꜣ.t 480
quotations.translation: Mercury | its evening rising | 1514 | its great year 480
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. quotations.transliteration: Sbk | pꜣy=f ḫꜥ ỉmnṱ 1513 | tꜣy=f rnp.t ꜥꜣ.t 480
quotations.translation: Mercury | its western rising 1513 | its great year 480
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.transliteration: (n)-ṯꜣy pꜣ gn⟨ḥ⟩ḏ 6 šꜥ ỉḫ.t 26 r swsw 110 ỉw=f mšꜥ | tny ỉwṱ 20 r mꜣꜥ ḫꜥ 3 r swsw 1 ỉw=k ỉr 3 {100} sp 110 r 330
quotations.translation: From Cancer 6° to Libra 26° is 110 degrees, proceeding at the rate of 0;20, as a part of rising, 3 (of them) make 1 degree. You shall multiply 3 times 110, it makes 330.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.transliteration: ỉw=k wꜣḥ nkt r pꜣy=f ỉry n-ỉm=w r mꜣꜥ ḫꜥ 1513 ꜥn
quotations.translation: You add the numbers to one each other it makes the part of rising 1513 again
quotations.publication: Winkler, A., 2022. The First zodiac Sign and the Daimon: The Advent of an Astrological Tradition and Seven Elaborate Horoscopes, Studien zur Altägyptischen Kultur 51:

quotations.transliteration: (ḥr-pꜣ)-kꜣ pꜣ-nty-ꜣtḥ 25 tꜣy=f dny.t ḥꜥ=f ỉw=f wꜣḥ
quotations.translation: Saturn: Sagittarius 25°: its own terms: it adds
quotations.publication: Winkler, A., 2022. The First zodiac Sign and the Daimon: The Advent of an Astrological Tradition and Seven Elaborate Horoscopes, Studien zur Altägyptischen Kultur 51:

quotations.transliteration: (n)-ṯꜣy pꜣ gn⟨ḥ⟩ḏ 6 šꜥ ỉḫ.t 26 r swsw 110 ỉw=f mšꜥ | tny ỉwṱ 20 r mꜣꜥ ḫꜥ 3 r swsw 1 ỉw=k ỉr 3 {100} sp 110 r 330
quotations.translation: From Cancer 6° to Libra 26° is 110 degrees, proceeding at the rate of 0;20, as a part of rising, 3 (of them) make 1 degree. You shall multiply 3 times 110, it makes 330.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.original: BE-ma ME ana GI₆ DIRI u₄-mu A.RA₂ 4 tal-lak
quotations.translation: If the day(light) exceeds the night you multiply the day(light) by 4.
quotations.publication: Brack-Bernsen, Lis, and Hunger, Hermann. 2002. TU 11. A Collection of Rules for the Prediction of Lunar Phases and of Month Lengths. SCIAMVS 3: 3–90.

quotations.original: 10 ABSIN0 3.20 ša₂ al 10 ABSIN0 DIRI A.RA₂ 40 DU TA 3.20 LA₂
quotations.translation: 10 Virgo 3,20. (The amount) by which it exceeds 10 Virgo you multiply by (0);40, subtract from 3,20.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: (25') ana 1 UŠ KI ša₂ al 13 (26') ⸢ABSIN0 DIRI⸣ GAM 15 DU KI 1.58.45.42 TAB ana NIM lu ana SIG GAR
quotations.translation: For 1 UŠ by which the position exceeds 13 (26’) Virgo you multiply by (0);15, you add it to 1,58;45,42, you put it down as the ‘height’ or the ‘depth’.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.transliteration: pꜣy=f ḥtp ỉꜣbṱ 1223 tꜣy=f rnp.t ꜥꜣ.t 388
quotations.translation: Its eastern setting 1223; its great year 388
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.original: (7) ⸢U₄.MEŠ ša₂ UŠ ša₂ ŠU₂ ana UŠ ša₂ ŠU₂⸣ (8)  ⸢GU zib.ME 9.51⸣ TAB (9)  [ḪUN] ⸢MUL₂ MAŠ 10.1 TAB⸣ (10)  [ALLA A] ⸢9.59 TAB⸣ (11)  [ABSIN RIN₂] ⸢GIR₂.TAB 9.46 TAB⸣ (12)  [PA] MAŠ₂ 9.49 TAB
quotations.translation: (7) The "days" for western station to western station: (8) Aquarius, Pisces you add 9,51, (9) [Aries], Taurus, Gemini you add 10,1, (10) [Cancer, Leo] you add 9,59, (11) [Virgo, Libra], Scorpio you add 9,46, (12) [Sagittarius], Capricorn you add 9,49.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.transliteration: (n)-ṯꜣy ỉsw 5 šꜥ ḥtr.w 30 r swsw 85 ỉw=f mšꜥ any ỉwt 20 | r mꜣꜥ ḥtp 3 r swsw 1 ỉw=k ỉr 3 r sp 85 r 255
quotations.translation: From Aries 5° to Gemini 30° makes 85 degrees, proceeding at the rate of 0;20°, as the part of setting, 3 (of them) make 1 degree. You shall multiply 3 times 85, it makes 255.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.transliteration: ỉw=k wꜣḥ nkt r pꜣy=f ỉry n.ỉm=w r pꜣy=f mꜣꜥ n ḥtp 1223 ꜥn
quotations.translation: You shall add the numbers to one another, it makes the part of setting 1223 again.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.original: (28') TA UŠ IGI-tu₂ EN UŠ ar₂-tu₂ (29') ša₂ ME 12 ana ar₂-ki-šu₂ LA₂-is-ma UŠ
quotations.translation: (28') From the first station until the second station (29') per day (0);12 it recedes backwards, then it becomes stationary.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.transliteration: pꜣy-ms=w r pꜣ nṯr-t(w)ꜣ n rꜥ-ḥtp ỉw=f ꜥšꜣ wꜥw ỉrm s-ḥm.t
quotations.translation: The one who was born when Venus was in the descendant, he wỉll be in a lot of strife with a woman.
quotations.publication: Quack, J. F., 2008, Texte aus Ägypten: Demotische, magische und divinatorische Texte. In B. Janowski and B. Wilhelm (eds), Omina, Orakel, Rituale und Beschwörungen. Texte aus der Umwelt des Alten Testaments, Neue Folge 4. Gütersloh: Gütersloher Verlagshaus.

quotations.original: [ŠU₂ IGI u] ⸢UŠ⸣ ša₂ ⸢KUR⸣ ana ŠU₂ IGI u UŠ ša₂ KUR 9.35.30 KI TAB
quotations.translation: [Setting, appearance and] station of the east to setting, appearance and station of the east: you add 9,35,30 (to) the position.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: (1) ŠU₂ ša₂ KUR a-na ŠU₂ ša₂ KUR (2) zib.ME ḪUN 3.45.20 TAB (3) MUL₂ MAŠ ALLA 3.29.40 TAB (4) A ABSIN 3.28.50 TAB (5) RIN₂ GIR₂.TAB PA 3.38.30 TAB (6) ⸢MAŠ₂ GU⸣ 3.35.10 TAB
quotations.translation: (1) Eastern setting to eastern setting: (2) Pisces Aries you add 3,45,20; (3) Taurus Gemini Cancer you add 3,29,40, (4) Leo Virgo you add 3,28,50, (5) Libra Scorpio Sagittarius you add 3,38,30, (6) Capricorn, Aquarius you add 3,35,10.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.transliteration: ḫr-ỉr=k wꜣḥ wꜥ pyngs n ꜥš wnw.t ḥr nꜣ tbꜣ.w mtw=k wꜣḥ nꜣ syw.w ḥr-ꜣ.t=f
quotations.translation: You shall put down a table of reading the hour on the bricks and you shall place the "stars" on top of it.
quotations.publication: Faraone, Ch. and Torallas Tovar, S. 2022, Greek and Egyptian Magical Formularies: Text and Translation, vol. I (Berkeley CA)

quotations.original: 2.51 BAR 14 ina KUR 21.10 ḪUN IGI
quotations.translation: (Year) 2,51 month I (day) 14 in the East 21;10 Aries it appears.
quotations.publication: Neugebauer, Otto, 1955, Astronomical Cuneiform Texts

quotations.original: 3 dil-bat ina NIM ar2 GIGIR IGI
quotations.translation: (Month III), (day) 3, Venus appears in the East behind the Chariot.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: 22 GU4.UD ina NIM ina PA.BIL IGI
quotations.translation: (Month VIII), (day) 22, Mercury appears in the East in Pabilsag.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: 7 dil-bat ina NIM ina SAG LU ŠU₂
quotations.translation: (Month XII2), (day) 7, Venus sets in the East in the beginning of Aries
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original:
(1) ⸢u₄⸣-mu dil-bat ina ŠU₂ IGI lu ina KUR ŠU₂-u₂ U₄.MEŠ u KI.MEŠ ana igi-gub-u₂ [x]
(2) ina ŠU.2-ka tu-kal
quotations.translation: (1) The day when Venus appears in the West or sets in the East: (2) you hold the "days" and the positions for the igigubbû-coefficients [...] in your hands.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: 10 GU4.UD ina ŠU₂ ina UR.A 3 KUŠ3 ina IGI dil-bat ana ŠU₂ IGI 16 [NA-su in 8 IGI]
quotations.translation: (Day) 10, Mercury appears in the West in the Lion, 3 cubits in front of Venus to the West, its [NA (sunset to setting of Mercury)] is 16 (UŠ), the (ideal first) appearance was on (day) 8.]
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (16') TA ŠU₂ ana IGI (17') 6.15 KI DU IGI
quotations.translation: (16') From setting to appearance (17') the position proceeds (by) 6;15, (then) it (= Jupiter) appears.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: 28 MUL₂.BABBAR ina SAG MAS.MAS IGI 10 UŠ NA-su
quotations.translation: (Day) 28, Jupiter appears in the beginning of Gemini, its NA (= time from sunset to setting of Jupiter) is 10 UŠ.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: GI₆ 23 ina ZALAG₂ sin SIG MUL₂ ar₂ ša SAG ḪUN 5 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of the 23rd, last part of the night ('at dawn'), Sin (Moon) was 5 cubits below the Rear Star of the Head of the Hired Man.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1989. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. II: Diaries from 261 B.C. to 165 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (18') MU.1-me-1-šu-6.KAM m.A-lek-sa-an-dar LUGAL BAR in EN 10 AN ana NIM ki UŠ-u₂ 1 KUŠ₃ ar₂ 4.AM₃ IGI.ME (19') ša₂ PA ša₂ ana ZA maš-lu UŠ
quotations.translation: (18') Year 1 hundred 66, Alexander was king. Month I, around until (day) 10, when Mars became stationary to the East, it became stationary 1 cubit behind the four front (ones) of Pabilsag which are similar to the (sign) ZA.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. 2006. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. VI: Goal-Year Texts. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (2) [GI₆ 5 SAG GI₆ sin] (3) ina IGI MUL₂ SIG sa SAG GIR₂.TAB 2 2/3 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: (2) [Night of (day) 5, beginning of the night, Sin] (3) was 2 2/3 cubits in front of the lower star of the head of the scorpion.

quotations.original: Ἡμέρα λέγεται διχῶς, καθ’ ἕνα μὲν τρόπον χρόνος ὁ ἀπ’ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου μέχρι δύσεως, καθ’ ἕτερον δὲ τρόπον ἡμέρα λέγεται χρόνος ὁ ἀφ’ ἡλίου ἀνατολῆς μέχρις ἡλίου ἀνατολῆς.
quotations.translation: A day is spoken of in two ways, on the one hand as the time from sunrise till sunset, but on the other hand a day is spoken of as the time from sunrise till sunrise.

quotations.original: Μεγάλη δέ ἐστι διαφορὰ ἀνατολῆς καὶ ἐπιτολῆς. Ἀνατολὴ μὲν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ προειρημένη, ἐπιτολὴ δὲ ἡ γινομένη πρὸς τὸν ὁρίζοντα φάσις μετὰ τῆς πρὸς τὸν ἥλιον ἀποστάσεως ἀπολαμβανομένη.
quotations.translation: And there is a big difference between a (diurnal) rising and a (heliacal) rising. For a (diurnal) rising is the aforementioned, but a (heliacal) rising is the appearance happening at the horizon that is being taken together with the distance to the sun.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original:
Ἦν δ’ οὐδὲν αὐτοῖς οὔτε χείματος τέκμαρ
οὔτ’ ἀνθεμώδους ἦρος οὔτε καρπίμου 
θέρους βέβαιον, ἀλλ’ ἄτερ γνώμης τὸ πᾶν
ἔπρασσον, ἔστε δή σφιν ἀντολὰς ἐγὼ 
ἄστρων ἔδειξα τάς τε δυσκρίτους δύσεις.
quotations.translation:
And they didn't have any sign - neither of winter, 
nor of flowery spring, nor of fruitful 
summer - that was certain, but they did it all without
sense, until I then showed them the risings 
of the stars and the hard to discern settings.
quotations.publication: Aeschylus. 1930. Aeschylus, with an English translation by Herbert Weir Smyth, ed. H.W. Smith. London: William Heinemann.

quotations.original: (6) KI sin NIM KI sin u KI šamaš₂ ša₂ al-la 10 lu-maš DIRI GAM0 16 DU KI BAR.NUN ša₂ l[u-maš] (7) ša₂-šu₂ ki TAB TAB ki LA₂ LA₂ ana muḫ-ḫi a-ḫa-miš₂ GAR.GAR-ma ½-šu₂-nu GIŠ-ma ana BAR.NUN ⸢GAR⸣-[an]

You accumulate (them) together, compute half of it and put it down as the ṣiliptu-coefficient.

Πληιάδων Ἀτλαγενέων ἐπιτελλομενάων
ἄρχεσθ' ἀμήτου, ἀρότοιο δὲ δυσομενάων.
quotations.translation:
When the Pleiades - sprung from Atlas - rise, 
start with the harvesting, and [start] with the ploughing when they set.

quotations.translation: For it happens around these places that the night becomes utterly short, 2 hours for some, 3 for others, so that while a small pause is taking place after the setting, the sun is rising straightaway again.

quotations.original: Τούτου δὲ ὃ μέν τι καλεῖται ἑῴα μὴ φαινομένη ἐπανατολή, ὅταν ὁ ἀστὴρ ἀρχόμενος κρύψιν ποιεῖσθαι μετὰ τὸν ἥλιον εὐθέως αὐτὸς ἀνατείλῃ, ὃ δέ τι καλεῖται ἑῴα συνανατολὴ ἀληθινή, ὅταν ὁ ἀστὴρ ἅμα καὶ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ γένηται τῷ ἡλίῳ ἐπὶ τοῦ πρὸς ἀνατολὰς ὁρίζοντος, ὃ δέ τι καλεῖται ἑῴα προανατολὴ φαινομένη, ὅταν ὁ ἀστὴρ ἀρχόμενος ἐπιτολὴν ποιεῖσθαι προανατείλῃ τοῦ ἡλίου.
quotations.translation: And of this, one is called a dawn invisible following rising, when the star which is starting to make a disappearance is rising itself directly after the sun, and another is called a true dawn simultaneous rising, when the star comes at the same time and at the same place as the sun at the eastern horizon, and another is called a dawn visible leading rising, when the star which is starting to make a heliacal rising is rising before the sun.
quotations.publication: Ptolemy. 1903. Claudii Ptolemaei opera quae exstant omnia volumen I, Syntaxis Mathematica Pars II, Libros VII-XIII continens, ed. J.L. Heiberg. Leipzig: B.G. Teubner.

quotations.original:
Κεῖνος γὰρ ἄλλης ἡμέρας, ὅθ᾽ ἱππικῶν
ἦν ἡλίου τέλλοντος ὠκύπους ἀγών,
εἰσῆλθε πολλῶν ἁρματηλατῶν μέτα.
quotations.translation:
For on another day, when there was 
the swift-footed horse contest as the sun was rising, 
he entered it together with many charioteers.
quotations.publication: Sophocles. 1913. Sophocles. Vol. 2: Ajax, Electra, Trachiniae, Philoctetes, with an English translation by F. Storr. In: The Loeb Classical Library 21, ed. F. Storr. London: William Heinemann & New York: The Macmillan Company.

quotations.original:
Ἠέλιος δ’ ἀνόρουσε, λιπὼν περικαλλέα λίμνην,
οὐρανὸν ἐς πολύχαλκον, ἵν’ ἀθανάτοισι φαείνοι
καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἐπὶ ζείδωρον ἄρουραν.
quotations.translation:
The sun sprang up, leaving the very beautiful sea, 
into the heaven wrought of bronze, to shine for the immortals
and the mortal men upon the wheat-giving land.
quotations.publication: Homer. 1919. Homer. The Odyssey with an English translation by A.T. Murray, Ph.D. in two volumes, ed. A.T. Murray. Cambridge Massachusetts: Harvard University Press & London: William Heinemann.

quotations.original: [ⲁϥϬⲱ ⲉⲟ]ⲩⲛⲧϥ ⲡⲣⲉ ⲺⲥⲟⲩϦⲁⲛ ⲥⲟⲩⲕⲏ ⲛⲧⲟⲩⲁⲣⳖⲁⳖⲉ
quotations.transliteration: [afcô eo]untf pre–souxan soukê ntouarčače
quotations.translation: If he has the sun as a friendly star with Mercury, and they were at the enmity
quotations.publication: J. Černý, P.E. Kahle, and R.A. Parker, 1957, The Old Coptic Horoscope, Journal of Egyptian Archaeology 43, 86-100.

quotations.transliteration: ḫpr=f mtw rmṯ nb rḫ=s ḏd pꜣ h̭m r.wn-nꜣ.w | n wš ẖn pꜣ smn n nꜣ ṱꜣ.w ỉrm nꜣ rnp.wt ỉrm nꜣ md.wt nty (n) hp n rḫ=w ḥr nꜣ mšꜥ.w n tꜣ p.t ỉrm nꜣ sḫny.w (r) dỉ.t mtr=w
quotations.translation: It happened so that everyone may know that the little that was lacking in establishing the times, the year, and the matters that are to be known about the movements of the heavens and the constellations—to have it corrected
quotations.publication: S. Pfeiffer, 2008, Das Dekret von Kanopos (238 v. Chr.): Kommentar und historische Auswertung eines dreisprachigen Synodaldekretes der ägyptischen Priester zu Ehren Ptolemaios' III. und seiner Familie.

quotations.original: Παρανατέλλει δὲ νοτόθεν καὶ τοῦ Ποταμοῦ τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ Ὠρίων.
quotations.translation: And it (i.e. Gemini) rises besides the remaining part of Eridanus (= Ποταμός), and so does Orion.
quotations.publication: Vettius Valens. 1986. Vettii Valentis Antiocheni Anthologarium Libri Novem, ed. D. Pingree. Leipzig: B.G. Teubner.

quotations.original: οἱ δὲ τῆς αἱρέσεως κύριοι Κρόνος καὶ Ἑρμῆς ἀγαθοδαιμονοῦντες εὑρέθησαν.
quotations.translation: The lords of the sect, Saturn and Mercury, were found to be in (the place of) Agathos Daimōn.
quotations.publication: (GH L 62)

quotations.original: ὁ π̣ρ̣[ῶτος κλῆρος τῆς γ]ε̣νέσεως ὅ ἐστιν Ἀγαθὸς Δαίμω̣ν̣ [ἐν Ταύρωι μοιρῶν . . λε]π̣τῶν λδʹ οἴκωι Ἀφροδείτης ὑψώ[ματι Σελήνης ὁρίοις] Ἑρμοῦ καὶ Ἄρεως.
quotations.translation: The first lot of the nativity, that is, Agathos Daimōn, is in Taurus, [..] degrees, 34 minutes, house of Venus, exaltation of the Moon, terms of Mercury and Mars.
quotations.publication: GH 95

quotations.original: ἐπεὶ οὖν νυκτερινὴ ἡ γένεσις ζητῶ Σελήνην· αὕτη τυγχάνει Καρκίνῳ τριγώνῳ Ἄρεως· τὸν δὲ τοῦ Ἄρεως εὕρομεν ἐπαναφερόμενον ἰδίῳ οἴκῳ καὶ τριγώνῳ καὶ αἱρέσει ἰδίᾳ
quotations.translation: Now, since the nativity is nocturnal, I look for the Moon: it is in Cancer, the triangle of Mars, and we found Mars in a succedent place in its own house and triangle and its own sect
In order to know its sign: you ‘raise’ (0);59,8,58,16,17,46,40 to 6,4;30, then (10’) it gives you 5,59;20.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer

quotations.original: 15 ina ZALAG₂ sin⸣ ina IGI šur GIGIR ša₂ SI 2 ⸢KUŠ₃⸣
quotations.translation: Night of (day) 15, last part of the night, Sin was 2 cubits in front of the northern rein of the chariot.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: ⸢USAN⸣ MUL₂.BABBAR SIG šur SI 2 1/2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: First part of the night, Jupiter was 2 1/2 cubits below the northern rein (of the chariot).
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1989. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. II: Diaries from 261 B.C. to 165 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: GE₆ 8 SAG GE₆ sin ina IGI MUL₂ IGI ša₂ še-pit MAŠ.MAŠ 1 1/2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of the 8th, beginning of the night, Sin was 1 1/2 cubits in front of the front star of the twins' feet.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (28) GE₆ 23 USAN AN e MUL₂ ar₂ (29) [ša₂ še]-⸢pit⸣ MAŠ.MAŠ 20 SI
quotations.translation: Night of the 23rd, first part of the night, Mars was 20 fingers above the rear star of the twins' feet.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (18) ⸢GE₆⸣ [6] (19) SAG GE₆ sin e MAŠ.MAŠ ša₂ SIPA 20 SI
quotations.translation: (18) Ni[ght of (day) 6,] (19) beginning of the night, Sin was 20 fingers above the twins’ star of the shepherd.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (31) ma-la ina 18-ka kun-nu u ṭe-pi KI-šu₂ la ṭe-pu-u₂ u₃ nis-ḫu TA ŠA₃ ZI-ma al-la ITI (32) ša₂ UGU-šu₂ LA₂-u₂ ana kun-nu E
quotations.translation: (31) Whatever (month) in your (year) 18 (preceding it) is full, and to which there is no addition added, and a subtraction is subtracted from it, and which is (32) less than the month preceding it, you declare it as full.
quotations.publication: Brack-Bernsen, Lis, and Hunger, Hermann. 2002. TU 11. A Collection of Rules for the Prediction of Lunar Phases and of Month Lengths. SCIAMVS 3: 3–90.

quotations.original: Ἡμέρα λέγεται διχῶς, καθ’ ἕνα μὲν τρόπον χρόνος ὁ ἀπ’ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου μέχρι δύσεως, καθ’ ἕτερον δὲ τρόπον ἡμέρα λέγεται χρόνος ὁ ἀφ’ ἡλίου ἀνατολῆς μέχρις ἡλίου ἀνατολῆς.
quotations.translation: A day is spoken of in two ways, on the one hand as the time from sunrise till sunset, but on the other hand a day is spoken of as the time from sunrise till sunrise.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Οἰκοῦσι δ᾽ οὗτοι πρὸς βορέαν τοῦ Σκόμβρου ὄρους καὶ παρήκουσι πρὸς ἡλίου δύσιν μέχρι τοῦ Ὀσκίου ποταμοῦ.
quotations.translation: And they (i.e. the Treres and Tilataeans) live to the north of the mountain Skombros and they have come along to the west as far as the river Oskios.
quotations.publication: Thucydides. 1942. Thucydides. Historiae in two volumes, eds. H. Stuart-Jones & J.E. Powell. Oxford: Oxford University Press.

quotations.original: Εἰ γὰρ δύναμίν τινα προσεφέρετο ὁ Κύων, ἔδει κατὰ τὴν ἀληθινὴν ἐπιτολὴν τῶν καυμάτων γίνεσθαι ἐπίτασιν· τότε γὰρ ἅμα συνανατέλλει τῷ ἡλίῳ.
quotations.translation: For if the Dog Star would be contributing any power, increase of the burning heat would have occurred at the true heliacal rising: for then it rises simultaneously with the sun.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Εἰ δέ γε ἀπὸ τῆς ἀνατολῆς ἐπὶ τὴν δύσιν ἐφέρετο ὁ ἥλιος, ἀεὶ τοὺς προανατέλλοντας ἀστέρας ἀθεωρήτους ἂν εἶναι συνέβαινεν· (...)
quotations.translation: But if the sun would be moving from the east to the west, it would follow that the stars rising slightly earlier would always be unperceivable; (...)
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Εἰ δέ γε ἀπὸ τῆς ἀνατολῆς ἐπὶ τὴν δύσιν ἐφέρετο ὁ ἥλιος, ἀεὶ τοὺς προανατέλλοντας ἀστέρας ἀθεωρήτους ἂν εἶναι συνέβαινεν· (...)
quotations.translation: But if the sun would be moving from the east to the west, it would follow that the stars rising slightly earlier would always be unperceivable; (...)
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: οἱ τριγωνικοὶ δεσπόται τοῦ ὡροσκόπου καὶ τοῦ αἱρετικοῦ φωτὸς ἀπέκλιναν ἐναντιούμενοι ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ὑπὸ Ἄρεως θεωρούμενοι
quotations.translation: The masters of the triangles of the Ascendant and of the luminary of the sect were in cadent places, being in opposition to themselves and under the aspect of Mars

quotations.original: DIŠ ina iti.APIN ina še-rim mul2.UR.IDIM 2.20 meš-ḫu im-šuḫ A.DAM ⌈BAL.MEŠ⌉-ma A.AB.BA ib-bal
quotations.translation: If in Araḫsamna during the morning-watch, 'The Mad-Dog' - 2,20 - produced a glow; the pasture land(s) will be passed over and the sea will dry up.
quotations.genre: schematic astronomy: 'three stars each' + rising times

quotations.original: DIŠ MUL ša2 ina IGI mul.UZ3 GUB-zu mul.UR.GI7
quotations.translation: ¶ The star which stands in front of the Goat: the Dog.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: ἀναγκαῖον καὶ ἕτερον τόπον ἐκ πείρας δοκιμάσαι (ὃν ἀφθόνως ἐπιδείξω), ὅς ἐστιν αἰτιατικὸς καὶ φόβων καὶ κινδύνων καὶ δεσμῶν παραίτιος. ἔστι μὲν οὖν καὶ οὗτος ὁ τόπος ἰσχυρός, λαμβανόμενος ἡμέρας ἀπὸ Κρόνου ἐπὶ Ἄρεα, νυκτὸς δὲ ἀπὸ Ἄρεως ἐπί Κρόνον, καὶ τὰ ἴσα ἀπὸ ὡροσκόπου.
quotations.translation: It is necessary to test another place by experience (which I will demonstrate amply), which is the “causal” one of fears and dangers and responsible for bonds. This place is also powerful, being measured by day from Saturn to Mars, and by night from Mars to Saturn, and the same distance from the Ascendant.
quotations.publication: Vettius Valens. 1986. Vettii Valentis Antiocheni Anthologarium Libri Novem, ed. D. Pingree. Leipzig: B.G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ἥλιος, Ζεὺς Αἰγοκέρωτι, Σελήνη, Κρόνος Λέοντι, Ἄρης Ἰχθύσιν, Ἀφροδίτη, ὡροσκόπος Σκορπίῳ, Ἑρμῆς Τοξότῃ. οἱ αἰτιατικοὶ τόποι εὑρέθησαν Ἰχθύσι καὶ Σκορπίῳ· ἐν δὲ Σκορπίῳ Ἀφροδίτη, ἐν Ἰχθύσιν Ἄρης.
quotations.translation: Sun, Jupiter in Capricorn; the Moon, Saturn in Leon; Mars in Pisces; Venus, the Ascendant in Scorpio; Mercury in Sagittarius. The causal places were found in Pisces and Scorpio, and in Scorpio, Venus, in Pisces, Mars.
quotations.publication: (GH L 123,I)

quotations.original: τὸν μὲν Ἥλιον καὶ τὸν ὡροσκόπον εἶχε Κριῷ, Σελήνην Ταύρῳ, Κρόνον Κριῷ μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς ἐπὶ ἑῴας ἀνατολῆς τὴν φάσιν ποιούμενον, Ἑρμῆν ὁμοίως ἐν Κριῷ ἐπὶ ἑῴας δύσεως, Δία ἐν Ἰχθύσι ἐπὶ ἑῴας ἀνατολῆς, Ἀφροδίτην ἐν Ἰχθύσι ἐπὶ στηριγμοῦ ἑῴου, Ἄρεα Ὑδροχόῳ ἐπὶ ἀνατολῆς ἑῴας (...) τὸ δὲ κακόβουλον γεγενῆσθαι διὰ τὸ τὸν τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ καὶ τοῦ Κρόνου ἐν ἀρρενικῷ ζῳδίῳ τετυχηκέναι καί τινα τῶν τοῦ γένους ἀπολέσαι διὰ τὸ αὐτὸ σχῆμα· τὸ δὲ αὐτὸν κατακοπῆναι διὰ τὸ τὴν Σελήνην εἶναι ἐν Σκορπίῳ μελεοκοπουμένῳ ζῳδίῳ καὶ ἀκτινοβολεῖν τὸν Ἄρεα ἐπὶ τῆς ἐπαναφορᾶς τοῦ μεσουρανίου ὄντα.
quotations.translation: (The native) had the Sun and the Ascendant in Aries, the Moon in Taurus, Saturn in Aries, making its appearance at eastern rising after three days, Mercury likewise in Aries at western rising, Jupiter in Pisces at eastern rising, Venus in Pisces at evening station, Mars in Aquarius at eastern rising (...) His bad advice happened because Mercury and Saturn happened to be in a masculine zodiac-sign, and he lost someone from his family because of the same configuration, and the fact that he was cut to pieces was because the Moon was in Scorpio, a mutilated zodiac-sign, and was shooting a ray at Mars, which was in the succeedent place to Midheaven.
quotations.publication: (GH L 113,IV)

quotations.original: Ἥλιος Καρκίνου μοίρᾳ κθʹ λʹ, Σελήνη Ἰχθύων μοίρᾳ ιβʹ, Κρόνος Τοξότου μοίρᾳ κζʹ ηʹ, Ζεὺς Αἰγοκέρωτος μοίρᾳ κβʹ ιγʹ, Ἄρης Σκορπίου μοίρᾳ ζʹ κγʹ, Ἀφροδίτη Καρκίνου μοίρᾳ κηʹ ιγʹ, Ἑρμῆς Λέοντος μοίρᾳ ιαʹ κεʹ, ὡροσκόπος Ἰχθύων μοίρᾳ ιζʹ, μεσουράνημα Τοξότου μοίρᾳ κεʹ (...) ἡ οὖν ἄφεσις ἀπὸ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου ἕως τῆς τετραγώνου πλευρᾶς καὶ τῆς πρὸς Κρόνον ἀπὸ διαμέτρου ἀκτινοβολίας εἰς κακοποιοῦ ὅριον· Ἄρης γὰρ τὴν διάμετρον ἀκτῖνα παρήλλαξε διὰ τὸ ἰσόμοιρον εὑρεθέντα Δία κεκωλυκέναι τὴν ἀναίρεσιν.
quotations.translation: The Sun in degree 29;30 of Cancer, the Moon in degree 12 of Pisces, Saturn in degree 27;08 of Sagittarius, Jupiter in degree 22;13 of Capricorn, Mars in degree 7;23 of Scorpio, Venus in degree 28;13 of Cancer, Mercury in degree 11;25 of Leo, the Ascendant in degree 17 of Pisces, Midheaven in degree 25 of Sagittarius (...) The release (start of lifespan) was from the Ascendant up to the side of the quartile and the ray-shooting at Saturn from diametrical opposition into the term of a malefic: for Mars altered its diametrical ray because Jupiter, which was found in equal degree, hindered the effect of the destroyer.
quotations.publication: (GH L 75)

quotations.original: Ἥλιος, Σελήνη, Ζεύς, ὡροσκόπος Κριῷ. Κρόνος, Ἀφροδίτη Ὑδροχόῳ, Ἄρης Διδύμοις, Ἑρμῆς Ἰχθύσιν· ὁ τοιοῦτος ἡγεμονικός, τυραννικός· ἐπίκεντροι γὰρ καὶ ὡροσκοποῦντες οἱ κύριοι τοῦ τριγώνου εὑρέθησαν, καὶ εἰς τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ὁ κλῆρος καὶ ὁ δαίμων καὶ ἡ βάσις καὶ τὸ ὕψωμα ἐξέπεσεν. ὁ δὲ τούτων κύριος Ἄρης ἐκπαραπεσὼν καὶ †ἀμαρτύρητος τῷ τόπῳ† ἐναντία καὶ φυγαδείαν καὶ βιαιοθανασίαν ἐποίησεν· ἦν γὰρ καὶ τῆς συνόδου κύριος.
quotations.translation: The Sun, the Moon, Jupiter, the Ascendant in Aries; Saturn, Venus in Aquarius, Mars in Gemini, Mercury in Pisces. The one with such a nativity was hegemonic, tyrannical: for the rulers of the triangle were found to be at cardinal points, and in the Ascendant, and the lot and the Daimōn and the Foundation and the Exaltation came out in the same place. The ruler of these, Mars, coming out not in aspect to the place, caused adversity and exile and violent death: for it was also ruler of the conjunction.
quotations.publication: (GH L 78)

quotations.original: Ἥλιος, Ἄρης, Ἀφροδίτη Λέοντι, Σελήνη Ὑδροχόῳ, Κρόνος Κριῷ, Ζεὺς Ἰχθύσιν, Ἑρμῆς Καρκίνῳ, ὡροσκόπος Παρθένῳ (...) οἱ κακοποιοὶ ὑπὸ τῆς ἡλιακῆς ἀκτῖνος ἀφαιρετικοὶ καὶ ἀμαυρότεροι γεγόνασι καὶ εἰς ἀσθενεστέρους τόπους πεπτώκασιν.
quotations.translation: The Sun, Mars, Venus in Leo; the Moon in Aquarius; Saturn in Aries; Jupiter in Pisces; Mercury in Cancer; the Ascendant in Virgo (...) The malefics were “subtractive” (retrograde) beneath the ray of the Sun, and dimmer, and they came out at weaker places.
quotations.publication: (GH L 112,VII)

quotations.original: Διὸ τάς τε ἀνατολὰς καὶ παρανατολὰς τῆς κατὰ μῆκος κινήσεως καὶ τὰς ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἀποδιδομένας ἐκλύτους καὶ ῥᾳθύμους αἰτίας τῆς ὑπολείψεως λεγομένης παραιτεῖται.
quotations.translation: For this reason he (i.e. Eudemus) rejects the risings and adjacent risings as (effects) of movement in longitude and the explanations rendered by the elders as weak and facile causes of the direct motion.
quotations.source: Theon of Smyrna, On Mathematics Useful for the Understanding of Plato
quotations.publication: Theon of Smyrna. 1892. Théon de Smyrne, philosophe platonicien. Exposition des connaissances utiles pour la lecture de Platon, traduite pour la première fois du grec en français, ed. J. Dupuis. Paris: Librairie Hachette.

quotations.original: [GE₆ 19] DIR AN ZA ULU₃ GIN ina ZALAG₂ sin ar₂ MAŠ.MAŠ ar₂ 1 KUŠ₃ sin 5 KUŠ₃ ana ULU₃ SIG
quotations.translation: [Night of (day) 19,] clouds were in the sky, the south wind blew; last part of the night, Sin was 1 cubit behind the rear twin, Sin being 5 cubits low to the south.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1989. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. II: Diaries from 261 B.C. to 165 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.translation: [Night of (day) 19,] clouds were in the sky, the south wind blew; last part of the night, Sin was 1 cubit behind the rear twin, Sin being 5 cubits low to the south.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1989. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. II: Diaries from 261 B.C. to 165 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.translation: (3) For Saturn: the ‘height’ is 25;24,5, [the ‘depth’ is 22;41,25], (4) the difference is (0);12; thus [for the ‘days’].
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer

quotations.original: [DIŠ MUL ša2 KI z]a-ri-i ša2 MAR.GID2.DA GUB-zu [m]ul.KA5.A d.Er3-ra gaš-ri DINGIR.MEŠ
quotations.translation: ¶ The star which stands in the shaft of the Wagon: the Fox, Erra, the strong one of the gods.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: DIŠ ⌈MUL ša2⌉ ina ⌈SAG⌉.KI mul.MAR.GID2.DA GUB-zu mul.U8 d.A-a
quotations.translation: ¶ The star which stands in the front part of the Wagon: the Ewe, Aja.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: DIŠ mul.MU.BU.KEŠ2.DA d.A-num GAL-u2 ša2 AN-e
quotations.translation: ¶ The Hitched Yoke, great Anu of heaven.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: DIŠ mul.MAR.GID2.DA.AN.NA d.Dam-ki-an-na
quotations.translation: ¶ The Wagon of Heaven, Damkianna.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: DIŠ MUL ša2 ina ṭur-ri-šu2 GUB-zu mul.IBILA.E2.MAḪ DUMU res-tu-u2 ša2 d.A-nu-um
quotations.translation: ¶ The star which stands in its knot: the Heir of the Sublime Temple, the first-ranking son of Anu.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: GE₆ 22 ina ZALAG₂ sin ar₂ MUL₂ ar₂ ša₂ ALLA ša₂ ULU₃ 2 1/2 KUŠ₃ sin 1 KUŠ₃ ana ULU₃ SIG
quotations.translation: Night of (day) 22, last part of the night, Sin was 2 1/2 cubits behind the rear star of the crab to the south, Sin being 1 cubit low to the south.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: ⸢ina ZALAG₂ dil-bat SIG⸣ SAG A 4 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Last part of the night, Venus was 4 cubits below the head of the lion.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: ⸢ina ZALAG₂⸣ dil-bat e LUGAL 2 SI dil-bat 4 SI ana ŠU₂ LAL
quotations.translation: Last part of the night, Venus was 2 fingers above the king (star), Venus being 4 fingers back to the west.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (5) [GE₆ 10] (6) [SAG] ⸢GE₆ sin SIG⸣ MUL₂ TUR ša₂ 4 [KUŠ₃] ⸢ar₂⸣ LUGAL 1 2/3 KUŠ₃ sin 8 SI ana NIM DIB
quotations.translation: [Night of (day) 10, beginning] of the night, Sin was 1 2/3 cubits below the small star which is 4 cubits behind the king, Sin having passed 8 fingers to the east.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: GI₆ 12 ⸢SI GIN⸣ [ina] ⸢ZALAG₂⸣ MUL₂.BABBAR SIG GIŠ.KUN A 4 1/2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of (day) 12, the north wind blew; last part of the night, Jupiter was 4 1/2 cubits below the rump of the lion.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.transliteration: [ⲁϥⳓⲱ ⲉⲟ]ⲩⲛⲧϥ ⲡⲣⲉ ⲻⲥⲟⲩϧⲁⲛ ⲥⲟⲩⲕⲏ ⲻⲧⲟⲩⲁⲣⳗⲁⳗⲉ ⲻⲡⲓⲥ[ⲟⲩ ...]
quotations.translation: [if] he [had] the sun as a friendly star and Mercury, they were hostile to this st[ar ...
quotations.publication: J. Černý, P.E. Kahle, and R.A. Parker, 1957, The Old Coptic Horoscope, Journal of Egyptian Archaeology 43, 86-100.

quotations.transliteration: ⲁϥϬⲱⲡⲉ ⲟⲩⲛⲺ ⲥⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ ⲧⲓ ⲛⲉϥ Ⳅⲉⲙ ...
quotations.translation: If he had a beneficent star giving him a sign ...
quotations.publication: J. Černý, P.E. Kahle, and R.A. Parker, 1957, The Old Coptic Horoscope, Journal of Egyptian Archaeology 43, 86-100.

quotations.transliteration: (n)-ṯꜣy pꜣ gn⟨ḥ⟩ḏ 6 šꜥ ỉḫ.t 26 r swsw 110 ỉw=f mšꜥ | tny ỉwṱ 20 r mꜣꜥ ḫꜥ 3 r swsw 1 ỉw=k ỉr 3 {100} sp 110 r 330
quotations.translation: From Cancer 6° to Libra 26° is 110 degrees, proceeding at the rate of 0;20, as a part of rising, 3 (of them) make 1 degree. You shall multiply 3 times 110, it makes 330.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. and A. Winkler, 2018. Chaldeans on the Nile: Two Egyptian Procedure Texts with Babylonian System A1 and A2 for Mercury, in Scaffolding of Our Thoughts: Essays on Assyriology and the History of Science in Honor of Francesca Rochberg, eds. J. Crisostomo et al. (Leiden: Brill, 2018), 282-418

quotations.transliteration: ḥsb.t 23.t n ỉꜥḥ rnp.t ꜥꜣ.t tꜣy
quotations.translation: Numbering year 23 of the Moon is a great year.
quotations.publication: Neugebauer, O. & Parker, R.A. EAT 3

quotations.original: Ἐμοὶ γάρ, ὦ ἄνδρες, ὅπερ καὶ πρότερον εἶπον, φίλος ὢν Σώστρατος καὶ οἰκείως διακείμενος ἀπαντήσας ἐξ ἀγροῦ περὶ ἡλίου δυσμὰς συνεδείπνει, καὶ ἐπειδὴ καλῶς εἶχεν αὐτῷ, ἀπιὼν ᾤχετο.
quotations.translation: For, gentleman, as I have said before as well, Sostratos, being a friend of mine and disposed as a house friend, came from the country to meet me around sunset and had dinner with me, and after it had been going well for him, he departed and left.
quotations.source: Lysias 1, On the Murder of Eratosthenes
quotations.publication: Lysias. 1930. Lysias with an English translation by W.R.M. Lamb, ed. W.R.M. Lamb. Cambridge Massachusetts: Harvard University Press & London: William Heinemann.

quotations.original: GI₆ 9 SAG GI₆ sin ina IGI GIR₃ ar₂ ša₂ A 2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of (day) 9, beginning of the night, Sin was 2 cubits in front of the rear foot of the lion.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: Ὡς δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ Στρυμόνος ἐπορεύετο ὁ στρατός, ἐνθαῦτα πρὸς ἡλίου δυσμέων ἐστὶ αἰγιαλὸς ἐν τῷ οἰκημένην Ἄργιλον πόλιν Ἑλλάδα παρεξήιε· αὕτη δὲ καὶ ἡ κατύπερθε ταύτης καλέεται Βισαλτίη.
quotations.translation: And as the army marched from the Strumon, it passed Argilos, there in the west is a sea-shore on which it is situated, a Greek city: and this itself and its upper country are called Bisaltiē.
quotations.publication: Herodotus. 1920. Herodotus, with an English translation by A.D. Godley, ed. A.D. Godley. Cambridge Massachusetts: Harvard University Press.

quotations.original: GI₆ 4 SAG GI₆ sin ina IGI RIN₂ ša₂ ULU₃ 2 1/2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of the 4th, beginning of the night, the moon was 2 1/2 cubits in front of the southern (part of) the scales.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: Ἀπορεῖται δή, πῶς καὶ ἐν ταῖς μακροτάταις καὶ ἐν ταῖς βραχυτάταις νύκτεσιν ἡμικύκλιον τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ κύκλου καὶ ἀνατέλλει καὶ δύνει.
quotations.translation: The question is then, how both in the longest and in the shortest nights a semicircle of the zodiac both rises and sets.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: ina ZALAG₂ GU₄.UD SIG RIN₂ ša₂ SI 2 SI
quotations.translation: Last part of the night, Mercury was 2 fingers below the northern (part of) the scales.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: ki-i TAB-u₂ ina 20 ME 2-ta ŠU.2 ḪAB-rat GAR-an
quotations.translation: When it (the solar eclipse) began in 20 (UŠ) of daytime it made two thirds of the disk.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.
