quotations.original: ¶ mul.dil-bat ina iti.Š[E i]ti.DIRI.ŠE d.30 mul.ŠU.PA
quotations.translation: When Venus in Month XII, intercalary month XII Sin ŠU.PA
quotations.publication: Reiner, E., Pingree, D. 1998. Babylonian Planetary Omens: Part Three.

quotations.original: ¶ ina iti.DIRI.ŠE.KIN.KU₅ BAL-e MAR.TU-i
quotations.translation: ¶ an intercalary Month XII (belongs to) the Amorite reign
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: Εἰσί δὲ δύσεις διτταί· οἵ τε γὰρ ἀφανισμοὶ δύσεις εἰσί· τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν ὅταν ἅμα συνδύνῃ τῷ ἡλίῳ τὸ ἄστρον, καὶ ὅταν ἀνατέλλοντος δύνῃ.
quotations.translation: And the settings are twofold; for the disappearances are settings; and this happens when the star sets simultaneously with the sun, and when it sets during the rising [of the sun].
quotations.publication: Theophrastus. 1916. Enquiry into Plants, Volume II: Books 6-9. On Odours. Weather Signs. Translated by Arthur F. Hort, ed. A.F. Hort. Loeb Classical Library 79. Cambridge Massachusetts: Harvard University Press.

quotations.original: u₃ APIN 30 TA 14 ša₂ DU₆ a-di 12 ša₂ APIN
quotations.translation: and month VIII (begins on day) 30 (of the preceding month): from (day) 14 of month VII until (day) 12 of month VIII
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer

quotations.original: TA 27 zib EN 13 ABSIN₀ AB₂ ana AB₂ 1.58.45.42 TAB u LA₂ lib₃ -bu-u₂ ša₂ MURUB₄ -tu₂ KUR-ad₂
quotations.translation: From 27 Psc until 13 Vir you add and subtract 1,58;45,42 month by month, whereby you reach the central part.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: ⸢GI₆⸣ 26 ŠU₂.ŠU₂ ina ZALAG₂ sin ina IGI MUL₂ e ša₂ SAG GIR₂ 1 1/2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of (day) 26, very overcast; last part of the night, Sin was 1 1/2 cubits in front of the upper star of the head of the scorpion.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1989. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. II: Diaries from 261 B.C. to 165 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: GE₆ 18 ina ZALAG₂ sin ina IGI SI₄ 1 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of the 18th, last part of the night, Sin was 1 cubit in front of Lisi.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original:
Οἷος δ’ ἐκ νεφέων ἀναφαίνεται οὔλιος ἀστὴρ
παμφαίνων, τοτὲ δ’ αὖτις ἔδυ νέφεα σκιόεντα,
ὣς Ἕκτωρ ὁτὲ μέν τε μετὰ πρώτοισι φάνεσκεν,
ἄλλοτε δ’ ἐν πυμάτοισι κελεύων· (...)
quotations.translation:
And as a baneful star plainly appeared out of the clouds 
beaming, and then again sank into the shadowy clouds,
so Hector would appear now with the foremost 
and then among the hindmost, giving orders; (...)
quotations.publication: Homer. 1920. Homeri Opera in five volumes, eds. D.B. Monro & T.W. Allen. Oxford: Oxford University Press.

quotations.original: ὁ Ἥλιος ἐν Παρθένῳ μοίραις ιδʹ, ἡ Σελήνη Ἰχθύσι θʹ, Κρόνος Παρθένῳ ιαʹ, Ζεὺς Τοξότῃ κϛʹ, Ἄρης Ζυγῷ κʹ, Ἀφροδίτη ἐν Παρθένῳ κδʹ, Ἑρμῆς Λέοντι ιηʹ, ὡροσκόπος Ταύρῳ κηʹ, μεσουράνημα Ὑδροχόῳ <ιδʹ>, ἀναβαίνων Κριῷ, κλῆρος Τύχης Σκορπίῳ.
quotations.translation: The Sun in Virgo, 14 degrees; the Moon in Pisces, 9 (degrees); Saturn in Virgo, 11; Jupiter in Sagittarius, 26; Mars in Libra, 20; Venus in Virgo, 24; Mercury in Leo, 18; Ascendant in Taurus, 28; Midheaven in Aquarius, <14>, Ascending (Node) in Aries, Lot of Fortune in Scorpio.

quotations.original: ἡ δὲ θεὰ καὶ σελασφόρος Σελήνη (...) ἐπὶ τῆς ῥάχεως ἀναβιβάζουσα τοῦ Ταύρου.
quotations.translation: The goddess, the light-bearing Moon (...) was ascending upon the backbone of the Bull (Taurus).

quotations.original: Πυρόε[ι]ς δ’ ὁ τοῦ Ἄρεως ἀστὴ̣ρ Ὑδρο̣χόου μοίρας ἀν̣εβίβαζεν δε[κα]ὲξ εἰκοστόν.
quotations.translation: The fiery one, the star of Ares (Mars) was ascending sixteen degrees (and) one twentieth of Aquarius.

quotations.original: ἔστω ὑποδείγματος χάριν Ἥλιος Ταύρου μοίρᾳ αʹ, Σελήνη Διδύμων μοίρᾳ ιϛʹ, ὡροσκόπος Ταύρου μοίρᾳ ιδʹ, ἡ σύνοδος περὶ μοίρας κζʹ τοῦ Κριοῦ, ἀναβιβάζων Αἰγοκέρωτος μοίρᾳ κεʹ
quotations.translation: As an example, let the Sun be in degree 1 of Taurus, the Moon in degree 16 of Gemini, the Ascendant in degree 14 of Taurus, the conjunction (prenatal syzygy) at about 27 degrees of Aries, the ascending (node) in degree 25 of Capricorn.
quotations.publication: (GH L 74,IV)

quotations.original: [ὁ κλῆρος] τῆς ἀνάγκης εὑρέθη Κριῷ μοιρῶν ϛʹ οἴκῳ Ἄρεως [ὁρίοις Διός· οὗ]τος σημαίνει τὸν περὶ ἐκχθρῶν καὶ παν̣τ̣ο̣δα̣π̣οῦ [δυστυχήμα]τος
quotations.translation: The lot of necessity was found in 6 degrees of Aries, the house of Mars, terms of Jupiter. This signifies the (character) concerning enemies and misfortune of all kinds

quotations.original: κλ(ῆρος) ἀνάγκης Τ̣[αύρῳ] μυρ(ῶν) ιʹ λε(πτῶν) θ̣ʹ
quotations.translation: The lot of necessity: in 10 degrees, 9 minutes of Taurus

quotations.original: GE₆ 20 AN DUL ina ZALAG₂ sin ina IGI KIR₄ šil-taḫ PA 1/2 KUŠ₃
quotations.translation: Night of (day) 20, rain DUL; last part of the night, Sin was 1/2 cubit in front of the tip of Pabilsag’s arrow.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.translation: Night of (day) 6, beginning of the night, Sin was 1 2/3 cubits behind the bright star of the tip of Pabilsag’s arrow.

quotations.original: 28 AN.MI šamaš₂ ki PAP NU IGI
quotations.translation: (Day) 28, eclipse of Šamaš, when I watched I did not see it.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: in 18 MUL₂.KAK.BAN IGI ⸢NU PAP⸣
quotations.translation: Around (day) 18 the bow star appeared; I did not watch.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: (30) GE₆ 2 ina ZALAG₂ dele-bat SIG GIR₃ ar₂ ša₂ A (31) ⸢2⸣ SI DIM₄
quotations.translation: (30) Night of (day) 2, last part of the night, Venus came near 2 fingers below the rear foot of the lion.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

(13') 29 24 ME NIM-a šamaš₂ AN.MI A₂ ⸢ULU₃⸣ [u] ⸢MAR⸣ ki-i TAB-[u₂ ...]
(14') [dil]-bat GU₄.UD u MUL₂ ŠID.MEŠ IGI.MEŠ MUL₂.BABBAR u AN ša₂ ina bi-ib-lu ina AN.MI-šu₂ IGI.MEŠ [...]
(15') TA MAR u ULU₃ ana SI u KUR iš-ta-ḫaṭ 35 GAR IR₂ u ZALAG₂-ru
quotations.translation: (13') (Day) 29, (at) 24 (UŠ) after sunrise, solar eclipse; when it began on the south and west side, [...] (14') [Ven]us, Mercury, and the counting stars were visible; Jupiter and Mars, which were in their period of invisibility, were visible in its eclipse [...] (15') it threw off (the shadow) from west and south to north and east; 35 (UŠ) onset, "weeping", and clearing.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: Ὅθεν ἐπὶ μὲν τῆς ὀρθῆς σφαίρας οἱ συμμεσουρανοῦντες ἀεὶ καὶ συνανατέλλουσιν καὶ συγκαταδύνουσιν, ἐφ᾽ ὅσον οὐ γίνεταί γε αὐτῶν ἡ περὶ τοὺς τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ πόλους μετάβασις αἰσθητή, ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς ἐγκεκλιμένης οἱ συμμεσουρανοῦντες οὔτε συνανατέλλουσιν οὔτε συγκαταδύνουσιν, ἀλλὰ οἱ νοτιώτεροι τῶν βορειοτέρων ἀεὶ ὕστεροι ἀνατέλλουσι καὶ πρότεροι καταδύνουσιν.
quotations.translation: Whence, for the 'sphaera recta', the culminating [heavenly bodies] always both rise and set simultaneously, inasmuch as their shifting around the poles of the zodiac does not become perceptible, and for the '[sphaera] obliqua' the culminating [heavenly bodies] neither rise simultaneously nor set simultaneously, but the more southern ones always rise later than the more northern ones and they set earlier.
quotations.publication: Ptolemy. 1903. Claudii Ptolemaei opera quae exstant omnia volumen I, Syntaxis Mathematica Pars II, Libros VII-XIII continens, ed. J.L. Heiberg. Leipzig: B.G. Teubner.

quotations.original:
Ἦμος δ’ ἠέλιος κατέδυ καὶ ἐπὶ κνέφας ἦλθε,
δὴ τότε κοιμήσαντο παρὰ πρυμνήσια νηός·
quotations.translation:
And when the sun had set and had gone to darkness, 
then they went to sleep near the stern-cables of the ship.
quotations.publication: Homer. 1920. Homeri Opera in five volumes, eds. D.B. Monro & T.W. Allen. Oxford: Oxford University Press.

quotations.original: Εὐκατανόητον δέ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν συγκαταδύσεων, ἐάν εἰς τὰ προηγούμενα τοῦ Θ ἴσην τῇ ΘΕ περιφέρειαν ἀπολάβωμεν, οἷον τὴν ΘΚ, τῷ Κ σημείῳ τοῦ ἰσημερινοῦ συγκαταδύσεται ὁ ἀστὴρ διὰ τὸ καὶ τότε τήν τε κατάδυσιν ἐπ᾽ ἴσης τῇ ΒΗ περιφερείας γίνεσθαι καὶ ἴσην γωνίαν εἰς τὰ προηγούμενα τοῦ μεσημβρινοῦ πάλιν ἀπολαμβάνεσθαι τῇ κατὰ τοῦτο τὸ σχῆμα εἰς τὰ ἑπόμενα ὑπὸ τῶν ΑΖ καὶ ΖΘ περιεχομένῃ.
quotations.translation: And it is easy to observe, that also for the simultaneous settings, if we would take from Θ to the forward points an arc equal to ΘΕ, namely ΘΚ, the star would set simultaneously with point K of the equator due both to the setting then taking place on an arc equal to ΒΗ and to it cutting off an equal angle, to the forward points from the meridian in turn, to what is being encompassed in this figure to the backward points by the [arcs] ΑΖ and ΖΘ.
quotations.publication: Ptolemy. 1903. Claudii Ptolemaei opera quae exstant omnia volumen I, Syntaxis Mathematica Pars II, Libros VII-XIII continens, ed. J.L. Heiberg. Leipzig: B.G. Teubner.

quotations.original: (...) καὶ ὅταν προδύνῃ τοῦ ἡλίου καὶ ὅταν ἐπικαταδύνῃ τῷ ἡλίῷ, ἐπέστραπται τὸ λαμπρὸν πρὸς τὸν ἥλιον.
quotations.translation: (...) and when [the Moon] sets before the sun and when it sets after the sun, the bright (side) is turned towards the sun.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ὅταν δὲ πλεῖον γένηται διάστημα τῶν υʹ σταδίων, προανατολαὶ καὶ προδύσεις γίνονται.
quotations.translation: But when (the) interval becomes more than these 400 stadia, risings before other risings and settings before other settings happen.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: aš2-ša2 UD-1-KAM ša2 iti.BAR d.SAG3.ME.GAR KI 30 ŠU2-u2 UD-12 AN.GE6 30 GAR-nu 3.20 ša2 ina EŠ2.GAR3 iq-bu-u2 ana UD-20-KAM 3.20 UG7

quotations.original: (10') NIM u SIG ša₂ ḪAB AN.MI (11') A.RA₂ 20 DU ina NIM (12') KI 17.24 TAB ina SIG (13') ZI
quotations.translation: (10') The height and depth of the disk of the eclipse (11') you multiply by (0);20. When it is high (12') you add it with 17;24; when it is low (13') you tear it out.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: (11') ana tar-ṣa 1 : ŠU.SI ḪAB-rat ḫe-pit₂-tu₂ 1.⸢38⸣.2⸢4⸣ (12') NIM u SIG GAR-an ša₂ al 1 ḪAB-rat ḫe-pit₂-tu₂ LA₂ TA 1 LA₂ ša₂ TA[G₄ A.RA₂ 6 DU] (13') KI 1.38.24 NIM u SIG TAB-ma ana SIG NIM GAR-an
quotations.translation: (11') Opposite 1 finger, the broken disk, you put 1,3[8];24 (12’) as the height and depth. That which is less than 1, the broken disk, you deduct from 1. What rem[ains you multiply by 6,] (13') add to 1,38;24, the ‘height and depth’, and you put it down as the depth, ascending.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: (6') ki-i NIM NIM u lu-⸢u₂ LA₂ BUR₃⸣ šu-u₂ (7') ⸢TA⸣ BE ša₂ A.RA₂ BAR.N[UN tal-lik] ⸢LA₂⸣ ki-i BUR₃ BUR₃ u lu-u₂ BUR₃ LA₂ šu-u₂ KI BE ša₂ A.RA₂ (8') BAR.NUN tal-lik TAB ana ⸢ŠU₂⸣ [xx] ⸢GAR⸣-an
quotations.translation: (6')  If (the Moon) is high, ascending, or high, descending, you subtract this (7') from the elongation which [you had multiplied] by the ṣiliptu-coefficient. If it is low, descending, or low, ascending, you add this with the elongation which you had multiplied by (8') the ṣiliptu-coefficient. You put it down as ŠU₂ [...].
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.translation: The ribbon of the swallow: .. 26?;[1]5 (zodiac sign corresponding to) month XII.
quotations.publication: Roughton, N. A.; Steele, J. M.; and Walker, C. B. F. 2004  A Late Babylonian Normal and Ziqpu-Star Text. Archive for History of Exact Science 58: 537–572.

quotations.original: Ἥλιος Καρκίνου μοίρᾳ κθʹ λʹ, Σελήνη Ἰχθύων μοίρᾳ ιβʹ, Κρόνος Τοξότου μοίρᾳ κζʹ ηʹ, Ζεὺς Αἰγοκέρωτος μοίρᾳ κβʹ ιγʹ, Ἄρης Σκορπίου μοίρᾳ ζʹ κγʹ, Ἀφροδίτη Καρκίνου μοίρᾳ κηʹ ιγʹ, Ἑρμῆς Λέοντος μοίρᾳ ιαʹ κεʹ, ὡροσκόπος Ἰχθύων μοίρᾳ ιζʹ, μεσουράνημα Τοξότου μοίρᾳ κεʹ (...) ἡ οὖν ἄφεσις ἀπὸ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου ἕως τῆς τετραγώνου πλευρᾶς καὶ τῆς πρὸς Κρόνον ἀπὸ διαμέτρου ἀκτινοβολίας εἰς κακοποιοῦ ὅριον· Ἄρης γὰρ τὴν διάμετρον ἀκτῖνα παρήλλαξε διὰ τὸ ἰσόμοιρον εὑρεθέντα Δία κεκωλυκέναι τὴν ἀναίρεσιν.
quotations.translation: The Sun in degree 29;30 of Cancer, the Moon in degree 12 of Pisces, Saturn in degree 27;08 of Sagittarius, Jupiter in degree 22;13 of Capricorn, Mars in degree 7;23 of Scorpio, Venus in degree 28;13 of Cancer, Mercury in degree 11;25 of Leo, the Ascendant in degree 17 of Pisces, Midheaven in degree 25 of Sagittarius (...) The start (of lifespan) was from the Ascendant up to the side of the quartile and the ray-shooting at Saturn from diametrical opposition into the term of a malefic: for Mars altered its diametrical ray because Jupiter, which was found in equal degree, hindered the effect of the destroyer.
quotations.publication: (GH L 75)

quotations.original: Ἥλιος Καρκίνῳ, Σελήνη Ἰχθύσιν, Κρόνος, Ἄρης, Ἑρμῆς Διδύμοις, Ζεὺς Αἰγοκέρωτι, Ἀφροδίτη Λέοντι, ὡροσκόπος Ζυγῷ. κλῆρος τύχης Διδύμοις· ἐν τούτοις Κρόνος, Ἑρμῆς, Ἄρης φρουρηθέντες, ἀλλήλων ὄντες ἀναιρέται, ὑπὸ Σελήνης ἐμαρτυρήθησαν, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ὁ κύριος τῆς πανσελήνου ἀπόστροφος. Ζεὺς δὲ τῷ θανατικῷ τόπῳ ἐπὼν καὶ ἀκρόνυχος γενόμενος οὐκ ἴσχυσε βοηθῆσαι. ὁ τοιοῦτος ἐτραχηλοκοπήθη.
quotations.translation: The Sun in Cancer, the Moon in Pisces, Saturn, Mars, Mercury in Gemini, Jupiter in Capricorn, Venus in Leo, the Ascendant in Libra. The Lot of Fortune was in Gemini: Saturn, Mercury, Mars, being kept under guard in this (sign), being destroyers of each other, were in aspect with the Moon, and likewise the lord of the (prenatal) full moon was turned away (not in aspect), and Jupiter, being present in the Place of Death and at its acronychal rising, was not able to help. The person with such a nativity was beheaded.
quotations.publication: (GH L 87,VII)

quotations.original: Ἥλιος Ζυγῷ εʹ ηʹ, Σελήνη Ταύρῳ ηʹ, δʹ, Κρόνος Ταύρῳ κεʹ, Ζεὺς Ζυγῷ κγʹ ηʹ, Ἄρης Αἰγοκέρῳ κϛʹ ηʹ, Ἀφροδίτη Σκορπίῳ κϛʹ, Ἑρμῆς Ζυγῷ κγʹ, ὡροσκόπος Ὑδροχόῳ κγʹ λʹ, μεσουράνημα Ταύρῳ εʹ γʹ, πανσέληνος Κριῷ βʹ μβʹ, Τύχη Παρθένῳ κϛʹ λδʹ, Δαίμων Καρκίνῳ κʹ λδʹ, ὕψωμα γενέσεως Παρθένῳ, κλῆρος ἀναιρέτου Ὑδροχόῳ.
quotations.translation: Sun in Libra 5;08, Moon in Taurus 8;04, Saturn in Taurus 25, Jupiter in Libra 23;08, Mars in Capricorn 26;08, Venus in Scorpio 26, Mercury in Libra 23, Ascendant in Aquarius 23;30, Midheaven in Taurus 5;03, (prenatal) full Moon in Aries 2;42, Fortune in Virgo 26;34, Daimōn in Cancer 20;34, exaltation of the nativity in Virgo, lot of the destroyer in Aquarius.
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original: ἡ Σελήνη ἄρα παραλαβοῦσα τοὺς χρόνους ἀπὸ ἐτῶν ξϛʹ <μηνῶν ζʹ> ἡμερῶν εʹ, διακρατήσει ἕως ἐτῶν ἄλλων κϛʹ μηνῶν γʹ ἡμερῶν ιβʹ, τουτέστιν ἕως ὅλων ἐτῶν ϟβʹ μηνῶν ιʹ ἡμερῶν ιζʹ· τὸ δὲ ἐντεῦθεν ἡ τοῦ Κρόνου διάμετρος ἀναιρετικὴ οὖσα ἀνεῖλεν.
quotations.translation: Then the Moon, having taken over the time starting with 66 years <7 months> 5 days, will control up to another 26 years 3 months 12 days, that is up to 92 years 10 months 17 days in all, and from then on the diameter (of the orbit) of Saturn, being destructive, has destroyed (ended the life).
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.1 (GH L 488)

quotations.original: ἡ Σελήνη ἄρα παραλαβοῦσα τοὺς χρόνους ἀπὸ ἐτῶν ξϛʹ <μηνῶν ζʹ> ἡμερῶν εʹ, διακρατήσει ἕως ἐτῶν ἄλλων κϛʹ μηνῶν γʹ ἡμερῶν ιβʹ, τουτέστιν ἕως ὅλων ἐτῶν ϟβʹ μηνῶν ιʹ ἡμερῶν ιζʹ· τὸ δὲ ἐντεῦθεν ἡ τοῦ Κρόνου διάμετρος ἀναιρετικὴ οὖσα ἀνεῖλεν.
quotations.translation: Then the Moon, having taken over the time starting with 66 years <7 months> 5 days, will control up to another 26 years 3 months 12 days, that is up to 92 years 10 months 17 days in all, and from then on the diameter (of the orbit) of Saturn, being destructive, has destroyed (ended the life).
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4  (GH L 488)

quotations.original: μετὰ ἔτος ξαʹ μῆνας ιʹ φθάνει ἡ μοῖρα τοῦ ὡροσκόπου καὶ ἡ Σελήνη εἰς τὸ τετράγωνον τοῦ Κρόνου, ὅπερ καὶ οὐκ ἀναιρεῖ διὰ τὸ μαρτυρεῖν αὐτῷ τὴν Ἀφροδίτην ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ
quotations.translation: After the 61st year, 10 months, the degree of the Ascendant and the Moon come into quartile with Saturn, which also does not destroy (end the life) because Venus is in aspect with it in the second (place).
quotations.publication: (GH L 76)

quotations.original: [Φαέ]θ̣ω̣ν ὁ τοῦ Διὸς ἐν Καρκίνωι [μοι]ρ̣ῶ̣ν ι̣θ̣ʹ ἐ̣ν̣ ἀναποδισμῶι ὁ̣ρ̣ί̣ο̣ι̣[ς] Κ̣ρ̣[όν]ο̣υ̣.
quotations.translation: The shining one, the (star) of Zeus (Jupiter) (was) in Cancer, 19 degrees, in retrograde, terms of Kronos (Saturn).

quotations.original: USAN AN ⸢e⸣ GIR₃ ar₂ ša₂ A 1 SI AN 2 SI ana NIM DIB

quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: προκρίνονται δὲ ἐν τούτοις εἰς δύναμιν ἐπικρατήσεως πρῶτον μὲν τὸ ὑπὲρ γῆν μεσουράνημα (...), εἶτα τὸ κατὰ τὴν ἀνατολὴν ἤγουν τὴν ὡροσκοποῦσαν μοῖραν.
quotations.translation: Among these (the aphetikoi topoi) (the following) are preferred, in terms of power to control, first the Midheaven above the Earth (...), then the (cardinal point) at the rising, that is, the degree in the Ascendant.

quotations.original: τὸ δὲ ἕκτον ἀπὸ ὡροσκόπου καλεῖται Κακὴ Τύχη καὶ ποινὴ καὶ πρόδυσις καὶ ἀπόκλιμα φαῦλον
quotations.translation: The sixth place from the Ascendant is called Bad Fortune and Punishment and Setting-in-advance and Ill Decline

quotations.original: Τούτου δὲ πάλιν τὸ μὲν τι καλεῖται ἑσπερία ἐπικατάδυσις φαινομένη, ὅταν ὁ ἀστὴρ ἀρχόμενος κρύψιν ποιεῖσθαι μετὰ τὸν ἥλιον εὐθὺς αὐτὸς καταδύνῃ, τὸ δέ τι καλεῖται ἑσπερία συγκατάδυσις ἀληθινή, ὅταν ὁ ἀστὴρ ἅμα καὶ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ τῷ ἡλίῳ καταδύνῃ, τὸ δέ τι καλεῖται ἑσπερία πρόδυσις μὴ φαινομένη, ὅταν ὁ ἀστὴρ ἀρχόμενος ἐπιτολὴν ποιεῖσθαι προκαταδύνῃ τοῦ ἡλίου.
quotations.translation: And from this again, one is called evening appearing following setting, when the star beginning to make its disappearance sets itself immediately after the sun, and another one is called evening apparent simultaneous setting, when the star sets together with and at the same time as the sun, and yet another one is called evening non-appearing leading setting, when the star beginning to make its heliacal rising sets earlier than the sun.
quotations.publication: Ptolemy. 1903. Claudii Ptolemaei opera quae exstant omnia volumen I, Syntaxis Mathematica Pars II, Libros VII-XIII continens, ed. J.L. Heiberg. Leipzig: B.G. Teubner.

quotations.original: 21 GENNA ana ME E-a DIR NU PAP AN.BAR₇ šamaš₂ TUR₃ NIGIN₂ ma-diš iq-tur₇
quotations.translation: (Day) 21, Saturn’s rising to daylight; clouds, I did not watch. Middle part of the day, the sun was surrounded by a cattle pen, it billowed very much.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: ὁ ὄγδοος τόπος καλεῖται ἀργὸς καὶ ἐπικαταφορὰ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου καὶ ἐπικατάδυσις καὶ ἀμαύρωσις
quotations.translation: The eighth place is called Idle and Following-descent of the Ascendant and Setting-after and Dimming
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.4

quotations.original:
“Ζεύ κύδιστε μέγιστε κελαινεφὲς αἰθέρι ναίων
μὴ πρὶν ἐπ’ ἠέλιον δῦναι καὶ ἐπὶ κνέφας ἐλθεῖν
πρίν με κατὰ πρηνὲς βαλέειν Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον
αἰθαλόεν, πρῆσαι δὲ πυρὸς δηΐοιο θύρετρα,
Ἑκτόρεον δὲ χιτῶνα περὶ στήθεσσι δαΐξαι
χαλκῷ ῥωγαλέον (...)”
quotations.translation:
“Zeus, noblest one, greatest one, black with clouds, dwelling in the sky,
grant that the sun does not set and darkness does not come, 
before I have overthrown headlong down the roof of Priam,
black of smoke, and burned with ravaging fire the door,
and torn around the breast the tunic of Hector, 
cleft with bronze (...)”
quotations.publication: Homer. 1920. Homeri Opera in five volumes, eds. D.B. Monro & T.W. Allen. Oxford: Oxford University Press.

quotations.original: DIŠ MUL.MEŠ um-mu-lu-tu4 ša2 ina GABA mul.lu-lim GUB.MEŠ-zu d.Ḫar-ri-ru d.TIR.AN.NA
quotations.translation: ¶ The scintillating stars which stand in the chest of the Stag: The Vole, the Rainbow god.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: αὕτη μὲν οὖν ἐν Αἰγοκέρωτι ἐγένετο κατὰ τὸ ἀνατολικὸν κέντρον.
quotations.translation: This (eclipse) happened in Capricorn at the rising center (Ascendant).

quotations.original: ἔθηκα τὰ ἐλάχιστα τῆς Σελήνης κεʹ ἔτη, καὶ τοῦ Καρκίνου τὴν ἀναφορὰν τοῦ δευτέρου κλίματος ἔτη λβʹ, καὶ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου τῆς Σελήνης, Διός, ἔτη ιβʹ· γίνονται ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἔτη ξθʹ. τοσούτων ἐτῶν ἐτελεύτα.
quotations.translation: I added the minimum years of the Moon, 25, and the rising time of Cancer for the second clime, 32 years, and of Jupiter, the housemaster of the Moon, 12 years: they total 69 years. That was at his death.
quotations.publication: (GH L 75)

quotations.original: καὶ αὕτη ἡ γένεσις κατ’ ἀρχὰς ἀνωμάλως καὶ μετρίως διῆξεν, ἐξ ὑστέρου δὲ ἀνεβιβάσθη καὶ στεμμάτων καὶ ἀρχιερωσύνης μετέσχεν· ἐπὶ τῆς ἐπαναφορᾶς γὰρ εὑρέθησαν οἱ κύριοι τοῦ τριγώνου, ὁ δὲ γʹ κύριος τοῦ τριγώνου καὶ ὁ κύριος τοῦ κλήρου μεσουρανῶν, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ὑψώματος κατὰ τὸν κλῆρον μεσουρανῶν καὶ ὁ κύριος τοῦ δαίμονος.
quotations.translation: This nativity proceeded irregularly and with middling (success) at the beginning, but later (the native) was elevated and partook of garlands and high-priesthood: for the lords of the triangle were found in a rising place (i.e., following a cardinal point), and the third lord of the triangle and the lord of the lot in Midheaven, and likewise the lord of the exaltation according to the lot in Midheaven, and the lord of the Daimōn.
quotations.publication: (GH L 72)

quotations.original: 33 MUL.MEŠ šu-ut d.En-lil2
quotations.translation: 33 stars of Enlil.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: τὸν δὲ ὡρονόμον ὡροσκόπον προσδεῖ δι’ ὅλην τὴν [ἀν]αλογίαν ἐκ τοῦ ἀναφορικοῦ πρὸς κλεψύδραν· ἐκπείπτει ἐν Καρκίνωι περὶ μοιρῶν κεʹ.
quotations.translation: It is also necessary (to calculate) the hour apportioning Ascendant from the (table) of rising times in complete proportion by water clock: the result is in Cancer, about 25 degrees.

quotations.original: ἀνοικοδεσπότητος ἡ γένεσις διὰ τὸ ὑπὸ δύσιν ἐμπεπτωκέναι Ἀφροδίτην τὴν κυρίαν τῶν ὁρίων τῆς Σελήνης.
quotations.translation: The nativity is without a housemaster because Venus, the lord of the terms of the Moon, has fallen below the Descendant.
quotations.publication: (GH L 75)

quotations.original: ŠU 1 27 na ina šamaš₂ GUB IGI AGA a-pir
quotations.translation: Month IV, (day) 1 (which followed day 30 of the preceding month), NA (= time from sunset to moonset) was 27 (UŠ), it (Sin) appeared while Šamaš was present, it was covered with a crown.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: Ἥλιος, Ἀφροδίτη Ὑδροχόῳ, Σελήνη, Ζεὺς Τοξότῃ, Κρόνος Λέοντι, Ἑρμῆς Αἰγοκέρωτι, Ἄρης, ὡροσκόπος Ζυγῷ. τῷ λεʹ ἔτει ἐκινδύνευσε συσχεθῆναι διὰ στάσιν καὶ βίαν· εἶχε γὰρ καὶ ἡ Σελήνη ἑξάγωνον σχῆμα πρὸς Ἄρεα, καὶ αὐτὸς Ἄρης παρειληφὼς παρ’ αὐτῆς τὸν ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ Κρόνῳ παραδεδωκώς· αὗται οὖν αἱ ἀντιπαραδόσεις χαλεπαὶ καὶ ἐπιτάραχοι.
quotations.translation: Sun, Venus in Aquarius; Moon, Jupiter in Sagittarius; Saturn in Leo; Mercury in Capricorn; Mars, the Ascendant in Libra. In his 35th year (the native) was at risk of being imprisoned on account of sedition and violence: for the Moon had a sextile configuration in relation to Mars, and Mars itself had taken over the year from it and handed (it) over to Saturn. These transfers (of chronokratoria) are difficult and disruptive.

quotations.original: Ἥλιος, Ἀφροδίτη, ὡροσκόπος Ταύρῳ, Σελήνη Ὑδροχόῳ, Κρόνος Καρκίνῳ, Ζεὺς Ζυγῷ, Ἄρης, Ἑρμῆς Διδύμοις. ἐν τοῖς πρώτοις χρόνοις φαντασίας μεγάλας καὶ πράξεις καὶ πίστεις πολιτικὰς ἔσχεν· ἔτυχον γὰρ οἱ κύριοι τοῦ τριγώνου ἐπίκεντροι. ἐξ ὑστέρου δὲ καθαιρεθεὶς τῷ βίῳ ἀλήτης γέγονεν· ἠναντιώθη γὰρ τῇ περιποιήσει Ἄρης καὶ Ἑρμῆς, καὶ οἱ κύριοι τοῦ κλήρου καὶ τοῦ περιποιητικοῦ ἀποκεκλίκασιν.
quotations.translation: Sun, Venus, Ascendant in Taurus, Moon in Aquarius, Saturn in Cancer, Jupiter in Libra, Mars, Mercury in Gemini. In his first years he had great prestige and deeds and positions of civic trust, for the lords of the triangle were at cardinal points. Later he was deposed and became a wanderer by way of life, for Mars and Mercury were opposed to security, and the lords of the lot and of the (place) of security were in falling places.
quotations.publication: (GH L 61,V)

quotations.translation: (15) (The month) is full and (the day) is transgressed: the day (corresponds) to the (same) day. quotations.original: Ὁ τῶν ζῳδίων κύκλος διαιρεῖται εἰς μέρη ιβʹ, καὶ καλεῖται κοινῶς μὲν ἕκαστον τῶν τμημάτων δωδεκατημόριον, ἰδίως δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐμπεριεχομένων ἀστέρων ὑφ’ ὧν καὶ διατυποῦται ἕκαστον αὐτῶν ζῴδιον.
quotations.translation: The zodiac is divided in 12 parts, and each of the sections is named a “twelfth part” generally, but after the encompassing stars through which each of them is also formed a “zodiac sign” specifically.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

Οἷος δ’ ἐκ νεφέων ἀναφαίνεται οὔλιος ἀστὴρ
παμφαίνων, τοτὲ δ’ αὖτις ἔδυ νέφεα σκιόεντα,
ὣς Ἕκτωρ ὁτὲ μέν τε μετὰ πρώτοισι φάνεσκεν,
ἄλλοτε δ’ ἐν πυμάτοισι κελεύων· (...)
quotations.translation:
And as a baneful star plainly appeared out of the clouds 
beaming, and then again sank into the shadowy clouds, 
so Hector would appear now with the foremost 
and then among the hindmost, giving orders; (...)

quotations.original: τὸ δὲ τὴν Σελήνην ἀπερρευκέναι τῆς Ἀφροδίτης καὶ τῷ Διὶ συνάπτειν τὰς τύχας συνῆπτε τοῦ τε ἀποστείλαντος καὶ τοῦ ὑποδεξαμένου

quotations.original: ἀλλ’ οὐ προσέσχον πρῶτον τὸν πολεύοντα καὶ διέποντα Ἑρμῆν εἰς πάθος ἐμπεπτωκότα· καὶ γὰρ μεγίστην ἀπόστασιν ἀπεῖχε τοῦ Ἡλίου καὶ ὑπὸ Κρόνου μόνου ἐθεωρεῖτο· ὃ καὶ βιαιοθάνατον ἀπετέλει.
quotations.translation: But (those who previously interpreted this horoscope) did not pay attention first of all to Mercury, the one inhabiting and managing (the day and hour), which had fallen into suffering, for it had its greatest elongation from the Sun and was in aspect with Saturn only, and that caused violent death.

quotations.original: ἀλλ’ οὐ προσέσχον πρῶτον τὸν πολεύοντα καὶ διέποντα Ἑρμῆν εἰς πάθος ἐμπεπτωκότα· καὶ γὰρ μεγίστην ἀπόστασιν ἀπεῖχε τοῦ Ἡλίου καὶ ὑπὸ Κρόνου μόνου ἐθεωρεῖτο· ὃ καὶ βιαιοθάνατον ἀπετέλει.
quotations.translation: But (those who previously interpreted this horoscope) did not pay attention first of all to Mercury, the one inhabiting and managing (the day and hour), which had fallen into suffering, for it had its greatest elongation from the Sun and was in aspect with Saturn only, and that caused violent death.

quotations.original: Κατὰ γὰρ τὸν αὐτὸν χρόνον οἷς μὲν ὁ ἥλιος ὅλος ἐκλείπει, οἷς δὲ τὸ ἥμισυ, οἷς δὲ τὸ ἔλαττον τοῦ ἡμίσεος, οἷς δὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐδὲν μέρος τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλελοιπὸς θεωρεῖται.
quotations.translation: For at the same time, for some the Sun is eclipsed whole, but for some half of it, and for some less than half, and for some no part of the Sun at all is observed to have been eclipsed.

quotations.original: Πάλιν δὲ ἕκαστον τῶν δωδεκατημορίων διαιρεῖται εἰς μέρη λʹ, καὶ καλεῖται τὸ ἓν τμῆμα μοῖρα, ὥστε τὸν ὅλον κύκλον τῶν ζῳδίων περιέχειν ζῴδια μὲν ιβʹ, μοίρας δὲ τξʹ.
quotations.translation: And each of these twelve zodiac signs is divided in 30 parts, and a single section is called a “degree”, so that the whole zodiac comprises 12 zodiac signs, and 360 degrees.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.translation: And each of these twelve zodiac signs is divided in 30 parts, and a single section is called a “degree”, so that the whole zodiac comprises 12 zodiac signs, and 360 degrees.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἄλλο μέντοι γέ ἐστι μοῖρα καὶ ἄλλο ἡμέρα. Μοῖρα μὲν γάρ ἐστι διάστημά τι λʹὸν μέρος ὑπάρχον τοῦ ζῳδίου, ἡμέρα δέ ἐστι χρόνος λʹὸν μέρος ὡς ἔγγιστα τοῦ μηνιαίου χρόνου. Καὶ ἡ μὲν μοῖρα τξʹον μέρος ἐστὶ τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ κύκλου, ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα τξεʹον καὶ δʹον μέρος ὡς ἔγγιστα τοῦ ἐνιαυσιαίου χρόνου. Καὶ πάντα μὲν τὰ ζῴδια τριακονταμόριά ἐστιν, οὐ πάντα δὲ τριακονθήμερα.
quotations.translation: A degree is one thing though and a day another. For a degree is a certain interval, being a 30th part of the zodiac sign, while a day is a time period, as close as possible to a 30th part of the time of a month. Also, the degree is a 360th part of the zodiac, and the day as close as possible to a 365th and a 4th part of the time of a year. Also, all zodiac signs consist of thirty degrees, but not all of thirty days.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: ἡ Σελήνη αὐξιφωτοῦσα ἐν τριγώνῳ σχήματι πρός τε Κρόνον καὶ Δία εὐδαίμονα καὶ πολυχρήματον ἀπειργάσατο καὶ τῇ πατρίδι πολλὰ ἀναθήματα καὶ δωρεὰς παρέχοντα

quotations.translation: Saturn in 11 (degrees) 32 minutes of Aries, acronychal, in retrograde

quotations.original: Ἥλιος Καρκίνου μοίρᾳ κθʹ λʹ, Σελήνη Ἰχθύων μοίρᾳ ιβʹ, Κρόνος Τοξότου μοίρᾳ κζʹ ηʹ, Ζεὺς Αἰγοκέρωτος μοίρᾳ κβʹ ιγʹ, Ἄρης Σκορπίου μοίρᾳ ζʹ κγʹ, Ἀφροδίτη Καρκίνου μοίρᾳ κηʹ ιγʹ, Ἑρμῆς Λέοντος μοίρᾳ ιαʹ κεʹ, ὡροσκόπος Ἰχθύων μοίρᾳ ιζʹ, μεσουράνημα Τοξότου μοίρᾳ κεʹ. ἀνοικοδεσπότητος ἡ γένεσις διὰ τὸ ὑπὸ δύσιν ἐμπεπτωκέναι Ἀφροδίτην τὴν κυρίαν τῶν ὁρίων τῆς Σελήνης. ἀφέτης ὡροσκόπος· τῶν ὁρίων κύριος Ἑρμῆς, καὶ αὐτὸς ὑπὸ δύσιν ἀποκεκλικὼς εὑρέθη. ἡ οὖν ἄφεσις ἀπὸ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου ἕως τῆς τετραγώνου πλευρᾶς καὶ τῆς πρὸς Κρόνον ἀπὸ διαμέτρου ἀκτινοβολίας εἰς κακοποιοῦ ὅριον
quotations.translation: The Sun in 29;30 degrees Cancer, the Moon in 12 degrees Pisces, Saturn in degree 27;8 Sagittarius, Jupiter in 22;13 degrees Capricorn, Mars in 7;23 degrees Scorpio, Venus in 28;13 degrees Cancer, Mercury in 11;25 degrees Leo, the Ascendant in 17 degrees Pisces, Midheaven in 25 degrees Sagittarius. The nativity is without a house-master on account of Venus, ruler of the terms of the Moon, falling below the horizon. The releaser is the Ascendant, the ruler of the terms is Mercury, and it too was found in a declining place below the horizon. The releasing (at start of lifetime calculation) is from the Ascendant up to the side of the square and the diametrical ray-casting towards Saturn into the term of a malefic.
quotations.publication: (GH L 75)

(1) ina 18 MU.MEŠ 2.⸢47⸣.23? UŠ sin LA₂
(2) mim-ma ša₂ al 1.57.47.57.46.40 DIRI A.RA₂
(3) 10.05.20 DU-ma KI 11.36 ZI TAB IGI.GUB-šu₂
(4) GIŠ-ma ⸢A⸣.RA₂ 2.47.22 DU A.RA₂ 6 DU-ma
(5) ⸢TA⸣ 3.⸢16⸣.21 E₁₁-ma si-man ša₂ GI₆-ka LA₂
(6)  1 U₄ 20? ZI ⸢ME NIM?⸣.A GI₆ DU TAB
quotations.translation: (1) In 18 years Sin lacks(?) 2.47.23? . (2) Whatever (the amount) by which it exceeds 1,57;47,57,46,40: (3) you multiply it by (0);10,5,20 and add it with 11;36, the displacement. (4) You compute its igigubbû-coefficient, and you multiply it by 2.47.22, you multiply it by 6, and (5) you deduct it from 3.16.21, and you subtract the duration of your night, (6) 1 day of the Sun? you subtract; the time since sunrise , (the time by which) the night has progressed, you add.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer
quotations.comment: The meaning of igigubbû in this example is unclear.

quotations.original: (6) KI sin NIM KI sin u KI šamaš₂ ša₂ al-la 10 lu-maš DIRI GAM0 16 DU KI BAR.NUN ša₂ l[u-maš] (7) ša₂-šu₂ ki TAB TAB ki LA₂ LA₂ ana muḫ-ḫi a-ḫa-miš₂ GAR.GAR-ma ½-šu₂-nu GIŠ-ma ana BAR.NUN ⸢GAR⸣-[an]
quotations.translation: (6) The position of the Moon and the position of the Sun: (the amount) by which they exceed 10 of the zodiacal sign you multiply by (0;0),16. You accumulate (them) together, compute half of it and put it down as the ṣiliptu-coefficient.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: τῷ ναʹ ἔτει ἐξενίτευσεν, καὶ ἐπὶ βασιλέως ἐλθὼν δίκην ὑπὲρ φίλου ἀρχιερωσύνης ἐνίκησεν· ἦν γὰρ ἡ παράδοσις ἀπὸ Σελήνης καὶ Ἀφροδίτης καὶ ὡροσκόπου <ἐπὶ> Ἑρμῆν ὄντα ἐν τῷ περὶ θεοῦ καὶ βασιλέως. ἐν δὲ τῷ αὐτῷ ἔτει καὶ τέκνου θάνατος ἐγένετο· Ἄρης γὰρ ἀπὸ θανατικοῦ τόπου Κρόνῳ παρέδωκεν ὄντι ἐν τῷ περὶ τέκνων τόπῳ.
quotations.translation: In the 51st year (of life) he went abroad, and coming before a king he won a court case on behalf of a friend’s chief-priesthood: for the transfer (of chronokratoria) was from Moon and Venus and Ascendant to Mercury, which was in the (place) concerning god and king. In the same year the death of a child also occurred: for Mars handed over (the chronokratoria) from the place of death to Saturn, which was in the place concerning children.

quotations.original: τῷ δὲ κγʹ ἔτει Ζεὺς ἀπὸ βασιλικοῦ τόπου (ὁ γὰρ γʹ καὶ ὁ θʹ ἀπὸ ὡροσκόπου τόπος θεὸν καὶ βασιλέα δηλοῖ) παραδιδοὺς τοῖς φωσὶ καὶ Ἀφροδίτῃ καὶ ὡροσκόπῳ καὶ Ἑρμῇ διὰ δωρεᾶς παρέσχεν ἐξουσιαστικὸν συνέδριον.
quotations.translation: In the 23rd year (of life), Jupiter, handing over (the chronokratorship) from the royal place (for the 3rd and the 9th places from the Ascendant indicate god and king) to the luminaries and Venus and the Ascendant and Mercury, provided a powerful counsellor through gift-giving.

(12) ki DIŠ.U₄ ša₂ NIM al-la BE u BAR.NUN DIRI-at₂ BE u BAR.NUN TA lib₃-bi [NI]M
(13) ana NA GAR-an
quotations.translation: (12) If the DIS̆.U₄ of height exceeds the elongation and the ṣiliptu-coefficient you subtract the elongation and the ṣiliptu-coefficient from it, (13) you put it down as NA.

quotations.original:
(9)  KI sin u KI šamaš₂ ša₂ al-la 10 lu-maš DIRI GAM₀ 8 DU KI ⸢BAR⸣.NUN ša₂ NIM u SIG ⸢ša₂⸣-[šu₂]
(10)  ki TAB TAB ki LA₂ LA₂ ana muḫ-ḫi a-ḫa-miš₂ GAR.GAR-ma ½-šu₂-nu GIŠ-ma GAM₀ DIŠ.U₄ ša₂ [NIM] u S[IG]
(11)  ša₂ taš-kun DU
quotations.translation: (9) (The amount) by which the position of Sin and the position of Šamaš exceed 10 (UŠ) of the zodiacal sign you multiply by (0;0),8. You add it with the corresponding ṣiliptu-coefficient for ‘height and depth’ if it is increasing, subtract if it is decreasing. You accumulate (them) together, you compute half of it, and you multiply it by the DIŠ.U₄ of height and depth which you had put down.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: εὗρον ἐγὼ τὸν μὲν Δία μοιρικῶς ὡρονομοῦντα καὶ τὴν Ἀφροδίτην κατὰ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου καὶ τῆς Σελήνης καὶ τοῦ Διὸς καὶ τοῦ κλήρου τῆς τύχης ἀγαθοδαιμονοῦσαν καὶ ἑῴαν ἀνατολικὴν, καὶ τοῖς ἀριθμοῖς προσθετικὴν, καὶ δεκατεύουσαν τὴν τριταίαν τῆς Σελήνης, καὶ τὸ δωδεκατημόριον αὐτῆς Σκορπίον τετυχηκότα καὶ τὸν διέποντα τοῦ ὡροσκόπου τὸν Δία κατὰ κάθετον ὡρονομοῦντα.
quotations.translation: I found Jupiter apportioning the hours (i.e, in the Ascendant) in terms of degree, and Venus—with respect to the Ascendant and the Moon and Jupiter and the lot of fortune—being in (the place of) Agathos Daimon, at its eastern rising, additive in its numbers, and in superior (quartile) aspect to the Moon on the third day, and Scorpio happened to be its dodecatemorion, and the hour-ruler of the Ascendant, Jupiter, was apportioning the hours along the perpendicular.

quotations.original: ἡ Σελήνη φερομένη ἐπὶ τὸν οἰκοδέκτορα αὐτῆς καὶ ἐπιβλέπουσα τὸν κύριον τοῦ κλήρου τῆς Τύχης Ἄρεα καὶ τὴν τούτου ὁμοίωσιν· καὶ ὁ Ἥλιος ἀπὸ τριγώνου βλέπων τὸν ὡροσκόπον καὶ κατὰ ἑξάγωνον τὴν Τύχην καὶ κατὰ συμπαρουσίαν τὴν κυρίαν τοῦ ὡροσκόπου

quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Hi namque nimis altis ac subtilibus disputationibus suis ex ipsis primo mathematicorum responsis quasi per cuniculum quemdam ad labefactandam hanc totam scientiam conantur irrepere;
quotations.translation: By using far-fetched and extremely theoretical arguments, drawn in the first place from the professional responses of astrologers, these men are trying to creep in, as it were, through an underground passage to undermine and topple the edifice of our science
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] quanto vehementius pugnant quantumque persuadendi vias quaerunt, tanto fidem astrologiae vehementius fortiusque confirmant
quotations.translation: But the more aggressively they attack, the more various the ways in which they seek to convince us, the more strongly they bolster our faith in astrology.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nec hoc est admiratione dignum, cum sciamus inter ipsos quanta sit ipsa deorum naturae dissensio quantisque disputationum argumentis uim totam divinitatis conantur evertere
quotations.translation: This is not surprising since we know how much difference of opinion there is among them about the nature of the gods, and with how many different theories they are trying to destroy the whole force of astrological divination.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: id est si Luna facit candidos, Mars rubeos, Saturnus nigros, cur omnes in Aethiopia nigri, in Germania candidi, in Thracia rubei procreantur
quotations.translation: that is, if the Moon makes people fair-skinned, Mars red, Saturn black, why is the whole population of Ethiopia black, of Germany blond, of Thrace red-haired?
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: id est si Luna facit candidos, Mars rubeos, Saturnus nigros, cur omnes in Aethiopia nigri, in Germania candidi, in Thracia rubei procreantur
quotations.translation: that is, if the Moon makes people fair-skinned, Mars red, Saturn black, why is the whole population of Ethiopia black, of Germany blond, of Thrace red-haired?
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: facit [...] Iuppiter maturos, bonos, benignos ac modestos
quotations.translation: Jupiter [makes men] mature, kindly, generous, temperate
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: facit [...] Venus luxuriosos, venustos et honesto gratiae splendore fulgentes
quotations.translation: Venus [makes men] pleasure-loving, charming, handsome
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: facit [...] Mercurius astutos, callidos et concitati animi mobilitatibus turbulentos
quotations.translation: Mercury [makes men] shrewd, clever, excitable, changeable
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: minuuntur autem etiam haec, si sic positum Solem malivolum sidus impediat.
quotations.translation: these things however are lessened if a malefic planet impedes the sun in that position
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sit iniquus, sit perfidus, sit malivolus, sit irreligiosus, quia haec vitia mala, Mercuri cum Marte perfecit constellatio!
quotations.translation: If he is unjust, treacherous, spiteful, impious, it is because these vices are brought about by the conjunction of Mercury with Mars!
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: cur [...] mortem doloresque contemnimus, si gloriae laudem et potentissimae dignitatis insignia nec appetentibus nobis Sol Iovis bona coniunctionis societate largitur?
quotations.translation: why [...] do we despise pain and death [...], if praise and rewards come from the Sun in favorable association with Jupiter?
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: frustra gravitatis instinctu aequitatis modestiam iuraque conquirimus, si Mercurius, Iovis ac Lunae bonis radiationibus temperatus, ad desideria nos et cupiditates istius virtutis inflammat.
quotations.translation: in vain we strive for law and moderation if Mercury, influenced by the favorable aspects of the Moon and Jupiter, excites us with desire for that kind of behavior.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: si non suo studio, sed stellarum vitiosa coactus est radiatione peccare, non habetis, magistratus, iustam animadvertendi substantiam
quotations.translation: If he were forced to sin by the baleful aspect of the planets, not by his own desire, you, magistrates, have no cause for punishment.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed ad liquidum propter partium minutorumque brevitatem ac velocissimum siderum cursum caelique pronum rotatae vertiginis lapsum neminem pervenire posse confirmant
quotations.translation: But they add that no one can get definite results because of the smallness of the degrees and minutes, the tremendous speed of the stars' orbits, and the inclination of the heavens.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed ad liquidum propter partium minutorumque brevitatem ac velocissimum siderum cursum caelique pronum rotatae vertiginis lapsum neminem pervenire posse confirmant
quotations.translation: But they add that no one can get definite results because of the smallness of the degrees and minutes, the tremendous speed of the stars' orbits, and the inclination of the heavens.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed ad liquidum propter partium minutorumque brevitatem ac velocissimum siderum cursum caelique pronum rotatae vertiginis lapsum neminem pervenire posse confirmant
quotations.translation: But they add that no one can get definite results because of the smallness of the degrees and minutes, the tremendous speed of the stars’ orbits, and the inclination of the heavens.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed ad liquidum propter partium minutorumque brevitatem ac velocissimum siderum cursum caelique pronum rotatae vertiginis lapsum neminem pervenire posse confirmant
quotations.translation: But they add that no one can get definite results because of the smallness of the degrees and minutes, the tremendous speed of the stars' orbits, and the inclination of the heavens.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: debemus [...] responsionum apotelesmatumque constantia divinae istius scientiae confirmare praecepta
quotations.translation: we must [...] uphold the unchanging nature of the astrological responses, and confirm the teachings of this god-given skill
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ipse et huius scientiae rationem, ipse computos tradidit
quotations.translation: It has shown us the theory of this science, the computations
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quinque etiam stellae errantes, quae planetae a Graecis vocantur,
quotations.translation: also five wandering stars which are called πλανῆται by the Greeks
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: a nobis errantes, a Graecis vero planetae dicuntur
quotations.translation: called wandering by us, and 'planets' by the Greeks
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ecce cognoscitur et invenitur quo in signo Saturni gaudeat stella
quotations.translation: This is how we can recognize in what sign the planet Saturn is exalted
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ecce cognoscitur [...] quando frigus eius fomento alieni ardoris incalescat
quotations.translation: This is how we can recognize [...] how his cold is warmed by another's heat
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ecce cognoscitur [...] quando frigus eius fomento alieni ardoris incalescat
quotations.translation: This is how we can recognize [...] how his cold is warmed by another's heat
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: praedicimus etiam quando retrogradus ad stationem pristinam revertatur
quotations.translation: We even predict when he will retrograde and when return to his former station
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: praedicimus etiam quando retrogradus ad stationem pristinam revertatur
quotations.translation: We even predict when he will retrograde and when return to his former position
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] post quantum tempus ad eandem signi partem, unde semel recesserat, pigra rursus molitione perveniat
quotations.translation: [...] how long it will be before he returns to the same degree from which he set out
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: licet enim breuiori temporis spatio, simili tamen etiam ipsa per XII signa agitatione percurrit.
quotations.translation: Although in a shorter space of time he passes through the twelve signs in a similar motion.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Haec omnia mathematicorum collegit ingenium et, computatione sollerti, divinae dispositionis secreta perdidicit.
quotations.translation: Astrologers have traced all these phenomena and with their mathematical skill have taught us their secrets.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: nunc directo cursu, nunc retrogrado, nunc stativa tarditate subsistunt et intentionem quaerentium ex ista cursus sui varietate confundunt
quotations.translation: sometimes in directmotion, sometimes retrograde, sometimes sluggish (they always confuse the researcher by the variety of their courses)
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: nunc directo cursu, nunc retrogrado, nunc stativa tarditate subsistunt et intentionem quaerentium ex ista cursus sui varietate confundunt
quotations.translation: sometimes in directmotion, sometimes retrograde, sometimes sluggish (they always confuse the researcher by the variety of their courses)
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ex hoc animo hi sempiterni stellarum ignes, qui globosae rotunditatis specie formati circulos suos orbesque celeri festinatione perficiunt
quotations.translation: Out of this Soul the everlasting fires of the stars accomplish the swift completion of their orbits
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: tu vero, Gradive Mars rutilo semper horrore metuende, qui in tertiis caeli regionibus contineris
quotations.translation: and you, Mars Gradivus, always with your fearful red color, whose home is the third region of the sky
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Conditiones etiam diurnarum ac nocturnarum stellarum diligenter inspicies, sed et qualia singulis locis benivolae stellae testimonia perhibeant, qua vero haec loca malivolae stellae radiatione percutiant.
quotations.translation: Look carefully to see which planets are nocturnal and which are diurnal, as well as the kind of influence the favorable and the unfavorable planets have on individual houses.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Zodiacus orbis, in quo duodecim signa infixa sunt
quotations.translation: The circle of the zodiac in which the twelve signs are fixed
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Signa autem ipsa duodecim his nominibus nominantur: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpius, Sagittarius, Capricornus, Aquarius et Pisces.
quotations.translation: The twelve signs themselves are called by these names: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Horum signorum diversa sunt genera, nam alia sunt ex his masculina, alia feminina
quotations.translation: These signs are of different gender, some masculine, some feminine
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Horum signorum diversa sunt genera, nam alia sunt ex his masculina, alia feminina
quotations.translation: These signs are of different gender, some masculine, some feminine
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Horum signorum diversa sunt genera, nam alia sunt ex his masculina, alia feminina
quotations.translation: These signs are of different gender, some masculine, some feminine
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Veneris domus sunt Taurus et Libra, ex quibus Libra masculinum signum est, femininum vero Taurus.
quotations.translation: The signs/houses of Venus are Taurus and Libra, of which Libra is masculine and Taurus is feminine.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in quibus singuli imperium habent ac domicilium constitutum.
quotations.translation: in these [signs] they have rulership and their house.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in quibus singuli imperium habent ac domicilium constitutum.
quotations.translation: in these [signs] they have rulership and their house.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: nam qui a nobis Saturnus dicitur, ab Aegyptiis Faenon vocatur
quotations.translation: for the one we call Saturn the Egyptians call Faeno;
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quae a nobis Venus, ab illis Fosforos vocatur
quotations.translation: the one called Venus by us is Fosforos to them
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Est itaque Solis Leo et in hoc signo habet domicilium et potestatem; Lunae Cancer.
quotations.translation: The house of the Sun is Leo, and in this sign he has his home and his power; and that of the Moon is Cancer.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Scire etiam altitudinem et humiliationem debemus
quotations.translation: We must also know about exaltation and fall
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quae sint earum deiectiones, in quibus constitutae oppressa auctoritatis suae potestate minuuntur
quotations.translation: and what are their falling places in which is suffers loss of its force
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In altitudinibus itaque suis gaudent[es] constitutae
quotations.translation: When planets are in their own exaltations we say that they rejoice
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: tunc maximae felicitatis decernuntur insignia, quotiens in genituris hominum maxima stellarum pars partiliter altitudinum suarum signa possederint
quotations.translation: Whenever in a nativity chart the majority of the planets is in the exact degree of their exaltation, then they indicate the greatest prosperity.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Altitudines autem dictae sunt ob hoc quod, cum in ipsa parte fuerint stellae in qua exaltantur
quotations.translation: They are called exaltations, because the planets are in the degrees in which they are exalted
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sol in Arietis parte XIX. exaltatur, in Libra vero parte XIX. deicitur
quotations.translation: The Sun is exalted at 19° Aries but is in its fall at 19° Libra
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Singula signa in tres partes dividuntur, singulae autem partes habent singulos decanos
quotations.translation: Each sign is divided into three parts, and each part has one decan
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quem nos Mercurium dicimus, illi Stilbontem vocant
quotations.translation: the one we call Mercury they call Stilbon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quem nos Iovem vocamus, Aegypti Faethontem vocant
quotations.translation: the one we call Jupiter the Egyptians call Faetho
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: qui a nobis Mars, ab illis Pyrois dicitur
quotations.translation: Mars to us is Pyrois to them
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quidam hunc locum volentes suptilius explicare terna numina decanis singulis applicarunt, quos munifices applicandos esse voluerunt ita ut per signa singula novem possint munifices inveniri, ut ternis munificibus decani singuli praeferantur.
quotations.translation: Some who wish to elaborate this in more detail add three divinities each to every decan, which they call munifices, so that for every sign nine munifices can be found and every decan is divided into three munifices.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: U₄.n(?) GU₄.UD ina NIM UD.DA ŠU₂-šu₂ DIB
quotations.translation: In day n(?), Mercury in the east - light - its setting will be omitted
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88, 1–164.
quotations.comment: Translation according to: Hunger, H., Sachs, A. J. (2014). Almanacs and Normal Star Almanacs (Vol. 7). Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften. pp. XIII-XIV.

quotations.original: Singula signa triginta habent partes; pars est autem in signo tantus locus quantum Solis aut Lunae orbis in circuitu complectitur; sed una pars in minuta dividitur sexaginta.
quotations.translation: Each sign has thirty degrees. A degree is as large a space in each sign as the Sun and Moon embrace in their circuit. One degree is divided into sixty minutes.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Singula signa triginta habent partes; pars est autem in signo tantus locus quantum Solis aut Lunae orbis in circuitu complectitur; sed una pars in minuta dividitur sexaginta.
quotations.translation: Each sign has thirty degrees. A degree is as large a space in each sign as the Sun and Moon embrace in their circuit. One degree is divided into sixty minutes.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: tamen partes eius quasi propriae stellis singulis dividuntur, quae partes fines stellarum nominantur
quotations.translation: yet the degrees of this sign are divided among all the planets, and these degrees are called the "terms" of the planets
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: hos fines Graeci oria vocant
quotations.translation: These terms the Greeks call oria (boundaries)
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: non ideo in diurnis genituris in oportunis locis positi [...]
quotations.translation: if placed in a diurnal nativity in no good places [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nam si deficientem Lunam deficiens Venus exceperit aut Mars in nocturna genitura, tunc prospera omnia deficiens Luna felicitatesque decernit
quotations.translation: If Venus and Mars aspect the waning moon in a nocturnal chart, the waning Moon indicates all kinds of prosperity and good fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nam si deficientem Lunam deficiens Venus exceperit aut Mars in nocturna genitura, tunc prospera omnia deficiens Luna felicitatesque decernit
quotations.translation: If Venus and Mars aspect the waning moon in a nocturnal chart, the waning Moon indicates all kinds of prosperity and good fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nam si deficientem Lunam deficiens Venus exceperit aut Mars in nocturna genitura, tunc prospera omnia deficiens Luna felicitatesque decernit
quotations.translation: If Venus and Mars aspect the waning moon in a nocturnal chart, the waning Moon indicates all kinds of prosperity and good fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: si vero plena lumine uel crescens Luna Veneri vel Marti se aliqua radiatione coniunxerit, maximas calamitates et maxima facit infortunia concitari.
quotations.translation: But if a full or waxing Moon comes into aspect with Venus or Mars, it brings about the greatest catastrophes and stirs up enormous ill fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: si vero plena lumine uel crescens Luna Veneri vel Marti se aliqua radiatione coniunxerit, maximas calamitates et maxima facit infortunia concitari.

quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.translation: But if a full or waxing Moon comes into aspect with Venus or Mars, it brings about the greatest catastrophes and stirs up enormous ill fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Stellae quinque, id est Saturnus, Iuppiter, Mars, Venus, Mercurius, matutinae sunt aut vespertinae aut occiduales aut absconsae, quae a Graecis afaneis et synodicae dicuntur, aut acronyctae.
quotations.translation: The five planets, that is, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury, are either matutine, vespertine, setting, or hidden (by the Sun's rays). These the Greeks call afaneis (hidden), synodicae (in conjunction with he sun), or acronyctae (at nightfall).
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Stellae quinque, id est Saturnus, Iuppiter, Mars, Venus, Mercurius, matutinae sunt aut vespertinae aut occiduales aut absconsae, quae a Graecis afaneis et synodicae dicuntur, aut acronyctae.

quotations.original: cum Solis radiis fuerit oppressus, naturalem enim malitiam Solem veneratus amittit
quotations.translation: for in being subservient to the Sun [Mars] loses his natural malefic qualities
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Cum Sole ceterae stellae in matutino ortu constitutae gaudent
quotations.translation: Some planets located with a morning rising rejoice in company with the Sun
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Pisces sunt signum femininum, duplex, humidum, aquosum, biforme, fecundum, squamosum, maculosum, incuruum, mutum, mobile
quotations.translation: Pisces are a feminine sign, dual, damp, watery, double-bodied, fertile, scaly, spotted, curved, silent, mutable
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Pisces sunt signum femininum, duplex, humidum, aquosum, biforme, fecundum, squamosum, maculosum, incuruum, mutum, mobile
quotations.translation: Pisces is a feminine, dual, humid, watery, double-bodied, fertile, scaly, speckled, bent, mute, mobile sign
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nunc de XII signorum natura, formis, qualitate, substantiis, anaforis explicare debemus
quotations.translation: We must now explain about the nature of the twelve signs, their appearance, essential qualities, their principles and risings
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: domus Martis, altitudo Solis circa partem XIX., deiectio Saturni circa partem XX., trigonum per diem Solis, per noctem Iovis.
quotations.translation: It is the sign of Mars, in which the Sun is exalted at about 19°, with Saturn in its fall at about 19°, aspected in trine to the Sun by day, by night to Jupiter
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Aequinoctiale vel solstitiale ideo dictum est quod, in hoc signo, horas noctis ac diei aequata moderatione componit, quod a Graecis tropicon isemerinon appellatum est.
quotations.translation: This sign is called equinoctial or solstitial because in it the hours of the day and night have equal measure, which the Greeks call tropicon isemerinon.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Aequinoctiale vel solstitiale ideo dictum est quod, in hoc signo, horas noctis ac diei aequata moderatione componit, quod a Graecis tropicon isemerinon appellatum est.
quotations.translation: This sign is called equinoctial or solstitial because in it the hours of the day and night have equal measure, which the Greeks call tropicon isemerinon.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Tropicum autem ideo dictum est quod in eo signo Sol constitutus vernum tempus faciat
quotations.translation: The sign is called tropical because when the Sun is located in that sign it makes the spring season
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: cum primam eius signi partem Sol fuerit ingressus
quotations.translation: when the Sun has entered the first degree of this sign
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Pisces sunt signum femininum, duplex, humidum, aquosum, biforme, fecundum, squamosum, maculosum, incuruum, mutum, mobile
quotations.translation: Pisces are a feminine sign, dual, damp, watery, double-bodied, fertile, scaly, spotted, curved, silent, mutable
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] quoto anno unumquodque signum in genituris oriatur
quotations.translation: [...] after how many years each particular sign rises in the charts
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Afelioti, quem nos Solanum dicimus, Gemini, Libra, Aquarius
quotations.translation: To the afeliotes, which we call the east wind, are subject the signs Gemini, Libra, Aquarius
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Afelioti, quem nos Solanum dicimus, Gemini, Libra, Aquarius
quotations.translation: To the afeliotes, which we call the east wind, are subject the signs Gemini, Libra, Aquarius
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Africo, qui a Graecis Libs dicitur, Cancer, Scorpius, Pisces.
quotations.translation: To the south-west wind, which the Greeks call libs, are subject the signs Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Africo, qui a Graecis Libs dicitur, Cancer, Scorpius, Pisces.
quotations.translation: To the south-west wind, which the Greeks call libs, are subject the signs Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Deficit Iovis benignitas, cum infirmitate signi vel partium vel decani vel conditionis immutatione benignitas eius fuerit impedita
quotations.translation: The favorable influence of Jupiter fails when, because of the weakness of the sign, or a shift of a degree or decan or condition, his favorable influence is hindered
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quicquid in decreto celatur, ex duodecatemoriis posse prodi significant.
quotations.translation: whatever is hidden in the chart can be revealed by the duodecatemoria
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: quicquid in decreto celatur, ex duodecatemoriis posse prodi significant.

quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nunc ad expositionem cardinum locorumque omnium transferatur intentio
quotations.translation: Now we must give our attention to the cardinal points and places
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: partiliter ostendemus rationem, qua possint loca singula secretis inquisitionibus colligi
quotations.translation: we shall show in detail the way in which the individual places may be exactly located
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Platice vitae locus est in eo signo in quo est horoscopus constitutus
quotations.translation: In general the House of Life is in the sign in which the ascendant is located
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Platice vitae locus est in eo signo in quo est horoscopus constitutus
quotations.translation: In general the Place of Life is in the sign in which the ascendant is located
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: spei vel pecuniae in secundo horoscopi signo
quotations.translation: of Expectation of Inheritace and Wealth in the second sign from the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: spei vel pecuniae in secundo horoscopi signo

quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: fratrum in tertio
quotations.translation: the [place] of the brothers [is] in the third [sign]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: ana ULU₃ MAR ŠUR UD.DA-su ina KI IGI
quotations.translation: [a shooting star] flashed to the south-west; its light was seen on the ground.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.original: parentum in quarto
quotations.translation: the [place] of the parents [is] in the fourth [sign]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: filiorum in quinto
quotations.translation: the [place] of the children [is] in the fifth [sign]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: valitudinis in sexto
quotations.translation: the [place] of health [is] in the sixth [sign]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: coniugis in septimo
quotations.translation: the [place] of the spouse [is] in the seventh [sign]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: mortis in octavo
quotations.translation: the [place] of death [is] in the eighth [sign]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Medium vero caelum est ab horoscopo X. signum
quotations.translation: The midheaven is the tenth sign from the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Ortus est pars horoscopi
quotations.translation: The rising is the degree of the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: et in quocumque signo CLXXXI pars fuerit inventa, in ipso signo vel parte geniturae constituitur occasus
quotations.translation: and in whatever sign the 181st degree is found, in that sign or section of the chart is located the descendant, or setting
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Imum vero caelum, quod a Graecis ypogeon dicitur, in quarto horoscopi constituitur loco
quotations.translation: The Imum caelum, which by the Greeks is called Ypogeon, is located in the fourth house from the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in genituris cardines sunt quattuor, ortus occasus medium caelum immum caelum, quae loca a Graecis solent appellari his nominibus: anatole, dysis, mesuranima, ypogeon

quotations.translation: which is called western opposite by the Greeks
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Dea est tertius ab horoscopo locus, id est tertium ab horoscopo signum;
quotations.translation: The Goddess is the third place from the ascendant, i. e. the third sign from the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Dea Deus Bona fortuna ac Bonus daemon, quae a Graecis hactenus nominantur: thea, theos, agathe tyche, agathos daemon
quotations.translation: Goddess, God, Good fortune, Bad fortune, which are called by the Greeks as follows: thea, theos, agathe tyche, agathos daemon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.
