quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: [iti.NE 14.KAM AN.GE6 30] | ina ZIB.ME al-la 2-ta [ŠU.2.MEŠ] | ḪAB-rat DIR GAR-an
quotations.translation: [Month V, on the 14th, a lunar eclipse] | in Pisces, beyond two-[thirds] | of the disk it (the moon) made.
quotations.date: 2nd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: S.E. 187 VI.22 = -124 Oct. 1)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: iti.ŠE GE6 1[4 AN.GE6 30] | ina RIN2 TIL-tim GAR-a[n] | U4.28 AN.[GE6 20] | ina ḪUN BAR DIB
quotations.translation: Month XII, night of the 1[4th a lunar eclipse,] | in Libra totality occurr[ed]. | On the 28th day an ecl[ipse of the sun] | in Aries, one-half (month) having passed (since the previous lunar eclipse).
quotations.date: 3rd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: 92 S.E. VII.12(?) = -219 Oct. 21)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: iti.APIN GE6 13 AN.GE6 30 | TIL-ti3 ina MUL2.MUL2 GAR-an
quotations.translation: Month VIII, night of the 13th, a lunar eclipse. | Totality occurred in Taurus
quotations.date: 3rd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: S.E. 24 V.19 = -287 Sept. 1)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: In hoc itaque libro id principe loco explicabitur, quod in posterioribus tertii libri partibus promisimus, idest Lunae omnes species ac formae, coniunctiones etiam, defluctiones et quicquid ad eius numinis pertinet potestatem;
quotations.translation: In this book, in the first place, will be explained, what we promised in the last parts of book 3: the shapes and appearances of the moon, also the conjunctions, defluxions and whatever pertains to her power
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Fortunae etiam locus et daemonis, geniturae dominus, quem Graeci oecodespoten vocant, diligenti ratione tractabitur, et eius etiam, qui actus decernit, efficacias explicabo;
quotations.translation: The lot of fortune and of the daemon, the chart ruler, whom the Greeks call οἰκοδεσπότης will be treated diligently, and the effects of that [planet] which decides the occupations
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Fortunae etiam locus et daemonis, geniturae dominus, quern Graeci oecodespoten vocant, diligenti ratione tractabitur, et eius etiam, qui actus decernit, efficacias explicabo
quotations.translation: The lot of fortune and of the daemon, the chart ruler, whom the Greeks call οἰκοδεσπότης will be treated diligently, and the effects of that [planet] which decides the occupations
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Plenae sunt itaque is partes, in quibus decani fuerint inventi, vacuae vero, ad quas partes numquam decanorum numen accedat.
quotations.translation: Therefore, full are the degrees in which the decans are found, empty however are those to which no decan belongs
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Plenae sunt itaque is partes, in quibus decani fuerint inventi, vacuae vero, ad quas partes numquam decanorum numen accedat.
quotations.translation: Therefore, full are the degrees in which the decans are found, empty however are those to which no decan belongs
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Scire debemus quod in omnibus signis et masculini generis et feminini <et masculinae> et [quae] femininae sint partes. Ex his enim partibus invenitur, cuius genitura sit, masculina an feminina.
quotations.translation: We need to know what parts of both the masculine and feminine signs are the masculine and feminine degrees, for from these degrees it is found out whether the nativity is male or female
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed et plenas partes ac vacuas earumque decreta monstrabo
quotations.translation: but I will also show the full and empty degrees and their indications
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Lunae nos omnes cursus in principiis huius libri explicaturos esse promisimus et quid qua ratione decernat;
quotations.translation: We have promised to explain all courses of the moon in the preface of this book and why it indicates what things
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In posterioribus enim caeli regionibus collocata et terrae imperium ex vicinitate sortita omnia corpora, quae inspiratione divinae mentis anirnantur, cursus sui multiplici varietate sustentans et per signa omnia festina celeritate discurrens et omnibus stellis adsiduis se coniunctionibus socians ex contrariis mixturis et ex disparibus elementis Integra compositi operis substantia mutuata omnia animantium corpora et concepta procreat et generata dissolvit.
quotations.translation: Since she is located in the lower regions of the heavens, because of her nearness she has been allotted power over the Earth and all the bodies animated by the breath of the Divine Mind. She maintains her course with infinite variety and runs with speed through all the signs, joining herself to all the planets. From different elements she builds up the human body, once conceived, and dissolves it again into its elements.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Laborandum itaque et in omni geniturae substantia ista <pars> magno opere requirenda, in qua est Luna constituta;
quotations.translation: Therefore one has to work out in every substance of a nativity that degree with great effort, in which the moon is located
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: nam in nocturnis genituris initium ac dominium ipsa suscipit temporum, in diurnis vero genituris Sol;
quotations.translation: for in night charts the beginning and rulership of time she [the Moon] possesses herself, in day charts, however, the Sun  does
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: posteaquam enim de diametro Solis recedens luminis sui coeperit damna sentire ad synodum festinans, qualibet luminis sui figuratione pro mensura uniuscuiusque deis cernit exitium.
quotations.translation: For, after receding from opposition to the Sun, she feels her light waning as she hastens to the synodic position; in whatever shape she is she indicates destruction for everyone, according to her form.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Est itaque Luna aut synodica aut plena aut dichotomos aut menoides aut amficyrtos et per has mutata formas cursum menstrui luminis complet.
quotations.translation: Therefore the moon is either new or full or half or crescent or gibbous and changed through these shapes she completes the course of monthly light.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Est itaque Luna aut synodica aut plena aut dichotomos aut menoides aut amficyrtos et per has mutata formas cursum menstrui luminis complet.
quotations.translation: Therefore the moon is either new or full or half or crescent or gibbous and changed through these shapes she completes the course of monthly light.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Est itaque Luna aut synodica aut plena aut dichotomos aut menoides aut amficyrtos et per has mutata formas cursum menstrui luminis complet.
quotations.translation: Therefore the moon is either new or full or half or crescent or gibbous and changed through these shapes she completes the course of monthly light.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Est itaque Luna aut synodica aut plena aut dichotomos aut menoides aut amficyrtos et per has mutata formas cursum menstrui luminis complet.
quotations.translation: Therefore the moon is either new or full or half or crescent or gibbous and changed through these shapes she completes the course of monthly light.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: tertio rursus die diligenter debemus inspicere, et quibus se coniungat et <a> quibus defluat et recedat et quatenus se post primam coniunctionem secundis coniunctionibus societ
quotations.translation: again on the third day we must observe diligently also to which [planets] [the Moon] forms aspect and from which it separates and recedes and how it forms second aspects after the first aspect
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: tertio rursus die diligenter debemus inspicere, et quibus se coniungat et <a> quibus defluat et recedat et quatenus se post primam coniunctionem secundis coniunctionibus societ
quotations.translation: again on the third day we must observe diligently also to which [planets] [the Moon] forms aspect and from which it separates and recedes and how it forms second aspects after the first aspect
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] quando et ad quas stellas plena feratur <vel> minuta luminibus, qualiter conditionis suae stellis iungatur, quando in eadem parte posita synodica se copulatione coniungat [...]
quotations.translation: when and towards which planets it moves when waning, under which conditions it aspects the planets, when it comes into synodic aspect [= conjunction] in the same degree [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si se Luna Saturni adplicaverit stellae et crescens lumine ista se Saturno societate coniungat vel sic ad Saturnum feratur, matri viduitatem et muliebrium locorum adsiduos dolores decernit
quotations.translation: When the Moon applies itself to Saturn and while waxing aspects it in that way or moves toward Satur, this indicates widowhood for the mother and constant grief for the places of women
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed et ipsos facit aut vitiosos debiles aut oligochronios aut malo quodam exitu intereuntes, praesertim si in ista coniunctione in necessariis geniturae locis fuerit inventa, idest si [in] horoscopo partili radiatione iungatur.
quotations.translation: but it makes them also weak and sickly or short-lived or die some kind of evil death, especially if [the Moon] is found in this aspect in important places [of the chart], i.e. if she aspects the degree of the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: IV. LUNA AD MARTEM.
quotations.translation: 4. Moon [in respect] to Mars
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: facit [...] efficaces tamen et omnia complentes [...] praesertim si in primis geniturae locis fuerint constituti
quotations.translation: it makes them [...] successful and efficient, especially when they are in important places in the chart
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: et secundum cardinum diversos situs et secundum anaforas cardinum et secundum ea signa, quae aliena esse ab horoscopi societatibus diximus, decretorum diversa varietas invenitur.
quotations.translation: and according to the different situations of the angles, and the anaforas of the angles, and according to those signs which we have said are not in aspect to the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero per diem <in> principalibus geniturae locis sic fuerit inventa, is paternam substantiam dissipat,
quotations.translation: But if it is found in important places of the chart in that way, it squanders the inheritance
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed semper Luna in omni orbis sui figuratione si feratur ad Venerem, faciet praeposteris amorum vitiis implicates
quotations.translation: But always if the Moon—in any phase—moves towards Venus it will make extraordinary sexual vices and constant scandal
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed illis intra cutem malignus humor semper inlapidatos articulos obligat, praesertim si per vacuum currens, quam Graeci cenodromon dicunt
quotations.translation: they will suffer from malignant humors under the skin which will attack their joints, especially if the moon is running empty (void of course), which the Greeks call κενοδρόμος
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed illis intra cutem malignus humor semper inlapidatos articulos obligat, praesertim si per vacuum currens, quam Graeci cenodromon dicunt
quotations.translation: they will suffer from malignant humors under the skin which will attack their joints, especially if the moon is running empty (void of course), which the Greeks call κενοδρόμος
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Per vacua enim signa cursus suos dirigens primam aetatem facit miseris ac variis infortuniorum casibus implicari.
quotations.translation: A moon running empty involves the early years in wretched misfortunes
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed haec pro locorum vel signorum varietate decernit, de qua varietate etiam in aliis apotelesmatibus plenissime diximus.
quotations.translation: All these are indicated according to the variety of the signs and houses. We have written fully about this variety in other works on astrology.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: <facit> divites potentes imperiosos magnos  [...], praesertim si liberata a Solis radiis Luna in horoscopi signo fuerit inventa
quotations.translation: it makes [the native] rich and powerful, mighty, and great, especially when the Moon is found in the sign of the ascendant, not aspected by the Sun
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero in ceteris geniturae locis fuerit ista coniunctio, mediocres in facultatibus facit et qui artes metallicas exercere consueverint.
quotations.translation: This combination in other places of the chart makes natives of mediocre talents working in metal.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero a Saturno ad Martem feratur, mediocriter haec eadem facit; mulieribus vero tunc decernit vitia, cum eandem radiis suis inpugnaverit Saturnus.
quotations.translation: When it moves from Saturn to Mars, it does the same in a moderate manner; then it indicates vice for women when Saturn aspects [the Moon] badly
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: <si> enim Iuppiter et Venus istas omnes coniunctiones vel defluctiones, per quas misera hominibus decernuntur exitia, bona radiatione respexerint, decretorum malorum <et> miserae calamitatis exitia mitigantur.
quotations.translation: for if Jupiter and Venus aspect all those configurations and separations well which indicate miserable outcomes for natives, the outcome of miserable catastrophe is lessened
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: diligenter inspice cursum coniunctiones defluctionesque Lunae, longitudines altitudines et qui coniunctiones eius excipiant.
quotations.translation: diligently look at the course, the aspects and separations of the Moon, the elongations, exaltations and which planets aspect its configurations
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero deficiens ad ipsos radios Solis accesserit et ipsi orbi eius quodammodo glutinata fuerit [...]
quotations.translation: if it goes towards the very rays of the Sun and becomes, as it were, glued to his orb
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero per noctem minuta luminibus Saturno retrograde vel stationem facienti se Luna coniunxerit, magnarum infelicitatum decernit <incommoda>;
quotations.translation: If however in a night chart the waning Moon aspects Saturn while in retrograde or stationary, it indicates major misfortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed haec maiora efficiuntur, si Mars addat ad numerum.
quotations.translation: but these larger effects are indicated if Mars is direct
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: partiliter vero locus Fortunae ista ratione colligitur, quam tu sequi in omni disputatione debebis.
quotations.translation: the exact location of the Lot of Fortune is found in this manner which you must follow in every computation [of a nativity]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quae omnia tunc explicabimus, cum ad interpretationem venerimus sfaerae barbaricae;
quotations.translation: All this we will explain when we come to the interpretation of the sfaera barbarica;
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Appellatur autem, sicut Abraham designat, Lunae locus.
quotations.translation: [The lot of Fortune] is also called—as Abraham points out—Place of the Moon.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si enim generaliter fuerit inventus in his, in quibus diximus, locis, mediam genituram decernit
quotations.translation: If it is roughly found in the place we said, it indicates a mediocre nativity
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sin vero in signis cardinum non partiliter, sed platice fuerint inventi, mediae felicitatis incrementa decernunt.
quotations.translation: If they are found not exactly but approximately in the angular places, they indicate a moderate increment in fortune.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Hie locus vocatur et animae substantia; ex hoc loco actus omnisque augmenta substantiae quaerimus [invenimus],
quotations.translation: This lot is also called 'substance of the soul'; from this lot we ask/find the occupation and all increments in wealth
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: MU.48 ŠE GE6 [23(?)] | lu2.TUR a-lid | U4.BI 20 ina 13.30 LU | 30 ina 10 GU | BABBAR ina SAG A | dil-bat KI 20 | GU4 KI 20 | GENNA ina ALLA | AN ina TIL ALLA
quotations.translation: Year 48, month XII, night of the [23th(?)], | the child was born. | That day the sun was in 13;30 Aries, | the moon in 10° Aquarius, | Jupiter at the beginning of Leo, | Venus with the sun, | Mercury with the sun, | Saturn in Cancer, | Mars at the end of Cancer.
quotations.date: 3rd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: S.E. 48 XII.[23] =-262 April 4)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: MU.48 ŠE GE6 [23(?)] | lu2.TUR a-lid | U4.BI 20 ina 13.30 LU | 30 ina 10 GU | BABBAR ina SAG A | dil-bat KI 20 | GU4 KI 20 | GENNA ina ALLA | AN ina TIL ALLA
quotations.translation: Year 48, month XII, night of the [23th(?)], | the child was born. | That day the sun was in 13;30 Aries, | the moon in 10° Aquarius, | Jupiter at the beginning of Leo, | Venus with the sun, | Mercury with the sun, | Saturn in Cancer, | Mars at the end of Cancer.
quotations.date: 3rd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: S.E. 48 XII.[23] =-262 April 4)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: DU6 22 mul2.BABBAR ina GU UŠ | ina ŠE 2 ina KUN ŠU2
quotations.translation: Month VII the 22nd, Jupiter's (2nd) stationary point in Aquarius. | Around the 2nd of month XII, (Jupiter's) last visibility in Pisces.
quotations.date: 5th-4th century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: Darius II., Year 13, X.24 = -409 Jan. 12/13)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: ZIZ2 14 dil-bat ina NIM ina IGI GU ŠU2 ŠE DIRI
quotations.translation:
The 14th of month XI, Venus's last visibility in the east in front (west) of
Aquarius. (The year had) an intercalary month XII.
quotations.date: 5th-4th century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: Darius II., Year 13, X.24 = -409 Jan. 12/13)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: quia post Arietem ad Taurum secundo loco Luna transitum facit, Venus geniturae dominium possidebit
quotations.translation: because after Aries the Moon moves into Taurus in the second place, Venus [i. e. the ruler of Taurus] will possess rulership of the chart
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero Saturnus istam commixtionem in oportunis geniturae locis positus in nocturna genitura respexerit, faciet insidias pericula accusationes discrimina ei popularis invidiae crimen adnectit.
quotations.translation: If Saturn aspects this conjunction while located in important places of a night chart, he will indicate plots, dangers, accusations, crises, and scandal.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero vitiorum ac valitudinis possederit locum et malivolarum stellarum fuerit minaci radiatione constrictus, <ab> humoribus vitia decernit;
quotations.translation: If [Mercury] is in the house of health and illness and in aspect to malefic planets, he indicates affliction by bodily humors;
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in geniturae domini finibus constituti vel in domibus eorum collocati et locum ipsius prosperis radiationibus intuentes, plurimum ex natura sua communicatum decernunt
quotations.translation: located in the terms of the chart ruler or in their houses and aspecting their house well, they indicate much from their own nature
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si enim septeni et noveni anni, qui ebdomadici a Graecis et enneadici appellantur, gravia pericula hominibus semper indicunt, quid faciet LXIII. annus, qui utriusque numeri multiplicatam [...] perficit [...]?
quotations.translation: For if every seventh and ninth year, which are called ἐβδομαδικός by the Greeks and ἐννεαδικός, always indicate grave danger for humans, what will the 63rd year do, which is both numbers multiplied?
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si enim septeni et noveni anni, qui ebdomadici a Graecis et enneadici appellantur, gravia pericula hominibus semper indicunt, quid faciet LXIII. annus, qui utriusque numeri multiplicatam [...] perficit [...]?
quotations.translation: For if every seventh and ninth year, which are called ἐβδομαδικός by the Greeks and ἐννεαδικός, always indicate grave danger for humans, what will the 63rd year do, which is both numbers multiplied?
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Hac ex causa ab Aegyptiis androclas dictus est, quod omnem viri substantiam frangat ac debilitet.
quotations.translation: Therefore this year is called ἀνδροκλάς by the Egyptians, because it breaks and debilitates all substance of life.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero desertus Mars a benivolis fuerit habens ipse decernendi actus potestatem et eum malivolae stellae respexerint, faciet subiectos laboriosos et qui plus is inpendant quam illis ex suis artibus conferatur.
quotations.translation: But if Mars is not in aspect with the benefics while it itself has the power to decide the occupation [of the native] and he is aspected by malefics, he indicates subordinate, laborious jobs and spending more than one earns.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: ex ipso actu magnae gloriae nomen accipit, praesertim si recto cursu pergentes benivolae stellae, quae testimonium perhibent, in matutino ortu fuerint inventae.
quotations.translation: from this very act he earns the name of great glory, especially if the benefics are found in direct motion aspecting him and rising in the morning
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nechepso, iustissimus Aegypti imperator et astrologus valde bonus
quotations.translation: Nechepso, the most just emperor of Egypt and a very good astronomer/astrologer
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Illud etiam sciendum est, quod in omnibus signis, quotiens Luna novissimas possederit partes, ad nullum feratur;
quotations.translation: It is necessary to know that in all signs in which he possesses the last degrees, he moves towards nothing [i. e. has no effect]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero Mars sic Lunam positam minaci radiatione respexerit et utrique, idest Soli et Lunae, partili radiatione fuerit contrarius, corpus gravi vitio debilitat et indicit frequenter oculis caecitates.
quotations.translation: If however Mars is aspected to the Moon in such a bad way and one of the two, i. e. Sun and Moon, are exactly opposite, he debilitates the body with a defect and often indicates blindness for the eyes
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nunc illud tibi intimare debemus, qua ratione partiliter defluat Luna, qua etiam ratione iungatur, quas Graeci synafas aporroicas vocant.
quotations.translation: Now we need to show you why exactly the Moon separates and for which reason it is joined [to other planets]—which the Greeks call συναφή and ἀπορροική.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nunc illud tibi intimare debemus, qua ratione partiliter defluat Luna, qua etiam ratione iungatur, quas Graeci synafas aporroicas vocant.
quotations.translation: Now we need to show you why exactly the Moon separates and for which reason it is joined [to other planets]—which the Greeks call συναφή and ἀπορροική.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] et si sint ambo invicem sibi cardinaliter iuncti.
quotations.translation: [...] also if they are in aspect to each other while located on cardinal points
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original:
Aries. In hoc signo, idest in Ariete, quae sint partes plenae, quae vacuae, speciali significatione monstrabimus. Itaque in Ariete plenae partes XII, vacuae partes XVIII.

I locus partes III vacuus
II locus partes V Senator [idest asiccan]
III locus partes IX vacuus
IV locus partes IV Senacher [idest sentafora]
V locus partes V vacuus
VI locus partes IV Sentacher [uaucate idest asentacer]
quotations.translation:
Aries: In that sign, i. e. Aries, some degrees are full and some are empty. We will show this using a special figure. Therefore there are 12° full and 18° empty in Aries.
1. 3° empty
2. 5° Senator [i.e. Asiccan]
3. 9° empty
4. 4° Senacher [i.e. Sentafora]
5. 5° empty
6. 4° Sentacher [Uaucate i.e. Asentacer]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original:
In Tauri signo quae sint partes plenae, quae vacuae, hoc demonstratur exemplo. Sunt autem in Tauro plenae partes XX, vacuae partes X.

I locus partes III vacuus
II locus partes VII Suo [idest asicat]
III locus partes II vacuus 
IV locus partes VIII Aryo [idest ason/asou]
V locus partes V vacuus 
VI locus partes V Romanae [idest aarfi/arfa]
quotations.translation:
In the sign of Taurus, some degrees are full, some are empty. This will be shown by example. But in Taurus there are 20° full and 10° empty.
1. 3° empty
2. 7° Suo [i.e. Asicat]
3. 2° empty
4. 8° Aryo [i.e. Ason/Asou]
5. 5° empty
6. 5° Romanae [i.e. Aarfi/Arfa]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: cum primum circulum cursus sui Saturnus inpleverit, id est primos XXX annos, paternam et maternam substantiam minuit
quotations.translation: When Saturn fulfills its first orbit, i. e. in the first 30 years, he decreases the wealth of father and mother
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed tunc decernit uxorem, cum parodicus Saturnus (id est temporalis) aut Lunam de quadrato viderit, aut Sol ipsum de Leone vel Sagittario trigonica radiatione respexerit.
quotations.translation: But then he indicates the wife when Saturn having completed a full return (i. e. temporal) aspects either the Moon in a square or the Sun in a trine from Leo or Sagittarius.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed tunc decernit uxorem, cum parodicus Saturnus (id est temporalis) aut Lunam de quadrato viderit, aut Sol ipsum de Leone vel Sagittario trigonica radiatione respexerit.
quotations.translation: But then he indicates the wife when Saturn having completed a full return (i. e. temporal) aspects either the Moon in a square or the Sun in a trine from Leo or Sagittarius.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed tunc uxores dabuntur, cum post XXX annos Saturnus intrat in Cancrum
quotations.translation: Wives will be given when Saturn enters Cancer after 30 years
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed tamdiu laboris et infelicitatis oneribus deprimetur, quamdiu Saturnus Cancrum Libram Arietem et eorum quadrata transiverit.
quotations.translation: But he will be depressed by the burdens of work and ill fortune as long as Saturn transits Cancer, Libra, and Aries and their squares.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Turn yero in omnibus proficiet, cum Saturnus primam stationem in Leone vel in Capricorno solverit.
quotations.translation: Everything will go forward when Saturn moves from his first station in Leo or in Capricorn.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Cum enim in tropicas Cancri venerit partes Saturnus, tunc iacturam patrimonii faciet
quotations.translation: For when Saturn comes to the tropic degrees of Cancer, he will indicate loss of marriage
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed et in Pisces et in Geminos cum circumiens venerit, haec eadem decernit quae in tropicis.
quotations.translation: But when he—going around—enters Pisces and Gemini, he indicates the same things as he did in the tropical signs.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed et in Pisces et in Geminos cum circumiens venerit, haec eadem decernit quae in tropicis.
quotations.translation: But when he—going around—enters Pisces and Gemini, he indicates the same things as he did in the tropical signs.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: sed tunc malis fortioribus inplicantur, cum ad Capricornum vel ad Taurum Saturnus transitum fecerit
quotations.translation: but they will be involved in more serious evils when Saturn moves across to Capricorn or Taurus
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Per cetera vero signa pergens bonos actus bonas occupationes et bonae felicitatis decernit ornatum
quotations.translation: Going through the other signs he indicates good deeds and occupations, fame and increase in income
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed cum Saturnus ad hoc idem signum id est ad Scorpionem reversus fuerit, erunt fortiores
quotations.translation: But when Saturn returns to that same sign—i. e. to Scorpio—they will be stronger
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: et cum in quadratis lateribus fuerit, haec eadem simili ratione decernit
quotations.translation: but when he is in the squares (i. e. the signs sharing the quadruplicity/quality) he indicates the same for a similar reason
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: ἀστέρα τὸν ἐν τ̣ῆι Χ̣λαμύδι καλο̣ύ̣μ̣ενο̣ν Γανυμήδην ὁ̣μ̣ωνύμως τῶι ὅλωι εἰδώλωι
quotations.translation: The star in the Cloak, called Ganymede, homonymous with the entire constellation

quotations.original: ἡ δὲ Ἀφροδίτη ὡρονομοῦσα καὶ Ζεὺς ἀγαθοδαιμονῶν καὶ τὴν συναφὴν τῆς Σελήνης ἐκδεχόμενος ἐδήλουν τὴν ἡμερότητα
quotations.translation: Venus apportioning the hour (being in the Ascendant) and Jupiter being in the (lot of) the Good Divinity and receiving contact with the Moon indicated the tameness (of the animal concerned in the horoscope)

quotations.original: ἡ δὲ Ἀφροδίτη ὡρονομοῦσα καὶ Ζεὺς ἀγαθοδαιμονῶν καὶ τὴν συναφὴν τῆς Σελήνης ἐκδεχόμενος ἐδήλουν τὴν ἡμερότητα
quotations.translation: Venus apportioning the hour (being in the Ascendant) and Jupiter being in the (lot of) the Good Divinity and receiving contact with the Moon indicated the tameness (of the animal concerned in the horoscope)

quotations.original: ἧς τὸ δωδεκατημόριον Σκορπίου πάλιν περὶ τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον ἐξέλαμπεν̣
quotations.translation: Its dodekatemorion shone forth (i.e., resulted) in Scorpio again around the same place

quotations.original: οὗ τὸ δωδεκατημόριον διηύγαζεν Σκορπίου περὶ τὸν πρῶτον σφόνδυλον

quotations.original: ἀλλὰ πάλιν ζητήσας τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην τῆς Τύχης καὶ τῆς Σελήνης εὑρήσει τὸν Κρόνον ἀποκεκλικότα καὶ ἐν πάθει τῶν ἐκλειπτικῶν ἐκπεπτωκότα· ὃς ἐποίησε τὴν καθαίρεσιν μεθ’ ὕβρεως
quotations.translation: But if one searches for the house-master of (the lot of) Fortune and of the Moon, one will find Saturn in a declining place and resulting in a position of suffering from eclipse-effects, and it has caused (the subject's) removal (from office) with violence.

quotations.original:
(36) 6 DANNA LA₂ ša₂ ME ⸢ša₂⸣ ITI.ŠE U₄.28.KAM 3 6 DANNA ina 4.30 9 DANNA
(37) E₁₁ 1.30 ana KUR šamaš₂ re-ḫi 1.30 ina 6 12 DANNA E₁₁-ma 4.30 IB₂.TAG₄
(38) U₄.28.KAM 4.30 ⸢ME⸣ NIM.A ana KUR E.A GAR-an
quotations.translation: (36) The length of daylight for the 28th of month XII is 6 beru. You deduct 3,0 (UŠ i.e.) 6 bēru, from 4,30 (UŠ , i.e.) 9 bēru , (37) 1,30 (UŠ) until sunrise remains. You deduct 1,30 (UŠ) from 6,0 (UŠ, i.e.) 12 bēru, 4,30 is the remainder (38) for day 28. You put down 4,30 (UŠ) as the time (from New Moon) to sunrise in order to predict KUR.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.original: Ἐαρινὴ μὲν οὖν ἰσημερία γίνεται περὶ τὴν τῶν ἀνθέων ἀκμὴν ἐν Κριοῦ μιᾷ μοίρᾳ.
quotations.translation: Spring equinox then takes place around the hight of blooming time, (when the sun is) in the first degree of Aries.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἐαρινὴ μὲν οὖν ἰσημερία γίνεται περὶ τὴν τῶν ἀνθέων ἀκμὴν ἐν Κριοῦ μιᾷ μοίρᾳ.

quotations.original: Τροπὴ δέ θερινὴ γίνεται περὶ τὴν τῶν καυμάτων ἐπίτασιν ἐν Καρκίνου μιᾷ μοίρᾳ.
quotations.translation: And summer solstice takes place around the intensification of the heat, (when the sun is) in the first degree of Cancer.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Τροπὴ δέ θερινὴ γίνεται περὶ τὴν τῶν καυμάτων ἐπίτασιν ἐν Καρκίνου μιᾷ μοίρᾳ.
quotations.translation: And summer solstice takes place around the intensification of the heat, (when the sun is) in the first degree of Cancer.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἰσημερία δέ ἐστι φθινοπωρινή, ὅταν ὁ ἥλιος ἀπ’ ἄρκτων πρὸς μεσημβρίαν παροδεύων πάλιν ἐπὶ τοῦ ἰσημερινοῦ γένηται κύκλου καὶ ἴσην τὴν ἡμέραν τῇ νυκτερινῇ ποιήσηται.
quotations.translation: And it is autumnal equinox, when the sun, in passing from north to south, arrives at the celestial equator again and makes the day equal to the night.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἰσημερία δέ ἐστι φθινοπωρινή, ὅταν ὁ ἥλιος ἀπ’ ἄρκτων πρὸς μεσημβρίαν παροδεύων πάλιν ἐπὶ τοῦ ἰσημερινοῦ γένηται κύκλου καὶ ἴσην τὴν ἡμέραν τῇ νυκτερινῇ ποιήσηται.

quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Τροπὴ δέ ἐστι χειμερινή, ὅταν ὁ ἥλιος πορρωτάτω ἡμῶν τῆς οἰκήσεως γένηται καὶ ταπεινότατον ὡς πρὸς τὸν ὁρίζοντα καὶ νοτιώτατον κύκλον γράψῃ καὶ μεγίστην πασῶν τῶν ἐν τῷ ἐνιαυτῷ νύκτα ποιήσηται, ἐλαχίστην δὲ ἡμέραν· (...)
quotations.translation: And it is winter solstice, when the sun arrives the furthest from our place of residence and describes a circle as low as possible in reference to the horizon and the most southerly, and makes the longest night of all of them in the year, but the shortest day; (...)
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original:
Ἐν μὲν γαῖαν ἔτευξ’, ἐν δ’ οὐρανόν, ἐν δὲ θάλασσαν,
ἠέλιόν τ’ ἀκάμαντα σελήνην τε πλήθουσαν,
ἐν δὲ τὰ τείρεα πάντα, τά τ’ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται,
Πληϊάδας θ’ Ὑάδας τε τό τε σθένος Ὠρίωνος
Ἄρκτόν θ’, ἣν καὶ Ἄμαξαν ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν,
ἥ τ’ αὐτοῦ στρέφεται καί τ’ Ὠρίωνα δοκεύει,
οἴη δ’ ἄμμορός ἐστι λοετρῶν Ὠκεανοῖο.
quotations.translation:
On it he produced the earth, and on it the sky, and on it the sea,
and the untiring sun and the full moon,
and on it all the constellations, that the sky is wreathed with:
the Pleiades as well as the Hyades as well as the might of Orion
as well as the Bear, which they call Wagon as additional name,
and which revolves around itself and keeps an eye on Orion,
and which alone is without share of baths in Ocean.
quotations.publication: Homer. 1920. Homeri Opera in five volumes, eds. D.B. Monro & T.W. Allen. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
quotations.comment: "which alone is without share of baths in Ocean": i.e., Ursa Major does not set.

quotations.original: Βόρεια δέ ἐστιν, ὅσα τοῦ τῶν ζῳδίων κύκλου πρὸς ἄρκτους κεῖται. Ἔστι δὲ τάδε· ἡ Μεγάλη Ἄρκτος, ἡ Μικρά, Δράκων ὁ διὰ τῶν Ἄρκτων, Ἀρκτοφύλαξ, Στέφανος, Ἐνγόνασιν, Ὀφιοῦχος, Ὄφις, Λύρα, Ὄρνις, Ὀϊστός, Ἀετός, Δελφίς, Προτομὴ Ἵππου καθ’ Ἵππαρχον, Ἵππος, Κηφεύς, Κασσιέπεια, Ἀνδρομέδα, Περσεύς, Ἡνίοχος, Δελτωτὸν καὶ ὁ ὕστερον κατεστηριγμένος ὑπὸ Καλλιμάχου Βερενίκης Πλόκαμος.
quotations.translation: Northern (constellations) there are as many as lie to the north of the zodiac. These are the following: the Great Bear, the Little (Bear), Dragon between the Bears, Bear Keeper, Crown, Kneeling Man, Ophiuchus, Serpent, Lyre, Bird, Arrow, Eagle, Dolphin, Forepart of a Horse according to Hipparchus, Horse, Cepheus, Cassiopeia, Andromeda, Perseus, Charioteer, Triangle and the later by Callimachus established Lock of Berenikē.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Θερμότατος δὲ ἐστὶ ὁ ἥλιος τούτοισι τοῖσι ἀνθρώποισι τὸ ἑωθινόν, οὐ κατά περ τοῖσι ἄλλοισι μεσαμβρίης, ἀλλ᾽ ὑπερτείλας μέχρι οὗ ἀγορῆς διαλύσιος.
quotations.translation: But the sun is the hottest among those people in the morning, not at midday such as amongst all others, but from when it has completely risen until the moment when the market is closing.
quotations.publication: Herodotus. 1920. Herodotus, with an English translation by A.D. Godley, ed. A.D. Godley. Cambridge Massachusetts: Harvard University Press.

(8) ina 16 MU.MEŠ

quotations.original: 30 TA MURUB4 ana NIM pa-ni-šu2 GAR.MEŠ
quotations.translation: The moon sets its front from the middle toward positive latitude.
quotations.date: 3rd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: S.E. 77 III.4 = -234 June 2/3)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88, 1–164.

quotations.original: ina si-man-šu2 30 ina TIL MAŠ2 ina 18 | 20 ina TIL ḪUN ina 30
quotations.translation: In his hour (of birth), the moon was at the end of Capricorn in 18°, | the sun at the end of Aries in 30°.
quotations.date: 1st century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: 243 S.E. I.20 = -68 Apr.16)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: Ἐπιζητεῖται δὲ ἐν τούτοις, πῶς ἴσων ὄντων τῶν τεταρτημορίων τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ κύκλου ὁ ἥλιος ἰσοταχῶς κινούμενος διὰ παντὸς ἐν ἀνίσοις χρόνοις διαπορεύεται τὰς ἴσας περιφερείας.
quotations.translation: And it is a matter of question concerning these things: how - while the fourth parts of the zodiac are equal - does the sun, moving through each of them at constant speed, pass equal arcs in unequal times?
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.
quotations.comment: Right before this passage, Geminus discusses the intervals of time between the solstices and the equinoxes. Each of these 4 intervals consists of the amount of time during which the sun passes not just through a quarter of the zodiac, but through 3 specified entire zodiac signs.

quotations.original: i-nu-šu2 30 šap-lat SI GIR2.TAB
quotations.translation: At that time, the moon was below the Horn of the Scorpion.
quotations.date: 3rd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: [Darius II Year 14].I.14 = -409 April 29)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: Ἐπιζητεῖται δὲ ἐν τούτοις, πῶς ἴσων ὄντων τῶν τεταρτημορίων τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ κύκλου ὁ ἥλιος ἰσοταχῶς κινούμενος διὰ παντὸς ἐν ἀνίσοις χρόνοις διαπορεύεται τὰς ἴσας περιφερείας. Ὑποκείται γὰρ πρὸς ὅλην τὴν ἀστρολογίαν ἥλιόν τε καὶ σελήνην καὶ τοὺς εʹ πλανήτας ἰσοταχῶς καὶ ἐγκυκλίως καὶ ὑπεναντίως τῷ κόσμῳ κινεῖσθαι.
quotations.translation: And it is a matter of question concerning these things: how - while the fourth parts of the zodiac are equal - does the sun, moving through each of them at constant speed, pass equal arcs in unequal times? For it is assumed regarding all of astronomy, that the sun and the moon and the 5 planets move at constant speed and in a circle and in a manner contrary to the cosmos.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Ἐπιζητεῖται δὲ ἐν τούτοις, πῶς ἴσων ὄντων τῶν τεταρτημορίων τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ κύκλου ὁ ἥλιος ἰσοταχῶς κινούμενος διὰ παντὸς ἐν ἀνίσοις χρόνοις διαπορεύεται τὰς ἴσας περιφερείας.

quotations.original:
Ἐν μὲν γαῖαν ἔτευξ’, ἐν δ’ οὐρανόν, ἐν δὲ θάλασσαν,
ἠέλιόν τ’ ἀκάμαντα σελήνην τε πλήθουσαν,
ἐν δὲ τὰ τείρεα πάντα, τά τ’ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται,
Πληϊάδας θ’ Ὑάδας τε τό τε σθένος Ὠρίωνος
Ἄρκτόν θ’, ἣν καὶ Ἄμαξαν ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν,
ἥ τ’ αὐτοῦ στρέφεται καί τ’ Ὠρίωνα δοκεύει,
οἴη δ’ ἄμμορός ἐστι λοετρῶν Ὠκεανοῖο.
quotations.translation:
On it he produced the earth, and on it the sky, and on it the sea,
and the untiring Sun and the full Moon,
and on it all the constellations, that the sky is wreathed with:
the Pleiades as well as the Hyades as well as the might of Orion
as well as the Bear, which they call Wagon as additional name,
and which revolves around itself and keeps an eye on Orion,
and which alone is without share of baths in Ocean.
quotations.publication: Homer. 1920. Homeri Opera in five volumes, eds. D.B. Monro & T.W. Allen. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
quotations.comment: "which alone is without share of baths in Ocean": i.e., Ursa Major does not set.

quotations.original:
Δέδυκε μὲν ἀ σελάννα
καὶ Πληΐαδες· μέσαι δὲ
νύκτες, παρὰ δ’ ἔρχετ’ ὤρα,
ἔγω δὲ μόνα κατεύδω.
quotations.translation:
Set are the moon
and Pleiades; and it is
midnight, and time passes,
and I sleep alone.
quotations.publication: Sappho. 1990. Greek Lyric, 1. Sappho and Alcaeus, ed. D.A. Campbell, 2nd edition. Cambridge Massachusetts: Harvard University Press.
quotations.comment: The attribution of this fragment to Sappho is uncertain.

quotations.original: ὁ δὲ τούτων κύριος Ἄρης ἐκπαραπεσὼν καὶ ἀμαρτύρητος τῷ τόπῳ ἐναντία καὶ φυγαδείαν καὶ βιαιοθανασίαν ἐποίησεν
quotations.translation: The lord of these (sc. the Ascendant, lots, exaltation of nativity), Mars, being unfavorably situated (lit., having fallen outside) and not in aspect with the place(?), made opposite (effects) and exile and violent death.
quotations.publication: (GH L 78)

quotations.original: ἔστω δὲ ἐπὶ ὑποδείγματος Ἥλιος, Ἀφροδίτη Καρκίνῳ, Σελήνη, ὡροσκόπος Ἰχθύσιν, Κρόνος Τοξότῃ, Ζεὺς Αἰγοκέρωτι, Ἄρης Σκορπίῳ, Ἑρμῆς Λέοντι, ὁ κλῆρος τῆς τύχης Καρκίνῳ ἀγαθοδαιμονῶν. ἡ κυρία τοῦ κλήρου ἐπὶ τοῦ κέντρου εὑρέθη· ἔθηκα τὰ ἐλάχιστα τῆς Σελήνης κε ἔτη, καὶ τοῦ Καρκίνου τὴν ἀναφορὰν τοῦ δευτέρου κλίματος ἔτη λβ, καὶ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου τῆς Σελήνης, Διός, ἔτη ιβ· γίνονται ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἔτη ξθ. τοσούτων ἐτῶν ἐτελεύτα.
quotations.translation: As an example, let the Sun, Venus be in Cancer, Moon, Ascendant in Pisces, Saturn in Sagittarius, Jupiter in Capricorn, Mars in Scorpio, Mercury in Leo, the Lot of Fortune in Cancer and in the place of the Good Divinity. The lord of the lot has been found at a cardinal point: I set the minimum (years, sc. of the calculation of lifetime) of the Moon, 25 years, and the rising-time of Cancer in the second clima, 32 years, and (the minimum years) of the house-master of the Moon, Jupiter, 12 years. They total 69 years: at that age he died.
quotations.publication: (GH L 75)

quotations.original: [οὗ] τὸ δωδεκατημόριον ἐνλήγει ἐν Τοξότηι μοιρῶν κʹ
quotations.translation: Its dodekatemorion ends in Sagittarius, 20 degrees
quotations.publication: GH 95

quotations.original: ἀμφότεροι δὲ οἱ κακοποιοὶ ἐμπεριέσχον τὴν Ἀφροδίτην
quotations.translation: Both malefic (planets) enclosed Venus
quotations.publication: (GH L 122,XII)

quotations.original: Sed antequam ad explicationem mixturarum sermo noster accedat, pauca tibi de splendidarum stellarum dicam
quotations.translation: But before we come to speak about configurations of the planets, I want to tell you something about the bright stars
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed antequam ad explicationem mixturarum sermo noster accedat, pauca tibi de splendidarum stellarum dicam
quotations.translation: But before we come to speak about configurations of planets, I want to tell you something about the bright stars
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Claras stellas et augusta maiestatis radiatione fulgentes in signis omnibus invenimus, sed regales in quattuor, in Leone scilicet in Scorpione in Aquario et in Tauro.
quotations.translation: Bright stars and ones which glitter with majestic grandeur we find in every sign, but kingly [stars] only in four [signs]: in Leo as in Scorpio, in Aquarius and in Taurus
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Claras stellas et augusta maiestatis radiatione fulgentes in signis omnibus invenimus, sed regales in quattuor, in Leone scilicet in Scorpione in Aquario et in Tauro.
quotations.translation: Bright stars and ones which glitter with majestic grandeur we find in every sign, but kingly [stars] only in four [signs]: in Leo as in Scorpio, in Aquarius and in Taurus
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Claras stellas et augusta maiestatis radiatione fulgentes in signis omnibus invenimus, sed regales in quattuor, in Leone scilicet in Scorpione in Aquario et in Tauro.
quotations.translation: Bright stars and ones which glitter with majestic grandeur we find in every sign, but kingly [stars] only in four [signs]: in Leo as in Scorpio, in Aquarius and in Taurus
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quinta pars Leonis habet stellam lucido splendore fulgentem.
quotations.translation: The fifth degree of Leo has a star shining with brightness full of light.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero Sol superior effectus et dextrum possidens latus Saturnum in inferiori loco constitutum quadrata radiatione respexerit, paternam substantiam dispergit ista coniunctio
quotations.translation: If the Sun is in the superior position on the right and is in square aspect with Saturn in inferior position, this indicates loss of paternal inheritance
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero Sol superior effectus et dextrum possidens latus Saturnum in inferiori loco constitutum quadrata radiatione respexerit, paternam substantiam dispergit ista coniunctio
quotations.translation: If the Sun is in the superior position on the right and is in square aspect with Saturn in inferior position, this indicates loss of paternal inheritance
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed <haec mala> tunc fortius convalescunt, si in muto signo Mercurium constitutum Saturnus diametra radiatione respexerit
quotations.translation: But these bad effects are stronger when Mercury is in an unvoiced sign and opposite to Saturn
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quodsi ab his benivolarum stellarum recesserit radius, et ab omni salutarium siderum fuerint testimonio destituti, tunc matrem inhonesta corporis turpitudo dedecorat
quotations.translation: If the of the benefic recedes from them and they are unaspected by all benefic planets, then shameful ugliness disgraces the mother's body
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quodsi ab his benivolarum stellarum recesserit radius, et ab omni salutarium siderum fuerint testimonio destituti, tunc matrem inhonesta corporis turpitudo dedecorat
quotations.translation: If the of the benefic recedes from them and they are unaspected by all benefic planets, then shameful ugliness disgraces the mother's body
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero in ferinis signis constituti ista se radiatione respexerint, ex feris vel bestiis vel ex venenatis serpentium morsibus maximi periculi conparatur exitium.
quotations.translation: If they aspect each other in that way while in animal signs, a most dangerous death comes about through wild animals or bites of venomous snakes
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Iuppiter et Luna diametra se radiatione respexerint, et in contrariis constituti locis longa se invicem radiorum suorum potestate pulsaverint, et sit Luna plena luminibus, et partes Iovis Lunae partium numerus antecedat. principalia dignitatis insignia decernit ista radiatio,
quotations.translation: If Jupiter is opposite to the moon and they are located in opposite places and strongly strike each other with their rays, and if the moon is full and the degrees of Jupiter are less than the number of degrees of the moon, this aspect decrees principal signs of greatness
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: nunc iunctas stellarum societates manifesta sermonis interpretatione signabimus
quotations.translation: now we want to delineate the aspects of the planets with clear interpretations
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Saturnus et Iuppiter unum hospitium partis acceperint, et in uno loco pariter constituti aequabili societatis potestate iungantur, si in opportunis geniturae locis et in his in quibus gaudent signis vel partibus ista fuerint radiatione societatis coniuncti, felicitatis insignia [...] ex ista societate decernunt,
quotations.translation: If Saturn and Jupiter share the hospitality of one degree and conjunct each other equally in one place, if they conjunct each other in fortunate places of the nativity and in the signs or degrees of their exaltation, they decree fortune from this aspect
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Martis enim inconsulta temeritas et ardoris inprobitas et inflammati caloris ardor inpatiens coniuncto sibi Saturni frigore temperatur,
quotations.translation: The association with Saturn reduces the unthinking rashness and impatient ardor of Mars and blunts it with Saturn's coldness
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Martis enim inconsulta temeritas et ardoris inprobitas et inflammati caloris ardor inpatiens coniuncto sibi Saturni frigore temperatur,
quotations.translation: The association with Saturn reduces the unthinking rashness and impatient ardor of Mars and blunts it with Saturn's coldness
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Haec etiam in feminarum genituris Venus et Saturnus simul positi, aequata ra<dia>tionis societate decernunt.
quotations.translation: Venus and Saturn decree this when located in conjunction in nativities of women.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Tunc enim malitia eius coniunctionis nec praesentia potest Iovis nec testimonio mitigari.
quotations.translation: For then the malice of this aspect cannot even be mitigated by the presence or aspect of Jupiter.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero Sole in masculino signo constituto renata Luna feminini generis occupaverit signum, faciet principales vel principes civitatum
quotations.translation: If however the Sun is located in a male sign and the renewed moon occupies a female sign, it makes chiefs or magistrates of cities
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero Sol et Luna luminum suorum fuerint radiis adversi, tunc vita parentum ———
quotations.translation: If however sun and moon with their lights are in opposition, then the life of the parents ———
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quodsi simul Mercurium ac Venerem collocates malignum sidus Martis aspexerit, faciles nuptias sed cum quadam infamia ac nota decernunt.
quotations.translation: If Mercury and Venus are in conjunction and the malefic planet Mars aspects them, they decree easy but scandalous marriages
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quodsi simul Mercurium ac Venerem collocates malignum sidus Martis aspexerit, faciles nuptias sed cum quadam infamia ac nota decernunt.
quotations.translation: If Mercury and Venus are in conjunction and the malefic planet Mars aspects them, they decree easy but scandalous marriages
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna et Iuppiter partili fuerint radiatione coniuncti, et eos simul partiliter collocatos in dextro quadrato positus Saturnus partili radiatione respexerit, et Mars simili hos eosdem per quadratum minaci radiatione percutiat, Sol vero sit in VI. vel in XII. loco, ex ista coniunctione servilis genitura decernitur
quotations.translation: If the Moon and Jupiter are in exact conjunction and Saturn aspects them both in an exact right square and Mars strikes them in a square with malefic rays, if the Sun is in the 6th or in the 12th place—by this configuration the nativity of a slave is decreed
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna et Iuppiter partili fuerint radiatione coniuncti, et eos simul partiliter collocatos in dextro quadrato positus Saturnus partili radiatione respexerit, et Mars simili hos eosdem per quadratum minaci radiatione percutiat, Sol vero sit in VI. vel in XII. loco, ex ista coniunctione servilis genitura decernitur
quotations.translation: If the Moon and Jupiter are in exact conjunction and Saturn aspects them both in an exact right square and Mars strikes them in a square with malefic rays, if the Sun is in the 6th or in the 12th place—by this configuration the nativity of a slave is decreed
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Lunam de diametro Mars et Saturnus pariter aspexerint, et nulla benivolarum stellarum vel Lunam vel illos qui sunt in diametro constituti, salutari radiatione convenerit, aut servos efficiet ista coniunctio, aut privates parentum praesidio misero faciet orbitatis onere praegravari.
quotations.translation: If Mars and Saturn are equally in opposition to the moon and no benefic aspects either the Moon or the planets opposite her with benefic radiation, this configuration either makes slaves or orphans that are burdened with bereavement
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: et si hanc eandem partem id est horoscopum Sol et Luna qualibet radiatione viderint, Mars vero <et> Saturnus ab horoscopi parte malignos potestatis suae radios separarint, prospere natus prosperius nutrietur.
quotations.translation: and when Sun and Moon aspect the very degree, i. e. the ascendant, but Mars and Saturn separate the malefic rays of their power [from them], the native will be born and brought up in good fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quodsi sic malivolis sicut diximus constitutis horoscopo Venus aut luppiter testimonium conmodaverint, expositus colligetur et alienae misericordiae praesidio nutrietur.
quotations.translation: If as we said Venus and Jupiter aspect the malefic planets on the ascendant favorably, the exposed infant will be picked up and nourished by a stranger
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Iuppiter in horoscopo partiliter fuerit constitutus, et in diametro Mars positus horam et Iovem partili radiatione respexerit, ceteris stellis nullum his testimonium conmodantibus, mediocris substantiae facultatem decernit ista coniunctio.
quotations.translation: If Jupiter is on the ascendant and Mars is in exact opposition to the ascendant and to Jupiter while the other planets are not in favorable aspect to them, this configuration decrees mediocre fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In ferinis enim et in agrestibus constituti signis, ad necem praeparatos ferarum adferunt morsus.
quotations.translation: Located in animal and rural signs they bring death at the teeth of wild beasts.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna et Sol synodica fuerint radiatione coniuncti, et in eodem signo inter Solem et Lunam Mars medius fuerit inventus, et eos de quadrato Saturnus respiciat [...], qui sic habuerint stellas, vitiosis oppressi humoribus interibunt
quotations.translation: If Moon and Sun are in conjunction (by sign) and Mars is located in the same sign between them while Saturn stands in square aspect to them—he who has the planets configured as such will die oppressed by malignant humors
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in labris Arietis vel in Capricorno fuerit inventa, vel Tauri labra simili ratione possederit, mulieres quidem viragines faciet
quotations.translation: The Moon on the cusp of Aries or Taurus or in Capricorn makes women shrews
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Sol et Luna feminini generis possederint signa, <et> horoscopus in feminino signo fuerit inventus, et in horoscope sit Mercurius positus partiliter, manibus suis naturam suam amputare coguntur.
quotations.translation: If the Sun, Moon and ascendant are in feminine signs and Mercury is exact on the ascendant, the natives are forced to amputate their genitals with their own hands.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in MC. fuerit inventa, et in IMC. Venus constituta partili Lunam radiatione respiciat, ista coniunctio incestae cupiditatis ardore sorores fratribus iunget uxores.
quotations.translation: If the Moon is located on the MC and Venus on the IC and it exactly aspects the Moon, this configuration will make sisters into wives by way of incestuous love
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Hic ille est noster, cuius ingenio fabricata sphaera lapsum caeli et omnium siderum cursus exemplo divinae imitationis ostendit.
quotations.translation: He is our [fellow citizen Archimedes] whose ingeniously fabricated sphere demonstrates the rotation of the sky and all paths of the planets as an example of divine imitation
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in duodecimo ab horoscope loco id est in cacodaemone fuerit inventa, et sit in eo signo quod Saturni dicitur trigonum, id est in Aquario aut in Geminis aut in Libra [...]
quotations.translation: If the Moon is located in the twelfth place, i.e. in the place of the Bad Daemon, and she is in a sign which is called Saturn's triangle, i.e. in Aquarius or Gemini or Libra [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna et Mars in septimo sint ab horoscope loco constituti, id est in occasu, et sint in eo signo constituti, in quo Martis invenitur trigonum, id est aut in Cancro aut in Scorpione aut in Piscibus, [...]
quotations.translation: If Moon and Mars are located in the 7th place, i.e. the descendant, and they are located in the sign in which is found Mars' triangle, i.e. in Cancer or in Scorpio or in Pisces
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si [...] horoscopante Marte Venus cum Mercurio in occasu fuerit constituta [...]
quotations.translation: If Venus and Mars are located on the descendant while Mars is on the ascendant [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Iuppiter <in iis Piscium partibus> fuerit, in quibus est Andromeda constituta [...]
quotations.translation: If Jupiter stands in those degrees of Pisces in which Andromeda is located [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si <Venus in Tauro fuerit> constituta, et eas Tauri partes teneat, in quibus sunt Pleiades positae [...]
quotations.translation: If Venus is in Taurus and occupies those degrees of Taurus in which the Pleiades are located [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si <Venus in Tauro fuerit> constituta, et eas Tauri partes teneat, in quibus sunt Pleiades positae [...]
quotations.translation: If Venus is in Taurus and occupies those degrees of Taurus in which the Pleiades are located [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si in parte Aquarii humiliter Saturnus aut Luna constituatur aut Mars, et hanc eandem partem de diametro Saturnus aspiciat, filios faciet a parentibus separari.
quotations.translation: If Saturn or the Moon or Mars are located low in a degree of Aquarius and Saturn stands in exact opposition to this degree, it indicates that children are separated from their parents
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in Tauri pedibus fuerit inventa, aut in nebula Cancri, aut in iuba Leonis, aut in fronte Scorpionis, ab VIII. scilicet parte usque ad X., <aut> in Sagittario, aut in spinis Capricorni, aut in lino Piscium, aut in capite Arietis, et sit minuta luminibus [...], et eam aut Satnrnus aut Mars aliqua radiatione respiciant, caecos efficiet.
quotations.translation: If the moon is located in the feet of the Bull or in the nebula of the Crab or in the mane of the Lion or in the front of the Scorpion ca. from 8° to 10° or in Sagittarius or in the spine of Capricorn or in the line of the Fish, or in the head of Aries, and it is waning [...], and either Saturn or Mars aspect her in any way, she indicates blindness.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in Tauri pedibus fuerit inventa, aut in nebula Cancri, aut in iuba Leonis, aut in fronte Scorpionis, ab VIII. scilicet parte usque ad X., <aut> in Sagittario, aut in spinis Capricorni, aut in lino Piscium, aut in capite Arietis, et sit minuta luminibus [...], et eam aut Satnrnus aut Mars aliqua radiatione respiciant, caecos efficiet.
