quotations.original: Si Luna in Tauri pedibus fuerit inventa, aut in nebula Cancri, aut in iuba Leonis, aut in fronte Scorpionis, ab VIII. scilicet parte usque ad X., <aut> in Sagittario, aut in spinis Capricorni, aut in lino Piscium, aut in capite Arietis, et sit minuta luminibus [...], et eam aut Satnrnus aut Mars aliqua radiatione respiciant, caecos efficiet.
quotations.translation: If the moon is located in the feet of the Bull or in the nebula of the Crab or in the mane of the Lion or in the front of the Scorpion ca. from 8° to 10° or in Sagittarius or in the spine of Capricorn or in the line of the Fish, or in the head of Aries, and it is waning [...], and either Saturn or Mars aspect her in any way, she indicates blindness.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si locum patris partili volueris ratione colligere, et sit diurna genitura, conputes a parte Solis usque ad partem Saturni omnem partium numerum [...]
quotations.translation: If you want to compute the lot of the father in a diurnal chart, count from the degree of the Sun until the degree of Saturn the number of all degrees
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Respice etiam quatenus hoc idem signum benivolarum stellarum radiia ornetur.
quotations.translation: Also look at how the same sign is aspected by the benefics
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si matris locum partili volueris ratione colligere, et sit diurna genitura, a parte Veneris inchoans et per sequentia signa pergens, omnes partes usque ad Lunae conputes partem
quotations.translation: If you want to exactly calculate the lot of the mother in a day-chart, count the degrees beginning with the degree of Venus going through the following signs up until the degree of the Moon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si matris locum partili volueris ratione colligere, et sit diurna genitura, a parte Veneris inchoans et per sequentia signa pergens, omnes partes usque ad Lunae conputes partem
quotations.translation: If you want to exactly calculate the lot of the mother in a day-chart, count the degrees beginning with the degree of Venus going through the following signs up until the degree of the Moon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: et omnium partium summa collecta, ab horoscope inchoans totas partes sequentibus divides signis
quotations.translation: and when the sum of all degrees is collected, divide all degrees by the following signs, starting from the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: et omnium partium summa collecta, ab horoscope inchoans totas partes sequentibus divides signis
quotations.translation: and when the sum of all degrees is collected, divide all degrees by the following signs, starting from the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si locum fratrum partiliter volueris invenire, et sit diuma genitura, a parte Saturni inchoans usque ad partem conputa lovis [...]
quotations.translation: If you want to find the exact degree of the lot of brothers in a day-chart, count from the degree of Saturn until the degree of Jupiter [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si locum coniugis partiliter volueris invenire, conputa a parte Saturni usque ad partem Veneris [...]
quotations.translation: If you want to find the degree of the lot of the spouse, count from the degree of Saturn until the degree of Venus [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In nocturna vero genitura a Venere inchoans ad Saturnum conputabis, et similiter conlectum partium numerum ab horoscopo inchoans divides
quotations.translation: In a night-chart you will count from Venus to Saturn and similarly divide the summed number of degrees beginning with the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Cum enim idem signum in quo locus coniugis fuerit inventus, benivolae stellae possederint, <in> oportunis geniturae locis positae, et nulla humilitate deiectae, et condicionis suae secutae sint potestatem, dabunt uxores gloriosas divites
quotations.translation: For when the same sign in which the lot of the spouse is found also holds benefic planets, placed in fortunate places of the chart, none being in a falling place, following the power of their condition they will give rich and famous wives
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero in genitura mulieris locum mariti volueris invenire, et sit diurna genitura, a Marte ad Venerem ———
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of the husband in a woman's chart, if it is a day-chart, from Mars to Venus ——
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Locum nobis filiorum Venus et Mercurius semper ostendunt.
quotations.translation: Venus and Mercury always show us the lot of children.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero in uno <signo> fuerint constituti, ab eo inchoans * * * usque ad alium veneris, qui in eodem signo [qui] in posterioribus partibus fuerit inventus.
quotations.translation: If they are in the same sign, begin from the one that is in the earlier part of the sign until you come to another one
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vitiorum ac valitudinis locum partiliter volueris invenire, in diurna quidem genitura a Saturno inchoans usque ad Martem conputabis
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of afflictions and health by degree, in a day-chart count from Saturn up to Mars
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero hic locus possessus a malivolis nudus ab omni benivolarum stellarum praesidio relinquatur, perpetua vitia valitudinum et calamitatum exitiales exitus decernuntur.
quotations.translation: If this a malefic occupies this place, left naked without aspect to any benefic protector, perpetual illness and endless calamities are indicated
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero hic locus possessus a malivolis nudus ab omni benivolarum stellarum praesidio relinquatur, perpetua vitia valitudinum et calamitatum exitiales exitus decernuntur.
quotations.translation: If this a malefic occupies this place, left naked without aspect to any benefic protector, perpetual illness and endless calamities are indicated
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Locum desideriorum si partiliter volueris invenire, in diurna quidem genitura a parte Daemonis usque ad partem Fortunae conputa
quotations.translation: If you want to find the place of longing by degree in a day chart, count from the degree of the [lot of] spirit until the degree of [the lot of] fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Locum desideriorum si partiliter volueris invenire, in diurna quidem genitura a parte Daemonis usque ad partem Fortunae conputa
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of longing by degree in a day chart, count from the lot of the spirit until the lot of fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Locum desideriorum si partiliter volueris invenire, in diurna quidem genitura a parte Daemonis usque ad partem Fortunae conputa
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of longing by degree in a day chart, count from the lot of the spirit until the lot of fortune
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In nocturna vero <a> Fortuna usque ad Daemonem simillimis rationibus conputabis
quotations.translation: In a night-chart you will count from the lot of fortune to the lot of spirit
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In nocturna vero <a> Fortuna usque ad Daemonem simillimis rationibus conputabis
quotations.translation: In a night-chart count from the lot of fortune until the lot of the daemon in a most similar way
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si necessitatis locum partili volueris invenire ratione, in diurna quidem gentura a Fortuna conputabis ad Daemonem
quotations.translation: If you want to find the degree of the lot of necessity in a day-chart count from the lot of fortune to the lot of the daemon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si honorum locum partili volueris ratione colligere, <a> IX. semper conputabis ad Solem,
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of honors exact by degrees, count from the 9th place up to the sun
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si militiae locum partili volueris ratione colligere, a Marte semper conputabis ad Solem,
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of warfare by degrees always count from Mars up to the sun
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si peregrinationis locum partiliter volueris invenire, a Sole semper conputabis ad Martem
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of sojourn by degrees, count from the Sun up to Mars
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si existimationis famam partili volueris ratione colligere, a Sole usque ad MC. conputabis
quotations.translation: If you want to find the degree of the lot of opionion and rumors, you will count from the Sun to the MC
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si virtutem corporis partiliter volueris invenire, a Luna conputabis ad Iovem, et tantundem ab horoscope
quotations.translation: If you want to find the degree of the lot of bodily virtue, you will count from the Moon until Jupiter, and [add] that [amount of degrees] to the horoscope
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si possessionum substantiam partili volueris ratione colligere, a Mercurio semper conputabis ad Iovem, et tantundem ab horoscope
quotations.translation: If you want to find the degree of the lot of possessions, you will always count from Mercury up until Jupiter, and [add] that amount [of degrees] to the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si accusationis locum partili volueris ratione colligere, a Marte semper conputabis ad Saturnum
quotations.translation: If you want to find the degree of the lot of indictment, you will always count from Mars until Saturn
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si adversariorum locum et inimicorum partili volueris ratione colligere, per diem a Marte ad Mercurium conputabis
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of adversaries and enemies by degree, by day you will count from Mars until Mercury
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Gloriae nocte a Venere ad Iovem, die contra.
quotations.translation: [The lot of] Fame [can be calculated by adding to the ascendant the amount of degrees] from Venus until Jupiter, in a day-chart vice versa.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: potestatis nocte a Saturno ad Solem
quotations.translation: [The lot of] Power [can be calculated by adding to the ascendant the amount of degrees] from Saturn up to the Sun
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si amicorum locum partili volueris ratione colligere, per diem quidem a Iove ad Mercurium conputabis
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of friends by degree, you will count by day from Jupiter to Mercury
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nemesis nocte a Fortuna ad Lunam
quotations.translation: [The lot of] Nemesis [can be calculated by adding to the ascendant the amount of degrees] from the lot of fortune up to the Moon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: basis nocte a fortuna ad genium.
quotations.translation: [The lot of] basis [can be calculated by adding to the ascendant the amount of degrees] at night from the lot of fortune until the lot of the daemon
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si servorum locum partili volueris ratione colligere, a Mercurio semper conputabis Lunam, et tantundem ab horoscopo
quotations.translation: If you want to find the lot of slaves by degree, you will always count from Mercury up to the Moon and [add] this amount to the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si sepulturae ——— <sepulturae> exitum monstrat
quotations.translation: If [you want to calculate] the lot of burial ——— the lot of burial shows the end of life
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Saturnus temporum dominus effectus Marti deputaverit tempora, deputat quidem [et] ex decennio suo menses XV.
quotations.translation: If Saturn becomes the time-lord and allots its time to Mars, he allots 15 months of his ten-year period
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Saturnus temporum dominus effectus Marti deputaverit tempora, deputat quidem [et] ex decennio suo menses XV.
quotations.translation: If Saturn becomes the time-lord and allots its time to Mars, he allots 15 months of his ten-year period
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Cum Iovi X anni et IX menses delati fuerint, ipse sibi primus ex omni hoc tempore XII vindicat menses.
quotations.translation: When ten years and nine months are allotted to Jupiter, he himself takes twelve months.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Iuppiter temporum dominus fuerit effectus, ex decennio suo deputat Saturno XXX menses.
quotations.translation: If Jupiter becomes time lord, he allots 30 months of his own ten-year period to Saturn.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Sol dominus temporum fuerit, id est cum ei X annorum et IX mensium fuerit assignatum tempus, omnia etiam in ipso quae in ceteris diximus, simili debes ratione perspicere
quotations.translation: If the Sun becomes time lord, i. e. when 10 years and 9 months are allotted to it, you must look at it in the same manner which we described for the other planets
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original:
DIŠ KI mul2.ŠU.GI be-en-nu di-ḫu u ra-pa-du ḫe-pi2 SAG.KI.DAB.BA MUL-d.AMAR.UTU
ana be-en-nu A.RI.A d.Šul-pa-e3 be-en-nu
quotations.translation: If (the moon is) in the region of the Old-Man-star: epilepsy, fever, or joint-disease, (break), migraine. The 'Star of Marduk'(=Mercury) (is) for epilepsy, the ‘sperm of Šulpa’e’ (for) epilepsy.
quotations.publication: Geller, M. J., 2014. Melothesia in Babylonia: Medicine, Magic, and Astrology in the Ancient Near East. Boston, Berlin, and Munich: De Gruyter.

quotations.original: 2 MA.NA KI.LA₂ 12 UŠ i-na qaq-qa-ri 21 lim 6 me ⸢DANNA⸣ [ina AN-e] | TA mul.ŠUDUN.ANŠE EGIR-ti EN ⸢mul⸣.[GUR₂-ti]
quotations.translation: 2 minas weight, 12 UŠ on the ground, 21 thousand 6 hundred bēru [in heaven], from the Rear Harness to the [Circle].
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 2 1/2 MA.NA MIN 1/2 DANNA i-na KI.MIN 27 lim DANNA ina [AN-e] | TA mul.GAM-ti EN MUL ša₂ maš-a-ti
quotations.translation: 2 1/2 minas ditto (weight), 1/2 bēru on ditto (the ground), 27 thousand bēru in [heaven], |  from the Circle to the Star from the Doublets.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 2 1/2 MA.NA MIN 1/2 DANNA i-na KI.MIN 27 lim DANNA ina [AN-e] | TA mul.GAM-ti EN MUL ša₂ maš-a-ti
quotations.translation: 2 1/2 minas ditto (weight), 1/2 bēru on ditto (the ground), 27 thousand bēru in [heaven], |  from the Circle to the Star from the Doublets.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 1 5/6 MA.NA MIN 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN TA MUL ša₂ taš-ka-a-ti EN MUL DILI
quotations.translation: 1 5/6 minas ditto (weight), 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 18 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven),  from the Star from the Triplets to the Single Star.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 1 1/2 MA.NA KI.LA₂ 9 UŠ i-na qaq-qa-ri 16 lim 2 me DANNA [ina AN-e] | TA mul.ŠUDUN EN mul.ŠUDUN.[ANŠE EGIR]
quotations.translation: 1 1/2 minas weight, 9 UŠ on the ground, 16 thousand 2 hundred bēru [in heaven], from the Yoke to the [Rear] Harn[ess].
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 4 MA.NA 10 GIN₂ MIN 2/3 DANNA i-na KI.MIN 45 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN TA mul.a-ru₆ EN mul.ŠUDUN.ANŠE
quotations.translation: 4 minas, 10 shekels ditto (weight) 2/3 bēru on ditto (the ground) 45 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), from the Frond to the Harness.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: συνανατέλλει μὲν αὐτῷ ὁ ζῳδιακὸς ἀπὸ γʹ καὶ κʹ μοίρας τοῦ Σκορπίου ἕως Τοξότου μοίρας αʹ καὶ κʹ· μεσουρανεῖ δὲ ἀπὸ Παρθένου γʹ ἕως Ζυγοῦ ιʹ
quotations.translation: There rises with it (sc. the Beast, i.e. Lupus) the zodiac from 23 degrees of Scorpio up to 21 degrees of Sagittarius, and it culminates (lit. is in midheaven) from 3 of Virgo until 10 of Libra

quotations.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὰ ιβʹ ζῴδια τάδε· Κριός, Ταῦρος, Δίδυμοι, Καρκίνος, Λέων, Παρθένος, Ζυγός, Σκορπίος, Τοξότης, Αἰγόκερως, Ὑδροχόος, Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: And the 12 zodiac signs are these: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: 4 MA.NA 10 GIN₂ MIN 2/3 DANNA i-na KI.MIN 45 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN TA mul.a-ru₆ EN mul.ŠUDUN.ANŠE
quotations.translation: 4 minas, 10 shekels ditto (weight) 2/3 bēru on ditto (the ground) 45 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), from the Frond to the Harness.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: ὅ τε μέγας ἡγεμὼν ἡμέρας ἥλιος διττὰς καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτὸν ἀποτελῶν ἰσημερίας, ἔαρι καὶ μετοπώρῳ, τὴν μὲν ἐαρινὴν ἐν κριῷ, τὴν δὲ μετοπωρινὴν ἐν Ζυγῷ, ἐναργεστάτην παρέχεται πίστιν τοῦ περὶ τὴν ἑβδόμην θεοπρεποῦς· ἑκατέρα γὰρ τῶν ἰσημεριῶν ἑβδόμῳ γίνεται μηνί, καθ’ ἃς καὶ ἑορτάζειν διείρηται νόμῳ τὰς μεγίστας καὶ δημοτελεστάτας ἑορτάς
quotations.translation: The Sun also, the great leader of day, by effecting twin equinoxes each year, in spring and autumn, the spring one in Aries and the autumn one in Libra, furnishes a very clear confirmation of the godly quality of the hebdomad: for each of the equinoxes occurs in a seventh month, and on them (sc. the equinoxes) it has been determined in the Law to celebrate the greatest and most sovereign festivals

quotations.original: 1 5/6 MA.NA MIN 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN TA MUL ša₂ taš-ka-a-ti EN MUL DILI
quotations.translation: 1 5/6 minas ditto (weight), 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 18 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven),  from the Star from the Triplets to the Single Star.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἐστιν ἐπὶ πάσῃ καταρχῇ ζητεῖν καὶ τὰς μεσεμβολίας Ἡλίου καὶ τῶν ἀστέρων, καὶ τὰς ἐμπεριοχὰς τοῦ ὡροσκόπου καὶ τῆς Σελήνης καὶ τοῦ ἀστέρος τοῦ λόγον ἔχοντος πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδεσποτείαν τῆς καταρχῆς
quotations.translation: It is necessary in every inception to seek both the interpositions of the Sun and the planets and the enclosures of the Ascendant and the Moon and the planet that has the claim to the house-mastership of the inception.

quotations.translation: The 24th, clouds were in the sky, the north wind blew; in the afternoon, overcast.

quotations.translation: The 19th, strong gusty north wind. Night of the 20th, gusty wind.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1989. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. II: Diaries from 261 B.C. to 165 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 28 AN.GE6 20 ina ABSIN | ki PAP NU IGI
quotations.translation: On the 28th (of month V), an eclipse of the sun in Virgo; | when watched for (it) was not observed.
quotations.date: 2nd century BCE (date of birth in horoscope: S.E. 187 VI.22 = -124 Oct. 1)
quotations.publication: Rochberg, F. 1998. Babylonian Horoscopes. Transactions of the American Philosophical Society, 88.

quotations.original: Sed et si dominus Fortunae id est dominus eius signi (in) quo locus Fortunae fuerit inventus, et dominus eius signi in quo pars horoscopi constituta est, radiis sint Solis absconsi, aut in his signis in quibus ante diximus fuerint constituti, Saturnus vero aut Mars in occasu geniturae sint constituti, natus infans exponetur.
quotations.translation: Also if the ruler of Fortune, that is, the ruler of that sign which contains the Part of Fortune and the ruler of the sign in which the ascendant is hidden by the Sun's rays or in the signs we mentioned before, but Saturn and Mars are on the descendant, the native will be exposed at birth.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna sic fuerit constituta, ut malivolam stellam in praecedenti signo habeat, aliam in sequenti et sequens Lunam stella Solem quacumque radiatione respiciat, is qui natus fuerit aut exponetur aut statim ut natus fuerit interibit.
quotations.translation: If the Moon is so located that she has a malefic planet in the sign before hers and another in the sign following, and the one following is in any aspect to the Sun, the native will either be exposed or die at birth.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si in anafora horoscopi Iuppiter fuerit inventus, is et Lunam a Marte diametra radiatione percussam ipse quacumque radiatione respiciat, expositi et nutriti laqueis servilibus inplicantur.
quotations.translation: If Jupiter is on the anafora of the ascendant and himself opposes the Moon which is in square to Mars, the exposed are indicated to be nurtured but raised in slavery.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in aliquo cardine fuerit inventa, in fecundo scilicet signo, et cum ea benivola stella sit pariter constituta, horoscopus autem in duplici signo sit aut in fecundo aut cum Iove aut cum Mercurio, aut tres aut quinque nascentur.
quotations.translation: If the Moon is found on any angle in a fertile sign and a benefic planet is with her, and the ascendant is in a double or a fertile sign, or with Jupiter or Mercury, either three or five will be born.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed et si Lunam simili modo cum Venere in deiectis locis videris aut simul positas aut divisas, aut una in VI. sit ab horoscopo <loco>, alia in XII., matrem dic ancillam.
quotations.translation: But if you see the Moon in a similar way with Venus in the dejected houses, either together or separately, or one in the sixth house and the other in the twelfth, say that the mother has been a slave.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si Luna in contortis vel in ferinis signis fuerit inventa, id est in Tauro <aut> in Cancro aut in Scorpione aut in Capricorno aut in Piscibus, [...]
quotations.translation: If the Moon is found in curved or bestial signs, that is, in Taurus, Cancer, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Pisces [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed haec tibi omnia ex eo libro qui de fine vitae a nobis scriptus est, ex trigono orthogono manifestius intimantur.
quotations.translation: All these things are from our book which was written for you about the end of life and will be more clearly shown to you from triangles and right triangles.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero opitulante benivola stella et sie sicut diximus posita, dominus eius signi in quo est benivola stella collocata cum malivolis stellis vel cum Sole fuerit inventus, in praecedenti scilicet deiectione qua diximus, infortunia praedicta circa patrem vel matrem fortius convalescunt
quotations.translation: But if, with a helpful benefic planet located as we said, the ruler of the sign in which the benefic planet is found is with malefic planets or with the Sun, the aforesaid misfortune of the father and mother will be worse.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN | TA mul.GAM₃ EN mul.KIŠIB-GAM₃
quotations.translation: [...] 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 54 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), | from the Crook to the Crook's Handle.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: In genitura viri a Saturno numera ad Venerem, si sit diurna, et tantundem ab horoscope
quotations.translation: In the nativity of a man count from Saturn to Venus, if it is a day-chart, and [add] this amount to the ascendant
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN | TA mul.GAM₃ EN mul.KIŠIB-GAM₃
quotations.translation: [...] 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 54 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), | from the Crook to the Crook's Handle.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: Si <in> cupidinis loco id est cupiditatum Mars et Saturnus pariter fuerint inventi, et sit ipse locus in aliquo geniturae cardine constitutus, Venerem vero hi quos diximus qualibet radiatione respexerint, gonorroicas mortes efficient;
quotations.translation: If Mars and Saturn are found in the lot of desire and the house itself is on any angle, and Mars and Saturn are in aspect in any way to Venus, the natives will die of gonorrhea;
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si <in> cupidinis loco id est cupiditatum Mars et Saturnus pariter fuerint inventi, et sit ipse locus in aliquo geniturae cardine constitutus, Venerem vero hi quos diximus qualibet radiatione respexerint, gonorroicas mortes efficient;
quotations.translation: If Mars and Saturn are found in the lot of desire and the house itself is on any angle, and Mars and Saturn are in aspect in any way to Venus, the natives will die of gonorrhea;
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si locus necessitatis in Mercurii domo fuerit inventus, et Mercurius sit in aliquo cardine constitutus, Mars vero et Saturnus in anaforis sint cardinum vel in epicataforis positi, damnari perficient.
quotations.translation: If the lot of necessity is in the house of Mercury and Mercury is located on any angle, but Mars and Saturn are placed in the signs before or after the angles, they make the sentence carried out.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: [...] 1 DANNA i-na KI.MIN 54 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN | TA mul.KIŠIB-GAM₃ EN mul.MAŠ.TAB.BA
quotations.translation: [...] 1 bēru on ditto (the ground), 18 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), | from the Crook's Handle to the Twins.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: Si vero hoc loco sic sicut diximus constituto, Luna aut in primis partibus Piscium aut Capricorni aut Leonis fuerit, aut in Tauri novissimis, inpuris faciet libidinum vitiis inplicari.
quotations.translation: But if it is located as we said and the Moon is in the first degrees of Pisces, Capricorn, or Leo, or in the last degrees of Taurus, the natives will be involved in all vices.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed haec fortius convalescunt, si locus Fortunae et locus actus in cardine inventus praecedenti stellarum societati iungatur.
quotations.translation: But these indications are stronger if the Part of Fortune and the house of occupations are found on angles and joined to Mars, Mercury, and Venus.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero non fuerint in hoc loco, vide qui horoscopum ex ipsis cardinali radiatione respiciat, et tunc ex hoc tractatu artem poteris explicare.
quotations.translation: if they are not in that place, observe whether they are in aspect to the ascendant or on an angle. From this you will be able to determine the type of skill.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: οὗτοι γὰρ ἐὰν ἐναντίοι γένωνται, τοὺς κλιμακτῆρας καὶ τοὺς θανάτους σημαίνουσιν.
quotations.translation: For these (sc. the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant), when they are in opposition, signify (medical) crises (klimakteres) and death.
quotations.publication: (GH L 61,X)

quotations.original: οὗτοι γὰρ ἐὰν ἐναντίοι γένωνται, τοὺς κλιμακτῆρας καὶ τοὺς θανάτους σημαίνουσιν.
quotations.translation: For these (sc. the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant), when they are in opposition, signify (medical) crises (klimakteres) and death.
quotations.publication: (GH L 61,X)

quotations.original: ζητήσαντες καθὼς προεκτεθείμεθα εὕρομεν τὴν ἐναντίωσιν Ἄρεως καὶ Ἀφροδίτης χρηματίζουσαν οὕτως κατὰ τὸ ζʹ κλίμα καὶ τὴν τετράγωνον πλευρὰν Κρόνου
quotations.translation: By searching in the manner in which we have set out, we found the opposition of Mars and Venus thus active according to the 7th clime, and the square side (i.e., quadrangle) of Saturn

quotations.original: ζητήσαντες καθὼς προεκτεθείμεθα εὕρομεν τὴν ἐναντίωσιν Ἄρεως καὶ Ἀφροδίτης χρηματίζουσαν οὕτως κατὰ τὸ ζʹ κλίμα καὶ τὴν τετράγωνον πλευρὰν Κρόνου
quotations.translation: By searching in the manner in which we have set out, we found the opposition of Mars and Venus thus operative according to the 7th clime, and the square side (i.e., quadrangle) of Saturn

quotations.original: καὶ ἑξάγωνος Σελήνης στάσις πρὸς Ἀφροδίτην <ἐπιβουλὴν> ἐδήλου διὰ θηλυκῶν προσώπων κατὰ τὰ λγ ἔτη
quotations.translation: And the position of the Moon in sextile aspect with Venus indicated <treachery> through female persons at 33 years
quotations.publication: (GH L 120,XII)

quotations.original: ἐχρημάτισε γὰρ ἡ ἀναφορὰ τοῦ Ταύρου κγʹ καὶ Ἄρεως περίοδος ιεʹ· γίνονται ληʹ· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἑξάγωνος πλευρὰ Κρόνου καὶ Ἀφροδίτης ληʹ.
quotations.translation: For the rising(-time) of Taurus was active, 23 (years), and the period of Mars, 15, total 38, but also the hexagonal side of Saturn and of Venus  (i.e., one side of a hexagon along the zodiacal circle that coincides with their positions), (total) 38.
quotations.publication: (GH L 117,VI)

quotations.original:
(21′) a-ru-u₂ ne₂-me-qi₂ ᵈdiš-u₂-tu₂ ad.ḫal dingir.[meš gal.meš]
(22') mi₂.uru₃ um-man-nu zu-u₂ ana lu₂ [zu-u₂]
(23′) li-kal-lim la lu₂.zu-u₂ nu [igi-mar nig₂.gig]
(24′) ᵈa-nim ᵈen-lil₂ u₃ [ᵈe-a dingir.meš gal.meš]
quotations.translation: (21') Computation, wisdom of Anûtu, secret of the [great] gods, (22') guarded knowledge of the scholar. One who knows (23')may reveal it to one who knows, one who does not know may not see it, it is a taboo of (24') Anu, Enlil, [Ea, and the great gods]
quotations.publication: Neugebauer, Otto, 1955, Astronomical Cuneiform Texts

quotations.original: Quicquid enim Myriogenesis de singulis minutis pronuntiat, hoc nos de singulis faciemus partibus.
quotations.translation: For whatever the Myriogenesis says about the single minutes, we shall say about individual degrees.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Illud etiam addemus, quae partes in quibus signorum corporibus requirantur, quid etiam nonagesima pars operetur quae a Grraecis enenecontameris dicitur
quotations.translation: We shall also explain the measurement of the degrees and add which degrees are to be seen in the bodies of the signs; also what the 90th degree signifies, the one which the Greeks call enenecontameris.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Illud etiam addemus, quae partes in quibus signorum corporibus requirantur, quid etiam nonagesima pars operetur quae a Grraecis enenecontameris dicitur
quotations.translation: We shall also explain the measurement of the degrees and add which degrees are to be seen in the bodies of the signs; also what the 90th degree signifies, the one which the Greeks call enenecontameris.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Omnia enim pro naturae suae potestate perficiunt, si nonagesimam partem aut malivolae stellae minaci radiatione respexerint, aut benivolae prospero testimonio sublevarint.
quotations.translation: They indicate all according to the power of their own nature, either if malefics aspect the 90th degree unfavorably or if benefics aspect it favorably.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nunc quae stellae <se> videant, quae audiant explicabo. Aries Leonem non videt sed audit eum. Leo videt Arietem sed eum non audit.
quotations.translation: Now I will explain which stars see each other and which ones hear each other. Aries does not see Leo but hears him. Leo sees Aries but does not hear him.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Nunc quae stellae <se> videant, quae audiant explicabo. Aries Leonem non videt sed audit eum. Leo videt Arietem sed eum non audit.
quotations.translation: Now I will explain which stars see each other and which ones hear each other. Aries does not see Leo but hears him. Leo sees Aries but does not hear him.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed tres posteriores partes Piscium quae inter Arietem sunt et Pisces, obscura caligo semper innubilat.
quotations.translation: But the three last degrees of Pisces which are between Aries and Pisces are always obscured by fog.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Sed tres posteriores partes Piscium quae inter Arietem sunt et Pisces, obscura caligo semper innubilat.
quotations.translation: But the three last degrees of Pisces which are between Aries and Pisces are always obscured by a nebula.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In horum signorum lateribus aliae adhaerent stellae, sed quae numquam erratico cursu assignata sibimet deserant loca, sed tradita sibi spatia possidentes, currente mundo inmutabili semper agitatione volvuntur.
quotations.translation: To the sides of these signs cling other stars. But they never desert their own path in an erratic course but hold space assigned to them and turn always with the immutable revolution of the universe.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In horum signorum lateribus aliae adhaerent stellae, sed quae numquam erratico cursu assignata sibimet deserant loca, sed tradita sibi spatia possidentes, currente mundo inmutabili semper agitatione volvuntur.

quotations.original: Hae in vicinis signorum regionibus collocatae, cum XII signis oriuntur et cum ipsis occidunt rursus, inmutatum semper cursus sui ordinem reservantes.
quotations.translation: These are located in the neighboring regions of the signs, rise with the twelve and set with them, keeping always an unchanging course.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: <In Arietis dextro latere in Arietis parte scilicet IV.> oritur Navis.
quotations.translation: On the right side of Aries or in the 4th degree of Aries rises the Ship.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Arietis sinistro latere oritur Orion, in parte Arietis scilicet X.
quotations.translation: On the left side of Aries rises Orion, at ca. 10° Aries.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Arietis parte XV. ad Aquilonem versus exoritur Auriga.
quotations.translation: At 15° Aries turned to the north rises the Charioteer.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Arietis parte XX. ad Aquilonem versus oritur Haedus quem fert Auriga.
quotations.translation: At 20° Aries turned to the north rises the Young Goat whom the Charioteer drives.

quotations.original: In Arietis parte XXVII. oriuntur Hyades.

quotations.original: In Arietis parte XXX., quae pars totum signum supra terram semper ostendit, exoritur Capra, quam fabulosi poetae alimenta volunt Iovi inmulsisse nutricia.
quotations.translation: At the 30th degree of Aries which always holds the whole sign above the earth rises the She-goat. The poets said she was the fabled nurse of Jupiter.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Hoc astro [= Auriga] Oriente et Salmoneus et Bellorofontes nati esse narrantur.
quotations.translation: It is told that both Salmoneus and Bellerophon were born as this constellation was rising.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Occidentibus Pliadibus id est VI. parte Tauri si a malivolis haec pars radiata fuerit, hi qui nati fuerint naufragio peribunt.
quotations.translation: When the Pleiades i.e. 4° Taurus set and this degree is aspected by malefics, those who are born will die by shipwreck.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Geminorum parte VII. oritur Lepus.

quotations.original: Ὑποκείται γὰρ πρὸς ὅλην τὴν ἀστρολογίαν ἥλιόν τε καὶ σελήνην καὶ τοὺς εʹ πλανήτας ἰσοταχῶς καὶ ἐγκυκλίως καὶ ὑπεναντίως τῷ κόσμῳ κινεῖσθαι.
quotations.translation: For it is assumed regarding all of astronomy, that the sun and the moon and the 5 planets move at constant speed and in a circle and in a manner contrary to the cosmos.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: ἦν μὲν γὰρ ἡ παράδοσις τοῦ ἔτους ἀπὸ Κρόνου καὶ Σελήνης ἐπὶ Ἄρεα καὶ τὸν αἰτιατικὸν τόπον, καὶ ἀπὸ Διὸς καὶ [ἀπὸ] Ἡλίου ὄντων ἐν τῷ περὶ ἐξουσίας τόπῳ ἐπὶ Κρόνον καὶ Σελήνην ὄντας <ἐν> τῷ μεσουρανήματι καὶ πρακτικῷ τόπῳ
quotations.translation: The transfer of the year was from Saturn and Moon to Mars and the causal place, and from Jupiter and Sun, being in the place concerning property, to Saturn and Moon, being in Midheaven and the place of activity.

quotations.original: 1 2/3 MA.NA MIN 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN | TA 2 MUL.MEŠ ša₂ SAG.DU mul.UR.GU.LA EN MUL 4 ša₂ GABA-šu₂
quotations.translation: 1 2/3 minas ditto (weight), 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 18 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), | from the 2 stars of the head of the Lion to the 4 stars of its (the Lion's) breast.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: 1 2/3 MA.NA MIN 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN | TA 2 MUL.MEŠ ša₂ SAG.DU mul.UR.GU.LA EN MUL 4 ša₂ GABA-šu₂
quotations.translation: 1 2/3 minas ditto (weight), 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 18 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), | from the 2 stars of the head of the Lion to the 4 stars of its (the Lion's) breast.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.original: In parte XII. Geminorum quicumque habuerit horoscopum, Marte praesente, punctu teli morietur [...]
quotations.translation: He who has the ascendant at 12° Gemini with Mars present will die by the tip of a spear [...]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Inter oculos Cancri quicumque habuerint horoscopum, orbi vel unoculi erunt.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant between the eyes of Cancer will be bereft and/or one-eyed.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In parte VIII. Virginis quicumque habuerint horoscopum, id est in ipsa Spica, erunt religiosi iusti
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant at 8° Virgo, i.e. exactly on Spica, will be religious and just
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Haec pars inter oculos Cancri est. In IV. parte nebula est de qua frequentissime diximus.
quotations.translation: This is between the eyes of the Crab. At 4° Cancer is the nebula which we have very often spoken about.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quodsi Mars in ipsa parte fuerit, vel in occasu partis, mulieris causa publica morte plectentur.
quotations.translation: If Mars is in this degree or in the degree opposite, the native will be executed publicly because of a woman.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In parte XX. Librae quicumque habuerint horoscopum, in septentrionali scilicet parte, erunt medici famosa artis nobilitate perspicui.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant at 20° Libra, i. e. in the northern degree, will be a famous medic, famous for the excellence of their skill.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Boote quicumque habuerint horoscopum, erunt divini astrologi artis Chaldaicae periti.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in Bootes will be godly astrologers, skilled in the Chaldean art.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Qui in tertio pede habuerint horoscopum, erunt hortulani.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the third leg [of Scorpio] will be a gardener.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In parte XVI. Scorpionis quicumque habuerint horoscopum, erunt pistores.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant at 16° Scorpio will be a baker.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Qui in quarto pede habuerint horoscopum, erunt cinaedi, mulieres vero prostituto pudore meretrices.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the fourth leg [of Scorpio] will be homosexual, women however will be prostitutes.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Vulpe qui nati fuerint, erunt callidi fraudulenti circumscriptores cordatissimi
quotations.translation: Whoever is born in the Fox will be clever, fraudulent, deceptive and most wise
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Cynocefalo qui nati fuerint, erunt frenetici valitudinarii sine filiis oligochronii.
quotations.translation: The ones who are born in the Dog-headed one will be frantic, sickly, without children and short-lived.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si vero in extrema linea Sagittarii, id est super caudam, fuerit <inventus> horoscopus, figuli nascentur;
quotations.translation: If the ascendant is located in the last line of Sagittarius, i. e. above the tail, potters will be born
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In dextra parte Sagittarii oritur navis Argo, in sinistra Canis.
quotations.translation: In the right part of Sagittarius rises the ship Argo, in the left part the Dog.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In dextra parte Sagittarii oritur navis Argo, in sinistra Canis.
quotations.translation: In the right part of Sagittarius rises the ship Argo, in the left part the Dog.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Falce quicumque habuerit horoscopum, erit arator qui campos colens multas frumentorum copias colligat.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the Sickle will be a farmer who works the fields and collects large amounts of grain.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In ore Lupi quicumque habuerit horoscopum, erit saltator
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the mouth of the Wolf will be a dancer.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In ipso Lupo quicumque habuerint horoscopum, erunt fraudulenti fures crudeles homicidae
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the Wolf itself will be fraudulent, a thief, cruel and a killer
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In capite Aquarii minoris quicumque habuerit horoscopum, per deserta loca iter faciens multum errabit
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the head of the Small Waterbearer will travel and wander around desert places a lot
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Quicumque itaque horoscopum in cornibus Cervi habuerit, si Mars in ipsa parte fuerit inventus, erit praepositus armorum
quotations.translation: Therefore, whoever has the ascendant in the horns of the Stag, if Mars is located on this very degree, will be an army commander
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In ore Cervi quicumque habuerint horoscopum, erunt [...] biothanati.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the mouth of the Stag will die a violent death.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In pedibus Cervi quicumque habuerint horoscopum, errantes plurimum biothanata morte morientur.
quotations.translation: Those who have the ascendant in the feet of the stag will wander a lot and die a violent death.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In cauda Ceti quicumque habuerint horoscopum, si Mars in ipsa parte fuerit inventus, a bestiis lacerati morientur.
quotations.translation: Whoever has the ascendant in the tail of the Sea-Monster, if Mars is found on this degree, will be torn apart by wild beasts.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In Leonis parte II. stella limpida invenitur.
quotations.translation: A bright star is found at 2° Leo.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Cum enim ignitis sideribus aliorum siderum fuerit frigus oppositum, et frigoris glacies igniti ardoris fuerit flagrantia temperata, mixtura etiam temperationis efficitur.
quotations.translation: For when the coldness of other stars is opposite fiery stars, and the burning of the fire is lessened by the ice of the coldness, this leads to a mixture of temperatures.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Cum enim ignitis sideribus aliorum siderum fuerit frigus oppositum, et frigoris glacies igniti ardoris fuerit flagrantia temperata, mixtura etiam temperationis efficitur.
quotations.translation: For when the coldness of other stars is opposite fiery stars, and the burning of the fire is lessened by the ice of the coldness, this leads to a mixture of temperaments.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Arietis I. et II. partes in cornibus sunt constitutae
quotations.translation: The degrees 1°–2° consist of the horns [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: III. vero et IV. et V. in capite
quotations.translation: [The degrees] 3 and 4 and 5 consist of the head [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: VI. vero et VII. in facie
quotations.translation: [degrees] 6 and 7 are in the face [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: VIII. vero et IX. et X. in ore
quotations.translation: [degrees] 8 and 9 and 10 are in the mouth [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: 1 2/3 MA.NA MIN 10 UŠ i-na KI.MIN 18 lim DANNA ina KI.MIN | TA MUL 2 ša₂ GIŠ.KUN-šu₂ EN MUL DILI ša₂ KUN-šu₂
quotations.translation: 1 2/3 minas ditto (weight), 10 UŠ on ditto (the ground), 18 thousand bēru in ditto (heaven), |  from the 2 stars of its rump to the single star of its tail.
quotations.publication: Thureau-Dangin 1913, 'Distances entres étoiles fixes d'après une tablette de l'époque Séleucides', RA 10, 215-225

quotations.translation:
Athenian: O good men, we Greeks almost all speak falsely now of the great gods, the Sun as well as the Moon.

Kleinias: What kind of lie is it then?

Athenian: We say that they never go the same way, but also certain stars together with them, naming them "the wandering ones".
quotations.publication: Plato. 1903. Plato. Platonis Opera, ed. J. Burnet. Oxford University Press.

quotations.original: XI. vero et XII. in pectore
quotations.translation: 11–12° [of Aries] are in the chest
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: GE₆ 14 27 GE₆ GIN AN.MI sin BAR DIB
quotations.translation: Night of the 14th, 7° after sunset, lunar eclipse, „extraneous“, will be omitted.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. 2014. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. VII: Almanacs and Normal Star Almanacs. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.
quotations.comment: "F. Rochberg14 translates BAR = aḫû by „invisible“ because „this is the effective meaning“, quoting Steele approvingly. I agree with this argument but nevertheless use the literal translation „extraneous“ in this edition." (Hunger 2014: XV).

quotations.original: XIII. et XIV. et XV. in omni cervice
quotations.translation: the degrees 13, 14, and 15 are in the whole neck [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XVI. et XVII. in corde,
quotations.translation: [the degrees] 16 and 17 are in the heart [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XVIII. et XIX. in armo dextro
quotations.translation: [degrees] 18 and 19 are in the right shoulder [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XX. et XXI. et XXII. in anno sinistro
quotations.translation: [degrees] 20, 21, and 22 are in the left shoulder [of Aries]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in ventre vero ΧΧΠΙ. et XXIV. et XXV.
quotations.translation: in the belly [of Aries] are [the degrees] 23, 24, and 25
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: novissimi autem pedes XXVI. et XXVII. habent partem,
quotations.translation: the newest feet [of the Ram] have the 26th and 27th degree
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in cauda (habet) XXX. partem
quotations.translation: [Aries] has the 30th degree in its tail
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: I. et II. partes in Tauri cornibus sunt constitutae
quotations.translation: the 1st and 2nd degree of Taurus are located in its horns
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: VI. et VII. in cervice
quotations.translation: [the degrees] 6° and 7° are in the neck [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: III. vero et IV. et V. in omni facie
quotations.translation: the 3rd, 4th and 5th degrees are in the face [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: VIII. et IX. et X. in fronte
quotations.translation: the 8th, 9th and 10th are in the forehead [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XI. et XII. in corde
quotations.translation: the 11th and 12th [degree] are in the heart [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XIII. vero et XIV. et XV. in humeris
quotations.translation: the 13th, 14th and 15th degree however is in the shoulders [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: εὑρέθη γὰρ ὁ περιποιητικὸς τόπος Ἰχθύσιν, Διὸς ἰδιοτοποῦντος, ἡ δὲ τοῦ τριγώνου ἐπίκοινος Ἀφροδίτη καὶ τοῦ κλήρου καὶ τοῦ ὑψώματος κυρία μοιρικῶς ὡροσκοποῦσα.
quotations.translation: For the place of security was found in Pisces, with Jupiter in its own place (i.e., house), and Venus, the co-(ruler) of the triangle and ruler of the lot and exaltation, in the Ascendant in terms of degree.
quotations.publication: (GH L 65,X)

quotations.original: εὑρέθη γὰρ ὁ περιποιητικὸς τόπος Ἰχθύσιν, Διὸς ἰδιοτοποῦντος, ἡ δὲ τοῦ τριγώνου ἐπίκοινος Ἀφροδίτη καὶ τοῦ κλήρου καὶ τοῦ ὑψώματος κυρία μοιρικῶς ὡροσκοποῦσα.
quotations.translation: For the place of accomplishment was found in Pisces, with Jupiter in its own place (i.e., house), and Venus, the co-(ruler) of the triangle and ruler of the lot and exaltation, in the Ascendant in terms of degree.
quotations.publication: (GH L 65,X)

quotations.original: οὗτος ἡγεμονικὸς ὑπάρχων, ἡγεμονικῇ ἔχθρᾳ περιπεσὼν τῷ λδʹ ἔτει κατεδικάσθη εἰς μέταλλον· Ἄρης γὰρ σὺν Ἡλίῳ ἐπικρατεῖ τοῦ χρόνου.
quotations.translation: This person, being an associate of a prefect, fell under the prefect’s anger and was condemned in the 34th year to the mines: for Mars along with the Sun rules over the time-period.
quotations.publication: (GH L 102,XII,14)

quotations.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ πλείοσι τὴν συναφὴν ἐπεποίητο ἤτοι κατὰ κόλλησιν ἢ καὶ ἐπιμαρτύρησιν, καὶ πλείονας ἂν ἀδελφοὺς εἶχεν
quotations.translation: If (the Moon) had made contact with more (planets), that is, in terms of attachment (conjunction) or also aspect, he would also have had more brothers.

quotations.original: If (the Moon) had made contact with more (planets), that is, in terms of attachment or also aspect, he would also have had more brothers.
quotations.translation: εἰ δὲ καὶ πλείοσι τὴν συναφὴν ἐπεποίητο ἤτοι κατὰ κόλλησιν ἢ καὶ ἐπιμαρτύρησιν, καὶ πλείονας ἂν ἀδελφοὺς εἶχεν

quotations.original: ἔστω τὸν Λέοντα ἀναφέρεσθαι ἐν λϛ, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ <τὸν> Σκορπίον, τὸν δὲ Ταῦρον καὶ τὸν Ὑδροχόον ἐν κδ. λοιπὰ ιβ, ὧν τὸ γʹ δ· αὕτη προσθαφαίρεσις. οὕτως καὶ καθ’ ἕκαστον κλίμα ζητῶν ἐπιγνώσῃ.
quotations.translation: Let Leo rise in 36, and likewise Scorpio, and Taurus and Aquarius in 24. Remainder 12, of which the 3rd is 4: this is the difference (lit., addition-subtraction). In this way, searching according to every clima, you will recognize (it).
quotations.publication: (GH L 134,VI)

quotations.original: προσθαφαίρεσις 𐆊 ϛʹ μ̣[
quotations.translation: Difference (lit. addition-subtraction) 0;6;4[.];[?]

quotations.original: DIŠ ina iti.AB U4 15 KAM mul.SIM.MAḪ mul.ši-nu-nu-tu4 mul.IM.ŠEŠ | ina GIŠ.NIM IGI.LA2
quotations.translation: ¶ On the 15th day of Month X SIM.MAḪ, (i.e.) the Swallow (or) IM.ŠEŠ, | becomes visible in the east.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: DIŠ ina iti.AB U4 15 KAM mul.SIM.MAḪ mul.ši-nu-nu-tu4 mul.IM.ŠEŠ | ina GIŠ.NIM IGI.LA2
quotations.translation: ¶ On the 15th day of Month X SIM.MAḪ, (i.e.) the Swallow (or) IM.ŠEŠ, | becomes visible in the east.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: DIŠ mul.GABA GIR2.TAB u mul.UZ3 KUR.MEŠ-ma mul.ŠU.GI u mul.SIPA.ZI.AN.NA ŠU2.MEŠ
quotations.translation: ¶ The Breast of the Scorpion and the Goat rise, and the Old Man and the True Shepherd of Anu set.
quotations.publication: Hunger, H. and Steele, J., 2019. The Babylonian Astronomical Compendium MUL.APIN. London and New York: Routledge.

quotations.original: XVI. et XVII. in anterioribus pedibus Tauri ordinantur
quotations.translation: [degrees] 16 and 17 are appointed to the fore-feet of the Bull
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XVIII. vero et XIX. et XX. in ventre sunt
quotations.translation: [degrees] 18 and 19 and 20 however are in the belly [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XXI. in geniculis
quotations.translation: [the degree] 21 is in the knees [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XXII. et XXIII. et XXIV. et XXV. in posterioribus pedibus collocantur
quotations.translation: [degrees] 22 and 23 and 24 and 25 are located in the hind feet [of Taurus]
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: XXVI. vero et XXVII. in natura sunt Tauri
quotations.translation: [the degrees] 26 and 27 however are in the genitals of the Bull
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: In coxis vero XXVIII. et XXIX.
quotations.translation: In the hips [of Taurus] however are [the degrees] 28 and 29
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: in cauda vero sola pars XXX. reperitur.

quotations.original:
(0')  [ALLA A 36]
(1')  [ABSIN RI]N₂ ⸢4⸣2
(2')  GIR₂ PA 48

quotations.translation:
(0’) [Cnc, Leo (0);36.] 
(1’) [Vir, Lib] (0);42.
(2’) Sco, Sgr (0);48.
(3’) Cap, Aqr (0);54.
(4’) Psc, Ari (0);48.
(5’) Tau, Gem (0);42.
(6’) 3 "knots" 
(7’) of the displacement of Mars.

quotations.original:
16') ZI GAL-u₂ ana IGI-ka mim-ma ša₂ e ki-ṣir u mim-ma KI.TA k[i-ṣir ana UGU a-ḫa-miš₂]
(17') GAR.GAR-ma ½-šu₂-nu GIŠ.A taš-pil-tu₄ ana UGU TAB ZI GAL tam-ma[r ZI TUR ana IGI-ka]
(18')  mim-ma ša₂ e ki-ṣir u SIG ki-ṣir ana UGU a-ḫa-miš₂ GAR.GAR-ma ½-[šu₂-nu GIŠ.A taš-pil-tu₄]
(19') TA lib₃-bi E₁₁-ma ZI TUR
quotations.translation:
(16’) In order for you to see the largest displacement: whatever is above the ‘knot’ and whatever is below the ‘kn[ot’] you accumulate [together] (17’) and you compute half of it, you add the difference to (it), you see the largest displacement.
[In order for you to see the smallest displacement:] (18’) whatever is above the ‘knot’ and below the ‘knot’ you accumulate together and [you compute] half [of it], you subtract [the difference] (19’) from it, it is the smallest displacement.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer.

quotations.translation: Night of (day) 14, GE₆ (= sunset to moonrise) was [x]+1 (UŠ), measured (despite) clouds; beginning of the night, Sin was 1/2 cubit in front of Lisi (= α Sco), it was balanced to its lower horn.

quotations.original: In Arietis parte XX. ad Aquilonem versus oritur Haedus quem fert Auriga. Hoc sidere <oriente> quicumque nati fuerint, aliud ex fronte pollicentur, aliud latenter in moribus celant.
quotations.translation: Haedus rises at 20° Aries turned toward the north. He is the one Auriga carries. Those who are born with this star rising promise one thing from the front but hide another in their thoughts.
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Inspice etiam hoc ipsum signum, utrum benivolae stellae sit an malivolae, et quatenus dominus ipsius signi in genitura sit collocatus, vel in quo signo vel in quibus finibus, et <an> in primis an in secundis cardinibus adsistat,
quotations.translation: Also look at that sign itself, whether it houses a benefic or a malefic and how the ruler of this sign is located in the chart—in which sign and which terms—and whether he stands in cardinal or favorable place
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Inspice etiam hoc ipsum signum, utrum benivolae stellae sit an malivolae, et quatenus dominus ipsius signi in genitura sit collocatus, vel in quo signo vel in quibus finibus, et <an> in primis an in secundis cardinibus adsistat,
quotations.translation: Also look at that sign itself, whether it houses a benefic or a malefic and how the ruler of this sign is located in the chart—in which sign and which terms—and whether he stands in cardinal or favorable place
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Si enim aut in ipso signo Sol fuerit, aut in altitudine sua aut in principalibus cardinibus <aut> in V. aut in XI. ab horoscope loco, patrem ostendit affluentibus divitiis copiosum
quotations.translation: For if the sun is in that sign itself or in its exaltation or on a cardinal point or in the 5th or 11th place from the ascendant, it shows the father [of the native] to be very rich
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: si una malivola in conceptionali Sole fuerit inventa, is qui natus fuerit exponetur.
