quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec norunt obitus unoque in vertice mutant
in diversa situm caelumque et sidera torquent
quotations.translation: and [the Bears] know no setting and, shifting their opposed stations about the same high point, set sky and stars in rotation
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec norunt obitus unoque in vertice mutant
in diversa situm caelumque et sidera torquent
quotations.translation: and [the Bears] know no setting and, shifting their opposed stations about the same high point, set sky and stars in rotation
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aera per gelidum tenuis deducitur axis
libratumque regit diverso cardine mundum;
quotations.translation: from there an insubstantial axis runs down through the wintry air and controls the universe, keeping it pivoted at opposite poles
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aera per gelidum tenuis deducitur axis
libratumque regit diverso cardine mundum;
quotations.translation: from there an insubstantial axis runs down through the wintry air and controls the universe, keeping it pivoted at opposite poles
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aera per gelidum tenuis deducitur axis
libratumque regit diverso cardine mundum;
quotations.translation: from there an insubstantial axis runs down through the wintry air and controls the universe, keeping it pivoted at opposite poles
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sidereus circa medium quem volvitur orbis
aetheriosque rotat cursus
quotations.translation: it forms the middle about which the starry sphere revolves and wheels its heavenly flight
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
usque adeo tenue ut verti non possit in ipsum
nec iam inclinari nec se convertere in orbem
quotations.translation: [the axis is] so insubstantial that it cannot turn round upon itself or even submit to motion or spin in circular fashion
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
maioremque Helice maior decircinat arcum
(septem illam stellae certantes lumine signant)
quotations.translation: Helice, the greater, describes the greater arc; it is marked by seven stars which vie with each other in radiance
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
angusto Cynosura brevis torquetur in orbe,
quam spatio tam luce minor sed iudice vincit
maiorem Tyrio.
quotations.translation: Cynosura is small and wheels round in a narrow circle, less in brightness as it is in size, but in the judgement of the Tyrians it excels the larger bear.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
utraque caudam
vergit in alterius rostro sequiturque sequentem.
quotations.translation: each [bear] with its muzzle points at the other’s tail and follows one that follows it.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
utraque caudam
vergit in alterius rostro sequiturque sequentem.
quotations.translation: each [bear] with its muzzle points at the other’s tail and follows one that follows it.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Hunc inter mediumque orbem, quo sidera septem
per bis sena volant contra nitentia signa
quotations.translation: Between this northern and the middle zone, wherein the seven planets fly through the twelve signs that resist their passage
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: mixta ex diversis consurgunt viribus astra
quotations.translation: there rise constellations which have part in opposite qualities [or influences]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: nixa venit species genibus, sibi conscia causae.
quotations.translation: Next [to the chill Bears and the frozen north] comes a figure on bended knee, the reason for whose posture is known to none but him.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: a tergo nitet Arctophylax idemque Bootes
quotations.translation: In his rear shines the Bearward, called also Bootes
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Memoriae proditum est, quo die Urbem divus Augustus Apollonia reversus intravit, circa solem visum coloris varii circulum, qualis esse in arcu solet. Hunc Graeci halo vocant, nos dicere coronam aptissime possumus.
quotations.translation: It is recorded in history that the day the deified Augustus entered Rome on his return from Apollonia a circle of varied colours was seen around the sun, colours that usually appear in a rainbow. The Greeks call it a “halo.” We can call it, very appropriately, a “corona.”
quotations.publication: Seneca. Natural Questions, Volume I: Books 1-3. Translated by Thomas H. Corcoran. Loeb Classical Library 450. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1971.

quotations.original:
serpentem magnis Ophiuchus nomine gyris
dividit et torto cingentem corpore corpus
explicet ut nodos sinuataque terga per orbes.
quotations.translation: One called Ophiuchus holds apart the serpent which with its mighty spirals and twisted body encircles his own, that so he may untie its knots and back that winds in loops.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: nunc quoque diductas volitat stellatus in alas.
quotations.translation: Now too with outspread wings it flies among the stars.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hinc imitata nitent cursumque habitumque sagittae
sidera.
quotations.translation: Next shines a constellation which resembles the appearance and flight of an arrow.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: tum magni Iovis ales fertur in altum
quotations.translation: Then soars to the heights the bird of mighty Jupiter
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
succedit iniquo
divisis spatio, quod terna lampade crispans
conspicitur, paribus Deltoton nomine sidus
ex simili dictum
quotations.translation: There follows, with two equal sides parted by one unequal, a sign seen flashing with three stars and named Deltoton, called after its likeness.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
succedit iniquo
divisis spatio, quod terna lampade crispans
conspicitur, paribus Deltoton nomine sidus
ex simili dictum
quotations.translation: There follows, with two equal sides parted by one unequal, a sign seen flashing with three stars and named Deltoton, called after its likeness.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Andromedan, vastos metuentem Pristis hiatus
quotations.translation: Andromeda [...], who would shrink before the enormous gaping jaws of the Sea-monster
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ni veterem Perseus caelo quoque servet amorem
quotations.translation: did not Perseus even in heaven maintain his former love and come with timely aid
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tum vicina ferens nixo vestigia Tauro
Heniochus, studio mundumque et nomen adeptus
quotations.translation: Next, bearing his footsteps near the crouching Bull comes the Charioteer whose calling won him heaven and a name
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hunc subeunt Haedi claudentes sidere pontum,
nobilis et mundi nutrito rege Capella,
quotations.translation: Him follow the Kids e that with their constellation close the seas, and the goat famed for having suckled the king of heaven;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hunc subeunt Haedi claudentes sidere pontum,
nobilis et mundi nutrito rege Capella,
quotations.translation: Him follow the Kids e that with their constellation close the seas, and the goat famed for having suckled the king of heaven;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Aspice nunc infra solis surgentia cursus
quae super exustas labuntur sidera terras;
quotations.translation: Look now at the constellations which rise to the south of the Sun’s path and glide above torrid lands
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: nec numerosa minus nascuntur sidera in orbem.
quotations.translation: and no fewer are the stars which rise upon their world.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: hoc duce per totum decurrunt sidera mundum.
quotations.translation: [It is Orion who] leads the constellations as they speed over the full circuit of heaven.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: subsequitur rapido contenta Canicula cursu
quotations.translation: At his heels follows the Dog outstretched in full career:
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tum Notius Piscis venti de nomine dictus
exsurgit de parte Noti.
quotations.translation: Then rises the Southern Fish in the quarter of the wind after which it is named.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
cui iuncta feruntur
flexa per ingentis stellarum Flumina gyros:
alterius capiti coniungit Aquarius undas,
alter ab exserto pede profluit Orionis amnis;
et in medium coeunt et sidera miscent.
quotations.translation: To it are joined the Rivers which make their winding way along great curves of stars: Aquarius connects his waters with the upper reaches of the one stream, whilst the other flows from Orion’s out-thrust foot; they meet each other and blend their stars together.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quae notia antiqui dixerunt sidera vates.
quotations.translation: these stars the ancient poets have called southern.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
magna fides hoc posse color cursusque micantis
ignis ad os.
quotations.translation: Sure proof that the star has this power are its colour and the quivering of the fire that sparkles in its face.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et Phoebo sacer ales et una gratus Iaccho
Crater et duplici Centaurus imagine fulget
quotations.translation: Then shines the bird that is sacred to Phoebus [i. e. the Raven] and with it the Bowl beloved of Bacchus and the Centaur of twofold form;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et Phoebo sacer ales et una gratus Iaccho
Crater et duplici Centaurus imagine fulget
quotations.translation: Then shines the bird that is sacred to Phoebus and with it the Bowl beloved of Bacchus and the Centaur of twofold form
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aversas frontibus Arctos
uno distingui medias claudique Dracone
credimus exemplo
quotations.translation: We assume by analogy that Bears with faces averted from each other are separated and encircled by a single Dragon
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tu modo corporeis similis ne quaere figuras,
omnia ut aequali fulgentia membra colore
deficiat nihil aut vacuum qua lumine cesset.
quotations.translation: Only look not for shapes like bodily shapes or think to see all the members shining with equal brilliance with nothing missing or anywhere left devoid of light.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: medio cum luna implebitur orbe
quotations.translation: When in mid-course the Moon is full
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
certa nitent mundo tum lumina: conditur omne
stellarum vulgus;
quotations.translation: then most of all do the princely luminaries shine conspicuous in the heavens; the whole stellar populace fades from sight
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Arctos et Orion adversis frontibus ibant,
haec contenta suos in vertice flectere gyros,
quotations.translation: the Bear and Orion moved with fronts opposed, she content to describe her gyrations at the pole,
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec lunam certos excedere luminis orbes
sed servare modum, quo crescat quove recedat,
quotations.translation: that the Moon does not exceed her appointed orbs of light, but preserves the regularity of her waxing and waning;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: omnia concordi tractu veniuntque caduntque
quotations.translation: They all move on a consistent course, coming into view and setting
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sunt alia adverso pugnantia sidera mundo,
quae terram caelumque inter volitantia pendent
quotations.translation: There exist other stars, which strive against the contrary movement of the sky and in their swift orbits are poised between heaven and earth:
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Saturni, Iovis et Martis Solisque, sub illis
Mercurius Venerem inter agit Lunamque volatus.
quotations.translation: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and the Sun, and beneath them Mercury performing its flight between Venus and the Moon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Ipse autem quantum convexo mundus Olympo
obtineat spatium et quantis bis sena ferantur
finibus astra
quotations.translation: How great is the space occupied by the vault of the heavens and how great the territory within which the twelve signs of the zodiac move
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
summum igitur caelum bis bina refugit ab imo
astra, bis e senis ut sit pars tertia signis.
quotations.translation: Therefore the highest point of heaven is twice two signs distant from the lowest, a distance, that is, of one third of the twelve signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed quia per medium est tellus suspensa profundum,
binis a summo signis discedit et imo.
quotations.translation: But since the Earth is suspended in the middle of space, it is two signs separated from the north pole and two from the south.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed quia per medium est tellus suspensa profundum,
binis a summo signis discedit et imo.
quotations.translation: But since the Earth is suspended in the middle of space, it is two signs separated from the north pole and two from the south.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sex tanta rotundae
efficiunt orbem zonae, qua signa feruntur
bis sex aequali spatio texentia caelum
quotations.translation: six of these lengths make up the circle of the round belt, where move the twelve signs which weave in equal lengths the pattern of heaven
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Restat ut aetherios fines tibi reddere coner
filaque dispositis vicibus comitantia caelum,
per quae derigitur signorum flammeus ordo.
quotations.translation: I have still to try to expound to you the regions of the sky and the lines marking heaven at fixed intervals through which are directed the fiery ranks of the constellations.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Restat ut aetherios fines tibi reddere coner
filaque dispositis vicibus comitantia caelum,
per quae derigitur signorum flammeus ordo.
quotations.translation: I have still to try to expound to you the regions of the sky and the lines marking heaven at fixed intervals through which are directed the fiery ranks of the constellations.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: circulus ad borean fulgentem sustinet Arcton
quotations.translation: upholds the Bear gleaming at the north
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
alter ad extremi decurrens sidera Cancri,
in quo consummat Phoebus lucemque moramque
tardaque per longos circumfert lumina flexus,
aestivum medio nomen sibi sumit ab aestu
quotations.translation: Below it a second, touching the Crab’s extreme sign, wherein Phoebus completes the lingering of his light and slowly swings his rays through long curves, adopts from the heat of midsummer the name of summer tropic,
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et quinque in partes aquilonis distat ab orbe.
quotations.translation: and [the tropic of Cancer] is five degrees distant from the northern circle
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quattuor et gradibus sua fila reducit ab aestu.
quotations.translation: this circle withdraws its track four degrees away from that of the summer solstice.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
proximus hunc ultra brumalis nomine limes
ultima designat fugientis limina solis
quotations.translation: Next after this a boundary named the winter tropic marks the furthest station of the retreating Sun
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ultima designat fugientis limina solis
quotations.translation: [the tropic of Capricorn] marks the furthest station of the retreating Sun
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed finibus illis,
quos super incubuit, longa stant tempora luce
quotations.translation: although in the lands over which he hangs time halts, light tarries long
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
unus ab his superest extremo proximus axi
circulus, austrinas qui stringit et obsidet Arctos.
quotations.translation: it is the nearest to the distant pole and confines and beleaguers the southern Bears
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
unus ab his superest extremo proximus axi
circulus, austrinas qui stringit et obsidet Arctos.
quotations.translation: it is the nearest to the distant pole and confines and beleaguers the southern Bears
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
alter ab excelso decurrens limes Olympo
Serpentis caudam siccas et dividit Arctos
quotations.translation: One line, descending from the summit of the sky, passes through the Dragon’s tail and the Bears that shun ocean
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et iuga Chelarum medio volitantia gyro
quotations.translation: and the yoke of the Balance which revolves in the midmost circle
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Lanigerique notat fines clarumque Trigonum
quotations.translation: it marks [...] the boundary of the Ram, the bright Triangle
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Lanigerique notat fines clarumque Trigonum
quotations.translation: it marks [...] the boundary of the Ram, the bright Triangle
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: principiumque suum repetito cardine claudit
quotations.translation: and, the pole regained, ends with its beginning
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: perque pedes primos cervicem transit et Ursae
quotations.translation: it passes through the forefeet and neck of that Bear
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et Geminis Cancrum dirimit stringitque flagrantem
ore Canem clavumque Ratis, quae vicerat aequor
quotations.translation: it parts the Crab from the Twins and grazes the Dog with the blazing face and the rudder of the Ship which conquered ocean
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
seu quis eoos
seu petit hesperios
quotations.translation: whether one moves towards east or west
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
seu quis eoos
seu petit hesperios
quotations.translation: whether one moves towards east or west
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: caelum et diviso signantem culmine mundum
quotations.translation: so as to part the sky in the middle and mark a bisection of heaven’s vault
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: illis sexta manet, quos tum premit aureus orbis
quotations.translation: is the sixth hour for those who dwell immediately beneath the golden orb
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: nunc septem ad stellas nec mota sub astra
quotations.translation: now to the [Bear’s] seven twinklers and the stars that never disappear from view
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: [atque a fine trahens titulum memoratur horizon]
quotations.translation: taking its name from the fact that it limits our sight, is called horizon
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
His adice obliquos adversaque fila trahentis
inter se gyros
quotations.translation: To these you must add two circles which lie athwart and trace lines that cross each other.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
His adice obliquos adversaque fila trahentis
inter se gyros
quotations.translation: To these you must add two circles which lie athwart and trace lines that cross each other.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quorum fulgentia signa
alter habet, per quae Phoebus moderatur habenas
subsequiturque suo solem vaga Delia curru
quotations.translation: One [= the zodiac] contains the shining signs through which the Sun plies his reins, followed by the wandering Moon in her chariot
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et quinque adverso luctantia sidera mundo
exercent varias naturae lege choreas.
quotations.translation: and wherein the five planets which struggle against the opposite movement of the sky perform the dances of their orbits that nature’s law diversifies.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aestivosque secat fines Aquilamque supinam
temporaque aequantem gyrum
quotations.translation: it [= the Milky Way] cuts the summer boundary, the supine Eagle, the circle of equal day and night
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
inde suos sinuat flexus per crura pedesque
Centauri alterius
quotations.translation: from there it [= the Milky Way] winds its tortuous trail through the legs and hoofs of the southern Centaur
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
perque ipsos fiat nexus manifesta cicatrix
suturam faciens mundi, stipatus et orbis
aeriam in nebulam densa compagine versus
in cuneos alti cogat fundamina caeli.
quotations.translation: out of the connection is formed a conspicuous scar marking a suture of the skies, and transformed by its dense structure into ethereal mist the compressed seam causes the foundations of high heaven to harden into a solid joint.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
e niveo lactis fluxisse liquorem
pectore reginae divum caelumque colore
infecisse suo; quapropter lacteus orbis
dicitur,
quotations.translation: from the snow-white breast of heaven’s queen there flowed a stream of milk which left its colour upon the skies; wherefore is it called the Milky Way
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc prius incipiam stellis quam reddere vires
signorumque canam fatalia carmine iura
[...]
quotations.translation: Now before I proceed to ascribe to the stars their powers and tell in my song of the fateful laws of the signs [...]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sicut Cyllenius orbis
et Venus, accenso cum ducit vespere noctem,
saepe latent falluntque oculos rursusque revisunt
quotations.translation: just so do the orb of Mercury and the planet Venus, when she kindles her evening lamp and brings on night, oft disappear and elude our gaze and oft visit us again.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Lanigerum victo ducentem sidera ponto
quotations.translation: and the Ram who leads the signs for his conquest of the sea
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: non esset statio terris, non ambitus astris
quotations.translation: the Earth would not possess its stability, nor stars their orbits
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quantumque reliquit
aut dedit ille, refers et sidus sidere constas
quotations.translation: and as much as he has grudged or lavished on you do you reflect, your star dependent on his
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quantumque reliquit
aut dedit ille, refers et sidus sidere constas
quotations.translation: and as much as he has grudged or lavished on you do you reflect, your star dependent on his
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
attollunt animos caelumque et sidera servant
corporaque ad lunae nascentis cornua lustrant
quotations.translation: they lift up their minds and watch the sky and stars: they cleanse their bodies on beholding the horns of the nascent Moon
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: aeternum et stellis adversus sidera bellum
quotations.translation: and the planets’ everlasting war against the signs [of the zodiac]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: aeternum et stellis adversus sidera bellum
quotations.translation: and the planets’ everlasting war against the signs [of the zodiac]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nam mascula sex sunt,
diversi totidem generis sub principe Tauro
quotations.translation: For six are masculine, whilst as many, led by the Bull, are of the opposite sex
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ἄδικος δὲ μὴ κατηγορούμενος διὰ τὴν τοῦ Ἄρεως καὶ Ἑρμοῦ στάσιν ἐπὶ τοῦ μεσουρανήματος, ἀμφοτέρων ὄντων ὑπαύγων
quotations.translation: (The native was) unjust (but) not accused on account of the position of Mars and Mercury in Midheaven, both of them being under the rays (sc. of the Sun, i.e., invisible)
quotations.publication: (GH L 40)

quotations.original: ἐν τῷ μβʹ ἔτει ἐκληρονόμησε θηλυκὸν πρόσωπον· ἦν γὰρ διὰ ϛʹ παράδοσις ἀπὸ Σελήνης καὶ Ἑρμοῦ ὄντων ἐν τῷ θανατικῷ τόπῳ, Κριῷ, εἰς τὴν Παρθένον, οἶκον Ἑρμοῦ, καὶ ἀπὸ ὑψωματικοῦ ζῳδίου εἰς ὑψωματικόν.
quotations.translation: In the 42nd year (the native) became the heir to a female person: for the transmission (of rule) by (an interval of) 6 was from Moon and Mercury, which were in the Place of Death, Aries, to Virgo, a house of Mercury, and from a zodiac sign of an exaltation to a (zodiac sign) of an exaltation.
quotations.publication: (GH L 111,IV)

quotations.original: GE₆ 23 [...] e MULₓ(AB₂) TUR ša₂ 3 1/2 KUŠ₃ ar₂ SUḪUR-ša₂-MAŠ₂ GUB LAL₂
quotations.translation: Night of the 23rd, [... Mars?] was balanced abovesic the small star which stands 3 1/2 cubits behind Capricorn.
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1988. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. I: Diaries from 652 B.C. to 262 B.C. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

quotations.translation: The one who foretells the coming forth (heliacal rising) of Sothis, who observes her in the day of her first feast, who establishes her striding in the times of touching ground (?) who observes  all her doings every day. All that she has foretold is in his command.

quotations.original:
nunc binis insiste; dabunt geminata potentis
per socium effectus.
quotations.translation: Now turn to the double signs; being doubled they will exert influences the power of which is tempered by a partner.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nunc binis insiste; dabunt geminata potentis
per socium effectus.
quotations.translation: Now turn to the double signs; being doubled they will exert influences the power of which is tempered by a partner.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quin etiam Erigone binis numeratur in astris,
nec facies ratio duplex;
quotations.translation: Erigone, too, is numbered among the double signs, but the duality in her appearance is not the reason;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
idcirco tropicis praecedunt omnibus astra
bina, ut Lanigero, Chelis Cancroque Caproque
quotations.translation: Double signs precede all the tropic ones, the Ram, the Claws, the Crab, and the Sea-goat
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: Just as one of the twin brothers followed by the Crab round the zodiac imparts blossoming springtime, so the other brings on thirsting summer;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quin etiam Arcitenens, qui te, Capricorne, sub ipso
promittit, duplici formatus imagine fertur
quotations.translation: The Archer, too, who gives promise of Capricorn behind himself, comes shaped with twofold appearance
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quin etiam Arcitenens, qui te, Capricorne, sub ipso
promittit, duplici formatus imagine fertur:
quotations.translation: The Archer, too, who gives promise of Capricorn behind himself, comes shaped with twofold appearance
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quosque Aries prae se mittit, duo tempora Pisces
bina dicant
quotations.translation: And the two Fishes that the Ram sends before himself denote two seasons:
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ne mirere moras, cum sol aversa per astra
aestivum tardis attollat mensibus annum.
quotations.translation: so wonder not at the delay when in tardy months the Sun carries summertide aloft through signs which rise hind-first.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nec te praetereat nocturna diurnaque signa
quae sint perspicere et propria deducere lege
quotations.translation: Fail not to perceive and from true rule deduce what signs are nocturnal, and what diurnal
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nec te praetereat nocturna diurnaque signa
quae sint perspicere et propria deducere lege
quotations.translation: Fail not to perceive and from true rule deduce what signs are nocturnal, and what diurnal
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, quae terrena censentur sidera sorte,
princeps armenti Taurus regnoque superbus
lanigeri gregis est Aries pestisque duorum
praedatorque Leo et dumosis Scorpios arvis.
quotations.translation: Some stars are reckoned of earthly lot: they are the Bull, the chieftain of the herd; the Ram proud of his lordship over the woolly flock; the predator and bane respectively of both, the Lion and the Scorpion that haunts the thicket of the field.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, quae terrena censentur sidera sorte,
princeps armenti Taurus regnoque superbus
lanigeri gregis est Aries pestisque duorum
praedatorque Leo et dumosis Scorpios arvis.
quotations.translation: Some stars are reckoned of earthly lot: they are the Bull, the chieftain of the herd; the Ram proud of his lordship over the woolly flock; the predator and bane respectively of both, the Lion and the Scorpion that haunts the thicket of the field.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sunt etiam mediae legis communia signa,
ambiguus tergo Capricornus, Aquarius undis,
umida terrenis aequali foedere mixta.
quotations.translation: Some signs there are betwixt and between, of a middle dispensation, since Capricorn’s nature is compromised by its tail, the Waterman’s by his stream: they are signs in which watery and earthly elements are mixed in an even compact.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
fecundum est proprie Cancri genus, acer et ictu
Scorpios, et partu complentes aequora Pisces.
sed sterilis Virgo est, simili coniuncta Leoni,
nec capit, aut captos effundit, Aquarius ortus.
quotations.translation: The Crab’s kind is especially fertile, and fertile too are the sharp-stinging Scorpion and the Fishes that fill the ocean with their spawn. Barren is the Virgin, as also her neighbour the Lion; and the Waterman fails to receive seed or, if he does so, spills it.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
inter utrumque manet Capricornus corpore mixto
et qui Cretaeo fulget Centaurus in arcu,
communisque Aries aequantem tempora Libram
et Geminos Taurumque pari sub sorte recenset.
quotations.translation: Between the two groups fall Capricorn of compound form and the Centaur who glitters with his Cretan bow; also intermediate is the Ram who counts of like estate the equinoctial Scales, the Twins, and the Bull.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
inter utrumque manet Capricornus corpore mixto
et qui Cretaeo fulget Centaurus in arcu,
communisque Aries aequantem tempora Libram
et Geminos Taurumque pari sub sorte recenset.
quotations.translation: Between the two groups fall Capricorn of compound form and the Centaur who glitters with his Cretan bow; also intermediate is the Ram who counts of like estate the equinoctial Scales, the Twins, and the Bull.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sunt currentia quaedam,
ut Leo et Arcitenens Ariesque in cornua tortus;
quotations.translation: certain signs are running, as are the Lion, the Archer, and the Ram that ends in twisted horns;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aut quae recta suis librantur stantia membris,
ut Virgo et Gemini, fundens et Aquarius undas
quotations.translation: or that some stand erect with their limbs perfectly poised, as the Virgin and Twins and Waterman pouring forth his stream;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
vel quae fessa sedent pigras referentia mentes,
Taurus depositis collo sopitus aratris, 
Libra sub emerito considens orbe laborum,
tuque tuos, Capricorne, gelu contractus in artus;
quotations.translation: or that some sit fatigued and reflect their weariness of mind, the Bull slumberous now the plough has left his shoulder, the Balance that sinks down after discharging its round of tasks, and you, Capricorn, whose limbs are shrivelled by the frost;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quaeve iacent, Cancer patulam distentus in alvum,
Scorpios incumbens plano sub pectore terrae,
in latus obliqui Pisces semperque iacentes.
quotations.translation: or that some lie flat, the Crab sprawling with distended belly, the Scorpion reposing on the ground beneath its smooth breast, the Fishes swimming sideways, for ever horizontal.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Quod si sollerti circumspicis omnia cura,
fraudata invenies amissis sidera membris.
Scorpios in Libra consumit bracchia,
Taurus succidit incurvo claudus pede, lumina Cancro
desunt, Centauro superest et quaeritur unum.
quotations.translation: Now if you examine all the signs with keen attention, you will find some bereft of limbs which are lost. The Scorpion expends its arms on the Scales, the Bull sinks lame with leg doubled under it, the Crab lacks eyes, whilst of the Centaur’s one survives and one is missing.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aestas a Geminis, autumnus Virgine surgit,
bruma Sagittifero, ver Piscibus incipit esse.
quotations.translation: summer comes with the Twins, autumn with the Virgin; winter begins with the Archer, spring with the Fishes.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quattuor in partes scribuntur sidera terna;
hiberna aestivis, autumni verna repugnant.
quotations.translation: The four divisions of the year are each allotted three signs; winter’s are at war with summer’s, the vernal with those of autumn.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
consensu quoque fata movent et foedere gaudent
atque aliis alia succedunt sorte locoque.
quotations.translation: they also affect our destinies through their agreements with each other, for they rejoice in alliances and cooperate with one another according to their natures and locations.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Laniger ex paribus spatiis duo signa, Leonis
atque Sagittari, diverso conspicit ortu;
quotations.translation: The Ram beholds at equal distance the two signs of the Lion and the Archer rising on opposite sides of him;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Virginis et Tauri Capricorno consonat astrum;
quotations.translation: the signs of the Virgin and the Bull are in harmony with Capricorn;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
cetera sunt simili ratione triangula signa
per totidem sortes, desunt quae, condita mundo
quotations.translation: by the same principle the other trigonal signs which still remain are framed in the heavens in a like number of configurations
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, quae divisa quaternis
partibus aequali laterum sunt condita ductu
quorum designat normalis virgula sedes,
haec quadrata ferunt.
quotations.translation: But the signs which are separated by quarters of the circle and are situated upon a figure with equal sides, the positions of which a square rule draws, these signs are called quadrate.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Libram Capricornus et illum
conspicit ante Aries atque ipsum a partibus aequis
Cancer et hunc laeva subeuntis sidera Librae.
semper enim in dextris censentur signa priora.
quotations.translation: Capricorn views Libra, whilst the Ram sees Capricorn ahead and is in turn beheld at an equal distance by the Crab; and the Crab is perceived by Libra’s stars as it follows on the left: for preceding signs are reckoned as right signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: τὸ δὲ τάχιον αὐτὸν διαδεχθῆναι παρεσκεύασαν ὁ Ἄρης καὶ ὡροσκόπος καὶ ἡ Σελήνη ἐν τροπικῷ ζῳδίῳ καὶ ὀλιγαναφόροις τετυχηκότες
quotations.translation: The fact that he was succeeded quickly was provided by Mars and the Ascendant and the Moon, which were in a tropical zodiac sign and ones of short rising time.

quotations.original: τὸ δὲ τάχιον αὐτὸν διαδεχθῆναι παρεσκεύασαν ὁ Ἄρης καὶ ὡροσκόπος καὶ ἡ Σελήνη ἐν τροπικῷ ζῳδίῳ καὶ ὀλιγαναφόροις τετυχηκότες
quotations.translation: The fact that he was succeeded quickly was provided by Mars and the Ascendant and the Moon, which were in a tropical zodiac sign and ones of short rising time.

quotations.original:
mascula sed maribus respondent, cetera sexus
feminei secum iungunt commercia mundi
quotations.translation: masculine respond to male, whilst the remainder are of female sex and form among themselves a heavenly fellowship.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Iam vero nulla est haerentibus addita signis
gratia; nam consensus hebet, quia visus ademptus.
quotations.translation: But no friendliness towards one another has been granted to adjacent signs: sympathy between them is blunted because the sight of each other is denied them.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: in seducta ferunt animos, quae cernere possunt.
quotations.translation: Their [the signs'] attentions are bestowed on distant signs which they can see.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Sexta quoque in nullas numerantur commoda vires,
virgula per totum quod par non ducitur orbem
sed duo signa ferit mediis summota quaternis,
tertius absumpto ductus non sufficit orbe.
quotations.translation: Sixth signs [i.e. signs separated by four signs], as well, are not reckoned as capable of any influence, because their line is not traced through the whole circle in equal lengths, but strikes two signs with four intervening, whilst a third side does not fit in since the circle is exhausted.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et toto divisa manent contraria caelo
septima quaeque, loco quamvis summota feruntur,
ex longo tamen illa valent viresque ministrant
quotations.translation: though remote from each other by position, the ones separated by five (signs) exercise influence from afar and furnish their powers
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: [be sure] to match [...] Capricorn against Cancer, the Ram against the Balance (night and day in each are equal), Erigone against the Fishes, the Lion against the youth with his urn;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
His animadversis rebus quae proxima cura?
noscere tutelas adiectaque numina signis
quotations.translation: What step must one take next, when so much has been learnt? It is to mark well the tutelary deities appointed to the signs
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
His animadversis rebus quae proxima cura?
noscere tutelas adiectaque numina signis
quotations.translation: What step must one take next, when so much has been learnt? It is to mark well the tutelary deities appointed to the signs
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Quin etiam propriis inter se legibus astra
conveniunt, ut certa gerant commercia rerum,
inque vicem praestant visus atque auribus haerent
aut odium foedusve gerunt, conversaque quaedam
in semet proprio ducuntur prona favore.
quotations.translation: Moreover, the stars have agreements among themselves according to special laws, and so enjoy fixed associations: upon each other they direct their gaze and to each other give ear; else they bear hatred or friendship; some are introverted and in yielding to their self-esteem are drawn into themselves.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nam, quaecumque nitent humana condita forma
astra, manent illis inimica et victa ferarum.
quotations.translation: for to all the shining signs endowed with human form those of the beasts are ever hostile and ever by them vanquished.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Lanigero genitis bellum est cum Virgine natis
et Libra Geminisque et eis quos protulit Urna.
quotations.translation: The Ram’s children are at war with the offspring of the Virgin, the Balance, and the Twins, and with those whom the Urn has brought forth.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

et Libra Geminisque et eis quos protulit Urna.

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
in partus Tauri sub Cancro nata feruntur
pectora et in Chelis et quae dant Scorpios acer
et Pisces.
quotations.translation: Against the progeny of the Bull there advance men born under the Crab and under the Scales, and those produced by the fierce Scorpion and by the Fishes.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, quos Geminorum sidera formant,
his cum Lanigero bellum est eiusque trigono.
quotations.translation: But those created by the Twins’ stars have war with the Ram and his trigon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
in Cancro genitos Capricorni semina laedunt
et Librae partus et quos dat Virginis astrum
quique sub aversi numerantur sidere Tauri.
quotations.translation: The seed of Capricorn vexes those begotten under the Crab, and so do the children of the Balance, those produced by the Virgin’s sign, and those that are mustered under the constellation of the Bull averse.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
in Cancro genitos Capricorni semina laedunt
et Librae partus et quos dat Virginis astrum
quique sub aversi numerantur sidere Tauri.
quotations.translation: The seed of Capricorn vexes those begotten under the Crab, and so do the children of the Balance, those produced by the Virgin’s sign, and those that are mustered under the constellation of the Bull averse.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Lanigeri communis erit rabidique Leonis
hostis, et a totidem bellum subscribitur astris.
quotations.translation: The Ram shares his foes with the savage Lion; and the same signs levy war on both.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at quos aeternis perfundit Aquarius undis,
in pugnam Nemeaeus agit totumque trigonum,
turba sub unius fugiens virtute ferarum.
quotations.translation: But those poured forth by the Waterman with his ever-flowing stream are provoked to battle by the Nemean and all his trigon, a host of beasts that flees before the manhood of one.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Per tot signorum species contraria surgunt
corpora totque modis totiens inimica creantur.
quotations.translation: From so many configurations of signs come beings opposed to each other, and thus variously and thus often is enmity created.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Si tamen et cognata cupis dinoscere signa,
quae iungant animos et amica sorte ferantur, 
Lanigeri partus cum toto iunge trigono.
quotations.translation: But should you also wish to learn which related signs exchange affection and are subject to a destiny of friendship, connect the offspring of the Ram with all his trigon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Virgineos etiam partus, quicumque creantur Tauro,
complecti cupiunt, sed saepe queruntur.
quotations.translation: those begotten of the Bull are eager to embrace the Virgin’s children too, but often they quarrel.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quos Geminique dabunt Chelaeque et Aquarius ortus
unum pectus habent fideique immobile vinclum,
magnus et in multos veniet successus amicos.
quotations.translation: The issue of the Twins, the Scales, and the Waterman are of one heart and share a bond of loyalty which naught can sunder; and they will achieve conspicuous success in winning many friends.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Scorpios et Cancer fraterna in nomina ducunt
ex semet genitos, nec non et Piscibus orti
concordant illis.
quotations.translation: Scorpion and the Crab endow their sons with the name of brother, and the progeny of the Fishes is also united with them.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, quibus in lucem Pisces venientibus adsunt,
his non una manet semper sententia cordi,
commutant animos interdum et foedera rumpunt
ac repetunt, tectaeque lues sub fronte vagantur.
quotations.translation: And those whom the Fishes father at birth never keep in their hearts for long a constant affection; ever and anon they change their sympathies and now forswear their ties and now renew them, and beneath a mask of blandness unseen hatreds come and go.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nec satis hoc, tantum solis insistere signis:
contemplare locum caeli sedemque vagarum.
quotations.translation: Nor is it enough merely to consider the signs in isolation: you must observe their place in heaven and the position of the planets.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at Leo cum Geminis aciem coniungit et aurem
Centauro ferus et Capricorni diligit astrum.
quotations.translation: But the Lion joins his gaze to that of the Twins and his hearing—for he too is a fierce star—to that of the Centaur and loves the sign of Capricorn.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cancer et adverso Capricornus conditus astro
in semet vertunt oculos, in mutua tendunt
auribus, et Cancri captatur Aquarius astu.
quotations.translation: The Crab and the Sea-goat’s sign placed opposite turn their eyes upon themselves, at one another strain with their ears, whilst the Waterman is taken in by the wiles of the Crab.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Geminorum ducitur auris
ad iuvenem aeternas fundentem Piscibus undas
inque ipsos animus Pisces oculique Leonem.
quotations.translation: The hearing of the Twins is drawn to the youth who pours for the Fishes a never-ending stream, their hearts to the Fishes themselves, and their eyes to the Lion.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Here constructed in passive: to hear means that one's ear is lead by someone.

quotations.original:

quotations.translation: The Crab and the Sea-goat’s sign placed opposite turn their eyes upon themselves, at one another strain with their ears, whilst the Waterman is taken in by the wiles of the Crab.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Erigone Taurum spectat sed Scorpion audit
quotations.translation: Erigone looks at the Bull but hearkens to the Scorpion
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec non Arcitenens magno parere Leoni
auribus atque oculis sinum fundentis Aquari
conspicere assuevit solamque ex omnibus astris
diligit Erigonen.
quotations.translation: The Archer moreover has grown used to waiting on the mighty Lion with his ears and beholding with his eyes the pot that the Waterman empties; he adores Erigone alone of all the stars.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
contra Capricornus in ipsum
convertit visus (quid enim mirabitur ille
maius, in Augusti felix cum fulserit ortum?)
quotations.translation: Capricorn on the other hand turns his gaze upon himself (what greater sign can he ever marvel at, since it was he that shone propitiously upon Augustus’ birth?)
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at nudus Geminis intendit Aquarius aurem
sublimemque colit Cancrum spectatque reducta
tela Sagittiferi.
quotations.translation: And now to the Twins does the Waterman incline his ear, he naked too; he worships the Crab on high and contemplates the drawn bow of the Archer.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Pisces ad Scorpion acrem
derexere aciem cupiuntque attendere Taurum.
quotations.translation: The Fishes have fixed their glance upon the fierce Scorpion and crave to listen to the Bull.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.original:
at Leo cum Geminis aciem coniungit et aurem
Centauro ferus et Capricorni diligit astrum.
quotations.translation: But the Lion joins his gaze to that of the Twins and his hearing—for he too is a fierce star—to that of the Centaur and loves the sign of Capricorn.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: parte genus variant et vires linea mutat.
quotations.translation: The signs vary their nature according to their quarter of the sky, and a line which joins them likewise suffers change of its strength.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: For special properties accrue to squares, to trigons, to the line which traverses six chords, and to that which cuts the midspace of the sky with diametric track;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ver Aries, Cererem Cancer Bacchumque ministrans
Libra, caper brumam genitusque ad frigora piscis.
quotations.translation: the Ram brings spring, the Crab the summer’s corn, the Balance the vintage, and the Goat-fish, born to endure the cold, brings winter.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sic et simplicibus signis stat forma quadrata;
nam neque Taurus habet comitem, nec iungitur ulli
horrendus Leo, nec metuit sine compare quemquam
Scorpios, atque uno censetur Aquarius astro.
quotations.translation: Likewise the single signs also enjoy the figure of a square; for the Bull has no partner, nor has the fierce Lion another at his side; the mateless Scorpion has no one to fear, and the Waterman is counted as of single sign.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
idcirco affines signant gradibusque propinquis
accedunt unaque tenent sub imagine natos,
quotquot cardinibus, prona vertigine mundi
naturae vires propriae variante, moventur;
quotations.translation: For this reason the quadrate signs indicate connections by marriage, assist the near degrees of kinship, and stamp their children with identical features, when they move through the cardinal points, incurring the while variation of their natural powers owing to the sky’s forward rotation;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nam nihil in totum servit sibi: mixta feruntur,
ipsis dant in se partes capiuntque vicissim.
quotations.translation: for no sign ministers exclusively to itself; they intermingle as they revolve: they cede to each other parts in themselves and are ceded parts in turn.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
omnibus ex istis ratio est repetenda per artem,
pacata infestis signa ut discernere possis.
quotations.translation: It is from all such details that a true account is to be drawn in our science, if one is to distinguish peaceful from aggressive signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
omnibus ex istis ratio est repetenda per artem,

quotations.original:
quacumque in parti nascentum tempore Luna
constiterit, numeris hanc ter dispone quaternis,
sublimi totidem quia fulgent sidera mundo.
quotations.translation: Multiply thrice four times whatever degree the Moon occupies at the moment of nativity, since so many are the constellations which shine in high heaven.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
post cetera ducet
ordine quodque suo, sicut stant astra locata.
quotations.translation: subsequently she will occupy the remaining dodecatemories, each one in its turn, according to the established order of the signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nam totidem praefulgent sidera caelo
quae vaga dicuntur, ducunt et singula sortes
dimidias, viresque in eis et iura capessunt.
quotations.translation: for so many are the stars called wanderers which with passing brightness shine in heaven: they are each allotted half a degree wherein they assume power and authority.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
unus ab exortu caeli nascentis in orbem,
qua primum terras aequali limite cernit,
alter ab adversa respondens aetheris ora,
unde fugit mundus praecepsque in Tartara tendit;
quotations.translation: One looks out from the rising of the heavens as they are born into the world and has the first view of the Earth from the level horizon; the second faces it from the opposite edge of the sky, the point from which the starry sphere retires and hurtles headlong into Tartarus;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tertius excelsi signat fastigia caeli,
quo defessus equis Phoebus subsistit anhelis
reclinatque diem mediasque examinat umbras;
ima tenet quartus fundato nobilis orbe
quotations.translation: a third marks the zenith of high heaven, where wearied Phoebus halts with panting steeds and rests the day and determines the mid-point of shadows; the fourth occupies the nadir, and has the glory of forming the foundation of the sphere
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Πλειὰς μὲν ἤιει μεσοπόρου δι’ αἰθέρος
ὅ τε ξιφήρης Ὠρίων, ὕπερθε δὲ
Ἄρκτος στρέφουσ’ οὐραῖα χρυσήρη πόλωι·
quotations.translation:
The Pleiad swam her mid-sky path along,
And sword-begirt Orion; and, above,
The Bear's tail wheeled around the gold-gemmed sphere.
quotations.publication: J. Diggle, Euripidis fabulae, vol. 2, Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1981: 307-373.
quotations.comment: Translation by Arthur S. Way 1912.

quotations.original:
hinc modo dat mundus vires, modo deterit idem,
quaeque illic sumunt iras, huc acta reponunt.
quotations.translation: Hence the sky now adds strength and now takes it away, and the stars which conceive anger there discard it when driven here [below the horizon].
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: These points are charged with exceptional powers, and the influence they exert on fate is the greatest known to our science, because the celestial circle is totally held in position by them as by eternal supports;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae nisi perpetuis alterna sorte volantem
cursibus excipiant nectantque in vincula, bina
per latera atque imum templi summumque cacumen,
dissociata fluat resoluto machina mundo.
quotations.translation: did they not receive the circle, sign after sign in succession, flying in its perpetual revolution, and clamp it with fetters at the two sides and lowest and highest extremities of its compass, heaven would fly apart and its fabric disintegrate and perish.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tertius, aequali terris in parte nitentem
qui tenet exortum, qua primum sidera surgunt,
unde dies redit et tempus describit in horas,
hinc inter Graias horoscopos editur urbes,
nec capit externum, proprio quia nomine gaudet.
quotations.translation: The third cardinal, which on the same level as the Earth holds in position the shining dawn, where the stars first rise, where day returns and divides time into hours, is for this reason in the Greek world called the Horoscope, and it declines a foreign name, taking pleasure in its own.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hunc penes arbitrium vitae est, hic regula morum,
fortunamque dabit rebus, ducetque per artes,
qualiaque excipiant nascentis tempora prima,
quos capiant cultus, quali sint sede creati,
utcumque admixtis subscribent viribus astra.
quotations.translation: Within its domain lies the arbitrament of life and the formation of character; it will grant success to enterprises, open up the professions, and decide the early years that await men from their birth, the education they receive, and the station to which they are born, according as the planets approve and mingle their influences.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quidquid ab exortu summum curvatur in orbem,
aetatem primam nascentisque asserit annos.
quotations.translation: The curve which stretches from the orient to the topmost point of the circle claims the earliest age and infant years.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod summo premitur devexum culmine mundi
donec ad occasus veniat, puerilibus annis
succedit teneramque regit sub sede iuventam.
quotations.translation: The slope which sinks down from the summit of the sky till it reaches the Occident succeeds to the years of childhood and includes in its province control of tender youth.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
