quotations.translation: The slope which sinks down from the summit of the sky till it reaches the Occident succeeds to the years of childhood and includes in its province control of tender youth.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, qua perficitur cursus redeunte sub ortum,
tarda supinatum lassatis viribus arcum
ascendens, seros demum complectitur annos
labentemque diem vitae tremulamque senectam.
quotations.translation: But the part by whose return to the orient heaven’s course is done and which with enfeebled strength slowly ascends the backbent arc, this part embraces the final years, life’s fading twilight, and palsied age.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
locus imperat astris
et dotes noxamque facit;
quotations.translation: position governs the stars, and endows them with power to benefit or harm;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
vincit enim natura loci legesque ministrat
finibus in propriis et praetereuntia cogit
esse sui moris, vario nunc ditia honore,
nunc sterilis poenam referentia sidera sedis.
quotations.translation: The nature of the position prevails, exercises jurisdiction within its province, and subjects to its own character the signs as they pass by, which now are enriched with distinction of every kind and now bear the penalty of a barren abode.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: The [place] that is immediately above the Horoscope and is the next but one to heaven’s zenith is a temple of ill omen, hostile to future activity and all too fruitful of bane;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec melior super occasus contraque sub ortu
sors agitur mundi
quotations.translation: Not more fortunate is the portion of heaven above the Occident or that opposite it below the orient;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Here used as an adverb.

quotations.original:
nec melior super occasus contraque sub ortu
sors agitur mundi
quotations.translation: Not more fortunate is the portion of heaven above the Occident or that opposite it below the orient;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quocirca minime mirum, si proxima summo
atque eadem integrior Fortunae sorte dicatur
cui titulus Felix.
quotations.translation: There is thus small cause for wonder, if the station nearest the zenith, and more secure than it, is blessed with the lot of Happy Fortune.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Footnote Goold 1977: "The Greek astrologers usually call [place] 11 ἀγαθὸς δαίμων (“Good Spirit”) and employ the term ἀγαθὴ τύχη (“Good Fortune”) of [place] 5."

quotations.original:
huic in perversum similis deiecta sub orbe
imaque summersi contingens culmina mundi,
adversa quae parte nitet
quotations.translation: Like this temple, but with an inverse likeness, is that which is thrust below the world and adjoins the nadir of the submerged heaven, and which shines in the opposite region
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Applied to the 5th astrological place, a trine of the 1st place. Hence it cannot mean unaspected here.

quotations.original: imaque summersi contingens culmina mundi
quotations.translation: which adjoins the nadir of the submerged heaven
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Daemonien memorant Grai, Romana per ora
quaeritur inversus titulus.
quotations.translation: This seat the Greeks call Daemonie: a rendering of the name in Roman speech is wanting.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Footnote Goold 1977: "Housman can find only two occurrences of the term, each obscure and signifying [place] 6 (normally called κακὴ τύχη “Evil Fortune”)."

quotations.translation: The stars that follow midday, where the height of heaven first slopes downward and bows from the summit, these Phoebus nourishes with his splendour;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: The stars that follow midday, where the height of heaven first slopes downward and bows from the summit, these Phoebus nourishes with his splendour;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
arce sed in caeli, qua summa acclivia finem
inveniunt, qua principium declivia sumunt,
culminaque insurgunt occasus inter et ortus
suspenduntque suo libratum examine mundum,
asserit hanc Cytherea sibi per sidera sedem
et velut in facie mundi sua collocat ora,
per quae humana regit.
quotations.translation: But in the citadel of the sky, where the rising curve attains its consummation, and the downward slope makes its beginning, and the summit towers midway between orient and Occident and holds the universe poised in its balance, here does the Cytherean claim her abode among the stars, placing in the very face of heaven, as it were, her beauteous features, wherewith she rules the affairs of men.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
propria est haec reddita parti
vis, ut conubia et thalamos taedasque gubernet:
quotations.translation: To the abode is fittingly given the power to govern wedlock, the bridal chamber, and the marriage torch;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
haec tutela decet Venerem, sua tela movere.
nomen erit Fortuna loco, quod percipe mente
quotations.translation: and this charge suits Venus, the charge of plying her own weapons. Fortune shall be this temple’s name; and mark it well
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
viridis gelidis et Phoebus ab undis
enatat et fulvo paulatim accenditur igni
asperum iter temptans, | Aries qua ducit Olympum.
quotations.translation: and a pale Sun swims upward from the icy waves and begins by slow degrees to blaze with golden flame as it attempts the rugged path where the Ram heads the procession of the skies.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ne mirere, nigri si Ditis ianua fertur
et finem vitae retinetque repagula mortis.
quotations.translation: so wonder not if it is called the portal of sombre Pluto and keeps control over the end of life and death’s firm-bolted door.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tali sub sorte notandae
templorum tibi sunt vires: quae pervolat omnis
astrorum series
quotations.translation: This is the system by which you must mark the powers of the temples: through them revolves the entire procession of the zodiac
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
aliena capessunt
regna et in externis subsidunt hospita castris.
quotations.translation: they occupy realms not their own and sojourn in an alien camp.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nunc satis est caeli partes titulosque notasse
effectusque loci per se cuiusque deosque.
quotations.translation: it is enough for now to have recorded the temples of heaven and their names, the innate influences of each place, and the deities that dwell therein.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

nunc satis est caeli partes titulosque notasse

quotations.translation:
nunc satis est caeli partes titulosque notasse
effectusque loci per se cuiusque deosque.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae pervolat omnis
astrorum series ducitque et commodat illis
ipsa suas leges
quotations.translation: through them revolves the entire procession of the zodiac, which draws from them their laws and lends to them its own;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
[cui parti nomen posuit, qui condidit artem,
octotropos; per quod stellae diversa volantes
quos reddant motus, proprio venit ordine rerum]
quotations.translation: The founder of astrology gave to this section the title Octotropos; the motions of the planets, which fly through it in the opposite direction, shall follow at the proper place.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Manilius does not use this system. The verses have likely been interpolated, cf. Goold 1977, p. lxi f.

quotations.original:
(...), καὶ πλάνα φέγγη 
ἀπλανέων τ᾽ αὐγὰς πυριλαμπέας ἐξονομήνω, 
ζωιδίων τε πόλοιο περίδρομον, (...)
quotations.translation:
(...), of the wandering lights too,
and of the fiery-bright rays of the unwandering ones, let me speak of them by name,
and of the circuit of the sphere of the zodiac signs, (...)
quotations.publication: Lopilato, R., 1998. The "Apotelesmatika" of Manetho. Providence, Rhode Island: Brown University.

quotations.original: Ἀγαθοῦ δαίμονος τόπος· πολλὰ σχήματα.
quotations.translation: The place of Agathos Daimōn: many configurations.
quotations.publication: (GH L 134,VI)

quotations.original:
DIŠ 30 TAB-ma ba-ra-ri it-ta-ʾ-dar
AN.GI₆ LUGAL URI.ki
quotations.translation:
If the Moon is early and it darkens at the time of the evening watch
the eclipse (affects) the king of akkad
quotations.publication: Rochberg-Halton, F. (1988). Aspects of Babylonian Celestial Divination: The Lunar Eclipse Tablets of Enūma Anu Enlil. Verlag Ferdinand Berger & Söhne Gesellschaft.

quotations.original: וּנְשָׂאתֶם אֵת סִכּוּת מַלְכְּכֶם וְאֵת כִּיּוּן צַלְמֵיכֶם כּוֹכַב אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם׃
quotations.transliteration: ûnəśāʾt̲em ʾēt̲ sikkût̲ malkək̲em wəʾēt̲ kiyyûn ṣalmêk̲em kôk̲ab̲ ʾĕlōhêk̲em ʾăšer ʿăśît̲em lāk̲em.
quotations.translation: But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.
quotations.publication: Stieglitz 1988
quotations.comment: "The common Mesopotamian name for this planet was (mul)SAG.UŠ = Kay(y)amānu or Kay(y)ānu."

quotations.original:
alter ab excelso decurrens limes Olympo
Serpentis caudam siccas et dividit Arctos
et iuga Chelarum medio volitantia gyro
quotations.translation: One line [i.e. the equinoctial colure], descending from the summit of the sky, passes through the Dragon’s tail and the Bears that shun ocean, and the yoke of the Balance which revolves in the midmost circle.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
extremamque secans Hydram mediumque sub austris
Centaurum adverso concurrit rursus in axe
quotations.translation: [The equinoctial colure] cleaves the extremity of the Water-snake and the middle of the southern Centaur, and again converges upon the opposing circle at the pole;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et tenuem longis iaculantur tractibus ignem
praecipites stellae passimque volare videntur
quotations.translation: There are also shooting stars, which hurl long trails of slender fire and are seen flying everywhere
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hoc quoque servandum est alta discrimen in arte,
distat enim gemini duo sint duplane figura
quotations.translation: This distinction, too, must be preserved in our lofty art, for it makes a difference whether double signs are twin or of composite shape.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Debilia alternis data sunt commercia signis,
mutua nec magno consensu foedera servant,
invita angusto quod linea flectitur orbe.
quotations.translation: Weak is the connection between alternate signs, nor do they maintain with unfailing constancy the federation between each other, because the line is reluctant to bend in its circuit of short chords.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: οὐ γὰρ πάντες Αἰγύπτιοι ἐκ τῶν δυώδεκα μοιρέων πασέων ἐμαντεύοντο, ἄλλοι δὲ ἀλλοίῃσι μοίρῃσιν ἐχρέοντο, καὶ κριὸν μὲν σέβουσιν ὁκόσοι ἐς κριὸν ἀπέβλεπον, ἰχθύας δὲ οὐ σιτέονται ὁκόσοι ἰχθύας ἐπεσημήναντο, οὐδὲ τράγον κτείνουσιν ὅσοι αἰγόκερων ᾔδεσαν, καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι τὰ ἄλλα ὡς ἕκαστοι ἱλάσκονται. ναὶ μὴν καὶ ταῦρον ἐς τιμὴν τοῦ ἠερίου ταύρου σεβίζονται, καὶ ὁ Ἆπις αὐτοῖς χρῆμα ἱερώτατον τὴν χώρην ἐπινέμεται καί οἱ ἐκεῖ μαντήιόν γε ἀνατιθέασιν σημήιον τῆς ἐκείνου τοῦ ταύρου μαντικῆς.
quotations.translation: For not all Egyptians made predictions from all twelve parts (sc. of the zodiac), but different ones used different parts: those who(se birth) looked upon Aries venerate the ram, and those who have taken the sign of Pisces eat no fish, nor do those who knew Capricorn (the goat-horned one) (sc. at birth) kill the male goat, and the others otherwise as each of them seek to appease. Indeed they also worship the bull in honor of the bull (i.e. Taurus) up in the air, and Apis is the holiest thing to graze their country, and they dedicate an oracle to him there, a sign of the oracular skill of that bull.

quotations.original: ἐπεῖχε Καρκίνου μοίρας ἓξ καὶ ἔ̣τι λεπτὰ τρίτα δέκ̣[α]· ἃ δὴ μέρος μοίρης ἐστὶν δισμυροχιλεξακοσιοστόν
quotations.translation: (Jupiter) occupied six degrees of Cancer and further ten third(-order) minutes, which are a twenty-six-thousandth of a degree

quotations.original: [οὗ τὸ δωδεκατημόριον ἐν Σ]κορπίωι [μοιρ]ῶν ηʹ λεπτῶν νβʹ
quotations.translation: Its dodekatemorion is in Scorpio, at 8 degrees, 52 minutes
quotations.publication: GH 95

quotations.original:
ana la-tak u₄-me ki-nu-ti₃
šit-qul-ti MUL.MUL u d.30 ina ŠU.II-ka tu-kal
quotations.translation:
To predict the "correct" days
you study the "opposition" of the Pleiades and the Moon
quotations.publication: Oppenheim, A. L. 1974. A Babylonian Diviner’s Manual. Journal of Near Eastern Studies, 33(2), 197–220.
quotations.comment: I am not sure "opposition" is correct.

quotations.original: γίνεται γ γʹ ὅ ἐστιν αὐξομείωσις ἑκάστου ζῳδίου· τῷ αὐτῷ τρόπῳ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων ζῳδίων γνώσει
quotations.translation: The result is 3 1/3, which is the difference (between rising-times) for each zodiac sign; by the same method you will also know (the values) for the other zodiac signs.
quotations.publication: CCAG I

quotations.original: σαώς· ἥλιος. Βαβυλώνιοι
quotations.translation: Saōs: Sun. Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: σαυή· ὁ κόσμος. Βαβυλώνιοι
quotations.translation: sauē: the cosmos. Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.
quotations.comment: In the manuscript, only the reading σάνη is attested.

quotations.original: Φασὶ δ᾽ οἱ σοφοί, ὦ Καλλίκλεις, καὶ οὐρανὸν καὶ γῆν καὶ θεοὺς καὶ ἀνθρώπους τὴν κοινωνίαν συνέχειν καὶ φιλίαν καὶ κοσμιότητα καὶ σωφροσύνην καὶ δικαιότητα, καὶ τὸ ὅλον τοῦτο διὰ ταῦτα κόσμον καλοῦσιν, ὦ ἑταῖρε, οὐκ ἀκοσμίαν οὐδὲ ἀκολασίαν.
quotations.translation: And the wise men say, o Callicles, that sky and earth and gods and men are kept together by communion and friendship and propriety and temperance and justice, and the whole of this for this reason they call order ("cosmos"), my friend, not disorder nor dissoluteness.
quotations.publication: Plato. 1903. Plato. Platonis Opera, ed. J. Burnet. Oxford University Press.

quotations.original: αἰδώς· *αἰσχύνη ... τὴν τοῦ σώματος αἰσχρότητα, τὰ αἰδοῖα. καὶ ἡ σελήνη, παρὰ Χαλδαίοις
quotations.translation: Aidōs: *shame ... the ugliness of the body, the private parts. And the Moon, according to the Chaldeans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.
quotations.comment: In the manuscripts, the readings ἀϊδὴς, αἰδώ and αἰδῶ are attested.

quotations.original: Δελέφατ· ὁ τῆς Ἀφροδίτης ἀστήρ, ὑπὸ Χαλδαίων
quotations.translation: Delephat: the star of Aphrodite, amongst the Chaldeans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: σεχές· τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ ἀστήρ. Βαβυλώνιοι
quotations.translation: Seches: the star of Hermes. Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Στίλβων· ὁ τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ ἀστήρ
quotations.translation: Stilbōn: the star of Hermes.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Βελέβατος· ὁ τοῦ πῦρος ἀστήρ. Βαβυλώνιοι
quotations.translation: Belebatos: the star of fire. Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: μολοβόβαρ· ὁ τοῦ Δίος ἀστήρ, παρὰ Χαλδαίοις
quotations.translation: Molobobar: the star of Zeus, according to the Chaldeans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2020. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 2 (a. Epsilon – Iota, b. Kappa – Omicron), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.translation: Sin: the Moon. Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.
quotations.comment: The manuscript contains σεμνήν instead of σελήνην.

quotations.translation: Sin: the Moon. Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Ἀδάρ· μὴν παρὰ Χαλδαίοις
quotations.translation: Adar: a month according to the Chaldeans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.
quotations.comment: In the manuscript, only the reading Ἀδαεὶ is attested.

quotations.original: Σιόαν· οὕτω καλοῦσι Χαλδαῖοι τὸν Πάνημον μῆνα.
quotations.translation: Sioan: that is how the Chaldeans call the month Panemos.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: ἄβ· ὁ Γορπιαῖος μήν
quotations.translation: Ab: the month Gorpiaios.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Τήβηθ· Περίτιος μήν
quotations.translation: Tēbēth: the month Peritios.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2009. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 4 (Tau - Omega), eds. P.A. Hansen and I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Νισᾶν· ὁ Ἀρτεμίσιος μήν. καὶ † Ἰλίου πόλις
quotations.translation: Nisan: the month Artemisios. And Heliopolis.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2020. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 2 (a. Epsilon – Iota, b. Kappa – Omicron), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Δύστρος· ὑπὸ Μακεδόνων μήν
quotations.translation: Dustros: a month among the Macedonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: μισσυνή· ἡ ὀξύτης παρὰ Χαλδαίοις
quotations.translation: Missunē: sharpness according to the Chaldeans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2020. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 2 (a. Epsilon – Iota, b. Kappa – Omicron), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: πικόν· πικρόν. Χαλδαῖοι
quotations.translation: pikon: pointed. Chaldeans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.
quotations.comment: NB. The form is given by Hesychius in the accusative.

quotations.original: σαρός· ἀριθμός τις παρὰ Βαβυλωνίοις
quotations.translation: saros: a certain number, according to the Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: ἀρῶς· ἀριθμοῦ ὄνομα, παρὰ Πέρσαις
quotations.translation: arōs: name of a number, according to the Persians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: μινδαλόεσσα· ἀριθμῶν σύνταξις. καὶ τὰ περὶ <τὰ> οὐράνια ... Βαβυλώνιοι
quotations.translation: mindaloessa: system of numbers. And the (?) regarding <the> heavenly things ... Babylonians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2020. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 2 (a. Epsilon – Iota, b. Kappa – Omicron), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: ἀστρολόγος· γενεθλιολόγος
quotations.translation: astrologos: birth expert.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: ἀστρολόγος· γενεθλιολόγος
quotations.translation: astrologos: birth expert.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original:
Ἦν δ' οὐδὲν αὐτοῖς οὔτε χείματος τέκμαρ
οὔτ' ἀνθεμώδους ἦρος οὔτε καρπίμου
θέρους βέβαιον, ἀλλ' ἄτερ γνώμης τὸ πᾶν
ἔπρασσον, ἔστε δή σφιν ἀντολὰς ἐγὼ 
ἄστρων ἔδειξα τάς τε δυσκρίτους δύσεις.
quotations.translation:
And they didn't have any sign - neither of winter, 
nor of flowery spring, nor of fruitful 
summer - that was certain, but they did it all without
sense, until I then showed them the risings 
of the stars and the hard to discern settings.
quotations.publication: Aeschylus. 1930. Aeschylus, with an English translation by Herbert Weir Smyth, ed. H.W. Smith. London: William Heinemann.

quotations.original: πλάνος· πλανήτης, ἀπατέων
quotations.translation: planos: wandering, leading astray.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2005. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 3 (Pi - Sigma), ed. P.A. Hansen. Berlin, New York: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: תִּקְע֣וּ בַחֹ֣דֶשׁ שׁוֹפָ֑ר בַּ֝כֵּ֗סֶה לְי֣וֹם חַגֵּֽנוּ׃
quotations.transliteration: tiqʿû b̲aḥōd̲eš šôp̲ār bakkēseh ləyôm ḥaggēnû
quotations.translation: Blow in the month a trumpet, in the [full] moon, at the day of our festival,

quotations.original: Σελήνη ἐν Ταύρῳ ζῳδίῳ θηλυκῷ οἴκῳ [Ἀφροδίτης]
quotations.translation: The Moon (was) in Taurus, a female zodiac sign, house of Venus

quotations.original: ἐπιγνόντες τὴν τῶν ἑπτὰ θεῶν κείνησιν τὰ ὅλα σ̣[υ]νέχουσάν τε καὶ διοικοῦσαν ἀφ[θ]ό̣νως ἡμεῖν διὰ κανόνων αἰωνί̣ων ἀπέλειπ̣ον τὴν περὶ αὐτῶν γνῶσιν· ὅθεν ἕκαστον ψηφίσας ἀκριβῶς τέταχά σοι
quotations.translation: (The ancient Egyptians,) having recognized the motion of the seven (planetary) gods, which comprises and dispenses all things, have generously left us with the knowledge about them through perpetual tables: having precisely calculated each (planet’s position) by those means, I have set them out for you.

quotations.original: ἐπιγνόντες τὴν τῶν ἑπτὰ θεῶν κείνησιν τὰ ὅλα σ̣[υ]νέχουσάν τε καὶ διοικοῦσαν ἀφ[θ]ό̣νως ἡμεῖν διὰ κανόνων αἰωνί̣ων ἀπέλειπ̣ον τὴν περὶ αὐτῶν γνῶσιν· ὅθεν ἕκαστον ψηφίσας ἀκριβῶς τέταχά σοι
quotations.translation: (The ancient Egyptians,) having recognized the motion of the seven (planetary) gods, which comprises and dispenses all things, have generously left us with the knowledge about them through perpetual tables: having precisely calculated each (planet’s position) by those means, I have set them out for you

quotations.original: Ἀλλὰ μὴ γεωμέτρης ἐπιθυμεῖς, ἔφη, γενέσθαι ἀγαθός, ὥσπερ ὁ Θεόδωρος; Οὐδὲ γεωμέτρης, ἔφη. Ἀλλὰ μὴ ἀστρολόγος, ἔφη, βούλει γενέσθαι; ὡς δὲ καὶ τοῦτο ἠρνεῖτο, Ἀλλὰ μὴ ῥαψῳδός; ἔφη· καὶ γὰρ τὰ Ὁμήρου σέ φασιν ἔπη πάντα κεκτῆσθαι.
quotations.translation:
“Well, perhaps you want to be a good mathematician, like Theodorus?”1
“No, not that either.”
“Well, perhaps you want to be an astronomer?” And as he again said no, “Perhaps a rhapsodist, then? They tell me you have a complete copy of Homer.”

quotations.original: κόλλησίς ἐστιν ὅταν ἀστὴρ ἀστέρι προσέρχηται ὁ ταχύτερος τῷ βραδυτέρῳ οὐ πλέον ἀπέχων μοιρῶν γʹ·
quotations.translation: Attachment is whenever a planet approaches a planet, the faster to the slower, no more distant than 3 degrees.
quotations.publication: CCAG VIII.3

quotations.original: צְֽרוֹר־הַ֭כֶּסֶף לָקַ֣ח בְּיָד֑וֹ לְי֥וֹם הַ֝כֵּ֗סֶא יָבֹ֥א בֵיתֽוֹ׃
quotations.transliteration: Ṣərôr-hakkesep̲ lāqaḥ bəyād̲ô ləyôm hakkēseʾ yāb̲ōʾ b̲êt̲ô.
quotations.translation: A bag of money he hath taken in his hand, at the day of the [full] moon he cometh to his house.

quotations.original: וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃
quotations.transliteration: Wəzāraḥ haššemeš ûb̲āʾ haššāmeš wəʾel-məqômô šôʾēp̲ zôrēaḥ hûʾ šām.
quotations.translation: Also, the Sun hath risen, and the Sun hath gone in, and unto its place panting it is rising there.

quotations.original: וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃
quotations.transliteration: Wəzāraḥ haššemeš ûb̲āʾ haššāmeš wəʾel-məqômô šôʾēp̲ zôrēaḥ hûʾ šām.
quotations.translation: Also, the sun hath risen, and the sun hath gone in, and unto its place panting it is rising there.

quotations.original: וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃
quotations.transliteration: Wəzāraḥ haššemeš ûb̲āʾ haššāmeš wəʾel-məqômô šôʾēp̲ zôrēaḥ hûʾ šām.
quotations.translation: Also, the sun hath risen, and the sun hath gone in, and unto its place panting it is rising there.

quotations.original: וְנָמַ֙קּוּ֙ כָּל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם
quotations.transliteration: wənāmaqqû kol-ṣəb̲āʾ haššāmayim
quotations.translation: And consumed have been all the host of the heavens

quotations.original: אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־גּוֹיִֽם׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾêk̲ nāp̲altā miššāmayim hêlēl ben-šāḥar nig̲daʿtā lāʾāreṣ ḥôlēš ʿal-gôyim.
quotations.translation:
How are you fallen from heaven,
O Shining One, son of Dawn! 
How are you felled to earth,
O vanquisher of nations!

quotations.original: אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־גּוֹיִֽם׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾêk̲ nāp̲altā miššāmayim hêlēl ben-šāḥar nig̲daʿtā lāʾāreṣ ḥôlēš ʿal-gôyim.
quotations.translation:
How are you fallen from heaven,
O Shining One, son of Dawn! 
How are you felled to earth,
O vanquisher of nations!
quotations.comment: "Cf. Assyrian muštilil epith. of (Venus as) morning-star" (BDB, הָלַל)

quotations.original: וַיְהִ֞י בְּנֻסָ֣ם ׀ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֵ֞ם בְּמוֹרַ֤ד בֵּית־חוֹרֹן֙ וַיהֹוָ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֧וֹת מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וַיָּמֻ֑תוּ רַבִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־מֵ֙תוּ֙ בְּאַבְנֵ֣י הַבָּרָ֔ד מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְג֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ {ס}
quotations.transliteration: Wayhî bənusām  mippənê yiśrāʾēl hēm bəmôrad̲ bêt̲-ḥôrōn waihōwāh hišlîk̲ ʿălêhem ʾăb̲ānîm gəd̲ōlôt̲ min-haššāmayim ʿad̲-ʿăzēqāh wayyāmut̲û rabbîm ʾăšer-mēt̲û bəʾab̲nê habbārād̲ mēʾăšer hārəg̲û bənê yiśrāʾēl beḥāreb̲.
quotations.translation: While they were fleeing before Israel down the descent from Beth-horon, GOD hurled huge stones on them from the sky, all the way to Azekah, and they perished; more perished from the hailstones than were killed by the Israelite weapons.

quotations.original: Κρόνος ἐν Ὑδρό[χ]ῳ μοιρ[ῶν] γ 𐅵ʹ λεπτο(ὶ) ηʹ ἐν τῷ βʹ στηριγμῷ
quotations.translation: Saturn (was) in Aquarius, 3 ½ degrees, 8 minutes, in the 2nd station

quotations.original: ζῳδίωι Ἀφροδίτης ὑψώματι ἰδίωι ὁρίοις Ἑρμοῦ θηλυκῶι καὶ στερεῶι ζῳδίωι
quotations.translation: (The Moon was) in (Taurus), a zodiac sign of Venus, its own exaltation, terms of Mercury, a female and solid zodiac sign

quotations.original:
(8') [TA 13 R]IN₂ EN 27 zib.ME ITI ana I[TI]
(9') [2.6.15.4]2 TAB u LA₂-ka
quotations.translation: (8’) [From 13 Li]b until 27 Psc, month by m[onth] (9’) your addition and subtraction is [2,6;15,4]2.
quotations.publication: Ossendrijver, M. 2012. Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy: Procedure Texts. New York: Springer

quotations.original: [x x] ŠÚ šá sin dTIR.AN.NA šá MÚŠ.MEŠ-šú SUD TA SI ana Á ULÙ [GIB....]
quotations.translation: [....] and (?) setting of the moon, an aurora borealis (lit. a rainbow whose glow was DISTANT/RED? [stretched] from the north to the south side [....]
quotations.publication: Sachs, A. J., Hunger, H. 1996. Astronomical Diaries and Related Texts from Babylonia, Vol. III. Diaries from 164 B.C. to 61 B.C. Vienna, Austria: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.
quotations.comment: See also: Hayakawa, H., Mitsuma, Y., Ebihara, Y., Kawamura, A. D., Miyahara, H., Tamazawa, H., & Isobe, H. (2016). Earliest datable records of aurora-like phenomena in the astronomical diaries from Babylonia. Earth, Planets and Space, 68, 1-9.

quotations.original: DIŠ MUL.ZUBI zi-mu-šu uṣ-ṣa-na-la-mu
quotations.translation: If the Gamlu-star becomes darker and darker (i.e. if its glow becomes weaker and weaker
quotations.publication: Weidner, E. F. (1925). Ein astrologischer Kommentar aus Uruk. In K. Donner, H. Ehelolf, E. Flinck, C. J. Gadd, E. G. Gulin, R. Gyllenberg, A. Hjelt, H. Holma, U. Holmberg, L. Itkonen, P. Jensen, S. Langdon, Joh. Lindblom, B. Meißner, A. Poebel, A. F. Puukko, H. Ranke, Edv. Rein, J. N. Reuter, … K. Tallqvist (Eds.), Commentationes in honorem Knut Tallqvist (pp. 347–358). Societas Orientalis Fennica.
quotations.comment: See also Thavapalan, S. (2019). The meaning of color in ancient Mesopotamia (Vol. 104). Brill, p. 157.

quotations.original:
KI.ŠE₃ AN.KI TEŠ₂.BI LA₂.A.TA AN.UR₃.TA UM.TA.E₃.NA.Z[U.Š]E
ana e-ma ša-mu-u₂ u KI-tum DIŠ-niš na-an-du-ru iš-tu i-šid AN-e ina <a-še-ka>
quotations.translation: When you (Sun-god) rise at the place where heaven and earth embrace, from the horizon.
quotations.publication: Borger, R. (1967). Das dritte “Haus” der Serie bīt rimki (VR 50-51, Schollmeyer HGŠ NR. 1). Journal of Cuneiform Studies, 21, 1–17. https://doi.org/10.2307/1359353

quotations.original: NIN AN.USAS AN.ZA₃.ŠE₃ MAḪ.[AM₃]
quotations.translation: The lady of the evening (Inanna) [is] magnificent at the horizon
quotations.publication: Reisman, D. D. (1969). Two Neo-Sumerian Royal Hymns. University of Pennsylvania.

quotations.original:
MUL tul-tum  d.a-nu-ni-tum
KU₆MEŠ tu-la-a-tum u MUŠEN.MEŠ ḫu-'u₂-u₂
quotations.translation:
Constellation of the worm: Anunītu
Fishes are worms and birds are ...
quotations.publication: Weidner, E. F. (1959). Ein astrologischer Sammeltext aus der Sargonidenzeit. Archiv Für Orientforschung, 19, 105–113.
quotations.comment: Z. 28 (5). Für ḫu-'u₂-u₂ s. CAD 6, S. 212 unter hūa (die Übersetzung «hoot-owl» paßt aber hier nicht), hu'atu (ib.) ist zu streichen (Weidner 1959, 108)

quotations.original:
Consilium ipse suum est Aries, ut principe dignum est,
audit se Libramque videt, frustratur amando
Taurum; Lanigero qui fraudem nectit et ultra
fulgentis geminos audit per sidera Pisces,
Virgine mens capitur visa.
quotations.translation: As befits a leader, the Ram is his own counsel; he listens to himself and beholds the Balance, and his love for the Bull is thwarted. Against him the Bull weaves a net of deceit and hears the twin Fishes which shine beyond the Ram, whilst his heart is entranced at the sight of the Maid.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: As befits a leader, the Ram is his own counsel; he listens to himself and beholds the Balance, and his love for the Bull is thwarted.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: As befits a leader, the Ram is his own counsel; he listens to himself and beholds the Balance, and his love for the Bull is thwarted.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et Cancri captatur Aquarius astu.
quotations.translation: the Waterman is taken in by the wiles of the Crab.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Libra suos sequitur sensus solumque videndo
Lanigerum atque animo complexa est Scorpion infra.
quotations.translation: The Balance heeds his own counsel and has embraced with his gaze none but the Ram and with his heart the Scorpion beneath.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec non Arcitenens magno parere Leoni
auribus
quotations.translation: The Archer moreover has grown used to waiting on the mighty Lion with his ears
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at nudus Geminis intendit Aquarius aurem
sublimemque colit Cancrum spectatque reducta
tela Sagittiferi.
quotations.translation: And now to the Twins does the Waterman incline his ear, he naked too; he worships the Crab on high and contemplates the drawn bow of the Archer.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
maxima turba petit Libram, Capricornus et illi
adversus Cancer, Iuvenis quod utrimque quadratum est,
quaeque in Lanigeri numerantur signa trigonum.
quotations.translation: The Balance is assailed by the largest host—Capricorn, and Cancer opposite him, the quadrate signs on either side of the Youth, and those signs reckoned as of the Ram’s trigon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Scorpios in totidem fecundus creditur hostes;
aequoreum iuvenem, Geminos, Taurum atque Leonem,
Erigonen Libramque fugit metuendus et ipse,
quique Sagittari veniunt de sidere partus.
quotations.translation: The Scorpion is presumed prolific of as many foes; it flees before the lad with his waters, the Twins, the Bull, the Lion, and (to whom it is itself an object of fear) the Maid and the Balance, and also the offspring that issues from the Archer’s sign.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: at quos aeternis perfundit Aquarius undis ...
quotations.translation: But those poured forth by the Waterman with his ever-flowing stream ...
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Si tamen et cognata cupis dinoscere signa,
quae iungant animos et amica sorte ferantur,
Lanigeri partus cum toto iunge trigono.
quotations.translation: But should you also wish to learn which related signs exchange affection and are subject to a destiny of friendship, connect the offspring of the Ram with all his trigon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
crebrius adversis odium est, cognata quadratis
corpora censentur signis et amica trigonis.
quotations.translation: Between opposite signs exists mostly hatred; and to quadrate signs are mostly ascribed ties of kinship, ties of friendship to trigonal signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
crebrius adversis odium est, cognata quadratis
corpora censentur signis et amica trigonis.
quotations.translation: Between opposite signs exists mostly hatred; and to quadrate signs are mostly ascribed ties of kinship, ties of friendship to trigonal signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
crebrius adversis odium est, cognata quadratis
corpora censentur signis et amica trigonis.
quotations.translation: Between opposite signs exists mostly hatred; and to quadrate signs are mostly ascribed ties of kinship, ties of friendship to trigonal signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: For special properties accrue to squares, to trigons, to the line which traverses six chords, and to that which cuts the midspace of the sky with diametric track;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: For special properties accrue to squares, to trigons, to the line which traverses six chords, and to that which cuts the midspace of the sky with diametric track;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
[cui parti nomen posuit, qui condidit artem,
octotropos; per quod stellae diversa volantes
quos reddant motus, proprio venit ordine rerum]
quotations.translation: The founder of astrology gave to this section the title Octotropos; the motions of the planets, which fly through it in the opposite direction, shall follow at the proper place.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
germanosve patris referam matrisque nepotes,
natorumve epulas conversaque sidera retro
ereptumque diem
quotations.translation: I shall not tell of them that were brethren to their father, grandchildren to their mother [i. e. Oedipus], or of sons [of Thyestes] served up at table [by Atreus], whereat the stars recoiled and took away the light of day.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
pars semper ut eidem
confinis parti vicinis staret in astris.
quotations.translation: ... that any portion would always stand next to the same portion in adjacent signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: horum operum sortes ad singula signa locavit
quotations.translation: The lots of these activities she allocated each to a sign
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Fortunae sors prima data est. hoc illa per artem
censetur titulo, quia maxima continet in se
fundamenta domus domuique haerentia cuncta:
quotations.translation: The first lot has been assigned to Fortune. This is the name by which it is known in astrology, because it contains in itself the chief essentials of the home and all that attaches to the name of home:
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
post hinc militiae locus est, qua quidquid in armis
quodque peregrinas inter versantibus urbes
accidere assuevit titulo comprenditur uno.
quotations.translation: Thereafter follows the abode of warfare, where under a single title is comprised whatever is likely to happen in war or befall those that are busied in foreign cities.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quidquid propositas inter facundia leges
efficit, hoc totum partem concessit in unam
atque, utcumque regunt dominantia sidera, paret.
quotations.translation: All that eloquence can achieve in debating proposed legislation is concentrated in a single part, and obeys the dictates of the dominating planets.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quintus coniugio gradus est per signa dicatus
et socios tenet
quotations.translation: Throughout the signs the fifth station is dedicated to wedlock and controls alliances
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ... sidera ut inclinant vires et templa gubernant.
quotations.translation: ... according as the planets modify and the temples direct the influence [of this seat].
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ... sidera ut inclinant vires et templa gubernant.
quotations.translation: ... according as the planets modify and the temples direct the influence [of this seat].
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Et, quoniam certo digestos orbe labores
nominaque in numerum viresque exegimus omnis
(athla vocant Grai, quae cuncta negotia rerum
in genera et partes bis sex divisa coercent),
nunc, quibus accedant signis quandoque, canendum est.
quotations.translation: Since I have expounded the fixed circle of activities arranged in order, with all their names and powers (athla is the Greek name for the sections which contain all the affairs of life arranged in twice six classes and portions), now must my poem tell to which signs they are attached at any given moment.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
perpetuas neque enim sedes eademve per omnis
sidera nascentis retinent, sed tempore mutant,
nunc huc nunc illuc signorum mota per orbem,
incolumis tamen ut maneat qui conditus ordo est.
quotations.translation: For they do not remain in permanent abodes or stay attached to the same stars for every person born, but they change them according to time, moving now hither, now thither, through the circle of signs, yet in such a way that the fixed order of succession remains intact.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Fortunae conquire locum per sidera cuncta
quotations.translation: look through the whole zodiac for the position of Fortune
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
qui tibi cum fuerit certa ratione repertus,
cetera praedicto subeuntibus ordine signis
coniunges, teneant proprias ut singula sede.
quotations.translation: When you have accurately determined this, then join the others in the prescribed order to the sequence of signs, so that each holds its appropriate abode.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
qui tibi cum fuerit certa ratione repertus,
cetera praedicto subeuntibus ordine signis
coniunges, teneant proprias ut singula sede.
quotations.translation: When you have accurately determined this, then join the others in the prescribed order to the sequence of signs, so that each holds its appropriate abode.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et, ne forte vagus Fortunae quaerere sedem
incipias, duplici certam ratione capesse.
quotations.translation: And lest perchance you err in essaying the quest for the seat of Fortune, learn its correct location by a twofold procedure.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
transverso Phoebus si cardine celsior ibit
qui tenet exortum vel qui demergit in undas,
per tempus licet affirmes natum esse diei.
quotations.translation: if the Sun is moving above that horizontal cardinal which holds it at its rising or that which plunges it into the waves, you may be sure that the birth takes place in time of day.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at, si subiectis senis fulgebit in astris
inferior dextra laevaque tenentibus orbem
cardinibus, noctis fuerit per tempora natu.
quotations.translation: But if it is shining in the six submerged signs, beneath the cardinal points which hold the world in place on left and right, then the birth falls within the hours of night.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
a sole ad lunam numerabis in ordine partes
signorum, ortivo totidem de cardine duces,
quem bene partitis memorant horoscopon astris.
quotations.translation: number the degrees of the signs in order from the Sun to the Moon and count off as many from that ascendant point which is found after careful plotting of the zodiac and is called the Horoscope.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
consule tum Phoeben imitantem lumina fratris
semper et in proprio regnantem tempore noctis;
quotations.translation: Seek guidance then from the Moon, who ever reflects her brother’s radiance and reigns in the hours of night, her own domain;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quotque ab ea Phoebus partes et signa recedit
tot numerare iubet fulgens horoscopos a se.
quotations.translation: as many degrees and signs as is distant the Sun from her, so many the shining Horoscope bids you number from itself.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hunc Fortuna locum teneat subeuntibus athlis,
ordine naturae sicut sunt cuncta locata.
quotations.translation: This place let Fortune hold with the other activities following, all positioned in their natural order.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Forsitan et quaeras, agili rem corde notandam,
qua ratione queas, natalis tempore, nati
exprimere immerso surgentem horoscopon orbe.
quotations.translation: Perhaps you will ask—and the question requires a nimble brain’s attention—how at the moment of birth it is possible to determine the native’s horoscoping degree as it rises from the submerged bowl of the heavens.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Forsitan et quaeras, agili rem corde notandam,
qua ratione queas, natalis tempore, nati
exprimere immerso surgentem horoscopon orbe.
quotations.translation: Perhaps you will ask—and the question requires a nimble brain’s attention—how at the moment of birth it is possible to determine the native’s horoscoping degree as it rises from the submerged bowl of the heavens.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed, quanta effectu, res est tam plena laboris
cursibus aeternis mundum per signa volantem,
ut totum lustret curvatis arcubus orbem,
exprimere et vultus eius componere certos
ac tantae molis minimum deprendere punctum:
quotations.translation: But it is a matter as laborious as important to represent, as it revolves with the zodiac in ceaseless motion, the passage of heaven with its arched quadrants through the whole circle, to depict its exact features, and to determine a minute point of so vast a structure
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.translation: But it is a matter as laborious as important to represent, as it revolves with the zodiac in ceaseless motion, the passage of heaven with its arched quadrants through the whole circle, to depict its exact features, and to determine a minute point of so vast a structure
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae pars exortum vel quae fastigia mundi
obtineat summi demersosve aequoris undis
auferat occasus aut imo sederit orbe.
quotations.translation: the degree in which the ascendant or that in which the summit of the sky on high is situated, or that by which, sinking into the waters of the deep, the setting is appropriated, or that which rests on the circle’s bottom.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ... ut propius nodis aliquod vel longius astrum est.
quotations.translation: ... according as a sign is either nearer to the equinoctial points or farther off.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: sic media extremis pugnant extremaque summis.
quotations.translation: Thus the middle signs are at variance with the end ones, and the lowest with the highest.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc age, quot stadiis et quanto tempore surgant
sidera, quotque cadant, animo cognosce sagaci
quotations.translation: Now learn with a perceptive mind how many stades and how much time the stars take to rise and set
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nam, qua Phrixei ducuntur vellera signi
Chelarumque fides iustaeque examina Librae,
omnia consurgunt binas ibi signa per horas
quotations.translation: For in lands beneath the line where revolve the fleece of the Phrixean sign and the impartial Claws and Libra’s just balance, all signs occupy two hours in rising
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

nam, qua Phrixei ducuntur vellera signi

quotations.translation: For in lands beneath the line where revolve the fleece of the Phrixean sign and the impartial Claws and Libra’s just balance, all signs occupy two hours in rising
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ... litoreumne coquat Cancrum contrane feratur
quotations.translation: ... whether it roasts the shore-haunting Crab or is borne in the opposite sign
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et paribus spatiis per singula lustra resurgunt
quotations.translation: and their risings through individual arcs take uniform periods
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ac bene diviso mundus latet orbe patetque.
quotations.translation: and due to the perfect bisection of the Earth the sky is half hidden and half visible.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ac bene diviso mundus latet orbe patetque.
quotations.translation: and due to the perfect bisection of the Earth the sky is half hidden and half visible.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed, quantum inflexeris orbem,
tantum inclinabit caeli positura volantis
quotations.translation: But in proportion as you tilt the Earth, so will the axis of the rotating heavens incline
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed, quantum inflexeris orbem,

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et modo quae fuerant surgentia limite recto
sidera curvato ducentur in aethera tractu,
quotations.translation: and the signs which had just now risen in a vertical arc will now be drawn into the air over an inclined track
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et modo quae fuerant surgentia limite recto

quotations.translation: and the signs which had just now risen in a vertical arc will now be drawn into the air over an inclined track
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
atque erit obliquo signorum balteus orbe
qui transversus erat, statio quando illius una est,
nostrae mutantur sedes.
quotations.translation: and the baldric of signs which had just now moved from side to side across heaven will now move in an oblique orbit, since its location remains constant, whilst ours changes.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ultima quae fulgent, celeris merguntur in umbras.
quotations.translation: those that shine farthest away swiftly sink into the darkness.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tam magis effugiunt oculos brumalia signa,
vixque ortis occasus erit.
quotations.translation: so much the more do the winter signs recede from sight, and they have scarcely risen when they set.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
si longius inde
procedat, totis condentur singula membris 
ricenasque trahent conexo tempore noctes
et totidem luces adiment.
quotations.translation: If one proceed still farther, each one in all of its parts will be hidden and will bring thirty nights of consecutive duration and take away as many days.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.translation: If one proceed still farther, each one in all of its parts will be hidden and will bring thirty nights of consecutive duration and take away as many days.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
pluraque, per partes surrepto tempore, signa
quaerentur medio terrae celata tumore
quotations.translation: And as by degrees the time is snatched away, more signs will become invisible, concealed by the intervening curve of the Earth:
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hic erit una dies per senos undique menses
dimidiumque trahens contextis lucibus annum
numquam erit occiduus quod tanto tempore Phoebus
dum bis terna suis perlustrat cursibus astra,
sed circum volitans recto versabitur orbe.
quotations.translation: Everywhere here a single day will last six months, a day which will keep a half year in continuous light, for in all this time, during which his course will take him through six signs, Phoebus will never set but will rotate in circling flight around the erect heavens.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nam quisquis spectat ab axe,
dimidium e toto mundi videt orbe rotundi,
pars latet inferior
quotations.translation: For whoever looks out from the pole sees half of the whole sphere of the rounded heavens, whilst the lower is hidden;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
neque enim circumvenit illum
recta acies, mediaque tenus distenditur alvo.
quotations.translation: for the direct line of vision does not encompass the sky, but extends only as far as the extremity of its bulge.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: [κα]ὶ Λέ̣ων καὶ Τοξ[ό]της ἀ[κο]ύου[σ]ιν ἀλλήλων κα[ὶ] Ζυγὸς καὶ Κρειός.
quotations.translation: Leo and Sagittarius also hear each other, and Libra and Aries.

quotations.original:
titulus, quem Graecia fecit,
Daemonium signat dignas pro nomine vire.
quotations.translation: Daemonium is the name the Greeks have given it, denoting influences fitting the name.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Perspice nunc tenuem visu rem, pondere magnam
et tantum Graio signari nomine passam,
dodecatemoria, in titulo signantia causas.
nam, cum tricenas per partes sidera constent,
rursus bis senis numerus diducitur omnis;
ipsa igitur ratio binas in partibus esse
dimidiasque docet partes.
quotations.translation: Pray examine now a matter trivial in appearance, yet one of great moment, which does not permit description of itself save by a Greek word. I speak of the dodecatemories, of which the name proclaims the principle. The signs each consist of thirty degrees, and every total is further divided by twice six; the calculation therefore shows that in each division there are two and a half degrees.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
septima censetur saevis horrenda periclis,
si male subscribunt stellae per signa locatae.
quotations.translation:
The seventh is accounted grim with danger dire,
if the planets located in the signs ill accord.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hac in parte dies atque hac momenta dabuntur,
si bene convenient stellae per signa sequentes;
quotations.translation: this is the portion in which day and hour for decision shall be given, if the planets as they move through the zodiac are favourably situated.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
hic locus in binas annum noctesque diesque
per duo partitae dirimit divortia terrae.
quotations.translation: Such a place twice separates the year into night and day, once in each hemisphere of the divided Earth.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
at quae nocturnis fuerit mensura tenebris
in totidem partes simili ratione secanda est,
ut, quantum una ferat, tantum tribuatur ad ortus
temporis averso nascenti sidere Tauro.
quotations.translation: and the measurement of night’s darkness is likewise to be divided into as many parts, so that the time of one portion is to be assigned to the Bull’s rising when his hind-foremost constellation is born.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
has inter quasque accipiet Nemeeius horas
quod discrimen erit, per tris id divide partes
quotations.translation: Divide the difference between these hours and those received by the Nemean into three parts
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
has inter quasque accipiet Nemeeius horas
quod discrimen erit, per tris id divide partes
quotations.translation: Divide the difference between these hours and those received by the Nemean into three parts
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tertia ut accedat Geminis, qua tempora Tauri
vincant
quotations.translation: let one of these three parts be given to the Twins, so that they may exceed by it the hours of the Bull
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed certa sub lege, prioris semper ut astri
incolumem servent summam crescantque novando.
quotations.translation: but under the strict condition that they ever preserve intact the sum of the former sign and grow by accumulating.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
his usque ad Chelas horarum partibus aucta
per totidem e Libra decrescent sidera partes.
quotations.translation: With these fractions of hours the signs increase as far as the Claws; with the same gradations they will decrease after Libra.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
his usque ad Chelas horarum partibus aucta
per totidem e Libra decrescent sidera partes.
quotations.translation: With these fractions of hours the signs increase as far as the Claws; with the same gradations they will decrease after Libra.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quodque his exsuperat demptis id ducito in aequas
sex partes, sextamque ardenti trade Leoni.
quotations.translation: When this subtraction has been carried out, divide the remainder into six equal parts, and hand over a sixth to the blazing Lion.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quodque his exsuperat demptis id ducito in aequas
sex partes, sextamque ardenti trade Leoni.
quotations.translation: When this subtraction has been carried out, divide the remainder into six equal parts, and hand over a sixth to the blazing Lion.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quodque his exsuperat demptis id ducito in aequas
sex partes, sextamque ardenti trade Leoni.
quotations.translation: When this subtraction has been carried out, divide the remainder into six equal parts, and hand over a sixth to the blazing Lion.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
