quodque his exsuperat demptis id ducito in aequas
sex partes, sextamque ardenti trade Leoni.
quotations.translation: When this subtraction has been carried out, divide the remainder into six equal parts, and hand over a sixth to the blazing Lion.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: in nulla fallet regione horoscopos umquam
quotations.translation: in no latitude will the Horoscope ever elude you
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc, quibus hiberni momentis surgere menses
incipiant (neque enim paribus per sidera cuncta
procedunt gradibus, nivei dum vellera signi
contingant aequum luces cogentia et umbras
ferre iugum), magna est ratio breviterque docenda.
quotations.translation: Now let me explain with what increments the days of the winter months begin to grow; for not with equal gradation in every sign do they increase in their journey to the spotless fleece of the sign which forces day and darkness to shoulder the same yoke: the principle is important, yet may be briefly taught.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc, quibus hiberni momentis surgere menses
incipiant (neque enim paribus per sidera cuncta
procedunt gradibus, nivei dum vellera signi
contingant aequum luces cogentia et umbras
ferre iugum), magna est ratio breviterque docenda.
quotations.translation: Now let me explain with what increments the days of the winter months begin to grow; for not with equal gradation in every sign do they increase in their journey to the spotless fleece of the sign which forces day and darkness to shoulder the same yoke: the principle is important, yet may be briefly taught.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Qui duodecim ventos esse dixerunt, hoc secuti sunt totidem ventorum esse quot caeli discrimina.
quotations.translation: Those who say there are twelve winds follow this reasoning: there are the same number of winds as there are sectors of the sky.
quotations.publication: Seneca. Natural Questions, Volume II: Books 4-7. Translated by Thomas H. Corcoran. Loeb Classical Library 457. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1972.

quotations.translation: First you must measure in hours the shortest day and the longest night spent by Capricorn;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: totum in partes ita digere tempus.
quotations.translation: into these amounts must you apportion the whole time.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
namque Aries totidem deducit noctibus horas
quot prius abstulerant proprio sub nomine Pisces,
quotations.translation: For the Ram deducts as many hours from the nights as the Fishes had previously taken away on their own account
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
namque Aries totidem deducit noctibus horas
quot prius abstulerant proprio sub nomine Pisces,
quotations.translation: For the Ram deducts as many hours from the nights as the Fishes had previously taken away on their own account
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: This is the sequence in which the nights diminish and the days increase from the constellation of midwinter, and in which the year’s cycle revolves until the solstice takes place at the sign of the lingering Crab;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: This is the sequence in which the nights diminish and the days increase from the constellation of midwinter, and in which the year’s cycle revolves until the solstice takes place at the sign of the lingering Crab;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Illa etiam poterit nascens via ducere ad astrum
quod quandoque vadis emissum redditur orbi.
quotations.translation: The following method will also be able to guide you to the rising sign that at any given moment is released from ocean and given to the earth.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
atque hunc numerum revocabis in ipsum
multiplicans decies, adiectis insuper eidem
quinque tamen summis
quotations.translation: and [you must] repeatedly heap this number on itself by multiplying it ten times, adding to the amount, however, a further five times
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
atque hunc numerum revocabis in ipsum
multiplicans decies, adiectis insuper eidem
quinque tamen summis
quotations.translation: and [you must] repeatedly heap this number on itself by multiplying it ten times, adding to the amount, however, a further five times
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ex hac tricenas summa per sidera partes
distribues, primamque vicem, quo Phoebus in astro
fulserit, inde aliis, solem quaecumque sequentur.
quotations.translation: From this total you must distribute thirty degrees to each sign, the first portion to the sign in which the Sun is shining, then to the others as they follow in the wake of the Sun.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tricenas dabis ex illa per singula signa,
donec deficiat numerus;
quotations.translation: give thirty degrees of it to each sign, until the number fails [= is less than 30]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quaque ille sub astri
parte cadet, credas illam cum corpore natam
esse hominis pariterque orbem vidisse per umbras.
quotations.translation: and in whatever degree of a constellation it runs out, this, you can be confident, was born together with the native’s body and, at the same time as the native, beheld the earth through the darkness.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
fallere non possint summi fastigia caeli,
non celeres obitus, stent fundamenta sub imo
quotations.translation: the zenith of heaven on high will not be able to elude you, nor the swift a setting, and the foundations will be correctly fixed at the nadir
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: stent veri stellarum obitus verique subortus
quotations.translation: the true settings and true risings of the planets stand [correctly fixed]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Luna dabit menses, peragit quod menstrua cursum.
quotations.translation: The Moon shall denote the months, since in a month it completes its course.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tutelaeque suae primas horoscopos horas
asserit atque dies, traditque sequentibus astris.
quotations.translation: The Horoscope brings under its regency the first days and the first hours, and hands the others to the following signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et, quamquam socia nascantur origine cuncta,
diversas tamen esse vices
quotations.translation: however, even though all the periods proceed from a common origin, the sequences are dissimilar
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod tardius illa,
haec citius peragant orbem
quotations.translation: because some periods are slower, some quicker to complete the circle.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod tardius illa,
haec citius peragant orbem
quotations.translation: because some periods are slower, some quicker to complete the circle.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
difficile est in idem tempus concurrere cuncta,
unius ut signi pariter sit mensis et annus
atque dies atque hora simul: sibi discrepat ordo.
quotations.translation: It would be difficult for all the periods to revolve concurrently in the same time, so that together in a single sign the same year and month and day and hour coincide: the cycle of time is at variance with itself.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quod nunc illa nimis properant, nunc illa morantur
quotations.translation: The reason is that now these speed ahead, these lag behind;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quod nunc illa nimis properant, nunc illa morantur
quotations.translation: The reason is that now these speed ahead, these lag behind;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Scorpios aequabit tribuentem dona Leonem.
Centauri fuerint eadem quae munera Cancri.
quotations.translation:
Scorpion will equal the Lion’s bounty of gifts.
The award of the Centaur will be the same as the Crab’s.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Scorpios aequabit tribuentem dona Leonem.
Centauri fuerint eadem quae munera Cancri.
quotations.translation:
Scorpion will equal the Lion’s bounty of gifts.
The award of the Centaur will be the same as the Crab’s.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ter quinos, Capricorne, dares, si quattuor essent
appositi menses.
quotations.translation: You, Capricorn, would donate thrice five years, were four months added.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
triplicabit Aquarius annos
quattuor et menses vitam producet in octo.
quotations.translation: The Waterman will treble four years and prolong life a further eight months.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
templa quoque et partes caeli sua munera norunt
et proprias tribuunt certo discrimine summas,
cum bene constiterit stellarum conditus ordo.
quotations.translation: the temples and portions of the sky also have gifts of their own to bestow, and impart in a precise gradation their respective amounts, when the configuration formed by the planets proves auspicious.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
templa quoque et partes caeli sua munera norunt
et proprias tribuunt certo discrimine summas,
cum bene constiterit stellarum conditus ordo.
quotations.translation: the temples and portions of the sky also have gifts of their own to bestow, and impart in a precise gradation their respective amounts, when the configuration formed by the planets proves auspicious.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed mihi templorum tantum nunc iura canentur;
mox veniet mixtura suis cum viribus omnis,
cum bene materies steterit percognita rerum
non interpositis turbatarum undique membris.
quotations.translation: But I now shall sing only of the ordinances of the temples; later the whole complex design will appear with its full force, when the constituent parts of the universe are firmly grasped and not made confusing with portions scattered everywhere.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
bis quadragenos occasus dives in actus
solis erat, numero nisi desset olympias una.
quotations.translation: The setting were rich in twice forty circuits of the Sun, were not one lustrum lacking from the count.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod fuerit laevum praelataque signa sequetur
tricenos annos duplicat, tris insuper addit.
quotations.translation: The trigon on the left and following in the wake of the preceding signs doubles thirty years and adds three over and above.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod fuerit laevum praelataque signa sequetur
tricenos annos duplicat, tris insuper addit.
quotations.translation: The trigon on the left and following in the wake of the preceding signs doubles thirty years and adds three over and above.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quaeque super signum nascens a cardine primum
tertia sors manet et summo iam proxima caelo
haec ter vicenos geminat, tris abstrahit annos.
quotations.translation: And the temple which is separated by one intervening sign from the first sign rising at the cardinal point and which is now next to heaven’s peak, this multiplies a score by three and takes three years away.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quaeque super signum nascens a cardine primum
tertia sors manet et summo iam proxima caelo
haec ter vicenos geminat, tris abstrahit annos.
quotations.translation: And the temple which is separated by one intervening sign from the first sign rising at the cardinal point and which is now next to heaven’s peak, this multiplies a score by three and takes three years away.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae tropica appellant, quod in illis quattuor anni
tempora vertuntur signis nodosque resolvunt
quotations.translation: They are called tropic signs, since in them turn the four seasons of the year and untie the bonds which fasten them together;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae tropica appellant, quod in illis quattuor anni
tempora vertuntur signis nodosque resolvunt
quotations.translation: They are called tropic signs, since in them turn the four seasons of the year and untie the bonds which fasten them together;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cancer ad aestivae fulget fastigia zonae
extenditque diem summum parvoque recessu
destruit et, quanto fraudavit tempore luces,
in tantum noctes auget: stat summa per omnis.
quotations.translation: Gleaming in summer’s topmost circle, Cancer prolongs the day to its greatest length and then shortens it in retreating by small degrees, increasing night by the amount which it stole from day: for the sum of day and night remains constant.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cancer ad aestivae fulget fastigia zonae
extenditque diem summum parvoque recessu
destruit et, quanto fraudavit tempore luces,
in tantum noctes auget: stat summa per omnis.
quotations.translation: Gleaming in summer’s topmost circle, Cancer prolongs the day to its greatest length and then shortens it in retreating by small degrees, increasing night by the amount which it stole from day: for the sum of day and night remains constant.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cancer ad aestivae fulget fastigia zonae
extenditque diem summum parvoque recessu
destruit et, quanto fraudavit tempore luces,
in tantum noctes auget: stat summa per omnis.
quotations.translation: Gleaming in summer’s topmost circle, Cancer prolongs the day to its greatest length and then shortens it in retreating by small degrees, increasing night by the amount which it stole from day: for the sum of day and night remains constant.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Proxima in effectum et similis referentia motus
esse ferunt luces aequantia signa tenebris.
quotations.translation: Close to these in their influence and displaying variation similar to each other are, they say, the signs which level the hours of light and darkness.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Huic ex adverso simili cum sorte refulget
Libra diem noctemque pari cum foedere ducens
quotations.translation: Opposite the Ram the Balance shines back at it: its lot is like the Ram’s, for it treats day and night on equal terms
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
una dies sub utroque aequat sibi tempore noctem,
dum Libra atque Aries autumnum verque figurant;
quotations.translation: One day alone at either season makes equal to itself the night, while the Scales and Ram are shaping autumn and spring;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae quater et cum ter centum vicenaque constent,
detrahitur summae tota pars, quota demitur usque
omnibus ex horis aestivae nomine noctis,
solstitium summo peragit cum Phoebus Olympo.
quotations.translation: The stades amount in all to four times and to thrice a hundred, plus twenty, and from the total is subtracted a fraction proportionate to that which every year is subtracted from the day’s full hours for the credit of midsummer night, when the Sun accomplishes his solstice in the heights of heaven.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: lustra decem tribuent solis cum mensibus octo.
quotations.translation: they shall impart ten revolutions of the Sun together with eight months.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quemque locum superat nascens horoscopos, ille
dena quater revocat vertentis tempora solis
accumulatque duos cursus iuvenemque relinquit.
quotations.translation: That place, above which stands the rising Horoscope, four times repeats ten seasons of the revolving Sun and heaps thereon two courses, and leaves one still a young man.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc tibi signorum mores summumque colorem
et studia et varias artes ex ordine reddam.
quotations.translation: Now shall I declare to you in due order the characters, the predominant quality, the pursuits, and the different skills which the signs impart.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc tibi signorum mores summumque colorem
et studia et varias artes ex ordine reddam.
quotations.translation: Now shall I declare to you in due order the characters, the predominant quality, the pursuits, and the different skills which the signs impart.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: non alio potius genitus sit Servius astro
quotations.translation: Under no other sign would Servius more fittingly have been born
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, quibus in bifero Centauri corpore sors est
nascendi concessa, libet subiungere currus
ardentis et equos ad mollia ducere frena
quotations.translation: But they whose lot it is to be born under the Centaur of double form delight in yoking a team, in bringing a fiery horse to obey the pliant reins
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quippe etiam mundi faciem sedesque movebit
sidereas caelumque novum versabit in orbem.
quotations.translation: Why, water will even set in motion the face of heaven and the starry habitations, and will cause the skies to move in a novel rotation.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: They who issue from this sign are a gentle sort and a lovable breed, and no meanness of heart is theirs; they are prone to suffer losses; and of riches they have neither need nor surfeit. Even thus doth the urn’s stream flow.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
bene noverit orbem
fluminaque et portus, mundum ventosque, necesse est
iamque huc atque illuc agilem convertere clavum
et frenare ratem fluctusque effundere rector,
iam remis agere et lentas inflectere tonsas.
quotations.translation: The pilot must have sound knowledge of the earth, its rivers and havens, its climate and winds; how on the one hand to ply the mobile helm this way and that, and brake the ship and spread apart the waves, and how on the other to drive the ship by rowing and to feather the lingering blades.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
bene noverit orbem
fluminaque et portus, mundum ventosque, necesse est
iamque huc atque illuc agilem convertere clavum
et frenare ratem fluctusque effundere rector,
iam remis agere et lentas inflectere tonsas.
quotations.translation: The pilot must have sound knowledge of the earth, its rivers and havens, its climate and winds; how on the one hand to ply the mobile helm this way and that, and brake the ship and spread apart the waves, and how on the other to drive the ship by rowing and to feather the lingering blades.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Hos tribuunt mores atque has nascentibus artes
bis sex materia propria pollentia signa.
quotations.translation: These are the characters and these the skills which the twelve signs, by virtue of the powers its substance gives to each, bestow on men born under them.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Sed nihil in semet totum valet: omnia vires
cum certis sociant signis sub partibus aequis
et velut hospitio mundi commercia iungunt
conceduntque suas partes retinentibus astris.
quotations.translation: But no sign has exclusive control over itself: all share their powers with certain signs in equal portions, and in a spirit of hospitality, as it were, they form a heavenly fellowship and surrender the parts of which they are composed to the keeping of other signs.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quam partem Graiae dixere decanica gentes.
quotations.translation: This department of our art the Greeks have termed the system of decans.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
a numero nomen positum est, quod partibus astra
condita tricenis triplici sub sorte feruntur
et tribuunt denas in se coeuntibus astris
inque vicem ternis habitantur sidera signis.
quotations.translation: The name is derived from the numeral, since the signs, which consist of thirty degrees, enjoy a tripartite arrangement and allot ten degrees to each of the signs associating with themselves, the constellations one after the other providing a home for three signs each.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
verum aliis alia opposita est et fallit imago
mentiturque suas vires et munera celat.
quotations.translation: but the shape of one sign is placed in front of and conceals others, and dissimulates and hides its real influences and gifts.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
verum aliis alia opposita est et fallit imago

quotations.translation: but the shape of one sign is placed in front of and conceals others, and dissimulates and hides its real influences and gifts.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
verum aliis alia opposita est et fallit imago
mentiturque suas vires et munera celat.
quotations.translation: but the shape of one sign is placed in front of and conceals others, and dissimulates and hides its real influences and gifts.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc quae sint coniuncta quibus quove ordine reddam,
ne lateant aliae vires aliena per astra.
quotations.translation: Now shall I tell which signs are joined to which, and in what sequence, lest the influences which others exercise in signs foreign to them go unperceived.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
namque Aries primam partem sibi vindicat ipsi,
altera sors Tauro, Geminis pars tertia cedit.
quotations.translation: The Ram claims his first decan for himself, the second portion falls to the Bull, the third decan to the Twins.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sidera sic inter divisum dicitur astrum
totque dabit vires dominos quotcumque recepit.
quotations.translation: Thus the constellation is said to have been distributed among the signs, and it will exert the influences of as many masters as it has received.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
natura per astrum
stat tamen et proprias miscet per singula vires.
quotations.translation: Yet the Bull’s nature persists throughout his sign and blends his peculiar influences in every section.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
natura per astrum
stat tamen et proprias miscet per singula vires.
quotations.translation: Yet the Bull’s nature persists throughout his sign and blends his peculiar influences in every section.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: namque Aries primam partem sibi vindicat ipsi
quotations.translation: The Ram claims his first decan for himself
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: altera sors Tauro, Geminis pars tertia cedit.
quotations.translation: the second portion falls to the Bull, the third decan to the Twins.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: altera sors Tauro, Geminis pars tertia cedit.
quotations.translation: the second portion falls to the Bull, the third decan to the Twins.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et, ne forte vagus Fortunae quaerere sedem
incipias, duplici certam ratione capesse.
quotations.translation: And lest perchance you err in essaying the quest for the seat of Fortune, learn its correct location by a twofold procedure.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Libra decem partes Geminorum prima capessit
quotations.translation: The Balance is first to appropriate ten degrees of the Twins
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Scorpios adiunctas; Centauri tertia pars est
quotations.translation: Scorpio [claims] the adjacent [ten degrees]; the third decan is the Centaur’s
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Cancer in adversum Capricorni derigit astrum
quotations.translation: The Crab proffers twice five degrees to Capricorn’s opposite sign first
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cancer in adversum Capricorni derigit astrum
bis quinas primum partes, dignatus in illo
temporis articulo sub quo censetur et ipse,
quotations.translation: The Crab proffers twice five degrees to Capricorn’s opposite sign first, for in the latter he is deemed worthy of the seasonal juncture with which Capricorn himself is assessed
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod facit aequalis luces brumalibus umbris
cognatamque gerit diverso in cardine legem
quotations.translation: because in winter he makes the daylight equal to the darkness and at his opposite cardinal-point observes a kindred law
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quod facit aequalis luces brumalibus umbris
cognatamque gerit diverso in cardine legem
quotations.translation: because in winter he makes the daylight equal to the darkness and at his opposite cardinal-point observes a kindred law
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: alterius partis perfundit Aquarius ignes
quotations.translation: the fires of the second decan are bedewed by the Waterman
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: But the Lion, mindful of his partner under the trigon’s law, welcomes the Ram as leader, and next the Bull, who is united to him by square
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: But the Lion, mindful of his partner under the trigon’s law, welcomes the Ram as leader, and next the Bull, who is united to him by square
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
veris iuga temperat ille,
haec autumnalis componit lucibus umbras
quotations.translation: the Ram regulates the scales of spring, while the Balance matches autumn’s nights with autumn’s days.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
fontibus aeternis gaudens urnaque fluenti
iura sui Librae permittit prima regenda
quotations.translation: He that rejoices in the never-ending stream that pours from his urn transfers control of the first rights over himself to the Balance
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: haerentisque decem partes Nepa vindicat ipsi
quotations.translation: whilst the adjoining ten degrees are claimed by the Scorpion
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: summas Centaurus retinet iuvenale per astrum
quotations.translation: the last degrees in the young man’s sign are occupied by the Centaur
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et genus externum referunt aliena per astra
quotations.translation: that born under signs alien to their natures they display the qualities of other stars
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec tantum lanas Aries nec Taurus aratra
nec Gemini Musas nec merces Cancer amabit,
nec Leo venator veniet nec Virgo magistra,
mensuris aut Libra potens aut Scorpios armis
Centaurusque feris, igni Capricornus et undis
ipse suis Iuvenis geminique per aequora Pisces;
quotations.translation: Not only in wool will the Ram take pleasure, the Bull in the plough, the Twins in the Muses, or the Crab in trade; nor will the Lion come forth as a hunter only, or as a teacher the Maid; not only over measures will the Balance preside, the Scorpion over arms, the Centaur over beasts, Capricorn over fire, the Youth over his own waters, or over the seas the Fishes twain
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec satis est signis dominantia discere signa
per denos numeros et quae sint insita cuique;
quotations.translation: But it is not enough to learn of signs that hold sway in the decans of other signs, and which signs are thus installed in each;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nec satis est signis dominantia discere signa
per denos numeros et quae sint insita cuique;
quotations.translation: But it is not enough to learn of signs that hold sway in the decans of other signs, and which signs are thus installed in each;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed proprias partes ipsas spectare memento
vel glacie rigidas vel quas exusserit ignis,
et sterilis sine utroque tamen, quas largior umor
quasve minor iusto vitiat.
quotations.translation: But it is not enough to learn of signs that hold sway in the decans of other signs, and which signs are thus installed in each; you must be sure to notice individual degrees which are themselves either numbed with ice or scorched by fire and some which, though free from either of these defects, are nevertheless sterile, being marred by excessive or insufficient moisture.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
namque omnia mixtis
viribus et vario consurgunt sidera textu.
quotations.translation: For all the signs that rise possess a mixture of influences and a variety of texture.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ut signum signo, sic a se discrepat ipsum
momentoque negat vires usumque salubrem
quotations.translation: just as sign is at variance with sign, so it is at variance with itself, and but a minute shift causes it to withhold its influences and salutary effects
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
ut signum signo, sic a se discrepat ipsum
momentoque negat vires usumque salubrem
quotations.translation: just as sign is at variance with sign, so it is at variance with itself, and but a minute shift causes it to withhold its influences and salutary effects
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: accipe damnandae quae sint per sidera partes.
quotations.translation: Learn then of the degrees, sign by sign, which merit condemnation.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Lanigeri pars quarta nocet nec sexta salubris;
quotations.translation: The fourth degree of the Ram inflicts harm, and the sixth is also unwholesome;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Lanigeri pars quarta nocet nec sexta salubris;
quotations.translation: The fourth degree of the Ram inflicts harm, and the sixth is also unwholesome;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
unaque viginti numeris pars addita laedit
et quinta et duram consummans septima partem.
quotations.translation: added to the count of a score one degree is damaging, so too a fifth and a seventh, the last completing the adverse portion of the sign.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
unaque viginti numeris pars addita laedit
et quinta et duram consummans septima partem.
quotations.translation: added to the count of a score one degree is damaging, so too a fifth and a seventh, the last completing the adverse portion of the sign.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Tauri nona mala est, similis cui tertia pars est
quotations.translation: The ninth degree of the Bull is malign, and the third after the tenth is like it
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quaeque decem trisque ingeminat fraudatque duobus
triginta numeros et tu, tricesima summa, es.
quotations.translation: as well as that which doubles three and ten, that which robs of two the count of thirty, and you, O number thirty.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quaeque decem trisque ingeminat fraudatque duobus
triginta numeros et tu, tricesima summa, es.
quotations.translation: as well as that which doubles three and ten, that which robs of two the count of thirty, and you, O number thirty.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Pestifera in Geminis pars prima et tertia signi
quotations.translation: Baneful in the Twins are the first and third degrees of the sign
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: septima non melior, ter quintae noxia par est
quotations.translation: the seventh is no better, and the hurt of the treble-fifth is just as great
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: unaque bis denis brevior nocet unaque maior
quotations.translation: injurious are the degrees numbering one less than and one more than twice ten
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: unaque bis denis brevior nocet unaque maior
quotations.translation: injurious are the degrees numbering one less than and one more than twice ten
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et similis noxae veniet vicesima quinta
cumque duae subeunt vel cum se quattuor addunt.
quotations.translation: whilst the coming of the twenty-fifth will prove equally harmful, both of itself and when two or four are added to it.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nec Cancri prima immunis nec tertia pars est;
nec sexta
quotations.translation: Neither first nor third nor sixth degree of the Crab b is free from ill
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
decimaque peracta
prima rapit
quotations.translation: after the completion of a decade the first [degree] carries off its prey
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
septima post decimam luctum et vicesima portat
et quinta accedens et septima nonaque summa.
quotations.translation: the seventeenth brings grief, so does the twentieth, and also the fifth, seventh, and ninth degrees following.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Tu quoque contactu primo, Nemeaee, timendus,
et quarta sub parte premis;
quotations.translation: With you, too, Lion of Nemea, first contact is to be dreaded, and fearful is the onset of your fourth degree;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
e tribus appositis vitiat totidemque secutis
ultima, nec prima melior tricesima pars est.
quotations.translation: of the following three the last brings infection, and so does the last of a further three, whilst the thirtieth is no improvement on the first.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ad decimam nec quarta nec octava utilis umquam
quotations.translation: nor [are useful] of the second decade the first, fourth, and eighth
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: proxima viginti numeris et quarta timenda est
quotations.translation: beyond a count of twenty the first and fourth are full of terror
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Et quinta in Chelis et septima inutilis exstat,
quotations.translation: In the Balance the fifth confers no benefit, nor does the seventh;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Scorpios in prima reus est
quotations.translation: The Scorpion is arraigned in his first degree
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
undecimam geminans et quae vicesima quinta est
octavoque manet numero nonumque capessit.
quotations.translation: [bad are] the double of the eleventh, and of the twenties the fifth, that which resides at number eight, and the occupant of nine.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sex bisve peractis
octo, bis aut denis, metuendus dicitur aer
quotations.translation: double six or eight or ten, the atmosphere is termed fraught with dread;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Nec pars optanda est Capricorni septima
quotations.translation: The seventh of Capricorn is not a degree to be desired
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Hae partes sterilem ducunt et frigore et igni
aera vel sicco vel quod superaverit umor
quotations.translation: These degrees are allotted an atmosphere made sterile by reason of cold and fire or because of drought or superabundant moisture
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ubi se summis Aries extollet ab undis
quotations.translation: when the Ram emerges above the surface of the waves
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, quos prima creant nascentis sidera Tauri,
feminei incedunt.
quotations.translation: But they who are given life by the rising of the Bull’s foremost stars walk with an effeminate gait.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Pleiadum parvo referens glomeramine sidus
quotations.translation: for it [Taurus] brings with it the stars of the Pleiades massed in a tiny cluster
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, niger obscura Cancer cum nube feretur
qua velut exustus Phoebeis ignibus ignis
deficit et multa fuscat caligine sidus,
lumina deficient partus, geminamque creatis
mortem fata dabunt: se quisque et vivit et effert.
quotations.translation: But when that part of the Crab rises which is dimmed by a sombre cloud, where his own fire fails, as though burnt out by the Sun’s, and darkens the signs with impenetrable fog, the sight of those born then will fail, and fate will condemn them to death twice over: each one buries himself while still alive.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.original: Scorpios extremae cum tollet lumina caudae [...]
quotations.translation: When the Scorpion uplifts the stars which shine at the end of its tail [...]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nec non Arcitenens, prima cum veste resurgit,
pectora clara dabit bello
quotations.translation: As for the Archer, when the foremost portion of his cloak rises, he will give birth to hearts renowned in war
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Quod si quem sanctumque velis castumque probumque
hic tibi nascetur cum primus Aquarius exit.
quotations.translation: But if you would have a man that is pious, pure, and good, you will find him born when the first portion of the Waterman rises above the horizon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc age diversis dominantia sidera terris
percipe.
quotations.translation: Now you must learn the constellations which bear dominion over the several parts of the earth.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
asper ab axe ruit Boreas, fugit Eurus ab ortu,
Auster amat medium solem Zephyrusque profectum.
quotations.translation: Biting Boreas rushes from the pole whilst Eurus comes flying from the dawn: Auster delights in the midday sun and Zephyrus in the sun’s departure.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ipsa natat tellus pelagi lustrata corona
quotations.translation: The land itself is afloat, encircled by the crown of ocean
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: ac sua cuique dedit tutelae regna per orbem
quotations.translation: To each guardian power he has given a special region of the world to rule
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Cancrum inter gelidumque Caprum per tempora veris
quotations.translation: in springtime halfway between the Crab and chilly Capricorn
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Euxinus Scythicos pontus sinuatus in arcus
sub Geminis te, Phoebe, colit
quotations.translation: The Euxine sea, the shores of which curve in the shape of a Scythian bow, worships you, Phoebus, in the person of the Twins
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.translation: You, Lion of Nemea, attendant of the Idaean mother, hold sway over Phrygia, the warlike realm of the Cappadocians, and the mountain-ridges of Armenia
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Hesperiam sua Libra tenet
quotations.translation: Italy belongs to the Balance
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
inferius victae sidus Carthaginis arces
et Libyam Aegyptique latus donataque rura
Cyrenes lacrimis radicis Scorpios acris
eligit
quotations.translation: Scorpio, the sign beneath, chooses the towers of vanquished Carthage, Libya, the flank of Egypt, and the territory of Cyrene, gifted with the tears of a pungent root
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cnosia Centauro tellus circumdata ponto
paret
quotations.translation: The sea-girt land of Cnossus is subject to the Centaur
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Percipe nunc etiam quae sint ecliptica Graio
nomine, quod certos quasi delassata per annos
non numquam cessant sterili torpentia motu.
quotations.translation: Mark now, too, the signs which are, to use a Greek term, ecliptic, because over certain periods of years, as though worn out with toil, they sometimes lag with unavailing movement and fail.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
extremumque sequi pontum terraeque subire
pendentis tractus et toto vivere in orbe.
quotations.translation: to make for Ocean’s farthest horizon, descend to the inverted parts of the Earth, and inhabit the whole wide world.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
extremumque sequi pontum terraeque subire

quotations.translation: to make for Ocean’s farthest horizon, descend to the inverted parts of the Earth, and inhabit the whole wide world.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
saepe fit ut, mitis tulerint qui sideris annum,
asperioris agant mensem;
quotations.translation: It oft happens that those who have drawn the year of a gentle sign are passing the month of a harsher one
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
saepe fit ut, mitis tulerint qui sideris annum,
asperioris agant mensem;
quotations.translation: It oft happens that those who have drawn the year of a gentle sign are passing the month of a harsher one
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν καὶ τὰ μεγέθη τῶν ἡμερῶν ἴσα ἐστὶν ἐν Διδύμοις καὶ ἐν Καρκίνῳ, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὡροσκοπίοις αἱ ὑπὸ τῶν γνωμόνων γραφόμεναι γραμμαὶ ἴσον ἀπέχουσι τοῦ θερίνου τροπικοῦ καὶ ἐν Καρκίνῳ καὶ ἐν Διδύμοις· ἐξ ἴσου γὰρ κεῖται πρὸς τὸ θερινὸν σημεῖον τὰ δύο δωδεκατημόρια.
quotations.translation: For this reason the lengths of the days are equal in Gemini and in Cancer, and also on the sundials the lines described by the gnomons are equally far from the summer tropic both in Cancer and in Gemini: for the two ‘twelfth parts’ lie in an equal way in relation to the summer point.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Πρόδηλον δὲ τοῦτο καὶ ἐκ τῶν σκιοθήρων· τὸ γὰρ ἄκρον τῆς τοῦ γνώμονος σκιᾶς σχεδὸν ἐφ’ ἡμέρας μ ἐπιμένει ταῖς τροπικαῖς γραμμαῖς.
quotations.translation: And this is evident from the sundials too: for the tip of the gnomon’s shadow stays on the tropical lines for approximately 40 days.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Πᾶσαν οὖν τὴν ἀλήθει[αν] ἡμῖν ἐξετίθι καὶ ἐπ[ὶ το]ῦ ἔργου ἐδίκνυον ἐ[κ το]ῦ ὅλμου τοῦ λιθίνου [ὃς ἐκ]αλεῖτο Ἑλληνιστὶ [γν]ώμων.
quotations.translation: He then expounded to us the whole truth and showed it in practice from the stone cylinder, which was called “gnomon” in Greek.
quotations.publication: Grenfell, B.P. & A.S. Hunt, 1906. The Hibeh papyri, Vol. 1. London: The Egypt Exploration Fund.

quotations.original: ἀβέλιον· ἥλιον. Κρῆτες
quotations.translation: Abelios: Sun. Cretans.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.
quotations.comment: The form is given by Hesychius in the accusative.

quotations.original: ἀβελιακόν· ἡλιακόν. Παμφύλιοι
quotations.translation: abeliakos: solar. Pamphylians.
quotations.publication: Hesychius Alexandrinus. 2018. Hesychii Alexandrini Lexicon, Vol. 1 (A - Delta), ed. I.C. Cunningham. Berlin, Boston: Walter de Gruyter.

quotations.original: Νυνὶ δὲ κατώτερον φέρεται ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ἐπὶ ἐκκέντρου κύκλου κινεῖται, καθάπερ ὑπογέγραπται· οὐ γὰρ τὸ αὐτὸ κέντρον ἐστὶ τοῦ ἡλιακοῦ κύκλου καὶ τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ, ἀλλ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἓν μέρος παρῆκται ἡ τοῦ ἡλίου σφαῖρα. Διὰ δὲ τὴν τοιαύτην θέσιν εἰς δ μέρη ἄνισα διαιρεῖται ὁ ἡλιακὸς δρόμος· (...)
quotations.translation: Now, the Sun passes lower and moves upon an eccentric cycle, as has been indicated: for the centre of the solar circle is not the same as that of the zodiacal circle, but the sphere of the Sun is shifted to one side. And due to a position like this, the solar course is divided into 4 unequal parts; (...)
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: τοῦ ἐν τῶι νώιτωι λα̣μπροῦ ἀστέρος βορειότερος δακτύλο̣[ι]ς δυσί
quotations.translation: (Jupiter was in Cancer …) two fingers north of the bright star in the back (of the Crab [Cancer])

quotations.original: Ἑρμῆς Τοξότῃ μοιρῶν ι̅γ̣̅ λεπτῶ̣ν ν̅γ̅, οἶκος Διός, ὁ̣ρ̣ίοις Ἀφ[ρο]δίτης, μον[ο]μοιρίας Ἄ̣ρεως
quotations.translation: Mercury (was) in Sagittarius, at 13 degrees 53 minutes, a house of Jupiter, terms of Venus, monomoiria of (i.e., single degree assigned to) Mars
quotations.publication: D. Greenbaum and A. Jones, P.Berl. 9825: An elaborate horoscope for 319 CE and its significance for Greek astronomical and astrological practice (ISAW Papers 12 [2017])

quotations.original: λειτουρ̣[γ]ο̣ὶ̣ σ̣ε̣μ̣ν̣ο̣ὶ̣ τρεῖς π̣ε̣ρίεισιν ἕνα | ὡρονό̣[μον] κρατερόν· περὶ γὰρ τὸ ζῴδιον οὗτοι | ἐννέα λειτουργοὶ [ἀ]ν̣τολίην ἔλαχον
quotations.translation: Three august ministers (i.e., subdecans) accompany one mighty hour-apportioner (i.e., decan): for throughout the zodiac sign these nine ministers have their rising
quotations.publication: P. Schubert, Anoubion. Poème astrologique. Témoinages et fragments (Paris, 2015)

quotations.original:
caeloque rediret
ac per descensum medios percurreret ignes
Saturni, Iovis et Martis Solisque, sub illis
post Venerem et Maia natum te, Luna, vagantem.
quotations.translation: Here would another leave the celestial sphere and make his descent through the intervening fires of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and the Sun, and you, O Moon, beneath them, whose wandering path follows Venus and Maia’s son.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et ratis heroum, quae nunc quoque navigat astris
quotations.translation: the heroes’ ship that amid the stars sails even now
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Fluminaque errantis late sinuantia flexus
quotations.translation: the Rivers whose winding coils meander far and wide
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et biferum Cetos squamis atque ore tremendo
quotations.translation: the Whale which with its scales and dread jaws has part of two creatures
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Cetus has the scaly tail (and rear) of a fish, the jaws (and front) of a land animal.

quotations.original: Hesperidumque vigil custos et divitis auri
quotations.translation: the wakeful warder of the Hesperides and the golden treasure
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et Iuppiter alite tectus
quotations.translation: and Jupiter in swan’s disguise
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quid valeant ortu, quid cum merguntur in undas
quotations.translation: which influences they exert both when rising and when they sink into the waves
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: quid valeant ortu, quid cum merguntur in undas
quotations.translation: their influences both when rising and when they sink into the waves
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: et quota de bis sex astris pars quaeque reducat
quotations.translation: and which degree of the zodiac brings each of them back above the horizon
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
nunc quoque vicinam puppi, ceu naviget, Argo
a dextri lateris ducit regione per astra.
quotations.translation: even now draws Argo by the poop to its side, as though still on the seas, through the stars on its right.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
sed tum prima suos puppis consurgit in ignes,
quattuor in partes cum Corniger extulit ora.
quotations.translation: But the foremost part of the poop emerges to show its fires only when the Ram has brought four degrees of his countenance above the horizon.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
illa quisquis erit terris oriente creatus,
rector erit puppis
quotations.translation: Whoever is born on earth at the rising of Argo will be the captain of a ship;
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quo fulgente super terras caelumque trahente
ementita diem nigras nox contrahit alas
quotations.translation: when [Orion] shines over the horizon drawing heaven in his train, night feigns the brightness of day and folds its dusky wings.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Sed, cum se terris Aries ter quinque peractis
partibus extollit, primum iuga tollit ab undis
Heniochus clivoque rotas convellit ab imo,
qua gelidus Boreas aquilonibus instat acutis.
quotations.translation: But when the Ram raises himself above the earth with thrice five degrees completed, then straightway the Charioteer lifts his team from ocean and wrests his wheels up from the downward slope of the horizon where icy Boreas lashes us with his bitter blasts.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Sed, cum bis denas augebit septima partes
Lanigeri, surgent Hyades.
quotations.translation: The Hyades will rise when twenty degrees of the Ram are augmented by a seventh.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Ultima Lanigeri cum pars excluditur orbi,
quae totum ostendit terris atque eruit undis,
Olenie servans praegressos tollitur Haedos
egelido stellata polo, qua dextera pars est,
officio magni mater Iovis.
quotations.translation: When the zodiac releases the Ram’s last degree, which thus displays the whole of him to the earth, plucking him from Ocean’s waves, there rises the Olenian goat, keeping watch over the Kids which stray ahead, enstarred on the right in the cold north sky for her services as foster-mother of mighty Jove.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quae totum ostendit terris atque eruit undis,

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quibus aspirantibus almam
in lucem eduntur Bacchi Venerisque sequaces
perque dapes mensasque super petulantia corda
et sale mordaci dulcis quaerentia risus.
quotations.translation: Beneath their influence devotees of Bacchus and Venus are born into the kindly light, and people whose insouciance runs free at feasts and banquets and who strive to provoke sweet mirth with biting wit.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nunc Cancro vicina canam, cui parte sinistra
consurgunt Iugulae.
quotations.translation: Next shall I sing of the neighbours of the Crab. On its left rise the stars of the Belt.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: "The word ought to signify collar-bone, and so (but in the singular) Varro, De Ling. Lat. 7. 50, interprets it: there is, however, no star or group of stars between Orion’s shoulders (α and γ) which can plausibly be so designated." (Goold 1977: 314)

quotations.original:
exoritur candens latratque Canicula flammas
et rabit igne suo geminatque incendia solis
quotations.translation: the brilliant constellation of the Dog appears: it barks forth flame, raves with its fire, and doubles the burning heat of the sun
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
exoritur candens latratque Canicula flammas
et rabit igne suo geminatque incendia solis
quotations.translation: the brilliant constellation of the Dog appears: it barks forth flame, raves with its fire, and doubles the burning heat of the sun
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: talis effinget Crater umoris amator.
quotations.translation: Such are the men to be fashioned by the Bowl, lover of all that is wet.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Iam subit Erigone. quae cum tibi quinque feretur
partibus ereptis ponto, tollentur ab undis
clara Ariadnaeae quondam monumenta coronae
et mollis tribuent artes.
quotations.translation: Next to rise is Erigone. When you behold her ascending with five degrees wrested from the sea, there will emerge from the waves the bright memorial of what was once e Ariadne’s crown; and gentle will be the skills herefrom bestowed
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Quattuor appositis Centaurus partibus effert
sidera et ex ipso mores nascentibus addit.
quotations.translation: After a further four degrees the Centaur rears his stars and from his own nature assigns qualities to his progeny.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Quattuor appositis Centaurus partibus effert
sidera et ex ipso mores nascentibus addit.
quotations.translation: After a further four degrees the Centaur rears his stars and from his own nature assigns qualities to his progeny.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Arcitenens cum se totum produxerit undis,
ter decima sub parte feri formantibus astris
plumeus in caelum nitidis Olor evolat alis.
quotations.translation: When the Archer has fully emerged from the waves, the Swan ascends into heaven with this creature’s thirtieth degree, its down and glittering wings figured by stars.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Anguitenens magno circumdatus orbe draconis,
cum venit in regione tuae, Capricorne, figurae,
non inimica facit serpentum membra creatis.
quotations.translation: When Ophiuchus, encircled by the serpent’s great coils, rises beside the figure of Capricorn, he renders the forms of snakes innocuous to those born under him.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Anguitenens magno circumdatus orbe draconis,
cum venit in regione tuae, Capricorne, figurae,
non inimica facit serpentum membra creatis.
quotations.translation: When Ophiuchus, encircled by the serpent’s great coils, rises beside the figure of Capricorn, he renders the forms of snakes innocuous to those born under him.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, cum se patrio producens aequore Piscis
in caelumque ferens alienis finibus ibit, [...]
quotations.translation: But when the Southern Fish rises into the heavens, leaving its native waters for a foreign element, [...]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Cumque Fidis magno succedunt sidera mundo
quaesitor scelerum veniet vindexque reorum,
qui commissa suis rimabitur argumentis
in lucemque trahet tacita latitantia fraude.
quotations.translation: When the constellation of the Lute rises into the mighty heavens, there shall be born a man to investigate wrong-doing and punish the guilty: he will get to the bottom of crimes by sifting the evidence for them and bring to light all that lies hidden under the silence of deceit.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: Manilius here (mis-)understands Fides as Fidicula, which is a torture device.

qui commissa suis rimabitur argumentis
