quotations.translation: When the constellation of the Lute rises into the mighty heavens, there shall be born a man to investigate wrong-doing and punish the guilty: he will get to the bottom of crimes by sifting the evidence for them and bring to light all that lies hidden under the silence of deceit.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Caeruleus ponto cum se Delphinus in astra
erigit et squamam stellis imitantibus exit,
ambiguus terrae partus pelagique creatur.
quotations.translation: When the sea-dark Dolphin ascends from Ocean to the heavens and emerges with its scales figured by stars, birth is given to children who will be equally at home on land and in the sea.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, cum Cassiope bis denis partibus actis
aequorei iuvenis dextra de parte resurgit, [...]
quotations.translation: When after the appearance of twenty degrees of the watery youth Cassiope a rises on his right, [...]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, cum Cassiope bis denis partibus actis
aequorei iuvenis dextra de parte resurgit, [...]
quotations.translation: When after the appearance of twenty degrees of the watery youth Cassiopea rises on his right, [...]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
At, cum Cassiope bis denis partibus actis
aequorei iuvenis dextra de parte resurgit, [...]
quotations.translation: When after the appearance of twenty degrees of the watery youth Cassiope a rises on his right, [...]
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Piscibus exortis cum pars vicesima prima
signabit terrae limen, fulgebit et orbi,
aerius nascetur Equus caeloque volabit
quotations.translation: When the twenty-first degree of the rising Fishes illuminates earth’s threshold and shines upon the world, the winged Horse will appear and gallop aloft in the heavens.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
Nixa genu species et Graio nomine dicta
Engonasin, cui nulla fides sub origine constat,
dextra per extremos attollit lumina Pisces.
quotations.translation: The figure on bended knee and called by the Greek name of Engonasin, about whose origin no certainty prevails, brings forth its stars on the right simultaneously with the last portion of the Fishes.
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: tertia Pleiadas dotavit forma sorores
quotations.translation: The third magnitude has provided the dowry of the Pleiad sisters
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: invenitque parem sub te, Cynosura, colorem
quotations.translation: It includes as of like degree your brightness, Lesser Bear
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: invenitque parem sub te, Cynosura, colorem
quotations.translation: It includes as of like degree your brightness, Lesser Bear
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
et quos Delphinus iaculatur quattuor ignes
Deltotonque tribus facibus, similique nitentem
luce Aquilam et flexos per lubrica terga dracones.
quotations.translation: and the fires which the Dolphin emits from its four torches and the Triangle from its three; and, as shining with similar brightness, the Eagle and the snakes with their slippery coils
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tum quartum sextumque genus discernitur omni
e numero, summamque gradus qui iungit utramque
quotations.translation: Then out of all the remaining stars one distinguishes a fourth class and a sixth, and the degree which lies between these two magnitudes
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: signaque transgressus permutat tempora Phoebus
quotations.translation: and when, after its passage through the signs, the Sun renews the seasons of the year
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
tum conferta licet caeli fulgentia templa cernere
seminibus minimis totumque micare
stipatum stellis mundum
quotations.translation: Then may one see heaven’s shining temples teeming with minute points of light and the whole firmament sparkle with dense array of stars
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: maximus est populus summo qui culmine fertur
quotations.translation: But outnumbering all these is the populace which revolves about heaven's dome
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original:
quae neque per cunctas noctes neque tempore in omni
resplendet vasto caeli summota profundo
quotations.translation: sunk in the vast depths of heaven they shine neither every night nor in every season
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.

quotations.original: Olenie servans praegressos tollitur Haedos
quotations.translation: there rises the Olenian goat, keeping watch over the Kids which stray ahead
quotations.publication: Manilius. Astronomica. Edited and translated by G. P. Goold. Loeb Classical Library 469. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1977.
quotations.comment: "Olenian either as being on the left arm (ὠλένη) of the Charioteer, or as the daughter of Olenus (Schol. Aratus, Phaen. 164), or from Olenus in Achaea, its residence (Strabo 8. 7. 5)." (Goold 1977: 310)

quotations.original: נִלְאֵ֖ית בְּרֹ֣ב עֲצָתָ֑יִךְ יַעַמְדוּ־נָ֨א וְיוֹשִׁיעֻ֜ךְ (הברו) [הֹבְרֵ֣י] שָׁמַ֗יִם הַחֹזִים֙ בַּכּ֣וֹכָבִ֔ים מֽוֹדִעִים֙ לֶחֳדָשִׁ֔ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖אוּ עָלָֽיִךְ׃
quotations.transliteration: nilʾêt̲ bərōb̲ ʿăṣāt̲āyik̲ yaʿamd̲û-nāʾ wəyôšîʿuk̲ (hb̲rw) [hōb̲ərê] šāmayim haḥōzîm bakkôk̲āb̲îm môd̲iʿîm leḥŏd̲āšîm mēʾăšer yāb̲ōʾû ʿālāyik̲.
quotations.translation:
You are helpless, despite all your art.
Let them stand up and help you now,
The scanners of heaven, the star-gazers,
Who announce, month by month,
Whatever will come upon you.

quotations.original: תִּסְפֹּ֣ר יְרָחִ֣ים תְּמַלֶּ֑אנָה וְ֝יָדַעְתָּ֗ עֵ֣ת לִדְתָּֽנָה׃
quotations.transliteration: tispōr yərāḥîm təmalleʾnāh wəyād̲aʿtā ʿēt̲ lid̲tānāh.
quotations.translation:
Can you count the months they must complete?
Do you know the season they give birth,

quotations.original: אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾim-ʾerʾeh ʾôr kî yāhēl wəyārēaḥ yāqār hōlēk̲.
quotations.translation:
If ever I saw the light shining,
The moon on its course in full glory,

quotations.original: וְהָיָ֤ה אוֹר־הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃
quotations.transliteration: wəhāyāh ʾôr-halləb̲ānāh kəʾôr haḥammāh wəʾôr haḥammāh yihyeh šib̲ʿāt̲ayim kəʾôr šib̲ʿat̲ hayyāmîm bəyôm ḥăb̲ōš YHWH ʾet̲-šeb̲er ʿammô ûmaḥaṣ makkāt̲ô yirpāʾ.
quotations.translation: And the light of the moon shall become like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall become sevenfold, like the light of the seven days, when GOD binds up the wounds of this people and heals the injuries it has suffered.

quotations.original: וְהָיָ֤ה אוֹר־הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃
quotations.transliteration: wəhāyāh ʾôr-halləb̲ānāh kəʾôr haḥammāh wəʾôr haḥammāh yihyeh šib̲ʿāt̲ayim kəʾôr šib̲ʿat̲ hayyāmîm bəyôm ḥăb̲ōš YHWH ʾet̲-šeb̲er ʿammô ûmaḥaṣ makkāt̲ô yirpāʾ.
quotations.translation: And the light of the moon shall become like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall become sevenfold, like the light of the seven days, when GOD binds up the wounds of this people and heals the injuries it has suffered.

quotations.original: וְהָיָ֤ה אוֹר־הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃
quotations.transliteration: wəhāyāh ʾôr-halləb̲ānāh kəʾôr haḥammāh wəʾôr haḥammāh yihyeh šib̲ʿāt̲ayim kəʾôr šib̲ʿat̲ hayyāmîm bəyôm ḥăb̲ōš ʾăd̲ōnāi ʾet̲-šeb̲er ʿammô ûmaḥaṣ makkāt̲ô yirpāʾ.
quotations.translation: And the light of the moon shall become like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall become sevenfold, like the light of the seven days, when GOD binds up the wounds of this people and heals the injuries it has suffered.

quotations.original: אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾim-ʾerʾeh ʾôr kî yāhēl wəyārēaḥ yāqār hōlēk̲.
quotations.translation:
If ever I saw the light shining,
The moon [moving] on its course in full glory,

quotations.original: אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾim-ʾerʾeh ʾôr kî yāhēl wəyārēaḥ yāqār hōlēk̲.
quotations.translation:
If ever I saw the light shining,
The moon on its course in full glory,

quotations.original: וְהָי֤וּ לִמְאוֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהָאִ֖יר עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
quotations.transliteration: wəhāyû limʾôrōt̲ birqîaʿ haššāmayim ləhāʾîr ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wayhî-k̲ēn.
quotations.translation: and they shall serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.

quotations.original: וּמִן־אָ֡ז חָדַ֜לְנוּ לְקַטֵּ֨ר לִמְלֶ֧כֶת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְהַסֵּֽךְ־לָ֥הּ נְסָכִ֖ים חָסַ֣רְנוּ כֹ֑ל וּבַחֶ֥רֶב וּבָרָעָ֖ב תָּֽמְנוּ׃
quotations.transliteration: ûmin-ʾāz ḥād̲alnû ləqaṭṭēr limlek̲et̲ haššāmayim wəhassēk̲-lāh nəsāk̲îm ḥāsarnû k̲ōl ûb̲aḥereb̲ ûb̲ārāʿāb̲ tāmənû.
quotations.translation: But ever since we stopped making offerings to the Queen of Heaven and pouring libations to her, we have lacked everything, and we have been consumed by the sword and by famine.
quotations.comment:
Identified with Venus by Albani 2004: 186.

Albani, Matthias. 2004. ‘„Kannst du die Sternbilder hervortreten lassen zur rechten Zeit...?“ (Hi 38,32) Gott und Gestirne im Alten Testament und im Alten Orient’. In Das biblische Weltbild und seine altorientalischen Kontexte, edited by Bernd Janowski, Nachdr., Studienausg, 181–226. Forschungen zum Alten Testament 32. Tübingen: Mohr Siebeck.

quotations.original: וַֽיהֹוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם אַחֲרֵי֙ הִפָּֽרֶד־ל֣וֹט מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֑ם צָפֹ֥נָה וָנֶ֖גְבָּה וָקֵ֥דְמָה וָיָֽמָּה׃
quotations.transliteration: waYHWH ʾāmar ʾel-ʾab̲rām ʾaḥărê hippāred̲-lôṭ mēʿimmô śāʾ nāʾ ʿênêk̲ā ûrəʾēh min-hammāqôm ʾăšer-ʾattāh šām ṣāp̲ōnāh wāneg̲bāh wāqēd̲əmāh wāyāmmāh.
quotations.translation: And יהוה said to Abram, after Lot had parted from him, “Raise your eyes and look out from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west,

quotations.original: וְֽ֭אָמַרְתָּ מַה־יָּ֣דַֽע אֵ֑ל הַבְעַ֖ד עֲרָפֶ֣ל יִשְׁפּֽוֹט׃
quotations.transliteration: wəʾāmartā mah-yād̲aʿ ʾēl hab̲ʿad̲ ʿărāp̲el yišpôṭ.
quotations.translation:
You say, “What can God know?
Can He govern through the dense cloud?

quotations.original: בְּ֭רוּחוֹ שָׁמַ֣יִם שִׁפְרָ֑ה חֹלְלָ֥ה יָ֝ד֗וֹ נָחָ֥שׁ בָּרִֽחַ׃
quotations.transliteration: bərûḥô šāmayim šip̲rāh ḥōləlāh yād̲ô nāḥāš bāriaḥ.
quotations.translation:
By His wind the heavens were calmed;
His hand pierced the Elusive Serpent.
quotations.comment:
Identified with Hydra or Draco by Halpern (2002: 257). Schiaparelli (1904: 65f.) finds this implausible.

Halpern, Baruch. 2002. ‘Assyrian and pre-Socratic Astronomies and the Location of the Book of Job’. Orbis biblicus et orientalis 186. Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht. https://www.zora.uzh.ch/id/eprint/141560.
Schiaparelli, Giovanni. 1904. Die Astronomie im Alten Testament. Translated by Willy Lüdtke. Gießen: J. Rickersche Verlagsbuchhandlung. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783111665474.

quotations.original: מִי־שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חׇכְמָ֑ה א֤וֹ מִֽי־נָתַ֖ן לַשֶּׂ֣כְוִי בִינָֽה׃
quotations.transliteration: mî-šāt̲ baṭṭuḥôt̲ ḥok̲māh ʾô mî-nāt̲an laśśek̲wî b̲înāh.
quotations.translation:
Who put wisdom in the ṭḥwt?
Who gave understanding to śkwy (Perseus?)?
quotations.comment:
Identified as Perseus by Halpern (2002: 261).

Halpern, Baruch. 2002. ‘Assyrian and pre-Socratic Astronomies and the Location of the Book of Job’. In Kein Land für sich allein: Studien zum Kulturkontakt in Kanaan, Israel/Palästina und Ebirnâri für Manfred Weippert zum 65. Geburtstag, edited by Ulrich Hübner and Ernst Axel Knauf, 255–64. Orbis biblicus et orientalis 186. Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht. https://www.zora.uzh.ch/id/eprint/141560.

quotations.original: הֲ֭יָדַעְתָּ חֻקּ֣וֹת שָׁמָ֑יִם אִם־תָּשִׂ֖ים מִשְׁטָר֣וֹ בָאָֽרֶץ׃
quotations.transliteration: hăyād̲aʿtā ḥuqqôt̲ šāmāyim ʾim-tāśîm mišṭārô b̲āʾāreṣ.
quotations.translation:
Do you know the inscribings of heaven
Or impose its authority on earth?
quotations.comment:
See Halpern (2002: 261).

Halpern, Baruch. 2002. ‘Assyrian and pre-Socratic Astronomies and the Location of the Book of Job’. In Kein Land für sich allein: Studien zum Kulturkontakt in Kanaan, Israel/Palästina und Ebirnâri für Manfred Weippert zum 65. Geburtstag, edited by Ulrich Hübner and Ernst Axel Knauf, 255–64. Orbis biblicus et orientalis 186. Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht. https://www.zora.uzh.ch/id/eprint/141560.

quotations.original: וּשְׁטָחוּם֩ לַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵ֜חַ וּלְכֹ֣ל ׀ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲהֵב֜וּם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲבָדוּם֙ וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ הָלְכ֣וּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר דְּרָשׁ֔וּם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם לֹ֤א יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִקָּבֵ֔רוּ לְדֹ֛מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה יִהְיֽוּ׃
quotations.transliteration: ûšəṭāḥûm laššemeš wəlayyārēaḥ ûlək̲ōl  ṣəb̲āʾ haššāmayim ʾăšer ʾăhēb̲ûm waʾăšer ʿăb̲ād̲ûm waʾăšer hālək̲û ʾaḥărêhem waʾăšer dərāšûm waʾăšer hištaḥăwû lāhem lōʾ yēʾāsəp̲û wəlōʾ yiqqāb̲ērû ləd̲ōmen ʿal-pənê hāʾăd̲āmāh yihyû
quotations.translation: and exposed to the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven that they loved and served and followed, to which they turned and bowed down. They shall not be gathered for reburial; they shall become dung upon the face of the earth.

quotations.original: אִיתַ֨י גְּבַ֜ר בְּמַלְכוּתָ֗ךְ דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֣ין קַדִּישִׁין֮ בֵּהּ֒ וּבְיוֹמֵ֣י אֲב֗וּךְ נַהִיר֧וּ וְשׇׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחׇכְמָ֥ה כְּחׇכְמַת־אֱלָהִ֖ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת בֵּ֑הּ וּמַלְכָּ֤א נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּר֙ אֲב֔וּךְ רַ֧ב חַרְטֻמִּ֣ין אָֽשְׁפִ֗ין כַּשְׂדָּאִין֙ גָּזְרִ֔ין הֲקִימֵ֖הּ אֲב֥וּךְ מַלְכָּֽא׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾît̲ai gəb̲ar bəmalk̲ût̲āk̲ dî rûaḥ ʾĕlāhîn qaddîšîn bēh ûb̲əyômê ʾăb̲ûk̲ nahîrû wəśok̲lət̲ānû wəḥok̲māh kəḥok̲mat̲-ʾĕlāhîn hištək̲aḥat̲ bēh ûmalkāʾ nəb̲uk̲ad̲neṣṣar ʾăb̲ûk̲ rab̲ ḥarṭummîn ʾāšəp̲în kaśdāʾîn gāzərîn hăqîmēh ʾăb̲ûk̲ malkāʾ.
quotations.translation: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him; in your father’s time, illumination, understanding, and wisdom like that of the gods were to be found in him, and your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, appointed him chief of the magicians, exorcists, Chaldeans, and diviners.

quotations.original: וְהַ֨מַּשְׂכִּלִ֔ים יַזְהִ֖רוּ כְּזֹ֣הַר הָרָקִ֑יעַ וּמַצְדִּיקֵי֙ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים כַּכּוֹכָבִ֖ים לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: wəhammaśkilîm yazhirû kəzōhar hārāqîaʿ ûmaṣdîqê hārabbîm kakkôk̲āb̲îm ləʿôlām wāʿed̲.
quotations.translation: And the knowledgeable will be radiant like the bright expanse of sky, and those who lead the many to righteousness will be like the stars forever and ever.

quotations.original: אֶרְאֶ֙נּוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א עַתָּ֔ה אֲשׁוּרֶ֖נּוּ וְלֹ֣א קָר֑וֹב דָּרַ֨ךְ כּוֹכָ֜ב מִֽיַּעֲקֹ֗ב וְקָ֥ם שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמָחַץ֙ פַּאֲתֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב וְקַרְקַ֖ר כׇּל־בְּנֵי־שֵֽׁת׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾerʾennû wəlōʾ ʿattāh ʾăšûrennû wəlōʾ qārôb̲ dārak̲ kôk̲āb̲ miyyaʿăqōb̲ wəqām šēb̲eṭ miyyiśrāʾēl ûmāḥaṣ paʾăt̲ê môʾāb̲ wəqarqar kol-bənê-šēt̲.
quotations.translation:
What I see for them is not yet,
What I behold will not be soon:
A star rises from Jacob,
A scepter comes forth from Israel;
It smashes the brow of Moab,
The foundation of all children of Seth.

quotations.original: מִן־הַ֭חֶדֶר תָּב֣וֹא סוּפָ֑ה וּֽמִמְּזָרִ֥ים קָרָֽה׃
quotations.transliteration: min-haḥed̲er tāb̲ôʾ sûp̲āh ûmimmizrayim [ûmimməzārîm] qārāh.
quotations.translation:
The storm wind comes from its chamber,
And the cold from the [northern] constellations.
quotations.comment: Identified with the northern polar constellations by Schiaparelli 1904: 63.

quotations.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֗הוּ זֶה־לְּךָ֤ הָאוֹת֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהֹוָ֔ה כִּ֚י יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהֹוָ֔ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר הָלַ֤ךְ הַצֵּל֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֔וֹת אִם־יָשׁ֖וּב עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃
quotations.transliteration: wayyōʾmer yəšaʿyāhû zeh-lək̲ā hāʾôt̲ mēʾēt̲ YHWH kî yaʿăśeh YHWH ʾet̲-haddāb̲ār ʾăšer dibbēr hālak̲ haṣṣēl ʿeśer maʿălôt̲ ʾim-yāšûb̲ ʿeśer maʿălôt̲.
quotations.translation: Isaiah replied, “This is the sign for you from GOD that GOD will do the thing that was promised: Shall the shadow advance ten steps or recede ten steps?”

quotations.original: הַבּוֹנֶ֤ה בַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ מַעֲלוֹתָ֔ו וַאֲגֻדָּת֖וֹ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ יְסָדָ֑הּ הַקֹּרֵ֣א לְמֵֽי־הַיָּ֗ם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכֵ֛ם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ יְהֹוָ֥ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: habbôneh b̲aššāmayim maʿălôt̲āw waʾăg̲uddāt̲ô ʿal-ʾereṣ yəsād̲āh haqqōrēʾ ləmê-hayyām wayyišpək̲ēm ʿal-pənê hāʾāreṣ YHWH šəmô.
quotations.translation:
Who built the chambers in heaven
And founded the vault on the earth,
Who summons the waters of the sea
And pours them over the land—
Whose name is  GOD.

quotations.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן הִֽנֵּה־חֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ מָחָ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֛י יָשֹׁב־אֵשֵׁ֥ב עִם־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וְשִׁלַּחְתַּ֙נִי֙ וְנִסְתַּרְתִּ֣י בַשָּׂדֶ֔ה עַ֖ד הָעֶ֥רֶב הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁית׃
quotations.transliteration: wayyōʾmer dāwid̲ ʾel-yəhônāt̲ān hinnēh-ḥōd̲eš māḥār wəʾānōk̲î yāšōb̲-ʾēšēb̲ ʿim-hammelek̲ leʾĕk̲ôl wəšillaḥtanî wənistartî b̲aśśād̲eh ʿad̲ hāʿereb̲ haššəlišît̲.
quotations.translation: David said to Jonathan, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and I am to sit with the king at the meal. Instead, let me go and I will hide in the countryside until the third evening.

quotations.original: וַיִּקָּ֨הֲל֜וּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ כׇּל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּיֶ֥רַח הָאֵתָנִ֖ים בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃
quotations.transliteration: wayyiqqāhălû ʾel-hammelek̲ šəlōmōh kol-ʾîš yiśrāʾēl bəyeraḥ hāʾēt̲ānîm beḥāg̲ hûʾ haḥōd̲eš haššəb̲îʿî.
quotations.translation: The entire body of Israel gathered before King Solomon at the Feast [of Booths], in the month of Ethanim—that is, the seventh month.

quotations.original: וּבַשָּׁנָה֩ הָאַחַ֨ת עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה בְּיֶ֣רַח בּ֗וּל ה֚וּא הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י כָּלָ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת לְכׇל־דְּבָרָ֖יו וּלְכׇל־מִשְׁפָּטָ֑ו וַיִּבְנֵ֖הוּ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃
quotations.transliteration: ûb̲aššānāh hāʾaḥat̲ ʿeśrēh bəyeraḥ bûl hûʾ haḥōd̲eš haššəmînî kālāh habbayit̲ lək̲ol-dəb̲ārāyw ûlək̲ol-mišpāṭāw wayyib̲nēhû šeb̲aʿ šānîm.
quotations.translation: and in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul—that is, the eighth month—the House was completed according to all its details and all its specifications. It took him seven years to build it.

quotations.original: אֶת־חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב כִּי־ב֖וֹ יָצָ֣אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹא־יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾet̲-ḥag̲ hammaṣṣôt̲ tišmōr šib̲ʿat̲ yāmîm tōʾk̲al maṣṣôt̲ kaʾăšer ṣiwwît̲ik̲ā ləmôʿēd̲ ḥōd̲eš hāʾāb̲îb̲ kî-b̲ô yāṣāʾt̲ā mimmiṣrāyim wəlōʾ-yērāʾû p̲ānai rêqām.
quotations.translation: You shall observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread—eating unleavened bread for seven days as I have commanded you—at the set time in the month of Abib, for in it you went forth from Egypt; and none shall appear before Me empty-handed;

quotations.original: וַיְהִ֣י בִשְׁמוֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָ֣ה וְאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת שָׁנָ֡ה לְצֵ֣את בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מֵאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֩יִם֩ בַּשָּׁנָ֨ה הָרְבִיעִ֜ית בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ זִ֗ו ה֚וּא הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י לִמְלֹ֥ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּ֥בֶן הַבַּ֖יִת לַיהֹוָֽה׃
quotations.transliteration: wayhî b̲išmônîm šānāh wəʾarbaʿ mēʾôt̲ šānāh ləṣēʾt̲ bənê-yiśrāʾēl mēʾereṣ-miṣrayim baššānāh hārəb̲îʿît̲ bəḥōd̲eš ziw hûʾ haḥōd̲eš haššēnî limlōk̲ šəlōmōh ʿal-yiśrāʾēl wayyib̲en habbayit̲ laʾd̲ōnāi.
quotations.translation: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites left the land of Egypt, in the month of Ziv—that is, the second month—in the fourth year of his reign over Israel, Solomon began to build the House of GOD.

quotations.original: דִּבְרֵ֥י נְחֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חֲכַלְיָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י בְחֹֽדֶשׁ־כִּסְלֵו֙ שְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָֽה׃
quotations.transliteration: dib̲rê nəḥemyāh ben-ḥăk̲alyāh wayhî b̲əḥōd̲eš-kislēw šənat̲ ʿeśrîm waʾănî hāyît̲î bəšûšan habbîrāh.
quotations.translation:
The narrative of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah:
In the month of Kislev of the twentieth year, when I was in the fortress of Shushan,

quotations.original: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֗ן שְׁנַ֥ת עֶשְׂרִ֛ים לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥סְתְּא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יַ֣יִן לְפָנָ֑יו וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶת־הַיַּ֙יִן֙ וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹא־הָיִ֥יתִי רַ֖ע לְפָנָֽיו׃
quotations.transliteration: wayhî  bəḥōd̲eš nîsān šənat̲ ʿeśrîm ləʾartaḥšastəʾ hammelek̲ yayin ləp̲ānāyw wāʾeśśāʾ ʾet̲-hayyayin wāʾettənāh lammelek̲ wəlōʾ-hāyît̲î raʿ ləp̲ānāyw.
quotations.translation: In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was set before him; I took the wine and gave it to the king—I had never been out of sorts in his presence.

quotations.original: וַיִּקָּרְא֣וּ סֹפְרֵֽי־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ בָּֽעֵת־הַ֠הִ֠יא בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ סִיוָ֗ן בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֮ בּוֹ֒ וַיִּכָּתֵ֣ב כְּֽכׇל־אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה מׇרְדֳּכַ֣י אֶל־הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים וְאֶ֣ל הָאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִֽים־וְהַפַּחוֹת֩ וְשָׂרֵ֨י הַמְּדִינ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ מֵהֹ֣דּוּ וְעַד־כּ֗וּשׁ שֶׁ֣בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּמֵאָה֙ מְדִינָ֔ה מְדִינָ֤ה וּמְדִינָה֙ כִּכְתָבָ֔הּ וְעַ֥ם וָעָ֖ם כִּלְשֹׁנ֑וֹ וְאֶ֨ל־הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים כִּכְתָבָ֖ם וְכִלְשׁוֹנָֽם׃
quotations.transliteration: wayyiqqārəʾû sōp̲ərê-hammelek̲ bāʿēt̲-hahîʾ baḥōd̲eš haššəlîšî hûʾ-ḥōd̲eš sîwān bišlôšāh wəʿeśrîm bô wayyikkāt̲ēb̲ kək̲ol-ʾăšer-ṣiwwāh mordŏk̲ai ʾel-hayyəhûd̲îm wəʾel hāʾăḥašdarpənîm-wəhappaḥôt̲ wəśārê hamməd̲înôt̲ ʾăšer  mēhōddû wəʿad̲-kûš šeb̲aʿ wəʿeśrîm ûmēʾāh məd̲înāh məd̲înāh ûməd̲înāh kik̲t̲āb̲āh wəʿam wāʿām kilšōnô wəʾel-hayyəhûd̲îm kik̲t̲āb̲ām wək̲ilšônām.
quotations.translation: So the king’s scribes were summoned at that time, on the twenty-third day of the third month, that is, the month of Sivan; and letters were written, at Mordecai’s dictation, to the Jews and to the satraps, the governors and the officials of the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India to Nubia: to every province in its own script and to every people in its own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.

quotations.original: וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לֶאֱל֑וּל לַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנַ֖יִם יֽוֹם׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: wattišlam haḥômāh bəʿeśrîm waḥămiššāh leʾĕlûl laḥămiššîm ûšənayim yôm.
quotations.translation: The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, after fifty-two days.

quotations.original: וַתִּלָּקַ֨ח אֶסְתֵּ֜ר אֶל־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית מַלְכוּת֔וֹ בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֖י הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ טֵבֵ֑ת בִּשְׁנַת־שֶׁ֖בַע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃
quotations.transliteration: wattillāqaḥ ʾestēr ʾel-hammelek̲ ʾăḥašwērôš ʾel-bêt̲ malk̲ût̲ô baḥōd̲eš hāʿăśîrî hûʾ-ḥōd̲eš ṭēb̲ēt̲ bišnat̲-šeb̲aʿ ləmalk̲ût̲ô.
quotations.translation: Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, in his royal palace, in the tenth month, which is the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

quotations.original: בְּיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לְעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ שְׁבָ֔ט בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔הוּ בֶּן־עִדּ֥וֹא הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
quotations.transliteration: bəyôm ʿeśrîm wəʾarbāʿāh ləʿaštê-ʿāśār ḥōd̲eš hûʾ-ḥōd̲eš šəb̲āṭ bišnat̲ šətayim ləd̲ārəyāweš hāyāh d̲əb̲ar-YHWH ʾel-zək̲aryāh ben-berek̲yāhû ben-ʿiddôʾ hannāb̲îʾ lēʾmōr.
quotations.translation: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Darius—the month of Shebat—this word of GOD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah son of Iddo:

quotations.original: בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֔ן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ הִפִּ֣יל פּוּר֩ ה֨וּא הַגּוֹרָ֜ל לִפְנֵ֣י הָמָ֗ן מִיּ֧וֹם ׀ לְי֛וֹם וּמֵחֹ֛דֶשׁ לְחֹ֥דֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֖ר הוּא־חֹ֥דֶשׁ אֲדָֽר׃ {ס}
quotations.transliteration: baḥōd̲eš hāriʾšôn hûʾ-ḥōd̲eš nîsān bišnat̲ šətêm ʿeśrēh lammelek̲ ʾăḥašwērôš hippîl pûr hûʾ haggôrāl lip̲nê hāmān miyyôm  ləyôm ûmēḥōd̲eš ləḥōd̲eš šənêm-ʿāśār hûʾ-ḥōd̲eš ʾăd̲ār.
quotations.translation: In the first month, that is, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, pur—which means “the lot”—was cast before Haman concerning every day and every month, [until it fell on] the twelfth month, that is, the month of Adar.

quotations.original:
הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃ 
שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃
quotations.transliteration:
hēn qed̲em ʾehĕlōk̲ wəʾênennû wəʾāḥôr wəlōʾ-ʾāb̲în lô.
śəmōʾwl baʿăśōt̲ô wəlōʾ-ʾāḥaz yaʿṭōp̲ yāmîn wəlōʾ ʾerʾeh.

quotations.original:
הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃ 
שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃
quotations.transliteration:
hēn qed̲em ʾehĕlōk̲ wəʾênennû wəʾāḥôr wəlōʾ-ʾāb̲în lô.
śəmōʾwl baʿăśōt̲ô wəlōʾ-ʾāḥaz yaʿṭōp̲ yāmîn wəlōʾ ʾerʾeh.

quotations.original:
הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃ 
שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃
quotations.transliteration:
hēn qed̲em ʾehĕlōk̲ wəʾênennû wəʾāḥôr wəlōʾ-ʾāb̲în lô.
śəmōʾwl baʿăśōt̲ô wəlōʾ-ʾāḥaz yaʿṭōp̲ yāmîn wəlōʾ ʾerʾeh.

quotations.original:
הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃ 
שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃
quotations.transliteration:
hēn qed̲em ʾehĕlōk̲ wəʾênennû wəʾāḥôr wəlōʾ-ʾāb̲în lô.
śəmōʾwl baʿăśōt̲ô wəlōʾ-ʾāḥaz yaʿṭōp̲ yāmîn wəlōʾ ʾerʾeh.

quotations.original: הֲֽ֭מִבִּינָ֣תְךָ יַאֲבֶר־נֵ֑ץ יִפְרֹ֖שׂ כְּנָפָ֣ו לְתֵימָֽן׃
quotations.transliteration: hămibbînāt̲ək̲ā yaʾăb̲er-nēṣ yip̲rōś kənāp̲āw lət̲êmān.
quotations.translation:
Is it by your wisdom that the hawk grows pinions,
Spreads his wings to the south?

quotations.original: וַֽיהֹוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם אַחֲרֵי֙ הִפָּֽרֶד־ל֣וֹט מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֑ם צָפֹ֥נָה וָנֶ֖גְבָּה וָקֵ֥דְמָה וָיָֽמָּה׃
quotations.transliteration: waihōwāh ʾāmar ʾel-ʾab̲rām ʾaḥărê hippāred̲-lôṭ mēʿimmô śāʾ nāʾ ʿênêk̲ā ûrəʾēh min-hammāqôm ʾăšer-ʾattāh šām ṣāp̲ōnāh wāneg̲bāh wāqēd̲əmāh wāyāmmāh.
quotations.translation: And יהוה said to Abram, after Lot had parted from him, “Raise your eyes and look out from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west,

quotations.original: וַֽיהֹוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם אַחֲרֵי֙ הִפָּֽרֶד־ל֣וֹט מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֑ם צָפֹ֥נָה וָנֶ֖גְבָּה וָקֵ֥דְמָה וָיָֽמָּה׃
quotations.transliteration: wəYHWH ʾāmar ʾel-ʾab̲rām ʾaḥărê hippāred̲-lôṭ mēʿimmô śāʾ nāʾ ʿênêk̲ā ûrəʾēh min-hammāqôm ʾăšer-ʾattāh šām ṣāp̲ōnāh wāneg̲bāh wāqēd̲əmāh wāyāmmāh.
quotations.translation: And יהוה said to Abram, after Lot had parted from him, “Raise your eyes and look out from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west,

quotations.original: וְאֵ֖לֶּה שְׁמ֣וֹת הַשְּׁבָטִ֑ים מִקְצֵ֣ה צָפ֡וֹנָה אֶל־יַ֣ד דֶּֽרֶךְ־חֶתְלֹ֣ן ׀ לְֽבוֹא־חֲמָ֡ת חֲצַ֣ר עֵינָן֩ גְּב֨וּל דַּמֶּ֤שֶׂק צָפ֙וֹנָה֙ אֶל־יַ֣ד חֲמָ֔ת וְהָיוּ־ל֧וֹ פְאַת־קָדִ֛ים הַיָּ֖ם דָּ֥ן אֶחָֽד׃
quotations.transliteration: wəʾēlleh šəmôt̲ haššəb̲āṭîm miqṣēh ṣāp̲ônāh ʾel-yad̲ derek̲-ḥet̲lōn  ləb̲ôʾ-ḥămāt̲ ḥăṣar ʿênān gəb̲ûl dammeśeq ṣāp̲ônāh ʾel-yad̲ ḥămāt̲ wəhāyû-lô p̲əʾat̲-qād̲îm hayyām dān ʾeḥād̲.
quotations.translation: Now these are the names of the tribes: from the north end, beside the way of Hethlon to the entrance of Hamath, Hazar-enan, at the border of Damascus, northward, beside Hamath; and they shall have their sides east and west: Dan, one portion.

quotations.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: wayyiqrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm  lāʾôr yôm wəlaḥōšek̲ qārāʾ lāyəlāh wayhî-ʿereb̲ wayhî-b̲ōqer yôm ʾeḥād̲.
quotations.translation: God called the light Day and called the darkness Night. And there was evening and there was morning, a first day.

quotations.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: wayyiqrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm  lāʾôr yôm wəlaḥōšek̲ qārāʾ lāyəlāh wayhî-ʿereb̲ wayhî-b̲ōqer yôm ʾeḥād̲.
quotations.translation: God called the light Day and called the darkness Night. And there was evening and there was morning, a first day.

quotations.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: wayyiqrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm  lāʾôr yôm wəlaḥōšek̲ qārāʾ lāyəlāh wayhî-ʿereb̲ wayhî-b̲ōqer yôm ʾeḥād̲.
quotations.translation: God called the light Day and called the darkness Night. And there was evening and there was morning, a first day.

quotations.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ {פ}
quotations.transliteration: wayyiqrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm  lāʾôr yôm wəlaḥōšek̲ qārāʾ lāyəlāh wayhî-ʿereb̲ wayhî-b̲ōqer yôm ʾeḥād̲.
quotations.translation: God called the light Day and called the darkness Night. And there was evening and there was morning, a first day.

quotations.original: וַיַּכֵּ֥ם דָּוִ֛ד מֵהַנֶּ֥שֶׁף וְעַד־הָעֶ֖רֶב לְמָֽחֳרָתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־נִמְלַ֤ט מֵהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּי֩ אִם־אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת אִֽישׁ־נַ֛עַר אֲשֶׁר־רָכְב֥וּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃
quotations.transliteration: wayyakkēm dāwid̲ mēhannešep̲ wəʿad̲-hāʿereb̲ ləmoḥŏrāt̲ām wəlōʾ-nimlaṭ mēhem ʾîš kî ʾim-ʾarbaʿ mēʾôt̲ ʾîš-naʿar ʾăšer-rāk̲əb̲û ʿal-haggəmallîm wayyānusû.
quotations.translation: David attacked them from before dawn until the evening of the next day; none of them escaped, except four hundred young men who mounted camels and got away.

quotations.original: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם וְהַחֲשַׁכְתִּ֥י לָאָ֖רֶץ בְּי֥וֹם אֽוֹר׃
quotations.transliteration: wəhāyāh bayyôm hahûʾ nəʾum ʾăd̲ōnāi YHWH wəhēb̲ēʾt̲î haššemeš baṣṣohŏrāyim wəhaḥăšak̲tî lāʾāreṣ bəyôm ʾôr.
quotations.translation:
And in that day
—declares the Sovereign  GOD—
I will make the sun set at noon,
I will darken the earth on a sunny day.

quotations.original: כִּ֣י לְכׇל־חֵ֔פֶץ יֵ֖שׁ עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּֽי־רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם רַבָּ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃
quotations.transliteration: kî lək̲ol-ḥēp̲eṣ yēš ʿēt̲ ûmišpāṭ kî-rāʿat̲ hāʾād̲ām rabbāh ʿālāyw.
quotations.translation: For there is a time for every experience, including the doom; for a man’s calamity overwhelms him.

quotations.original: בִּשְׁנַת־מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה אֶת־אֲדֹנָ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֖א רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֑א וְשׁוּלָ֖יו מְלֵאִ֥ים אֶת־הַהֵיכָֽל׃
quotations.transliteration: bišnat̲-môt̲ hammelek̲ ʿuzziyyāhû wāʾerʾeh ʾet̲-ʾăd̲ōnāi yōšēb̲ ʿal-kissēʾ rām wəniśśāʾ wəšûlāyw məlēʾîm ʾet̲-hahêk̲āl.
quotations.translation: In the year that King Uzziah died, I beheld my Sovereign seated on a high and lofty throne; and the skirts of God’s robe filled the temple.

quotations.original: אַל־תִּירָ֖א כִּ֣י אִתְּךָ־אָ֑נִי מִמִּזְרָח֙ אָבִ֣יא זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֖ב אֲקַבְּצֶֽךָּ׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾal-tîrāʾ kî ʾittək̲ā-ʾānî mimmizrāḥ ʾāb̲îʾ zarʿek̲ā ûmimmaʿărāb̲ ʾăqabbəṣekkā.

quotations.original: אַל־תִּירָ֖א כִּ֣י אִתְּךָ־אָ֑נִי מִמִּזְרָח֙ אָבִ֣יא זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֖ב אֲקַבְּצֶֽךָּ׃
quotations.transliteration: ʾal-tîrāʾ kî ʾittək̲ā-ʾānî mimmizrāḥ ʾāb̲îʾ zarʿek̲ā ûmimmaʿărāb̲ ʾăqabbəṣekkā.

quotations.original: הוֹלֵךְ֙ אֶל־דָּר֔וֹם וְסוֹבֵ֖ב אֶל־צָפ֑וֹן סוֹבֵ֤ב ׀ סֹבֵב֙ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ וְעַל־סְבִיבֹתָ֖יו שָׁ֥ב הָרֽוּחַ׃
quotations.transliteration: hôlēk̲ ʾel-dārôm wəsôb̲ēb̲ ʾel-ṣāp̲ôn sôb̲ēb̲  sōb̲ēb̲ hôlēk̲ hārûaḥ wəʿal-səb̲îb̲ōt̲āyw šāb̲ hārûaḥ.
quotations.translation:
Southward blowing,
Turning northward,
Ever turning blows the wind;
On its rounds the wind returns.

quotations.original: הֲלֹא־הֵ֜מָּה בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן אַֽחֲרֵי֙ דֶּ֚רֶךְ מְב֣וֹא הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ בְּאֶ֙רֶץ֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בָּעֲרָבָ֑ה מ֚וּל הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל אֵ֖צֶל אֵלוֹנֵ֥י מֹרֶֽה׃
quotations.transliteration: hălōʾ-hēmmāh bəʿēb̲er hayyardēn ʾaḥărê derek̲ məb̲ôʾ haššemeš bəʾereṣ hakkənaʿănî hayyōšēb̲ bāʿărāb̲āh mûl haggilgāl ʾēṣel ʾēlônê mōreh.
quotations.translation: Both are on the other side of the Jordan, beyond the west road that is in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the Arabah—near Gilgal, by the terebinths of Moreh.

quotations.original:
(6') (...) BAR NE u GAN NITA : GU₄ KIN u AB MU[NUS SIG DU₆ u ZIZ2 NITA]	
(7′)	ŠU APIN u ŠE MUNUS : aš2-šu2 mul2.BABBAR ina KI MUNUS.MEŠ KI d.30 GUB-zu NITA U3.TU : aš2-šu2 d.GENNA ⸢lu⸣ [d.ṣal-bat-a-nu]	
(8′)	ina KI MUNUS.MEŠ KI 30 NITA U3.TU : aš2-šu2 d.GU₄.UD ina KI.MEŠ ša2 NITA u MUNUS KI 30 MUNUS ⸢U3⸣.[TU]	
(9′)	ša2 d.dil-bat KIMIN-ma
quotations.translation:
(6') (...) Month I, month V, and month IX (the first triplicity) are masculine. Month II, month VI, and month X (the second triplicty) are fem[inine. Month III, month VII, and month XI (the third triplicity) are masculine]. 
(7') Month IV, month VIII, and month XII (the fourth triplicity) are feminine. Because Jupiter stands in the region of the feminine signs (of the zodiac) with the moon, she will give birth to a boy. Because Saturn or
[Mars] 
(8') (stands) in the region of feminine signs (of the zodiac) with the moon,
she will give birth to a boy. Because Mercury (stands) in the region of masculine
or feminine (signs of the zodiac) with the moon, she will give birth to a girl.
(9') For Venus it is the same.
quotations.publication: Reiner, E. 2000. Early Zodiologia and Related Matters. In: Wisdom, Gods and Literature, Studies in Assyriology in Honour of W. G. Lambert, eds. Andrew R. George and I. L. Finkel. Winona Lake, Indiana: Eisenbauns: 421-427.

quotations.original: Κριός ἐστιν οἶκος Ἄρεως, ζῴδιον ἀρρενικόν, τροπικόν, χερσαῖον
quotations.translation: Aries is a house of Mars, a masculine zodiac sign, tropical, of dry land

quotations.original: Κριός ἐστιν οἶκος Ἄρεως, ζῴδιον ἀρρενικόν, τροπικόν, (…) ἡγεμονικόν
quotations.translation: Aries is a house of Mars, a masculine zodiac sign, tropical, (…) hegemonic

quotations.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף מָֽה־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם הֲל֣וֹא יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּֽי־נַחֵ֧שׁ יְנַחֵ֛שׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֹֽנִי׃
quotations.transliteration: wayyōʾmer lāhem yôsēp̲ māh-hammaʿăśeh hazzeh ʾăšer ʿăśît̲em hălôʾ yəd̲aʿtem kî-naḥēš yənaḥēš ʾîš ʾăšer kāmōnî.
quotations.translation: Joseph said to them, “What is this deed that you have done? Do you not know that a man like me practices divination?”

quotations.original: Κριός ἐστιν οἶκος Ἄρεως, ζῴδιον ἀρρενικόν, τροπικόν, χερσαῖον, ἡγεμονικόν, πυρῶδες, ἐλεύθερον, ἀνωφερές, ἡμίφωνον, ἀγαθόν, εὐμετάβολον, διοικητικόν, δημόσιον, πολιτικόν, ὀλιγόγονον, λατρῶδες, κόσμου μεσουράνημα καὶ δόξης αἴτιον, δίχρωμον ἐπεὶ ὁ Ἥλιος καὶ ἡ Σελήνη ποιοῦσιν ἀλφούς, λειχῆνας  ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἀσύνδετον, ἐκλειπτικόν
quotations.translation: Aries is a house of Ares, a masculine zodiac-sign, tropic, of dry-land, hegemonic, of fire, of free men, ascending, semi-voiced, good, variable, controlling, of the (common) people, political, of low fertility, servile, the midheaven of the cosmos and a source of glory, two-colored when Sun and Moon produce spots (and) cankers; it is also non-conjunctive, ecliptic

quotations.original: Ταῦρός ἐστι θηλυκόν, στερεόν, κείμενον ἐν τῇ ἐαρινῇ τροπῇ, ὀστῶδες, μελοκοπούμενον, ἀνατέλλον ἐκ τῶν ὀπισθίων, δῦνον δὲ ὀρθόν, οὗ τὸ πλεῖστον μέρος ἐν τῷ ἀφανεῖ κόσμῳ κεῖται
quotations.translation: Taurus is a feminine (sign), firm, lying in the vernal equinox (lit. springtime turning), bony, with mutilated limbs, rising back to front, but setting vertically, whose greater part lies in the invisible part of the cosmos

quotations.original: Δίδυμοί εἰσιν ἀρσενικοί, δίσωμοι, εὔφωνοι, οἶκος Ἑρμοῦ, ἀνωφερεῖς, ἀερώδεις, θηλυνόμενοι, δουλελεύθεροι, στειρώδεις, δημόσιοι.
quotations.translation: Gemini is masculine, two-bodied, good-voiced, a house of Mercury, ascending, of air, effeminate, of freedmen, barren, of the (common) people

quotations.original:
Καρκίνος εὐδεινός. κατὰ μέρος δὲ ἐπὶ τοὺς δύο ἀστέρας τοὺς πρώτους νοταπηλιωτικοὺς εὐτελής, φθαρτικός, πνιγώδης, σεισμοποιός· ἀπὸ δὲ
τούτων μέχρι μοίρας ιʹ ποιεῖ τὸν ἀέρα κάθυγρον, καυματώδη (...) τὰ δεξιὰ εὐτελῆ καὶ φθαρτικά. (...) ἔστι δὲ οἶκος Σελήνης, θηλυκόν, τροπικόν, ὡροσκόπος κόσμου, δοῦλον,
κατωφερές, ἄφωνον, ὑδατῶδες, ἀγαθόν, εὐμετάβολον, δημόσιον, ὀχλικόν,
πολιτικόν, πολύγονον, ἀμφίβιον.
quotations.translation: Cancer is mild; as for the part at its first two, southeastern stars, it is worthless, destructive, stifling, earthquake-causing, but from these up to 10 degrees it makes the air moist and hot (...); the right-hand parts are worthless and destructive. (...) It is a house of the Moon, a feminine (sign), tropic, the ascendant (horoskopos) of the cosmos, a slave (sic), descending, unvoiced, watery, good, variable, of the (common) people, of the crowd, political, fertile, amphibious

quotations.original: Λέων ἐστὶν ἀρρενικόν, οἶκος Ἡλίου, ἐλεύθερον, πυρῶδες, εὔκρατον, νοερόν, βασιλικόν, ἑδραῖον, ἀγαθόν, ἀνωφερές, εὐμετάβολον, στερεόν, ἡγεμονικόν, πολιτικόν, ἀρκτικόν, ὀργίλον
quotations.translation: Leo is a masculine (sign), a house of the Sun, of free men, of fire, temperate, intellectual, royal, firm-seated, good, ascending, variable, firm, hegemonic, political, imperious, irascible

quotations.original:
Παρθένος οἶκος Ἑρμοῦ, θηλυκόν, πτερωτόν, ἀνθρωποειδές, τρυφῆρες, σχήματι Δίκης ἑστώς, δίσωμον, στειρῶδες, δουλελεύθερον, ἄγονον,
κατωφερές, γεῶδες, κοινόν, ἡμίφωνον καὶ ἄφωνον, σωματικόν, ἀτελές,
εὐμετάβολον, ἐργαστηριακόν, διφυές.
quotations.translation: Virgo is a house of Mercury, a feminine (sign), winged, humanoid, delicate (or, voluptuous), standing in the form of Justice, two-bodied, barren, of freedmen, infertile, descending, of earth, common, semi-voiced and unvoiced, corporeal, incomplete, variable, of workmen, two-natured

quotations.original: Ζυγὸς οἶκος Ἀφροδίτης, ἀρρενικόν, τροπικόν, ἀνθρωποειδές, ἀνωφερές, ἀερῶδες, θηλυνόμενον, φωνῆεν, ἀγαθόν, εὐμετάβολον, ὑπαρχόντων μειωτικόν, ὑπόγειον κόσμου, δημόσιον, ἐκλειπτικόν, προεστὸς καρπῶν, οἰνικῶν, ἐλαϊκῶν, μυρεψικῶν, σταθμῶν, μέτρων, ἐργαστηριακῶν.
quotations.translation: Libra is a house of Venus, a masculine (sign), tropic, humanoid, ascending, of air, effeminate, vocal, good, variable, causing goods to decrease, the immum caelum of the cosmos, of the (common) people, ecliptic, presiding over crops, wine-, olive-cultivation, perfumery (or, aromatics-cultivation), weights, measures, working-trades.

quotations.original: Σκορπίος οἶκος Ἄρεως, θηλυκόν, στερεόν, ὑδατῶδες, πολύσπερμον, φθοροποιόν, κατωφερές, ἄφωνον, δουλικόν, ἀμετάβλητον, δυσωδίας αἴτιον, ὑπαρχόντων ἀφαιρετικόν, ἐκλειπτικόν, πολύχουν.
quotations.translation: Scorpio is a house of Mars, a feminine (sign), firm, of water, fertile, destructive, descending, unvoiced, of slaves, invariable, source of bad odor, remover of goods, ecliptic, manifold

quotations.original: ἡγεῖτο δὲ αὐτῶν ὁ ἐκ τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ Τοξότης
quotations.translation: They (sc. the 'Cloud-centaurs') were led by the Archer from the zodiac

quotations.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηματικοὶ τοὺς ὀκτὼ μῆνας ἀσυνδέτους φασὶν εἶναι πάσης γενέσεως, τοὺς δ’ ἑπτὰ συνδετικούς· τὰ δ’ ἀσύνδετα ζῴδια <...> ἐστιν, ἐὰν τῶν οἰκοδεσποτούντων ἀστέρων τυγχάνῃ· ἐὰν γάρ τις τούτων τὴν ζωὴν καὶ τὸν βίον κληρώσηται, δυστυχεῖς καὶ ἀχρόνους σημαίνει· ἀσύνδετα δ’ ἐστὶ ζῴδια ὀκτὼ ἀριθμούμενα, οἷον κριὸς πρὸς σκορπίον ἀσύνδετος, ταῦρος πρὸς τοξότην ἀσύνδετος, δίδυμοι πρὸς αἰγόκερων, καρκίνος πρὸς ὑδροχόον, λέων πρὸς ἰχθύας, παρθένος πρὸς κριόν, <ζυγὸς πρὸς ταῦρον>· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τὰ ἑπτάμηνα ὄντα καὶ δεκάμηνα γόνιμα εἶναι· τὰ δ’ ὀκτάμηνα διὰ τὸ ἀσύνδετον τοῦ κόσμου φθείρεσθαι.
quotations.translation: The astrologers say that the eight months of every nativity are non-conjunctive, but the seven are conjunctive. The non-conjunctive zodiac signs <...> are, if they attain one of the house-ruling planets (lit. stars): for if one of these has been allotted life and livelihood, it indicates unfortunate and short-lived (natives). The non-conjunctive zodiac signs are eight in number, as Aries is non-conjunctive to Scorpio, Taurus to Sagittarius, Gemini to Capricorn, Cancer to Aquarius, Leo to Pisces, Virgo to Aries, Libra to Taurus. Therefore, they say, both the seventh-month and ten-month (fetuses) are viable, but the eight-month ones perish because of the cosmic disconnection.

quotations.original: Ὑδροχόος ἐστὶν ἐν οὐρανῷ ζῴδιον ἀρρενικόν, στερεόν, ἀνθρωπόμορφον, πάρυγρον, μονογενές· ἔστι δὲ ἄφωνον, κατάψυχρον, ἐλεύθερον, ἀνωφερές, θηλυνόμενον, ἀμετάβλητον, κακόν, ὀλιγόγονον, αἴτιον μόχθων τῶν δι’ ἀθλήσεως ἢ βασταγμάτων καὶ σκληρουργίας, ἐργαστικόν, δημόσιον
quotations.translation: Aquarius is a zodiac sign in the heavens, masculine, firm, anthropomorph, mildly moist (or, of the waterside), single-offspring, and it is unvoiced, chilly, of free men, ascending, effeminate, invariable, bad, of low fertility, a source of troubles through (athletic) training (or, competition) or carrying burdens and hard labor, of laborers, of the (common) people

quotations.original: ἔστι δ’ ὁ μὲν θερινὸς κατὰ καρκίνον, ὁ δὲ χειμερινὸς κατ’ αἰγόκερων. καὶ προσγειότατος μὲν ὢν ἡμῖν ὁ καρκίνος εὐλόγως τῇ προσγειοτάτῃ Σελήνῃ ἀπεδόθη, ἀφανοῦς δ’ ἔτι ὄντος τοῦ νοτίου πόλου τῷ μακρὰν ἔτι ἀφεστηκότι καὶ ἀνωτάτῳ τῶν πλανωμένων πάντων ὁ αἰγόκερως ἀπεδόθη. καὶ ἔχουσί γε ἐφεξῆς αἱ θέσεις τῶν ζῳδίων· ἀπὸ μὲν καρκίνου εἰς αἰγόκερων πρῶτα μὲν λέοντα οἶκον Ἡλίου, εἶτα παρθένον Ἑρμοῦ, ζυγὸν δὲ Ἀφροδίτης, σκορπίον δὲ Ἄρεος, τοξότην Διός, αἰγόκερων Κρόνου· ἀπὸ δ’ αἰγόκερω ἔμπαλιν ὑδροχόον Κρόνου, ἰχθύας Διός, Ἄρεος κριόν, ταῦρον Ἀφροδίτης, διδύμους Ἑρμοῦ, καὶ Σελήνης λοιπὸν καρκίνον. δύο οὖν ταύτας ἔθεντο πύλας καρκίνον καὶ αἰγόκερων οἱ θεολόγοι, Πλάτων δὲ δύο στόμια ἔφη· τούτων δὲ καρκίνον μὲν εἶναι δι’ οὗ κατίασιν αἱ ψυχαί, αἰγόκερων δὲ δι’ οὗ ἀνίασιν
quotations.translation: The summer(-tropic) is in Cancer, and the winter(-tropic) is in Capricorn. Cancer, being closest to us on earth, has with good reason been assigned to the Moon; as the south pole is invisible, Capricorn has been assigned to the far-distant and uppermost of the planets (sc. Saturn). The sequential positions of the zodiac signs are as follows: from Cancer to Capricorn, first of all Leo as house of the Sun, then Virgo as that of Mercury, Libra as that of Venus, Scorpio as that of Mars, Sagittarius as that of Jupiter, Capricorn as that of Saturn; and backwards from Capricorn, Aquarius as that of Saturn, Pisces as that of Jupiter, Aries as that of Mars, Taurus as that of Venus, Gemini as that of Mercury, and the remaining Cancer as that of the Moon. The theologians have set Cancer and Capricorn as the two gates (sc. of the heavens), but Plato said that they were two mouths, and that of them Cancer is the one through which souls descend, and Capricorn, through which they ascend.
quotations.source: Porphyry of Tyre, On the Cave of the Nymphs

quotations.original:
In Geminorum signo quae sint partes plenae, quae vacuae, hoc demonstratur exemplo. Sunt autem in Geminis plenae partes XVIII, vacuae XII. 

I locus partes VII Thesogar [idest byy]
II locus partes II vacuus 
III locus partes V Ver [idest asuae/asra]
IV locus partes III vacuus 
V locus partes VI Tepis [idest acosoae/atosoae]
VI locus partes VII vacuus.
quotations.translation:
In the sign of Gemini some degrees are full, some empty. This will be shown by example. But in Gemini there are 18° full and 12° empty.
1. 7° Thesogar [i.e. Byy]
2. 2° empty
3. 5° Ver [i.e. Asuae/Asra]
4. 3° empty
5. 6° Tepis [i.e. Acosoae/Atosoae]
6. 7° empty
quotations.publication: Firmicus Maternus. 1897. Ivlii Firmici Materni Matheseos Libri VIII, ed. W. Kroll, F. Skutsch. Stuttgart: B. G. Teubner.

quotations.original: Αἱ τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλείψεις γίνονται κατ' ἐπιπρόσθησιν σελήνης. Μετεωρότερου γὰρ φερομένου τοῦ ἡλίου, ταπεινοτέρας δὲ τῆς σελήνης, ὅταν κατὰ τὴν αὐτὴν μοῖραν γένηται ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ἡ σελήνη, ὑποτροχάσασα ἡ σελήνη τῷ ἡλίῳ ἀντιφράττει ταῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἡλίου φερομέναις αὐγαῖς πρὸς ἡμᾶς.
quotations.translation: Solar eclipses happen due to covering by the Moon. For since the Sun moves higher, and the Moon lower, whenever the Sun and the Moon arrive at the same degree, the Moon, having run under the Sun, blocks the rays moving from the Sun towards us.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Διόπερ οὐδὲ ῥητέον αὐτὰς κυρίως ἐκλείψεις, ἀλλ' ἐπιπροσθήσεις. Τοῦ μὲν γὰρ ἡλίου οὐδὲ ἕν μέρος οὐδέποτε ἐκλείψει· ἡμῖν δὲ ἀθεώρητος γίνεται διὰ τὴν ἐπιπρόσθησιν τῆς σελήνης.
quotations.translation: And therefore, it should not be said that these [solar eclipses] are 'failings' in the proper sense, but rather 'coverings'. For not one part of the Sun will ever 'fail': it becomes invisible to us due to the covering by the Moon.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Αἱ τῆς σελήνης ἐκλείψεις γίνονται κατὰ τὴν εἰς τὸ σκίασμα τῆς γῆς ἔμπτωσιν τῆς σελήνης. (...) Ὅταν οὖν κατὰ διάμετρον γένηται ἡ σελήνη τῷ ἡλίῳ, τότε καὶ τὸ σκίασμα τῆς γῆς κατὰ διάμετρον γίνεται τῷ ἡλίῳ· ὅθεν ἡ σελήνη ταπεινοτέρα φερομένη τοῦ σκιάσματος εὐλόγως ἐμπίπτει εἰς τὸ σκίασμα τῆς γῆς.
quotations.translation: Lunar eclipses happen due to falling of the Moon into the shadow of the Earth. (...) So whenever the Moon becomes diametrically opposite the Sun, the shadow of the Earth too becomes diametrically opposite the Sun; whence the Moon, moving lower than the shadow, logically falls into the shadow of the Earth.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Κατὰ γὰρ τὸν αὐτὸν χρόνον οἷς μὲν ὁ ἥλιος ὅλος ἐκλείπει, οἷς δὲ τὸ ἥμισυ, οἷς δὲ τὸ ἔλαττον τοῦ ἡμίσεος, οἷς δὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐδὲν μέρος τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλελοιπὸς θεωρεῖται.
quotations.translation: For at the same time, for some the Sun is eclipsed whole, but for some half of it, and for some less than half, and for some no part of the Sun at all is observed to have been eclipsed.

quotations.original: ἀλλ’ οὐ προσέσχον πρῶτον τὸν πολεύοντα καὶ διέποντα Ἑρμῆν εἰς πάθος ἐμπεπτωκότα· καὶ γὰρ μεγίστην ἀπόστασιν ἀπεῖχε τοῦ Ἡλίου καὶ ὑπὸ Κρόνου μόνου ἐθεωρεῖτο· ὃ καὶ βιαιοθάνατον ἀπετέλει.
quotations.translation: But (those who previously interpreted this horoscope) did not pay attention first of all to Mercury, the one inhabiting and managing (the day and hour), which had fallen into suffering, for it had its greatest elongation from the Sun and was in aspect with Saturn only, and that caused violent death.

quotations.original: Principio Assyrii, ut ab ultimis auctoritatem repetam, propter planitiem magnitudinemque regionum, quas incolebant, cum caelum ex omni parte patens atque apertum intuerentur, traiectiones motusque stellarum observitaverunt, quibus notatis, quid cuique significaretur memoriae prodiderunt.
quotations.translation: First of all—to seek authority from the most distant sources—the Assyrians, on account of the vast plains inhabited by them, and because of the open and unobstructed view of the heavens presented to them on every side, took observations of the paths and movements of the stars, and, having made note of them, transmitted to posterity what significance they had for each person.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Principio Assyrii, ut ab ultimis auctoritatem repetam, propter planitiem magnitudinemque regionum, quas incolebant, cum caelum ex omni parte patens atque apertum intuerentur, traiectiones motusque stellarum observitaverunt, quibus notatis, quid cuique significaretur memoriae prodiderunt.
quotations.translation: First of all—to seek authority from the most distant sources—the Assyrians, on account of the vast plains inhabited by them, and because of the open and unobstructed view of the heavens presented to them on every side, took observations of the paths and movements of the stars, and, having made note of them, transmitted to posterity what significance they had for each person.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Qua in natione Chaldaei, non ex artis sed ex gentis vocabulo nominati, diuturna observatione siderum scientiam putantur effecisse, ut praedici posset quid cuique eventurum et quo quisque fato natus esset.
quotations.translation: And in that same nation the Chaldeans—a name which they derived not from their art but their race—have, it is thought, by means of long-continued observation of the constellations, perfected a science which enables them to foretell what any man’s lot will be and for what fate he was born.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Qua in natione Chaldaei, non ex artis sed ex gentis vocabulo nominati, diuturna observatione siderum scientiam putantur effecisse, ut praedici posset quid cuique eventurum et quo quisque fato natus esset.
quotations.translation: And in that same nation the Chaldeans—a name which they derived not from their art but their race—have, it is thought, by means of long-continued observation of the constellations, perfected a science which enables them to foretell what any man’s lot will be and for what fate he was born.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original:
Et, si stellarum motus cursusque vagantis
nosse velis, quae sint signorum in sede locatae
(quae verbo et falsis Graiorum vocibus errant,
re vera certo lapsu spatioque feruntur),
omnia iam cernes divina mente notata.
quotations.translation:
When one has learned the motions and variant paths of the planets,
Stars that abide in the seat of the signs, in the Zodiac’s girdle,
(Spoken of falsely as vagrants or rovers in Greek nomenclature,
Whereas in truth their distance is fixed and their speed is determined,)
Then will he know that all are controlled by an Infinite Wisdom.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original:
Nam primum astrorum volucris te consule motus
concursusque gravis stellarum ardore micantis
tu quoque, cum tumulos Albano in monte nivalis
lustrasti et laeto mactasti lacte Latinas,
vidisti et claro tremulos ardore cometas,
multaque misceri nocturna strage putasti
quotations.translation:
You, being consul, at once did observe the swift constellations,
Noting the glare of luminous stars in direful conjunction;
Then you beheld the tremulous sheen of the Northern aurora,
When, on ascending the mountainous heights of snowy Albanus,
You offered joyful libations of milk at the Feast of the Latins
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.translation:

quotations.comment: W. A. Falconer points to Seneca Quaestiones Naturales vii. 6. for cometes = aurora.

quotations.original:
cum claram speciem concreto lumine luna
abdidit et subito stellanti nocte perempta est.
quotations.translation:
Then, of a sudden, the moon at her full was blotted from heaven—
Hidden her features resplendent, though night was bejewelled with planets;
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original:
quid vero Phoebi fax, tristis nuntia belli,
quae magnum ad columen flammato ardore volabat,
praecipitis caeli partis obitusque petessens?
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original:
quid vero Phoebi fax, tristis nuntia belli,
quae magnum ad columen flammato ardore volabat,
praecipitis caeli partis obitusque petessens?
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original:
aut cum terribili perculsus fulmine civis
luce serenanti vitalia lumina liquit?
quotations.translation:
Then did a Roman depart from these radiant abodes of the living,
Stricken by terrible lightning from heavens serene and unclouded.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original:

quotations.original: Quorum alia sunt posita in monumentis et disciplina, quod Etruscorum declarant et haruspicini et fulgurales et tonitruales libri, vestri etiam augurales;
quotations.translation: Some are based upon records and usage, as is evident from the Etruscan books on divination by means of inspection of entrails and by means of thunder and lightning, and as is also evident from the books of your augural college;
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Quorum alia sunt posita in monumentis et disciplina, quod Etruscorum declarant et haruspicini et fulgurales et tonitruales libri, vestri etiam augurales;
quotations.translation: Some are based upon records and usage, as is evident from the Etruscan books on divination by means of inspection of entrails and by means of thunder and lightning, and as is also evident from the books of your augural college;
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Qui etsi causas ipsas non cernunt, signa tamen causarum et notas cernunt; ad quas adhibita memoria et diligentia et monumentis superiorum efficitur ea divinatio, quae artificiosa dicitur, extorum, fulgorum, ostentorum signorumque caelestium.
quotations.translation: The careful study and recollection of those signs, aided by the records of former times, has evolved that sort of divination, known as artificial, which is divination by means of entrails, lightnings, portents, and celestial phenomena.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Nam si obscurior et quasi caliginosa stella extiterit, pingue et concretum esse caeium, ut eius asspiratio gravis et pestilens futura sit; sin illustris et perlucida stella apparuerit, significari caelum esse tenue purumque et propterea salubre.
quotations.translation: For if the star rises dim and, as it were enveloped in a fog, this indicates a thick and heavy atmosphere, which will give off very unwholesome vapours; but if the star appears clear and brilliant, this is a sign that the atmosphere is light and pure and, as a consequence, will be conducive to good health.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Nam si obscurior et quasi caliginosa stella extiterit, pingue et concretum esse caeium, ut eius asspiratio gravis et pestilens futura sit; sin illustris et perlucida stella apparuerit, significari caelum esse tenue purumque et propterea salubre.
quotations.translation: For if the star rises dim and, as it were enveloped in a fog, this indicates a thick and heavy atmosphere, which will give off very unwholesome vapours; but if the star appears clear and brilliant, this is a sign that the atmosphere is light and pure and, as a consequence, will be conducive to good health.

quotations.original: Nonne perspicuum est ex prima admiratione hominum, quod tonitrua iactusque fulminum extimuissent, credidisse ea efficere rerum omnium praepotentem Iovem?
quotations.translation: It is perfectly evident that, out of the wonder and fear excited in primitive man by lightning and thunderbolts, sprang his belief that those phenomena were caused by omnipotent Jove.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Sed de auspiciis alio loco, nunc de fulguribus.
quotations.translation: But I shall speak of auspices in another connexion—now I am going to discuss lightnings.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Quae enim extis, quae fulgoribus, quae portentis, quae astris praesentiuntur, haec notata sunt observatione diuturna.
quotations.translation: For the results of those artificial means of divination, by means of entrails, lightnings, portents, and astrology, have been the subject of observation for a long period of time.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: nam et prognosticorum causas persecuti sunt et Boëthus Stoicus, qui est a te nominatus, et noster etiam Posidonius
quotations.translation: For example, the causes of meteorological phenomena have been investigated by Boëthus the Stoic, whom you mentioned, and by our friend Posidonius;
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Chaldaeis in praedictione et in notatione cuiusque vitae ex natali die minime esse credendum.
quotations.translation: No reliance whatever is to be placed in Chaldean astrologers when they profess to forecast a man’s future from the position of the stars on the day of his birth.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Chaldaeis in praedictione et in notatione cuiusque vitae ex natali die minime esse credendum.
quotations.translation: No reliance whatever is to be placed in Chaldean astrologers when they profess to forecast a man’s future from the position of the stars on the day of his birth.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Nominat etiam Panaetius, qui unus e Stoicis astrologorum praedicta reiecit, Anchialum et Cassandrum, summos astrologos illius aetatis, qua erat ipse, cum in ceteris astrologiae partibus excellerent, hoc praedictionis genere re non usos.
quotations.translation: Panaetius, too, who was the only one of the Stoics to reject the prophecies of astrologers, mentions Anchialus and Cassander as the greatest astronomers of his day and states that they did not employ their art as a means of divining, though they were eminent in all other branches of astronomy.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Sed ut ratione utamur omissis testibus, sic isti disputant qui haec Chaldaeorum natalicia praedicta defendunt.
quotations.translation: But let us dismiss our witnesses and employ reasoning. Those men who defend the natal-day prophecies of the Chaldeans, argue in this way : ...
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Vim quandam esse, aiunt, signifero in orbe, qui Graece ζωδιακός dicitur
quotations.translation: In the starry belt which the Greeks call the Zodiac there is a certain force
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: cum autem in eam ipsam partem orbis venerint, in qua sit ortus eius, qui nascatur, aut in eam, quae coniunctum aliquid habeat aut consentiens, ea ‘triangula’ illi et ‘quadrata’ nominant.
quotations.translation: But when they have come into that sign of the Zodiac under which someone is born, or into a sign having some connexion or accord with the natal sign, they form what is called a ‘triangle’ or ‘square.’
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Κριός ἐστιν (…) ζῴδιον (…) λατρῶδες
quotations.translation: Aries is a (…) servile zodiac sign

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἀσύνδετον
quotations.translation: (Aries) is also an unconnected (zodiac sign)

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἀσύνδετον, ἐκλειπτικόν
quotations.translation: (Aries) is also an unconnected, ecliptic (zodiac sign)

quotations.original: cum tempestatumque caeli conversiones commutationesque tantae fiant accessu stellarum et recessu ...
quotations.translation: since, through the procession and retrogression of the stars, the great variety and change of the seasons and of temperature take place ...
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: cum tempestatumque caeli conversiones commutationesque tantae fiant accessu stellarum et recessu ...
quotations.translation: since, through the procession and retrogression of the stars, the great variety and change of the seasons and of temperature take place ...
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: ... quanta humilitate luna feratur terram paene contingens
quotations.translation: ... how close the moon comes to the earth, which indeed it almost touches
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: quantum [Luna] absit a proxima Mercuri stella, multo autem longius a Veneris
quotations.translation: how far [the Moon] is from Mercury, the nearest star; how much further yet it is from Venus
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: deinde alio intervallo [luna] distet a sole, cuius lumine collustrari putatur
quotations.translation: and what a great interval separates [the moon] from the sun, which is supposed to give it light.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Quae potest igitur contagio ex infinito paene intervo paene intervallo pertinere ad lunam vel potius ad terram?
quotations.translation: In view, therefore, of these almost limitless distances, what influence can the planets exercise upon the moon, or rather, upon the earth?
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Quid? cum dicunt, id quod eis dicere necesse est, omnis omnium ortus, quicumque gignantur in omni terra, quae incolatur, eosdem esse, eademque omnibus, qui eodem statu caeli et stellarum nati sint, accidere necesse esse, nonne eius modi sunt, ut ne caeli quidem naturam interpretes istos caeli nosse appareat?
quotations.translation: Again, when the Chaldeans say, as they are bound to do, that all persons born anywhere in the habitable earth under the same horoscope, are alike and must have the same fate, is it not evident that these would-be interpreters of the sky are of a class who are utterly ignorant of the nature of the sky?
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Cum enim illi orbes, qui caelum quasi medium dividunt et aspectum nostrum definiunt, qui a Graecis ὁρίζοντες nominantur, a nobis ‘finientes’ rectissime nominari possunt
quotations.translation: For the earth is, as it were, divided in half and our view limited by those circles which the Greeks call ὁρίζοντες, and which we may in all accuracy term finientes or horizons.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Sed quae tanta dementia est, ut in maximis motibus mutationibusque caeli nihil intersit, qui ventus, qui imber, quae tempestas ubique sit!
quotations.translation: But what utter madness in these astrologers, in considering the effect of the vast movements and changes in the heavens, to assume that wind and rain and weather anywhere have no effect at birth!
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Sed quae tanta dementia est, ut in maximis motibus mutationibusque caeli nihil intersit, qui ventus, qui imber, quae tempestas ubique sit!
quotations.translation: But what utter madness in these astrologers, in considering the effect of the vast movements and changes in the heavens, to assume that wind and rain and weather anywhere have no effect at birth!
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: ... si haec non vis et natura gignentium efficeret, sed temperatio lunae caelique moderatio.
quotations.translation: ... if the characteristics of children were determined, not by the natural power of heredity, but by the phases of the moon and by the condition of the sky.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Quodsi haec astro ingenerata et tradita essent, nulla res ea mutare posset.
quotations.translation: But if such defects had been engendered and implanted by a star nothing could have changed them.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Quodsi haec astro ingenerata et tradita essent, nulla res ea mutare posset.
quotations.translation: But if such defects had been engendered and implanted by a star nothing could have changed them.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: omnesne qui Cannensi pugna ceciderint uno astro fuerint?
quotations.translation: Did all the Romans who fell at Cannae have the same horoscope?
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: L. quidem Tarutius Firmanus, familiaris noster, in primis Chaldaicis rationibus eruditus, urbis etiam nostrae natalem diem repetebat ab iis Parilibus, quibus eam a Romulo conditam accepimus, Romamque, in iugo cum esset luna, natam esse dicebat, nec eius fata canere dubitabat.
quotations.translation: Be that as it may, our good friend Lucius Tarutius of Firmum, who was steeped in Chaldaic lore, made a calculation, based on the assumption that our city’s birthday was on the Feast of Pales (at which time tradition says it was founded by Romulus), and from that calculation Tarutius even went so far as to assert that Rome was born when the moon was in the sign of Libra and from that fact unhesitatingly prophesied her destiny.
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Et, si ad rem pertinet, quo modo caelo affecto compositisque sideribus quodque animal oriatur, valeat id necesse est etiam in rebus inanimis ; quo quid dici potest absurdius?
quotations.translation: Again : if it matters under what aspect of the sky or combination of the stars every animate being is born, then necessarily the same conditions affect inanimate things also : can any statement be more ridiculous than that?
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Fac in puero referre, ex qua affectione caeli primum spiritum duxerit;
quotations.translation: Assume, if you will, that it matters in the case of a child under what arrangement of the heavenly bodies it draws its first breath
quotations.publication: Cicero. On Old Age. On Friendship. On Divination. Translated by W. A. Falconer. Loeb Classical Library 154. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1923.

quotations.original: Κρόνος, Ἑρμῆς ἀγαθοδαιμονοῦντες, ὁ μὲν ἐν τῷ ιαʹ, ὁ δὲ ἐν τῷ εʹ
quotations.translation: Saturn, Mercury being in propitious places (lit., being in Agathos Daimon), the one in the 11th (place), and the other in the 5th (place)

quotations.original: Ταῦρός ἐστι (…) ὀστῶδες
quotations.translation: Taurus is a (…) bony (zodiac sign)

quotations.original: Ταῦρός ἐστι (…) μελοκοπούμενον
quotations.translation: Taurus is a (…) mutilated (zodiac sign)

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον κόσμου περιποιητικόν
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is in the place of security for the universe

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον (…) γεῶδες
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is (…) earthly

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον (…) χωρικόν
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is (…) rustic

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον (…) γεωργικόν
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is (…) agricultural

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον (…) δουλελεύθερον
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is (…) libertine

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον (…) κατωφερές
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is … downward-inclined (or, prone to lewdness)

quotations.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ ζῴδιον (…) ἡμίφωνον καὶ ἄφωνον
quotations.translation: The zodiac sign (Taurus) is … semi-vocal and non-vocal

quotations.original: Τῆς δὲ πρὸς ἄλληλα τάξεως καὶ θέσεως τῶν ιβʹ ζῳδίων διαφοραί εἰσι τέσσαρες. Ἃ μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν λέγεται κατὰ διάμετρον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ τρίγωνον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ τετράγωνον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ συζυγίαν, ὑπό τινων δὲ ἀντισυζυγίαν.
quotations.translation: Of the arrangement in comparison with each other and position of the 12 zodiac signs, there are four distinctions. One of them is called “in opposition”, another one “in trine”, another one “in quartile” and another one “in syzygy”, but according to some “(in) antisyzygy”.

quotations.original: Κατὰ τρίγωνον δέ ἐστι Κριὸς Λέων Τοξότης, Ταῦρος Παρθένος Αἰγόκερως, Δίδυμοι Ζυγὸς Ὑδροχόος, Καρκίνος Σκορπίος Ἰχθύες, τὰ πάντα τρίγωνα ἰσόπλευρα δʹ· ὑποτείνει δὲ ἡ τοῦ τριγώνου πλευρὰ ὑπὸ ζῴδια μὲν δʹ, μοίρας δὲ ρκʹ.
quotations.translation: “In trine” are Aries - Leo - Sagittarius, Taurus - Virgo - Capricorn, Gemini - Libra - Aquarius, Cancer - Scorpio - Pisces, all 4 equilateral triangles; the side of the triangle subtends 4 zodiac signs, or 120 degrees.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Κατὰ συζυγίαν δὲ λέγεται ζῴδια τὰ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ τόπου ἀνατέλλοντα καὶ εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον δύνοντα· ταῦτα δέ ἐστι τὰ ὑπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν παραλλήλων παραλαμβανόμενα κύκλων.
quotations.translation: “In syzygy” are called the zodiac signs that rise from the same place and set in the same place; these are the ones that are associated with the same parallel circles.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Κατὰ διάμετρον μὲν οὖν εἰσι ζῴδια τὰ κατὰ τὴν αὐτὴν διάμετρον κείμενα. Ἔστι δὲ τάδε· Κριὸς Ζυγός, Ταῦρος Σκορπίος, Δίδυμοι Τοξότης, Καρκίνος Αἰγόκερως, Λέων Ὑδροχόος, Παρθένος Ἰχθύες.
quotations.translation: “In opposition” are the zodiac signs that lie on the same diameter. These are the following: Aries - Libra, Taurus - Scorpio, Gemini - Sagittarius, Cancer - Capricorn, Leo - Aquarius, Virgo - Pisces.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.

quotations.original: Τῆς δὲ πρὸς ἄλληλα τάξεως καὶ θέσεως τῶν ιβʹ ζῳδίων διαφοραί εἰσι τέσσαρες. Ἃ μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν λέγεται κατὰ διάμετρον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ τρίγωνον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ τετράγωνον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ συζυγίαν, ὑπό τινων δὲ ἀντισυζυγίαν.
quotations.translation: Of the arrangement in comparison with each other and position of the 12 zodiac signs, there are four distinctions. One of them is called “in opposition”, another one “in trine”, another one “in quartile” and another one “in syzygy”, but according to some “(in) antisyzygy”.
quotations.publication: Geminus. 1975. Géminos, Introduction aux Phénomènes, ed. G. Aujac. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.
quotations.comment:
It is suggested by Evans and Berggren (2006), 125 + 257-258, to read ἀντισυζυγίαν as ἀντισκίαν instead.

(Evans, J. and Berggren, J.L. 2006. Geminos’s Introduction to the Phenomena: a translation and study of a Hellenistic survey of astronomy. Princeton and Oxford: Princeton University Press.)

quotations.original: Τῆς δὲ πρὸς ἄλληλα τάξεως καὶ θέσεως τῶν ιβʹ ζῳδίων διαφοραί εἰσι τέσσαρες. Ἃ μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν λέγεται κατὰ διάμετρον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ τρίγωνον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ τετράγωνον, ἃ δὲ κατὰ συζυγίαν, ὑπό τινων δὲ ἀντισυζυγίαν.
